# VeOmni 仓库昨日提交分析

## 1. 主要更新类型
- **功能新增**（Feature）：为 SeedOmni 框架新增对 Qwen3 模型的支持，同时涉及配置、文档、Agent 及 CI 等多模块联动更新。

## 2. 关键变更点及与项目方向的关系
- 该提交在 **omni、model、config、docs、agent、ci** 六个模块同步落地，体现了项目以"模型为中心的分布式训练配方库"为核心的架构理念——新模型的接入并非单一代码改动，而是贯穿训练配置、文档说明、智能体支持与持续集成的全链路更新。
- Qwen3 作为当前主流开源大模型系列之一，其支持直接扩展了 VeOmni"Scaling Any Modality Model"的多模态/多模型覆盖能力，与项目论文（arXiv:2508.02317）所倡导的通用化训练框架目标高度一致。
- 由 Cursor AI 辅助生成（Co-authored-by: Cursor），反映出项目团队已在开发流程中引入 AI 编程工具，这与提交范围中包含 CI 更新相呼应，暗示自动化工具链的进一步完善。

## 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义
- **生态扩展**：接入 Qwen3 使用户可以在 VeOmni 上直接训练基于 Qwen3 的多模态/全模态模型，降低了新模型接入门槛，有利于吸引更多基于 Qwen 生态的研究者与开发者。
- **工程成熟度**：六模块协同改动说明项目已形成规范的"新模型接入 SOP"（配置模板 + 文档 + CI 测试），这对一个旨在提供"Recipe Zoo"（配方库）的项目而言，是配方可复用性与工程质量的重要信号。
- **社区与协作**：#1357 的 PR 编号表明项目迭代活跃度较高，AI 辅助开发的显式标注也体现了团队对透明协作的重视。

## 4. 值得关注的技术点
- **全链路模型接入模式**：观察该提交如何在 config 中定义 Qwen3 的训练超参、在 model 中实现结构封装、在 ci 中加入回归测试，可作为未来接入其他模型（如 LLaMA、GLM 系列）的参考模板。
- **Agent 模块的联动**：提交涉及 agent 模块，暗示 VeOmni 可能在探索"训练配方"与"推理/智能体"场景的打通，值得关注其后续是否发展为端到端的训练-部署闭环。
- **CI 中新增的测试覆盖**：Qwen3 相关测试的加入将约束后续改动不破坏该模型的训练链路，对长期维护质量有积极意义。

## 5. 对项目发展的整体影响
基于 README，VeOmni 的目标是提供一个覆盖任意模态的分布式训练配方库。本次提交通过将 Qwen3 这一重量级模型纳入配方体系，**实质性地扩充了配方库的内容广度**，并以规范化的多模块同步更新方式**验证了配方库架构的可扩展性**。这不仅增强了项目对 Qwen 生态用户的吸引力，也为后续持续接入更多模型奠定了工程范式基础，是项目从"框架可用"迈向"配方丰富"这一发展阶段的典型一步。随着此类提交的累积，VeOmni 有望在多模态大模型训练基础设施领域形成更强的社区共识与使用惯性。

## AI分析总结

## 主要更新类型

昨日 LightX2V 仓库共 3 次提交，涵盖**功能新增**（Depth Anything 3 深度估计支持、RelayVSR 可配置缩放比例）、**Bug 修复**（RelayVSR 奇数尺寸输出、DA3 位置编码缓存失效逻辑）以及**中英文文档更新**，以新功能开发为主，辅以相关缺陷修复。

## 关键变更点与项目方向的关系

- **Depth Anything 3 MONO-LARGE 接入**：为图像/视频生成相对深度预览，可选输出数值深度图与天空掩码，新增示例脚本——这与 LightX2V 作为轻量视频生成推理框架的定位一致，深度信息可用于视频生成的辅助控制（如景深、遮挡关系），拓展了框架的感知与控制能力。
- **RelayVSR 输出缩放比例可配置**：从仅支持特定比例放宽为模型变体范围内的任意浮点比例，低于原生比例时采用原生推理加抗锯齿双三次下采样，并将输出尺寸强制取偶数（最小 2 像素）。这直接服务于"轻量"目标——用户可按需权衡分辨率与算力开销。
- **DA3 位置嵌入缓存修复**：缓存键从不可靠的 `tensor._version` 改为 shape/dtype/device/指针，并在权重加载、设备/类型迁移、进入训练模式时清空缓存。这是对新引入 DA3 模块的即时健壮性补强。

## 对项目的影响和潜在意义

- 框架在视频生成推理之外，正向**辅助视觉能力**（深度估计）延伸，可能为后续深度条件生成、控制信号注入奠定基础，丰富 LightX2V 的生态。
- RelayVSR 的灵活性提升增强实用价值；DA3 缓存修复消除了多生命周期场景下的潜在精度错误，提升推理正确性与训练兼容性。
- 文档同步完善，降低用户上手门槛，符合开源项目社区化运营方向。

## 值得关注的技术点

1. **低比例下采样策略**：原生推理 + 抗锯齿双三次下采样而非低分辨率直接推理，兼顾质量与灵活性。
2. **偶数尺寸约束**：视频编码与推理管线普遍要求偶数分辨率，强制向下取整替代直接报错，提升鲁棒性。
3. **位置编码缓存失效设计**：以张量元信息与指针替代版本号，覆盖权重加载、设备迁移、训练模式切换等多生命周期事件，经过 H100 环境验证。
4. **DA3 MONO 的天空掩码输出**：反映该模型具备场景理解能力，对视频生成中的天空区域处理有潜在价值。

## 对项目发展的影响

结合 README，LightX2V 定位为轻量视频生成推理框架，强调推理效率与易用性。昨日提交呈现**双轨推进**：一方面通过 RelayVSR 缩放可配置与尺寸修复持续打磨核心推理能力的**灵活性与轻量化**；另一方面通过引入 Depth Anything 3 探索**深度感知这一辅助能力**，暗示项目可能朝"生成 + 控制/感知"的一体化方向演进。DA3 相关的快速修复也体现了对新模块质量的重视。总体上，这些提交在保持轻量推理核心的同时拓展功能边界，有利于吸引更多需要深度辅助能力的用户，推动项目生态发展。

# FlashInfer 昨日提交合并总结

## 一、主要更新
性能优化占绝对主导（约八九成），其余为正确性修复、功能新增与测试/CI 基础设施改进。改动集中于实验性 Cake 后端及其确定性 `*_det` 内核，覆盖 GEMM、MoE、RMSNorm、KDA、GDN、softmax、稀疏 MLA 与分页注意力、NVFP4 量化、causal conv1d、LM head loss 等算子族，横跨 sm_90/100/103/107（Hopper、B200、GB300、R200）及消费级 SM120，并延伸至推理与训练双场景。

## 二、关键变更
- **路由与微架构调优成为主战场**：多数提交不再新增内核，而是按 SM 计数（148/152/208/216）、实测 token 区间与形状在程序表中选更优变体——五 CTA/SM 配平、per-warp TMA 终态存储、空批早退、L2 hint 与 evict 提示调整（1–3% 收益）、split-K 覆盖、shape-to-route 路由目录，形成"测量—路由—优化"闭环；单项多为 1%–8%，个别达 2.45–3.8×。
- **训练纵深扩展**：权重梯度 GEMM、RMSNorm/KDA/GDN 训练前反向、MoK MXFP8 量化、融合 GEMM+all-reduce、wgrad 融合 `main_grad`，并与 Transformer Engine/Megatron 数值对齐，推动项目由推理内核库走向推理+训练全栈。
- **精度与正确性护栏**：非确定性程序须通过 FP64 参考误差池化中位数 ≤1.02、单点 ≤1.30 的强制门槛，不达标回退确定性程序；TwoSum 补偿与 FP64 固定顺序实现 run-to-run 0 ulp；修复有符号零致 top-k 解码为 -1、GDN P>1 分段梯度错误、split-vocab 多 stream workspace 竞争、混合架构 CuTe DSL 编译分发失败及批量回放 NaN 污染等问题。
- **生态与 API**：`checkpointing_ssu` 支持 strided 视图对齐 vLLM；`NVFP4KVMaterializer` 构造函数一次校验、`run()` 零分配且可被 CUDA graph 捕获；cuDNN prefill 补齐滑窗、attention sink 与标量 scale，使 `backend="auto"` 正确路由；KDA 新增 `ssm_state_indices` 状态池承接 TensorRT-LLM 补丁。
- **工程效率**：发布与夜间构建的重复 workflow 收敛、S3 共享编译缓存与有界并发 AOT、wheel 瘦身满足 PyPI 100MB 限制、Docker pip 层拆分降低拉取开销，以及 bot 测试的显式 scope/全量/AI 推荐三路径。

## 三、技术关注点
Gluon 方言利用寄存器 32 元素块使双布局 max 降为 warp shuffle；dsa_indexer 在 sm_107a 以票据字替代固定 CTA 分配，消除 1.3–1.8× 降速；NVFP4 稀疏 MLA 在 327KB SMEM 中用双槽记录环容纳第三 tile；TMA box 写回替代 16 字节 store、CLC 前瞻预取与 L2 数据驻留复用展示带宽/延迟权衡；kblock pipe 加 blocked FP32/FP64 累加以可忽略开销换取梯度精度；SM 计数敏感的 `ROUTER_RULES_BY_SM`、layout 级 swap-AB 与有符号零的整数位平局裁决均为可复用范式。

## 四、项目影响
在 Blackwell 全系上对标 DeepGEMM、trtllm-gen 普遍领先约 1.05–1.37×，直接提升 DeepSeek-V4、Kimi K3 等模型在 B200/GB300/R200 上的吞吐；同时诚实地披露批量 FP8 GEMM 中位数略低于 DeepGEMM，表明逐 shape 优化仍在推进。严格的冷 L2、A/B 交错、多种子统计检验与位级一致声明建立了可信的性能工程信誉，精度护栏、位精确测试与 CI 优化构成高频迭代下的回归安全网。项目已进入"高基线下的长尾榨取"阶段：横向扩展硬件与算子覆盖，纵向压榨寄存器与调度细节，也同步暴露规则表膨胀、跨硬件 CI 覆盖与发布体积等规模化工程债，正稳固其作为生产级训练/推理 GPU 内核基础设施的竞争力。

### [41bdd6c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/41bdd6c0559c6da4d990b9a1d3fa904a13b9eccd)

## 📌 Description

Both bot command paths now use the same run policy:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `@flashinfer-bot run tests/<path> [tests/...]` | Run the explicit
scope using the existing validator, without AI. |
| `@flashinfer-bot run all` | Run the full suite without AI; replaces
`run full`. |
| `@flashinfer-bot run` | Ask NVIDIA Inference Hub to recommend a scope.
Only an explained `full_suite` decision starts an unscoped run. Focused,
no-pytest-change and uncertain decisions only post advice for developer
review and an explicit run command. |

Advisory results do not publish scope statuses, apply labels, cancel CI
or launch jobs. Missing configuration, malformed model responses and
failed selection do not silently start the full suite. Existing
authorization, command parsing, manual scope checks, `rerun`, `rerun
failed` and `stop` remain intact.

AI inspects an isolated merge of the current target-branch tip and PR
head. It reads repository objects and trusted CI routing without
importing, executing or collecting PR code. AI full-suite runs clear
stale scope chunks, publish a snapshot with an empty-scope fingerprint,
and use the snapshot-protected `run-ci-focused` label. CI reconstructs
the pinned base/head merge and verifies its tree before testing and
before submodule initialization; a stale GitHub merge ref is not
authoritative. Explicit scopes and `run all` retain their existing
source preparation and use `run-ci`.

### Deployment instructions

1. **Set the Actions secret `INFERENCE_API_KEY` before enabling bare-run
recommendations.** Use a NVIDIA Inference Hub key entitled to the chosen
model. Configure it interactively with `gh secret set INFERENCE_API_KEY
--repo flashinfer-ai/flashinfer`, or under **Settings → Secrets and
variables → Actions**. Do not put the key in Git or command arguments.
Explicit scopes and `run all` need no inference key.
2. Preserve the existing `FLASHINFER_GITHUB_TOKEN` for
repository-role/team reads and `FLASHINFER_BOT_TOKEN` for comments,
reactions, labels and workflow controls. Keep the workflow's automatic
`GITHUB_TOKEN` for status publication. Label operations use the bot
token so their events can start downstream workflows. Authorized users
remain roles `admin`, `maintain`, `write`, `triage`, or members of
`ci-users`.
3. Ensure both labels exist: `run-ci` and `run-ci-focused`. Despite its
historical name within this feature, `run-ci-focused` is now used only
for AI-approved full-suite runs and requires matching snapshot metadata.
Advisory results apply neither label. Do not manually apply the
protected label without that metadata.
4. Optional Actions variables:

   | Variable | Default |
   | --- | --- |
   | `INFERENCE_BASE_URL` | `https://inference-api.nvidia.com/v1` |
   | `CI_BOT_TARGET_MODEL` | `us/aws/anthropic/eccn-claude-opus-5` |
| `CI_BOT_TARGET_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `240` (maximum `1800`; command job
limit is ten minutes) |

Allow the trusted command runner to reach GitHub and the configured
inference endpoint over HTTPS. PR metadata, patches and selected source
evidence are sent to that endpoint. If it requires internal network
access, use a suitably connected trusted runner; the workflow currently
uses `ubuntu-latest`.
5. Merge the helper and both workflow changes together into the default
branch. `issue_comment` runs default-branch code, so a PR cannot deploy
its own handler. Keep the trusted checkout, authorization gates and
`persist-credentials: false`. No continuous daemon or additional Python
package is required for this GitHub handler.
6. Verify deliberately after rollout: focused/uncertain bare-run
decisions should only comment; an AI full-suite decision should start an
unscoped run on the pinned source. Explicit scopes and `run all` should
bypass AI. Invalid or unavailable selection should start no jobs. These
are operational verification steps; no such commands were posted during
local validation.

The internal `/bot` daemon is configured separately in the companion MR.
Its host needs its own inference key; an Actions secret does not
configure that service. See `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
`docs/design_docs/ci_bot_and_targeted_testing.md`, and the companion
deployment guide for details.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Bare `run` requests an AI test-scope recommendation; recommendations
that don’t warrant a run provide advice without starting CI.
* Use `run all` for the full test suite or provide explicit pytest paths
for a manual run.
* Focused runs verify selected tests against a pinned snapshot of the
pull request and current base.

* **Bug Fixes**
* Invalid or outdated scopes and snapshot mismatches are rejected
without starting CI.
* Commands are recognized only when they appear as the first command
line outside fenced code blocks.

* **Documentation**
* Updated CI guidance explains command options and when runs are
accepted or rejected.

### [a77285b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a77285bf456d20c49481cafc984d96e2c119b50c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T23:52:04Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): three accumulation chains for the one-split sm_107a FP32 weight gradients (#8685)

`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` is the Cake dense
projection GEMM. On its `deterministic=False` path, the K1
weight-gradient GEMM (BF16 inputs, BF16 or FP32 output) has programs
with tile widths 64, 128, 192 and 256. These programs use one or more K
splits, in transposed-store and (192-wide) row-major-store forms. The
package also has an FP32 router GEMM family for forward, input gradient
and weight gradient. This PR adds one-split FP32-output K1 programs with
three accumulation chains: `dense_proj_gemm_atomic_nn_n128_f32_t_c3`,
`dense_proj_gemm_atomic_nn_n256_f32_t_c3` (both transposed store) and
`dense_proj_gemm_atomic_nn_n192_f32_c3` (row-major store). On 212-SM and
216-SM sm_107a parts, the planner sends the FP32 weight gradients 4096
-> 512, 4096 -> 1024, 5120 -> 512 and 5120 -> 1024 to these programs. It
does this at the token ranges in the new `K1_CHAIN_RANGES_BY_SM` table,
which all fall between 960 and 40961 tokens. On 212 SMs, these ranges
also cover token counts with an even number of 64-token blocks inside
the two-split ranges. At those token counts, the three-chain program
replaces the two-split program. Before this PR, the other rows in these
ranges ran the deterministic weight-gradient program. wgrad is the
weight gradient alone, bwd adds the input gradient, and ckpt is two
forwards plus bwd. Ranges are written eager / graph. Speedup is baseline
/ new, so a value below x1.00 means the baseline is faster. On 212 SMs,
the speedup over deterministic Cake is x1.13-x3.56 / x1.12-x3.76 for
wgrad, x1.07-x2.17 / x1.07-x2.23 for bwd and x1.01-x1.53 / x1.02-x1.54
for ckpt. Over the previous route it is x1.07-x3.53 / x1.07-x3.63 for
wgrad, x1.05-x2.03 / x1.06-x2.04 for bwd and x1.03-x1.53 / x1.02-x1.55
for ckpt. The new program is faster than the previous route in every
row, operation and mode. The non-Cake SOTA is faster than the new
program in most rows. Against it, the speedup is x0.68-x1.06 in both
modes for wgrad, x0.71-x0.99 in both modes for bwd and x0.71-x1.04 /
x0.60-x1.02 for ckpt. The library is faster in 39 of 40 wgrad rows in
both modes, in all 40 bwd rows, and in 33 (eager) and 35 (graph) of 40
ckpt rows. On 216 SMs, the speedup over deterministic Cake is
x1.03-x3.08 / x1.03-x3.09 for wgrad, x1.00-x2.12 / x1.02-x2.18 for bwd
and x1.03-x1.42 / x1.02-x1.47 for ckpt. Here the previous route ran the
deterministic weight-gradient program in every row. Over it, the speedup
is x1.03-x3.09 / x1.03-x3.08 for wgrad, x1.00-x2.12 / x1.02-x2.20 for
bwd and x1.02-x1.42 / x1.01-x1.47 for ckpt. Its lowest speedup over the
previous route is x1.00 (5120 -> 512 at 16384 tokens, bwd, eager). The
non-Cake SOTA is again faster in most rows. Against it, the speedup is
x0.69-x1.00 / x0.69-x0.99 for wgrad, x0.72-x0.96 / x0.71-x0.97 for bwd
and x0.64-x0.99 / x0.63-x1.01 for ckpt. The library is faster in 30
(eager) and 31 (graph) of 31 wgrad rows, in all 31 bwd rows, and in 31
(eager) and 29 (graph) of 31 ckpt rows.

R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), CUDA 13.4 build (nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, cuBLAS 13.8. Each of the 40 workload rows (d_in -> d_out,
FP32 output, tokens) has three operations. wgrad is the weight-gradient
GEMM alone. bwd is input gradient + weight gradient. ckpt is two
forwards + input gradient + weight gradient (a checkpointed step).
Deterministic Cake is the package's deterministic path, meaning its
forward, input-gradient and weight-gradient programs. Previous route is
this package's `deterministic=False` path before this PR. It uses the
same forward and input-gradient programs as the new column. Its weight
gradient ran either the deterministic program ("deterministic") or the
two-split program ("two-split", 18 of 40 rows). For each GEMM, non-Cake
SOTA is the fastest correct launch among cuBLAS (torch.mm) and the top 8
cuBLASLt heuristic algorithms, picked per GEMM and per mode on the same
GPU. bwd and ckpt chain those launches. Every cell is "eager / graph".
Speedup = baseline / new, so a value above x1.00 means the new program
is faster. Timing uses CUPTI kernel spans of eager launches and CUDA
graph replays, with L2 cold before every timed iteration and
programmatic dependent launch on in every Cake launch (the sm_107a
default). Each value is the median of 4 runs, one per GPU on one 4-GPU
node, and within each run wgrad is the median of 15 paired groups of 20
timed iterations and bwd / ckpt is the median of 9 paired groups.

operation | deterministic Cake us | previous route | previous route us |
non-Cake SOTA us | new us | speedup vs deterministic Cake | speedup vs

R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs), CUDA 13.4 build (nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, cuBLAS 13.8. Each of the 31 workload rows (d_in -> d_out,
FP32 output, tokens) has three operations. wgrad is the weight-gradient
GEMM alone. bwd is input gradient + weight gradient. ckpt is two
forwards + input gradient + weight gradient (a checkpointed step).
Deterministic Cake is the package's deterministic path, meaning its
forward, input-gradient and weight-gradient programs. Previous route is
this package's `deterministic=False` path before this PR. It uses the
same forward and input-gradient programs as the new column. Its weight
gradient ran the deterministic program in every row. For each GEMM,
non-Cake SOTA is the fastest correct launch among cuBLAS (torch.mm) and
the top 8 cuBLASLt heuristic algorithms, picked per GEMM and per mode on
the same GPU. bwd and ckpt chain those launches. Every cell is "eager /
graph". Speedup = baseline / new, so a value above x1.00 means the new
program is faster. Timing uses CUPTI kernel spans of eager launches and
CUDA graph replays, with L2 cold before every timed iteration and
programmatic dependent launch on in every Cake launch (the sm_107a
default). Each value is the median of 2 runs (two row orders) on one
GPU, and within each run wgrad is the median of 15 paired groups of 20
timed iterations and bwd / ckpt is the median of 9 paired groups.

The package's other K1 programs (BF16 and FP32 output, widths 64 to 256,
multi-split and one-chain one-split) and its router programs are
unchanged, and the package ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, with
the new three-chain programs shipping on sm_100a and sm_103a (128 and
256 wide) and on sm_107a (128, 192 and 256 wide) but routed only on
212-SM and 216-SM sm_107a parts.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added dense-projection GEMM support for selected GPU architectures and
workload ranges, including three-chain accumulation for certain FP32
weight-gradient workloads.
* The planner selects the supported accumulation strategy for eligible
workloads and retains existing routing for other shapes.
* **Performance**
* Documented measured performance and accuracy for newly supported
workloads, including repeatability results.

### [bcb0416](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/bcb0416a7c8ea610685c6c74bf3c3410f8369781)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T23:46:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): Gluon MXFP8 weight quantizer, one launch for gate/up/down (#8717)

`cake_mok_bf16` is FlashInfer's MoK mixture-of-experts training kernel
family, covering forward, checkpoint recompute and backward. This PR
speeds up its MXFP8 weight quantizer (`mxfp8_quantize` /
`quantize_routed_weights`). After each weight update, the quantizer
converts the routed weights into a normal layout for forward and
recompute and a transposed layout for backward. For contiguous inputs
that request both layouts, a new kernel written in Triton's Gluon
dialect replaces the fused Triton dual-layout kernel. Its register
layout keeps every 32-element block of both layouts inside one warp.
Both block maxima are therefore warp shuffles, and the transposed E4M3
tile is stored straight from registers with 4-byte vectors, with no
shared-memory byte transpose. Only the 512-byte scale tiles go through 1
KB of shared memory to get 4-byte stores. The explicit NaN mask and ±448
clamp are replaced by a NaN-propagating block max and the saturating
E4M3 conversion, which produce identical bytes.
`quantize_routed_weights` now quantizes gate, up and down in one launch.
Outputs are byte-identical to main.

Microbenchmark on one GPU, `triton.testing.do_bench` median with L2
flushed. Shapes are one EP8 rank's 36 local experts, H=4096, I=2048,
BF16. Times in ms.

| GPU | Operation | Shape | main | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VR200 (sm_107a) | `mxfp8_quantize`, both layouts | [36, 2048, 4096] |
0.3636 | 0.1484 | 2.45x |
| VR200 (sm_107a) | `mxfp8_quantize`, both layouts | [36, 4096, 2048] |
0.3633 | 0.1483 | 2.45x |
| VR200 (sm_107a) | `quantize_routed_weights` (gate, up, down) | 3
matrices above | 1.0857 | 0.4113 | 2.64x |
| GB200 (sm_100a) | `mxfp8_quantize`, both layouts | [36, 2048, 4096] |
0.642 | 0.2570 | 2.50x |
| GB200 (sm_100a) | `quantize_routed_weights` | 3 matrices | 1.912 |
0.7498 | 2.55x |
| GB300 (sm_103a) | `mxfp8_quantize`, both layouts | [36, 2048, 4096] |
0.647 | 0.2601 | 2.49x |
| GB300 (sm_103a) | `quantize_routed_weights` | 3 matrices | 1.924 |
0.7578 | 2.54x |

VR200 is NVIDIA Vera Rubin VR200 with 212 SMs and driver 620.69.
Software was PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0, with CUDA 13.5 ptxas
on VR200 and the 13.0 / 13.2 toolkits on the GB200 / GB300 hosts.

End-to-end EP8 MoE training ran on 8 NVIDIA VR NVL72 GPUs (sm_107a): two
4-GPU trays in one NVLink domain, driver 620.69, CUDA 13.4, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. The configuration was EP8, H=4096, I=2048,
288 experts, top-8, one shared expert, clamped SwiGLU, MXFP8 routed
experts and checkpoint recompute. Each side ran 4 times in ABBA order on
the same nodes, and the table shows the mean of medians. A training
update is 5 layers, with weights quantized once per layer. Peak memory
is unchanged. All times in ms.

| Workload | Weight quantize, main | this PR | MoE microbatch, main |
this PR | speedup | Training update (5 layers), main | this PR | speedup
|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 1.162 | 0.506 | 15.131 | 14.661 | 1.032x |
150.17 | 147.11 | 1.021x |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 1.149 | 0.491 | 18.779 | 18.289 | 1.027x |
185.61 | 182.38 | 1.018x |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 1.25x | 1.148 | 0.489 | 21.256 | 20.619 |
1.031x | 207.73 | 204.74 | 1.015x |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 2x | 1.148 | 0.490 | 37.663 | 37.106 |
1.015x | 374.70 | 371.47 | 1.009x |

- **Fallback:** The Gluon path needs Triton >= 3.5. If the first Gluon
build for a shape fails, the process warns once and uses the previous
Triton dual-layout kernel. Without Triton, or for single-layout or
non-contiguous inputs, the existing paths run unchanged. Tile corners
use 64-bit offsets when a matrix has >= 2^31 elements.
- **Correctness:** A uint8 comparison of data, scales, transposed data
and transposed scales shows byte-identical outputs to main. Inputs were
random and edge cases (NaN, ±Inf, zeros, subnormals, saturation and
power-of-two boundaries), plus shapes at the >= 2^31-element boundary.
This was run on sm_100a (GB200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a (VR200),
and also with Triton 3.5.1 through 3.8.0 on sm_100a/sm_103a. The tests
now cover the Gluon, Triton and PyTorch paths separately. End-to-end EP8
outputs and all gradients are bitwise identical to main on all 8 ranks.

The family also ships BF16 routed experts and the MXFP8 forward,
recompute and backward kernels, on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

- **提交信息**: ci: share release/nightly build pipeline via a reusable workflow (#7898)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`release.yml` and `nightly-release.yml` carried ~260 near-identical
lines each for the flashinfer-python, flashinfer-cubin, JIT-cache
provider/shim builds and provider-set validation. This moves that
pipeline into one reusable workflow,
`.github/workflows/release-build.yml` (`workflow_call`). Each caller
keeps only what really differs:

- triggers, concurrency and permissions;
- versioning (nightly date suffix / `nightly-v…` tag vs.
tag-must-match-`version.txt` / PR `test-v…-prN`);
- publishing (nightly: `flashinfer-ai/whl` release + nightly index + GPU
tests + summary; release: GitHub release, PyPI, index, docs).

Inputs of the shared workflow: `ref`, `repository`, `dev_suffix`,
`wheel_version`, `clean_self_hosted_runners` (nightly only, as before),
`cubin_retry_window_seconds` (nightly 86400, release 0, as before). The
two sccache secrets are passed explicitly; `vars` come from the caller
repo.

Intentional behavior changes (none on `flashinfer-ai/flashinfer` in
practice):
- Nightly now falls back to the same sccache bucket/region as release
(`flashinfer-build-cache` / `us-west-2`) when the repo variables are
unset; the repo variables already hold those values.
- Job names in the Actions UI become `build / JIT cache provider (…)`
etc. The publish jobs now `need: [setup, build]`; a called-workflow job
succeeds only if all its jobs do, so gating is unchanged.
- Release's `setup` no longer runs `validate_cuda_versions.py` itself;
the shared `setup` does, and `build` still waits on the tag/version
check.
- `release.yml`'s PR path filter now includes `release-build.yml`, so
changes to the shared pipeline get the release dry run.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Prepares the single place to apply the "Resolve builder image" step
(`scripts/resolve_aot_builder_image.sh`) from the AOT builder-image
work: it goes once into the provider/shim jobs of `release-build.yml`.

### [0df3b67](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0df3b67437f6a74a14a6a7409460dd9f8c76ffd1)

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): route SM107 FP8 64-head decode rows of two to four sparse tiles to the M64 body before the half wave (#8715)

The Cake backend of `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` has 49
programs: BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads
(several bodies per head count, picked per shape by the host route) and
an NVFP4-KV decode family. On sm_107a it ships six FP8 programs for the
DeepSeek-V4 decode route: three 128-head persistent programs (the
persistent program, the uniform-gather program and its K=64 sibling),
the 64-head single-CTA M64 single-tile and multi-tile programs, and the
SWA low-head prefill program. This PR changes only the sm_107a host
route and no program: before it, FP8 64-head decode rows switched from
the 128-head persistent uniform-gather program to the M64 programs only
past the half wave (2 x tokens > SM count). Now, rows whose sparse width
covers two, three or four 128-key tiles (tile count = ceil(sparse width
/ 128)) take the M64 programs from den x tokens > num x SM count on,
with (num, den) = (1, 8), (1, 4) and (3, 10) for two, three and four
tiles, which is from 27, 53 and 63 tokens on at 208 SMs and from 28, 55
and 65 at 216 SMs. Rows of one tile or of five and more tiles, and the
other architectures, keep the half-wave rule. Speedups are measured
against the previous Cake route (FlashInfer main c325578c), which runs
the moved rows on the 128-head persistent uniform-gather program, and
are 1.02x to 1.26x on those rows at 208 SMs (two tiles 1.04-1.26x, three
tiles 1.05-1.14x, four tiles 1.02-1.08x).

VR200 (sm_107a, 208 SMs), CUDA 13.4. The workload is DeepSeek-V4 MTP
decode with 64 query heads per rank and an FP8 query and KV cache, where
rows = batch x q_len with q_len 4. It covers the top-k 128x layer at
16K, 24K, 32K, 40K and 48K context (sparse widths 256, 320, 384, 448,
512) and the top-k 4x layer at 32K context (width 640). Each time is per
call, from eight back-to-back calls with `enable_pdl=True` in one CUDA
graph with a 512 MiB L2 flush before each graph launch, taking the
median of 4 rounds with alternating route order; speedup = previous /
this PR. Rows marked "program unchanged" run the same program on both
sides: rows below the new threshold, the 108-row rows (which already

### [c54c08e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c54c08ed6ac860910898de211be425ec5ee8ec73)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T22:38:29Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dense_projection_gemm): route router windows that fail the accuracy rule to the deterministic program (#8689)

This PR applies the accuracy rule to the router windows of
`cake_dense_projection_gemm`. A token window may run this package's
program only if its error passes for every seed. The error is the
relative Frobenius error against FP64 of the exact operands, worst of 20
runs. It must be at most 1.02 times the error of the plan the row takes
without the window. Windows that missed the rule now run that plan. That
plan is the deterministic program, except on sm_100a at hidden 5120 up
to 128 tokens, where it is the existing "waves" window. No router table
names a SIMT program any more, so the five SIMT programs leave the
registry.

## Changes

- **SIMT windows removed** (`cake_backend.py`). These are exact-FP32
programs: each CTA slice sums its FP32 products in one FFMA chain along
K.
- sm_100a (152 SMs): weight gradient at hidden 4096 (1-224 tokens), 5120
and 6144 (1-256); input gradient at hidden 4096/5120 (1-128), 6144
(1-64).
- sm_107a (212 SMs): weight gradient at hidden 4096 and 5120 (1-256),
6144 (1-192); input gradient at hidden 4096/5120 (1-128), 6144 (1-64).
- **Head/tail windows removed on 152-SM parts.**
- sm_100a: hidden 4096 "H1x5p44" (10240-16384 tokens), 5120 "H0.5x3"
(10240-32768).
- sm_103a: hidden 4096 "H1x4p44" (20480-49152), 5120 "H0.5x3"
(16172-32768), 6144 "H1x5p44" (16172-20480).
- **"waves" windows.** The sm_103a hidden 5120 window is shortened from
1-192 to 1-160 tokens.
- **Kept windows.** The sm_100a hidden 5120 "waves" window (1-128)
stays. Every sm_107a "H0.5x4" window stays (208/212/216 SMs). On 212 SMs
these measured 0.94-0.98x of the deterministic error.
- **Registry** (`cake_jit.py`, `build.json`).
- `router_fp32_gemm_simt_n128m64s2`, `router_fp32_gemm_simt_n64m64s2`,
`router_fp32_dgrad_simt_m32n64s4`, `router_fp32_dgrad_simt_m32n64s8` and
`router_fp32_dgrad_simt_m64n64s4` lose their MODULES / KERNELS records
and build.json libraries. Their sources (10 .cu files) are deleted.
- A SIMT spec set in a router table at run time now plans an
unregistered template and runs the deterministic program.
- The head/tail programs stay registered because the sm_107a windows use
them. The SIMT planner code stays.
- **Tests.**
- Planner tests force the former windows and register a SIMT template
where they plan one.
- New tests check that every failed window resolves to the plan without
it (CPU, every SM count).
- New GPU tests check that the failed windows give the deterministic
program's bits with no launch of this package's programs prepared.
- `test_registered_templates_are_the_ones_the_planners_name` is
unchanged.
- **README.** Updates the rule, the generated FP64 error table, the
routing table and the SIMT and head/tail sections.

## FP64 error of the windows

| row (256 experts) | token window | measured at (tokens, 10 seeds each)
| part | error / error without the window | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sm_100a` weight gradient hidden 4096 `"simt_n128m64s2"` | 1 to 224 |
1, 113, 224 | GB200, 152 SMs | x2.226-2.423 (x0.932-0.959 at 1 token) |
missed |
| `sm_100a` weight gradient hidden 5120 `"simt_n64m64s2"` | 1 to 256 |
1, 128, 129, 256 | GB200, 152 SMs | x2.300-2.536 (x0.928-0.951 at 1
token) | missed |
| `sm_100a` weight gradient hidden 6144 `"simt_n64m64s2"` | 1 to 256 |
1, 129, 256 | GB200, 152 SMs | x2.298-2.531 (x0.927-0.951 at 1 token) |
missed |
| `sm_100a` input gradient hidden 4096 `"simt_n64m32s4"` | 1 to 128 | 1,
64, 128 | GB200, 152 SMs | x1.697-2.067 | missed |

One row per GPU / shape / mode / operation. New = this PR's route; on
the changed rows it is the deterministic program, so det/new is about
1.00. Previous plan = the route on FlashInfer main 098d8eb5 (the removed
window). Speedups are det/new, SOTA/new and previous/new. Deterministic
Cake = `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm` (prepared
launch, `deterministic=True`). Non-Cake SOTA = per cell, the fastest
FP32 library route that meets the router accuracy budget. The candidates
are cublasSgemm (default math, no TF32), cublasLt FP32 compute (the
fastest of the heuristic's top 8 that passes), `torch.mm` FP32
(`allow_tf32=False`), cuBLAS FP32 BF16x9 emulation, and the per-op
fastest of these. Two cuBLAS builds: 13.8.0 and the torch wheel's
13.1.1. Timer: CUPTI kernel spans with cold L2 (L2 zeroed before every
iteration). Each cell runs 15 paired groups x 20 timed iterations in
rotated arm order. A cell is the median over 4 runs (two cuBLAS builds x
one long-lived process and a fresh process per row). Eager = prepared
launches; CUDA graph = graph replays. PDL is on in every Cake arm.
Backward = input gradient + weight gradient; checkpointed step = 2
forward + backward. 256 experts, FP32 router operands, hidden H, T
tokens. GB300: NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03, CUDA
13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), torch 2.14.1+cu130. The A/A band covers rows where
the previous and new plans run the same programs: eager 0.996-1.023,
graph 0.993-1.011. GB200: NVIDIA GB200, sm_100a, 152 SMs, driver
580.126.20, CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), torch 2.14.1+cu130; A/A band:
eager 0.968-1.011, graph 0.971-1.008. R200: NVIDIA R200, sm_107a, 212
SMs, driver 620.43, CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), torch 2.14.1+cu130; its
environment has one cuBLAS build (13.8), so all four runs of a cell use
it; A/A band: eager 0.993-1.024, graph 0.971-1.054. B200 and B300 (148
SMs) keep every route, so they have no rows.

### [c091378](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c091378cf91a8cabeb918bf0e16c1d8086275d2c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T22:27:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): SM107 FP8 H128 K=64 uniform-gather program double-buffers its output staging (#8713)

The Cake backend of `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` has 49
programs: BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads
(several bodies per head count, picked per shape by the host route) and
an NVFP4-KV decode family. sm_107a ships six FP8 programs for the
DeepSeek-V4 decode route: the two 128-head persistent programs
(lane-issued gathers, uniform gathers), the K=64 sibling of the
uniform-gather program, the 64-head single-CTA M64 single-tile and
multi-tile programs, and the SWA low-head prefill program. This PR
changes one of them and adds none. The changed program is the sm_107a
K=64 FP8 128-head uniform-gather persistent program
(`cake_dsv4_7074d4c5b808db91fcba`, loader key
`fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent_uniform_k64`, added in #8668). On
sm_107a it runs uniform-gather launches of 48 to 127 query rows, plus
the FP8 64-head rows that FlashInfer sends to that route. Since #8679 it
also runs short-query decode launches of 160 rows or more. With this PR,
each of the program's four correction warps stages its four 32-head x
64-dim output tiles in two 4 KiB shared-memory buffers in turn instead
of one, so the bulk store of one tile reads shared memory while the warp
packs the next; dynamic shared memory grows by 16 KiB to 272512 bytes.
Outputs are bitwise unchanged. The host route, every other program, and
sm_100a and sm_103a are unchanged. Speedups are measured against the
previous Cake version of the same program (FlashInfer main a2f011cc,
whose DeepSeek-V4 Cake sources equal this PR's base).

VR200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs), CUDA 13.4. The shapes come from the
DeepSeek-V4 decode tests' input helpers with an FP8 query and KV cache.
The context is 32768 tokens, except in the top-k 128x rows of width 1152
(context 131072). Rows = batch x q_len. Each time is per call, from
eight back-to-back calls with `enable_pdl=True` in one CUDA graph with
L2 flushed before each graph launch, taking the median of 6 rounds in
rotating order; speedup = previous / this PR. Every row matches the test
reference, and outputs are bitwise equal to the previous program's on
every row. The "program" column says which program the row runs. Rows
marked "unchanged" run another program on both sides: the K=32
uniform-gather program below 48 rows, and the lane-issued program for
long requests.

### [0ea313f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0ea313f4b5e7978e1fa1c2b67f8da9941e225fff)

- **作者**: tomeras91
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T22:26:43Z
- **提交信息**: feat(checkpointing_ssu): accept strided ring_start and prev_num_accepted (#8548)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`checkpointing_ssu` now accepts `ring_start` and
`prev_num_accepted_tokens` as strided 1-D views (`stride(0)` in [1,
2^31)). Before, both had to be contiguous. This lets vLLM keep these
ReplaySSM trackers inside the per-slot Mamba state page, so block copies
and KV-cache accounting cover them with no extra code.

- Binding: the two contiguity checks become a stride range check.
- Kernels (monolithic, 8-bit, and both halves of the two-kernel split)
read the trackers at `slot * stride`.

Tested: `tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py` on one B200 (CUDA 13.0,
torch 2.14): 300 passed, 8 skipped. New cases pass strided trackers
(stride 3, and a stride where slot × stride > 2^31) through the
monolithic and two-kernel paths, bf16 and int8 state, dense and varlen,
and through autotuning; each must match contiguous trackers bit for bit.
Not tested: GPUs other than B200; fp8 state and single-token decode with
strided trackers (they use the same loads as int8 and multi-token
decode).

Performance with contiguous trackers, `main` vs this PR. Setup: B200,
`benchmarks/bench_checkpointing_ssu.py --cupti` (CUDA graph, L2 flush),
Nemotron-3 Super shapes at TP 8 (16 heads, head_dim 64, d_state 128, 1
group), bf16 activations, max_window 16; batch 1/8/64/256 × MTP 1/4/8 ×
pnat 0/4/8; 2 runs per side, back to back. Run-to-run noise: median
0.2%, max 3%.

| Kernel | State | PR / main, geomean (min–max) over 36 configs |
|---|---|---|
| monolithic | bf16 | 0.987 (0.941–1.009) |
| monolithic | int8 | 1.005 (0.993–1.018) |
| two-kernel | bf16 | 1.002 (0.982–1.014) |

Median kernel time at MTP 4, pnat 4 (µs, main → PR):

| Kernel | State | batch 1 | batch 256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| monolithic | bf16 | 3.85 → 3.88 | 27.20 → 27.26 |
| monolithic | int8 | 4.28 → 4.28 | 26.25 → 26.73 |
| two-kernel | bf16 | 5.98 → 5.98 | 23.76 → 23.84 |

## 🔍 Related Issues

Needed for vllm-project/vllm#55688 follow-up work: storing the ReplaySSM
trackers in the Mamba state page.

- [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental
backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without
`FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an
`@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself
the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
- [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs
exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

<!-- Required for experimental PRs. Replace the commented lines below
with your targets.
Do not delete the fence or change its `experimental-tests` tag — the
experimental-track
watcher reads it verbatim to decide which targets to ask CI for. -->

```experimental-tests
# One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not
# supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under
# tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g.
#
#   tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py
#   tests/experimental/my_backend/
#
# Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every
# experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell.
```

## Reviewer Notes

The tracker offset uses 32-bit operands and a 64-bit product, and the
strides are stored as `int64` in the params struct. Both choices were
measured: a 64×64 multiply, or `int32` stride fields, made the
small-batch monolithic kernel up to ~6% slower on B200 (the tracker
loads sit on its serial prologue). Per-config differences of a few
percent in the table come from prologue scheduling, not extra work.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Checkpointing accepts strided one-dimensional views for ring-start and
previously accepted-token tracking data, instead of requiring contiguous
tensors. These views are read-only during kernel execution.
* For tensors with more than one element, strides must be between 1 and
the supported 32-bit maximum. Strides are respected across checkpointing
execution modes, including variable-length inputs.

### [94c7d61](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/94c7d61d8ca933b556e14bc3c664f4c69c89b203)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T22:18:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8): early exit for an all-empty batch in the SM100a N=7168, K=2048 serving program (#8709)

The masked grouped FP8 GEMM behind
`batch_deepgemm_fp8_nt_groupwise(backend="cake")` has two scale
variants: FP32 per-128-block scales, routed by shape, and packed UE8M0
scales, used by the serving programs. This PR changes one packed-UE8M0
serving program, the N=7168, K=2048, 32-group program, on sm_100a only.
When the whole batch is empty (every group's `masked_m` is 0), all CTAs
now exit early, before barrier setup; the sm_103a build of the program
is unchanged. The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer
main, and DeepGEMM is the second baseline.

| GPU (arch) | Workload | Previous Cake (µs) | This PR (µs) | Speedup vs
previous Cake (± noise) | Best DeepGEMM (µs) | Speedup vs best DeepGEMM
| Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B200 (sm_100a) | B=32, M=256, N=7168, K=2048, expected_m=1, masked_m
from p10 batches | 5.089 | 1.792 | 2.8393x ±0.0479 | 4.464 (FlashInfer
bundled) | 2.5674x | faster; WIN |
| B200 (sm_100a) | B=32, M=256, N=7168, K=2048, expected_m=1, masked_m
from p50 batches | 13.568 | 13.632 | 0.9911x ±0.0214 | 15.520 (upstream
2.8.2) | 1.1397x | same; WIN |
| B200 (sm_100a) | B=32, M=256, N=7168, K=2048, expected_m=1, masked_m
from p90 batches | 22.992 | 23.151 | 0.9941x ±0.0133 | 25.376 (upstream
2.8.2) | 1.0958x | same; WIN |

NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, CUDA 13.4. Each row is the median of 9
runs of paired A/B timing with cold L2. The masked_m values come from
the p10 / p50 / p90 batch distributions of an EP8 serving trace. The ±
value is the measurement noise band on the time ratio. "Same" means the
ratio falls within that band. DeepGEMM baselines: FlashInfer's bundled
DeepGEMM masked kernel and upstream DeepGEMM 2.8.2
`m_grouped_fp8_gemm_nt_masked`. Each row shows the faster of the two.

This change leaves the kernel's other Cake variants untouched: the
FP32-scale programs routed by shape and the other packed-UE8M0 serving
programs. The family ships on sm_100a and sm_103a, and this change
affects only sm_100a.

### [31a6dea](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/31a6dea4524cf1012ee0b332511d5221537e7115)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T22:16:05Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): per-warp TMA final-state store for the bounded direct turnover launches in BF16 KDA prefill (sm_100a, sm_103a) (#8711)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes only the prepared BF16-input path with FP32 state
(`flashinfer.prepare_bf16_kda_prefill`). The change applies to both
sm_100a and sm_103a. It targets the turnover launches of the bounded
direct route, which is used when a gate lower bound is set. Those
launches now use builds with the per-warp TMA final-state store. The
unbounded direct turnover launches already use this store. With it, each
epilogue warp writes a task's FP32 final state as one TMA box from a
staged panel. Before, the panel was read back and written with 16-byte
stores. Routes, bins and plans stay the same. Outputs are bit-identical.

The tables compare this PR with the previous Cake version on FlashInfer
main. They report the median latency per call in microseconds, with a
cold L2. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or
-5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. TIE means no difference beyond the
measurement band. Every faster row has a gate lower bound of -5 and a
BS16 x T128 or BS16 x T256 shape. In the fast-path table, the same four
rows are faster on both arches. With 12 heads, BS16 x T128 goes from
32.99 to 32.35 us on B200 (1.02x) and from 31.39 to 30.82 us on GB300
(1.02x). BS16 x T256 goes from 47.58 to 47.23 us on B200 (1.01x) and
from 44.67 to 44.35 us on GB300 (1.01x). With 16 heads, BS16 x T128 goes
from 34.30 to 33.60 us on B200 (1.02x) and from 32.19 to 31.55 us on
GB300 (1.02x). BS16 x T256 goes from 48.99 to 48.58 us on B200 (1.01x)
and from 45.76 to 45.31 us on GB300 (1.01x). In the serving table, the
same four rows are faster on B200. With 12 heads, BS16 x T128 goes from
33.18 to 32.54 us (1.02x) and BS16 x T256 from 47.58 to 47.23 us
(1.01x). With 16 heads, BS16 x T128 goes from 34.05 to 33.44 us (1.02x)
and BS16 x T256 from 48.93 to 48.51 us (1.01x). On GB300, two serving
rows are faster, both with 16 heads. BS16 x T128 goes from 32.10 to
31.46 us (1.02x) and BS16 x T256 from 45.66 to 45.25 us (1.01x). The two
12-head GB300 serving rows show 1.02x and 1.01x, but they stay inside
the measurement band, so they count as TIE. All other rows in both
tables are TIE. One GB300 fast-path row is marked † and is not counted:
16 heads, gate lower bound -5, 2x(8128+64). Its timing drifted on both
sides beyond the measurement guard within one run. The same drift also
happens when FlashInfer main is timed against itself. We also swept
every launch shape outside the tables that this PR moves (8, 12 and 16
heads, gate lower bound -5). None is slower. On B200, 238 of 262 are
faster and 24 are TIE, with latency ratios (this PR / main) from 0.9493
to 1.0047. On GB300, 291 of 334 are faster and 43 are TIE, with ratios
from 0.9448 to 1.0021.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. GB300: NVIDIA
GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.167.08. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

33.79 | 1.00x TIE |

- B200: speedup 0.99x .. 1.02x over 56 counted rows (4 faster, 52 TIE:
no difference beyond the measurement band)
- GB300: speedup 0.99x .. 1.02x over 56 counted rows (2 faster, 54 TIE:

The other Cake variants keep their programs, including the TF32-input

## 📌 Description

#8694 moved two block-scaled UE8M0 contiguous layouts onto the one-CTA
swap-AB route (`BS_SWAP_C1_ROUTE`): 896 rows at alignment 64 with N
1024, K 512 on SM100a, and 768 rows at alignment 32 with N 1024, K 256
on SM103a. Its tests assert the route and grid for these layouts but do
not run them numerically. This PR adds one case for each to
`BLOCK_SCALED_SMALL_CASES`. The existing test then checks that the
prepared launch takes `BS_SWAP_C1_ROUTE` on that architecture, compares
the output with the reference, and checks that its bits equal the
non-swapped route's. Each case is skipped on other architectures.
Test-only change.

The group counts are uneven and include an empty group. After per-group
padding and the tail rule they give 896 and 768 rows.

### [38db3b0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/38db3b09729fe63863706ebdcb2d5026b3de71af)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T22:01:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): route SM107 FP8 8-head prefill and 8/16/32-head two-wave SWA decode to the M64 programs (#8699)

Cake's DSv4 sparse MLA kernel, `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4(...,
backend="cake")`, has 49 BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128
query heads. It also has an NVFP4-KV decode family. On sm_107a it ships
six FP8 programs. Three are 128-head persistent prefill programs. Two
are 64-head single-CTA M64 persistent prefill programs:
`fp8_h64_prefill_source_persistent_m64` for 128-wide items and
`fp8_h64_prefill_source_persistent_m64_multi_tile` for wider items. The
sixth is the low-head prefill program, `fp8_lowhead_prefill`. This PR
changes only FlashInfer's routing on sm_107a. No program changes. Two
kinds of FP8 rows move from `fp8_lowhead_prefill` to the existing M64
programs. (a) Rows with 8 query heads and `max_q_len >= 257` move when
items have at most 1152 sparse slots. That is the M64 programs' width
limit. Wider items keep the low-head program. The 16-, 32- and 64-head
prefill rows already used the M64 programs. (b) Rows with 8, 16 and 32
query heads, sliding-window-only KV (sparse width 128) and `max_q_len <
257` move once 2 x query tokens exceed the SM count. The low-head
program launches two CTAs per token, so these rows need a second wave.
The M64 program launches one CTA per token. Rows with 2 x query tokens
<= SM count keep the low-head program. sm_100a and sm_103a keep their
routes. The baseline is the previous Cake route on sm_107a. That route
is the shipped low-head prefill program `fp8_lowhead_prefill`, which
already uses the K=64 FP8 MMA.

NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs), CUDA 13.4. Each value is the per-call
latency in a CUDA graph with programmatic dependent launch (PDL)
enabled. The measurement is a graph of one short predecessor kernel plus
8 back-to-back calls, minus a graph of the predecessor alone, divided by
8, taking the median of 100 replays. Each value is the median of 6
paired rounds. The speedup is the median of the 6 per-round previous /
this PR ratios. Query tokens are given as requests x query tokens per
request, with the total T in parentheses. "129/257" means two requests
of 129 and 257 tokens. Sparse width 128 means sliding-window KV only;
640 and 1152 add 512 and 1024 compressed-cache slots, and 192 adds 64
slots of a compressed cache with 2-row pages. Rows with 1 query token
per request are dense-layout decode calls. Rows 1-18 are case (a). Rows
19-52 are case (b) at 216 SMs, and all have 2 x T > 216.

### [9eee04b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9eee04b1775480cc1a8b88096068aaa7bef3621b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T22:00:52Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc): with grad, the non-deterministic collapse pass reads the mapping-pass input from L2 on sm_100a / sm_103a (#8677)

Cake's mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections) kernel with grad has
a deterministic mode (det) and an opt-in non-deterministic mode, nd
(`deterministic=False` of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`). The workload is X BF16
[T, 4, H] (4 streams) with an FP32 mapping and H = 4096, 5120 or 7168.
It is a local (non-KCP) operator and also runs on a context-parallel
rank's local shard.

This PR makes nd's forward mapping pass use the X-hint (L2-hint) forms
that FlashInfer #8582 added to the deterministic package. At hidden 4096
on sm_100a and sm_103a, for 64 < T <= 6144 tokens, the mapping pass now
leaves X in L2 so the collapse pass can read it from there, just as
det's forward does.

- **Changed:** nd's forward programs are again copies of det's forward
programs, and nd's records, routes and builds mirror det's again. det's
dual-layout checkpoint carry (FlashInfer #8312) is not copied. nd's
checkpointed backward keeps its own atomic fn split.
- **Text-only first commit:** the first commit re-renders the nd
package's kernel sources and build manifest from the unchanged registry.
It changes only text, and the compiled machine code of every library is
the same on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.
- **Unchanged:** hidden 5120 and 7168, every token count at or below 64
and above 6144 at hidden 4096, every sm_107a board, and the backward.
Backward-only control rows launch the same programs before and after on
B200 and GB300. det is not changed.
- **Outputs:** at the 9 token counts of Table 2, on both B200 and GB300,
nd's forward outputs, dX, dB, the saved-statistics gradients, dscale and
dbase are bitwise equal to det. nd's dfn relative L2 vs det is at most
8.48e-08 (B200) and 8.49e-08 (GB300).

## Speedup vs the previous nd version

Timing: 4 processes, one per GPU of one node, run concurrently. Each
process times every token count with all arms on the same inputs, and
the arms are rotated and mirrored inside each group.

- **evd:** eager calls timed with CUDA events after a 512 MiB L2 flush
and a GPU spin that lets the host enqueue the whole call first (16
groups x 16 calls).
- **graph:** CUDA-graph replays, each after a 512 MiB L2 flush (16
groups x 30 replays).

Each process takes the median over groups, and the table shows the
median over the 4 processes. previous = FlashInfer main's routing on
that GPU; new = this PR; speedup = previous / new. The operations are
forward and the checkpointed step (2x forward + backward). T = 8192 runs
the same kernels in both versions and serves as a control row. All
boards use X BF16 [T, 4, 4096], an FP32 mapping, 4 streams, non-KCP and
random inputs. The Cake kernels are built with CUDA 13.4, with PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0) and Triton 3.8.0.

(evd) and 1.000..1.062 (graph), up to 13.1 us (evd) / 13.3 us (graph)
faster.

## Speedup vs det and B0

- **det:** `deterministic=True` from the same build (this PR's head).
This is the original deterministic Cake implementation, and this PR does
not change it.
- **B0:** per row, the faster of IEEE-FP32 eager PyTorch and
`torch.compile` (inductor default, fullgraph=False, dynamic=False, TF32
off) running the same mHC function with grad. torch.compile won all 27
rows on both GPUs. B0's dfn relative L2 vs det is at most 2.00e-06
(B200) and 1.95e-06 (GB300), with 0 dX mismatches at 1e-2.
- **Why B0 is the strongest applicable baseline:** it is the only
non-Cake implementation of this exact function at these sizes.
TransformerEngine's mHC (TF32 mapping math, log-domain Sinkhorn without
eps) and Megatron-LM's fused mHC (TF32 projection) compute a different
function. FlashInfer's `flashinfer.mhc` kernels and DeepGEMM's mega_mhc
are inference only.
- **new:** nd with this PR.
- **Operations:**
  - forward = forward prepare + forward finish.
  - backward = backward prepare + backward finish from saved statistics.
- checkpointed step = forward + statistics recompute + backward on the
checkpoint path. det runs its checkpointed step the way its autograd
function does. For B0 it is a no-grad forward + a with-grad forward +
the backward.

The main columns show CUPTI kernel-sum latency, which is the sum of the
operation's kernel durations. Each value is the median over 4
ABBA-ordered groups of the per-group median of 64 iterations (warmup 8,
cold L2). All three arms run in one process on the same random inputs,
and 4 processes (one per GPU) run concurrently, each on a share of the
token counts. Speedup = det / new and B0 / new, so a value above 1 means
new is faster.

The check columns show det / new nd latency and ratio in Table 1's evd
and graph timings. Forward and checkpointed step come from Table 1's
runs, and backward comes from a separate run of the same method. The
check columns are needed because kernel-sum adds up kernel durations, so
time in which two kernels run at the same time is counted twice (for
example through programmatic dependent launch, PDL). nd's backward
overlaps more kernels than det's, so where kernel-sum reads below 1.000
it understates nd's backward and checkpointed-step speedup vs det.

GB200 has no Table 2 in this PR because only the previous-vs-new rows
were measured there.

The kernel's other Cake variants (the deterministic mode, and hidden
5120 and 7168) are not changed here; the family ships on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a, and this PR changes only nd's forward mapping pass
at hidden 4096 on sm_100a and sm_103a, plus the text of the copied
kernel sources.

Several tests still expect older backend behavior or enter GPU
compilation from mocked CPU paths.

Mock the generated-program loader in the Mamba dispatch tests, accept
SM107 in the Cake backend test, and expect the resolved PDL default.
Skip the FP4 trace initializer on GPUs that cannot quantize FP4. Update
the offline MoE tuning test to mock candidate exchange and check
backend-owned workspace cleanup.

### [aa1c3a8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/aa1c3a8e8991c64a4c092d6bd52af5cab9709b6f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T21:54:15Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP4 EP1 T128 / T512 / T1024 rank programs on sm_103a (#8706)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline in a single kernel launch. It has single-rank routed-FP4,
single-rank routed-FP8 and grouped-GEMM-routes variants, plus a TP/EP
rank variant. The rank variant has 32 programs, covering TP4 EP1, TP8
EP1, TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8 at 1 to 4096 tokens. This PR updates the rank
variant and changes 3 of its 32 programs: TP4 EP1 at 128, 512 and 1024
tokens. The other 29 rank programs are byte-identical.

Speedup over the previous Cake version (the rank variant on FlashInfer
main after #8682), for replicates a / b:

- TP4 EP1 at 128 tokens: 1.0046x / 1.0051x, saving 1.32 / 1.45 µs per
call.
- TP4 EP1 at 512 tokens: 1.0038x / 1.0036x, saving 1.15 / 1.08 µs per
call.
- TP4 EP1 at 1024 tokens: 1.0020x / 1.0024x, saving 0.65 / 0.78 µs per
call.

Speedup over the issue baseline, autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`: this PR is faster on all 32 shapes
in both replicates. The range is 1.0216x to 1.1792x in replicate a and
1.0220x to 1.1762x in replicate b. On the three changed shapes it is
1.0710x / 1.0692x (128 tokens), 1.0645x / 1.0636x (512 tokens) and
1.0462x / 1.0464x (1024 tokens).

(FlashInfer main after #8682), with speedup = previous / this PR.

using the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous version and this
PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6 rounds, with a
previous-vs-previous control. Each value is the median of the 6 process
medians. Columns a and b are two independent replicates, each run alone
on its own node. On the three TP4 EP1 rows, replicate a reads 1.35-1.61
% slower than b for both versions because of the node difference, and
each comparison stays within one node. Speedups are computed from the
latencies before they were rounded to two decimals and are shown to 4
decimals. The 3 changed programs are in bold. The savings quoted above
are the differences of the displayed latencies. The other 29 rank
programs are byte-identical between the two versions and compile to
identical machine code. Across both replicates, their ratios ranged from
0.9984 to 1.0012 and their latency moved by up to 0.09 µs. That is the
run-to-run noise envelope. All 3 changed programs sit outside it, with a
smallest saving of 0.65 µs at a ratio of 1.0020. Columns 9-14 compare
autotuned `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` with this PR, with speedup
= TRT-LLM / this PR. They come from a separate run with the same harness
used for #8669 and #8682, so the this-PR latencies there differ slightly
from columns 4 and 7.*

grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a, while the rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [ef1c179](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ef1c17974ee820b4e8d5cf3564297dc14e43faac)

- **作者**: Jonathan Dierksen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T21:41:38Z
- **提交信息**: ci: share the GPU compile cache through S3, written only by scheduled main runs (#7016)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Follow-up to flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6811 and
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7063 (merged). It is rebuilt on #7063's
`ci/compile_cache.sh` and on #6968's scheduled main runs.

The per-runner compile cache keeps compiled CuTe-DSL / Triton / TIRx /
KDA-PTX / cubin artifacts **per runner**. The A10G and T4 lanes get a
fresh EC2 instance per job, and new H100 runners start empty, so those
jobs always start cold. This PR adds a **shared S3 layer** under the
per-runner cache.

It also fixes a bug on main where #7063 and #6968 interact.
`CI_COMPILE_CACHE_MODE` is `read-write` only for `github.event_name ==
'push'`, but main no longer has a push trigger. As a result, no job ever
writes the per-runner seeds, and every PR job starts cold. The condition
is now `schedule`. This is a one-line change and can be split into its
own PR if preferred.

**Layout.** There is one gzipped tarball per (image ID, GPU, lane) at
`s3://flashinfer-build-cache/compile-cache/main/<image
ID>/<GPU>/<lane>.tar.gz`.
- The key uses the pulled image's immutable ID, matching #7063's local
namespace, so a rebuilt tag never reuses an object.
- The lane is `part1`..`part5` for the A10G shards and `all` for T4 and
H100. Targeted runs use the lane of the bare run they narrow.
- The GPU is part of the key because several CuTe-DSL kernel names embed
the SM count.

**Reads (every job, including fork PRs).** The bucket allows anonymous
read.
- **PR jobs (`read-only`):** under the runner lock,
`ci/compile_cache.sh` keeps an extracted mirror at
`runner-<hash>/s3/<image ID>/<lane>/tree`, refreshed by a conditional
(ETag) download. An unchanged object costs one 304 response. The mirror
is mounted at `/compile-cache-s3:ro`.
- `ci/compile_cache_entrypoint.sh` copies the mirror into the job's
private tree first, then merges the per-runner seed over it.
- A CuTe-DSL module directory is one unit, because its single
`meta.json` vouches for every `.o` in it. The seed's version of a module
is copied in whole when the S3 tree lacks it. When both have it, the
seed adds only missing objects, and only if the two `meta.json` files
are byte-identical; mixing objects would load them under the wrong key.
- Other artifacts are content-keyed by path, so seed files are copied
only when missing.
  - Mirrors of images unused for a week are evicted, as stale seeds are.
- **Writers (scheduled runs on main, once the upload role exists):** a
writer is a `read-write` job with `CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR` set.
- It **bypasses the seed** and compiles in a new
`${RUNNER_TEMP}/compile-cache-writer.XXXXXXXX` (a fresh path per job)
that holds only the S3 restore. It also runs without the shared pip
cache. PR containers on the same host can write both the seed and that
cache, so a writer never uploads a file a PR job could have placed or
influenced.
- It **retires its runner's seeds** (all images). Seeds stop growing
once writers exist; left frozen, they would shadow newer modules and
keep retired images on disk. PR jobs on that runner then start from the
S3 mirror alone.

**Writes (scheduled runs on main only).**
- After the tests, an `always()` step gets credentials through OIDC
(`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials`, 15-minute session). The next
step uploads the writer directory. It runs even when tests fail or the
run is cancelled, because whatever was compiled is still valid.
- Credentials are requested only after the test step, so they never
reach the test container.
- Only content-keyed artifacts are packed: `cached_ops/*_cute_dsl`,
`cached_ops/kda_tirx_*`, `cached_ops/kda_ptx`, the downloaded `cubins/`
and the Triton cache. nvcc modules, autotune results, generated sources,
`*.lock`, `*.tmp.*` and Triton `tmp.pid_*` files are never packed.
- **Tarball, not `aws s3 sync`.** One PUT replaces the object
atomically, so two concurrent writers cannot interleave one module's
`meta.json` rewrite or wipe with another job's objects; the later upload
wins. Scheduled runs are already serialized by their concurrency group,
so this is a backstop. A sync-based design would need per-module locking
in S3, and reads need only `curl`.
- The upload is skipped when the job built nothing new, using a content
hash of the artifacts taken after the restore.
- The upload is also skipped **when the writer's restore failed**
(network error, 5xx, unpack error). A writer that started cold by
accident would otherwise replace the lane's tarball with only its own
builds. The restore's manifest doubles as the completion marker.
- Growth is bounded. Old FlashInfer-version trees and Triton hashes
would otherwise accumulate until the image changes. When the tarball
exceeds `CI_COMPILE_CACHE_S3_MAX_MB` (default 4096), the writer uploads
only the files it compiled itself. That also drops kernels the job
reused from the tarball (restored files keep their archive mtimes);
later writers recompile and add them back. A lane whose real working set
exceeds the cap would alternate between full and cut tarballs, so the
cap should be raised once the first uploads show lane sizes.

**Fail open.** Every restore, fetch or upload failure prints a
`::warning::` and the job continues from the cache it has: 404/403,
network errors, unpack errors, missing credentials, ownership problems
and oversize tarballs. Containers write the writer directory as root, so
the upload `sudo -n chown`s it first.

**Rollout is inert for writes until an admin acts.** The writer path
turns on only when the repository variable `COMPILE_CACHE_S3_ROLE_ARN`
is set. Until then, scheduled main runs update per-runner seeds exactly
as #7063 intended (with the fix above). PR jobs fetch, find no object
(404), and continue.

### Measured (from #6811, H100, the six-file scope, 578 tests)

| | wall | CuTe-DSL builds | CuTe-DSL compile time (summed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold runner | 28m21s | 205 | 1571 s |
| warm runner (same host) | 6m43s | 0 | 0 s |

That warm cache was **41 MB**. This PR is meant to give A10G/T4 and new
H100 runners the warm column without a prior job on the same host.
#6810's sccache covers nvcc; this layer covers what sccache cannot cache
(CuTe-DSL, Triton, TIRx, KDA PTX). **I have not measured the full-suite
size:** the first scheduled writer job will print `Uploaded <N> MB to
s3://...` per lane. The 4096 MB cap is a guess pending that measurement.

### 🔐 Admin setup (required before uploads happen; I have not done any
of this)

1. **OIDC provider** (skip if the AWS account already has one): IAM →
Identity providers → add `token.actions.githubusercontent.com`, audience
`sts.amazonaws.com`.
2. **IAM role**, e.g. `flashinfer-ci-compile-cache-writer`, with this
trust policy. Scheduled and manually dispatched runs on main both carry
the subject `repo:flashinfer-ai/flashinfer:ref:refs/heads/main`. Use
`StringEquals`, never `StringLike` with a wildcard: pull request runs
also get a token (subject `repo:flashinfer-ai/flashinfer:pull_request`),
and only the exact main-ref subject must pass.
   ```json
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [{
       "Effect": "Allow",
"Principal": {"Federated":
"arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com"},
       "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
       "Condition": {
         "StringEquals": {
"token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com",
"token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub":
"repo:flashinfer-ai/flashinfer:ref:refs/heads/main"
         }
       }
     }]
   }
   ```
   Permissions policy: write only under the prefix. Reads are anonymous.
   ```json
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [{
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Action": ["s3:PutObject"],
"Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::flashinfer-build-cache/compile-cache/main/*"
     }]
   }
   ```
Keep the max session duration at the default (1 h); the workflow asks
for 15 min.
3. **Repository variable** `COMPILE_CACHE_S3_ROLE_ARN` = the role ARN
(Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables). It is a
variable, not a secret, because the ARN is not sensitive: the trust
policy is the control.
4. **Lifecycle rule** on `flashinfer-build-cache`: prefix
`compile-cache/`, expire current versions **30 days** after last write.
Image IDs change with every CI image, and retired prefixes stop being
written. If versioning is enabled, also expire noncurrent versions after
1 day, otherwise every upload keeps a full old copy.
5. **Deny everyone else writes under `compile-cache/`.** The sccache IAM
user's static keys reach branch-PR containers (AOT and, since #6810, GPU
lanes) and write to the same bucket. If its policy allows `PutObject`
bucket-wide, a branch PR could write `compile-cache/main/*`. Either
confirm that user's policy is scoped to the sccache prefixes, or add a
bucket-policy Deny for every principal but the upload role:
   ```json
   {
     "Effect": "Deny",
     "Principal": "*",
     "Action": ["s3:PutObject", "s3:DeleteObject"],
     "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::flashinfer-build-cache/compile-cache/*",
"Condition": {"ArnNotEquals": {"aws:PrincipalArn":
"arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:role/flashinfer-ci-compile-cache-writer"}}
   }
   ```
6. Check that anonymous `GetObject` covers `compile-cache/*`. Today
`https://flashinfer-build-cache.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2`
is publicly readable and listable, and the fetch relies on that. Keep
anonymous `s3:ListBucket`: without it S3 answers 403 for a missing
object, and a writer treats only a 404 as "no tarball yet", so no lane
would ever get its first upload.

### ⚠️ Related exposure found while doing this (not fixed here)

- **The sccache credentials can be reached from branch PRs, now on more
lanes.** `pr-test.yml` passes `secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` /
`SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` to the AOT jobs on `pull_request`, and since #6810
to the GPU lanes too. PRs from branches in this repo (about 14% of PRs)
receive repository secrets, and such a PR can edit `pr-test.yml` to read
them. Those keys can write the sccache objects in the same bucket
(`cuda129-x86_64/` etc.). `release.yml` and `nightly-release.yml` read
the same sccache prefixes, so a poisoned object could end up in a
**release wheel**. Suggested follow-up: move sccache writes to the same
OIDC pattern (main-only role), and give PR jobs read-only access
(`SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS=true` reads the public bucket).
- **Persistent self-hosted runners.** As `ci/COMPILE_CACHE.md` already
says, approved PR scripts run host commands on the H100 hosts that later
run main jobs. A malicious PR could leave something behind on the host
(a modified `docker`, a background process) that tampers with a later
writer's directory or uses its 15-minute credentials. The fresh writer
directory and the short-lived token close the easy paths. A10G/T4 run on
a fresh EC2 instance per job and do not have this exposure. If it is
unacceptable, limit uploads to those lanes by adding `&& matrix.kind !=
'h100'` to the writer condition in "Configure compile cache".

## 🔍 Related Issues

- Follow-up to flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6811 and
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7063 (compile cache),
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6968 (scheduled main runs).
- Complements flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6810 (nvcc through sccache for
the GPU lanes).

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit`
(or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files`
and fixed any reported issues. (Run on the touched files.)

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

`ci/tests/test_compile_cache_s3.py` adds 13 CPU-only `unittest` cases in
#7063's style. `pre-commit.yml` now discovers `test_compile_cache*.py`,
so it runs them next to the existing lifecycle tests. All 24 pass on
Ubuntu 22.04 (bash 5.1, GNU tar 1.34, the runners' userland). A local
HTTP server with ETag/304 support stands in for the bucket, and a fake
`aws` on PATH stands in for uploads. Covered:
- **Script:**
  - what gets packed, and what never does;
  - writer round trip, plus no upload when nothing new was built;
  - a same-size rebuild (new `meta.json` contents) still uploads;
- a failed restore blocks the upload, leaving the published tarball
untouched;
  - the writer refusing, and never uploading, a pre-populated directory;
  - the oversize reset;
  - mirror fetch, covering 404, ETag reuse, update and expiry;
- merge rules, including the `meta.json` guard and keeping existing
files;
  - image and lane validation;
  - fail-open.
- **`ci/bash.sh` with a mocked Docker:**
- writer mode mounts the fresh directory, restores S3 into it, and
retires the runner's seeds;
  - PR mode mounts the mirror and passes `COMPILE_CACHE_S3_TREE`;
- the real entrypoint prefers S3 and fills gaps from the seed without
mixing modules.

Mutation checks: each of the following, disabled, fails a test:
- the `meta.json` guard;
- `--skip-old-files`;
- the writer-directory wipe;
- the content hash in the manifest;
- the restore-completion check;
- seed retirement.

The workflow steps themselves cannot run before merge: writes need the
admin role and a scheduled run on main.

## Reviewer Notes

- The entrypoint keeps its `<seed> <dest> <command>` contract. The S3
tree arrives through `COMPILE_CACHE_S3_TREE`, so #7063's entrypoint test
is unchanged.
- The test job now has job-level `permissions` (`contents: read`,
`actions: read`, `id-token: write`). It drops `pull-requests: write` /
`statuses: read`, which nothing in the test job uses.
- Bucket and region fall back to `flashinfer-build-cache` / `us-west-2`
when `vars.*` are empty, as `release.yml` already does.
- Uploads use the host `aws` CLI if one exists; otherwise they run the
pinned `amazon/aws-cli:2.17.0` image (only on scheduled main runs).

### [649e2d5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/649e2d5cea157c196fa6c6dcfae4ed63a7edfbef)

- **作者**: Jonathan Dierksen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T21:39:10Z
- **提交信息**: ci: overlap PR AOT provider builds within one job (#7897)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The PR `AOT Build Import (<arch>, <cuda>)` job builds the six provider
wheels one after another on one 64-core runner. With 100% sccache hits
(run 40929394275, x64 cu130, 65,178 hits / 0 misses, read-only) it took
~55 min: ~5 min image pull, ~47 min of provider builds (sm80 3.3, sm89
3.3, sm90a 11, sm100a 11, sm103a 10.8, sm120f 7.7 min), ~1 min
shim/install/verify.

This builds the providers as a bounded pool (`AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY`)
in the same job:

- `run_bounded_parallel` (`scripts/jit_cache_build_common.sh`) keeps N
builds running and starts the next as a slot frees; the first failure
(also one that arrives while the pool is not full, or after the last
item started) kills the rest with their descendants. It tracks pids and
polls every 0.2 s rather than using `wait -n`, since bash drops finished
jobs from `jobs`; this also removes the bash >= 4.3 requirement.
- Each provider builds in a private copy of
`flashinfer-jit-cache-provider` (`python -m build` writes into the
package dir). `MAX_JOBS` is split between running builds, so total ninja
parallelism is unchanged.
- `_create_data_dir` (`build_backend.py`) no longer unlinks symlinks
that are already correct; concurrent builds would otherwise break each
other's include path at start-up.
- `pr-test.yml` passes `AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY` (repo variable,
default 2). Set the variable to 1 for the old serial behaviour, to A/B
time without a code change. The script default is 1.

Why overlap only: a cache hit costs ~8 CPU-s per TU, so the build is
CPU-bound and overlap adds no cores. It fills the 60-75 s of spec
generation before ninja starts (sm100a/sm103a/sm120f) and each build's
ramp-down tail.

**Measurements** (A/B of `AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY` 1 vs 2, same commit,
both runs started at ~17:07Z on 2026-11-02, so same merge ref and runner
pool). Runner: self-hosted `cpu` on-demand, 64 cores (GPU: N/A). sccache
hit rate was 99.97-100% in all twelve jobs with identical compile
request counts, so cache state is not a confounder. Full detail:
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/7897#issuecomment-6585864388

| Job | Provider wheels, conc. 1 | Provider wheels, conc. 2 | Job wall,
conc. 1 | Job wall, conc. 2 | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| x64 cu129 | 2752 s | 2120 s | 55:05 | 44:04 | 11:01 (20%) |
| x64 cu130 | 2858 s | 2281 s | 55:07 | 45:38 | 9:29 (17%) |
| x64 cu134 | 3297 s | 2599 s | 63:15 | 51:32 | 11:43 (19%) |
| arm64 cu129 | 2987 s | 2485 s | 58:56 | 50:20 | 8:36 (15%) |
| arm64 cu130 | 3727 s | 3172 s | 70:36 | 61:07 | 9:29 (13%) |
| arm64 cu134 | 4005 s | 3660 s | 76:01 | 69:50 | 6:11 (8%) |

## Reviewer Notes

- Gain is limited by CPU, not scheduling. Bigger wins need less CPU per
hit (preprocessor cache, restoring ninja state), a separate effort. A
variant splitting providers across runners (3 jobs, ~14/14/18 min +
assemble) is on branch `jdierksen/aot-split-jobs` of the fork; it scales
better but adds runners and an artifact handoff.
- Each build keeps `MAX_JOBS / concurrency` for its whole life, so cores
freed by a short build (sm80/sm89) are not reused by the one still
running.
- New CPU tests cover the pool (limit, slot reuse, failure) and the
script wiring. The full script and concurrent provider builds were not

see the measurements above.

on failure so container teardown cleans them up.

### [3030ed1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3030ed15383720ed8e6445a3e56886499851cd77)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T21:03:06Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm): fixed-claim column-task backward for the smallest token counts (#8704)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). The two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`, use the same forward and differ only in the
backward. Both modes support the forms listed in #8655 on sm_100a
(B200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a (R200):

- [T, H] rows with BF16 weight, or FP32 weight (`w32`)
- fused residual add (`res`, H6144)
- per-head views [T,24,256] (strided) and [T,4,256] (contiguous), with a
shared w[256]

This follow-up to #8577, #8626 and #8655 speeds up the
`deterministic=False` backward at small token counts on all three
architectures. It covers 12 backward routes per architecture: H1536,
H2048, H4096, H5120, H6144 and residual H6144, each with BF16 and FP32
weight. On each route, the backward for T in (0, cut] now runs a new
single-kernel program (fixed-claim TwoSum column task). The windows are:

|form|weight|B200 sm_100a|GB300 sm_103a|R200 sm_107a|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|H1536|BF16|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|
|H2048|BF16|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|
|H4096|BF16|(0, 64]|(0, 32]|(0, 64]|
|H5120|BF16|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|
|H6144|BF16|(0, 64]|(0, 32]|(0, 64]|
|H6144 residual|BF16|(0, 64]|(0, 48]|(0, 64]|
|H1536|FP32|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|
|H2048|FP32|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|(0, 64]|
|H4096|FP32|(0, 64]|(0, 32]|(0, 64]|
|H5120|FP32|(0, 64]|(0, 48]|(0, 64]|
|H6144|FP32|(0, 64]|(0, 48]|(0, 64]|
|H6144 residual|FP32|(0, 64]|(0, 48]|(0, 64]|

This PR does not change any other route or T, the forward or the
deterministic package.

Speedup = baseline latency / new latency. A value > 1 means the new
kernel is faster.

In the B200 and GB300 records, the new backward is faster than det on
every in-window bwd row: 1.18x to 1.65x on B200 and 1.05x to 1.59x on
GB300. 2xfwd+bwd is also faster than det on every in-window row except
two GB300 rows: H6144 w FP32 T48 (new 10.18 us vs det 9.79 us, 0.96x)
and H5120 w FP32 T48 (new 9.09 us vs det 9.06 us; the ratio prints as
1.00x). Against the strongest in-budget non-Cake SOTA, bwd reads 0.82x
to 2.09x on B200 and 0.70x to 1.84x on GB300. Most rows below 1 are at
T1, where torch.compile's backward is faster. A separate backward-only
timing also compares new with the `deterministic=False` program it
replaces. In that timing, new is faster than both det and the replaced
program on every in-window row of all three GPUs. Only the R200 rows of
that timing are shown below.
