Baselines and measurement (B200 and GB300 tables). Every row has two
baselines:

- det: the deterministic Cake kernel (`deterministic=True`) of the same
tree. The FlashInfer deterministic package is unchanged from main.
- SOTA: the fastest non-Cake candidate that has these outputs and meets
the accuracy budget. The budget is dx atol = rtol = 1e-2, and dw per
element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64, taking the worst of 5 seeds.
Candidates timed:
  - QuACK 0.6.5, heuristic and autotuned
  - torch.compile, max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and default mode
  - Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton 3.8.0)
  - Transformer Engine 2.20.2

new is the non-deterministic Cake kernel (`deterministic=False`) with
this PR's programs. Accuracy (new / det / SOTA) is pass / pass / pass on
every row.

Timing setup:

- Sessions: 4 sessions (s1/s3 forward, s2/s4 reverse) run in parallel on
the node's 4 GPUs.
- Latency: the median of the CUPTI span of one CUDA-graph replay with
cold L2, over 2 sessions x 3 interleaved rounds x 201 replays, pooled.
The p10-p90 ranges are omitted here.
- Span contents: each span includes the implementation's own setup,
reduction, cast and copy kernels.
- Workload: eps 1e-6. y / dx / h_new are BF16, and rstd and dw are FP32,
for every implementation.
- Process: all implementations of a row run in one process that also
loads every non-Cake candidate, including torch.compile.
- Order: the implementation order rotates, so every implementation takes
every position equally often.

Key:

- Workload `H<H> plain|res T<T> w BF16|FP32`: x [T, H] is BF16, and w is
BF16 or FP32. `plain` = no residual. `res` = fused residual add (h_new =
BF16(h + u), combined grad), H6144.
- op: `2xfwd+bwd` = two forwards and one backward (checkpointed). On
every fwd row, det and new launch the same programs. The printed fwd
ratios are measured values.
- SOTA names:
- TC = torch.compile (torch 2.14.1+cu130, inductor mode
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, emulate_precision_casts=True) of the
explicit FP32-statistics reference
  - TCd = the same with torch.compile default mode
- QA = QuACK 0.6.5 rmsnorm_fwd_tuned / rmsnorm_bwd_tuned (exhaustive
per-shape autotune, cached before timing)
- Liger = Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton 3.8.0), casting_mode gemma (FP32
math)
  - Transformer Engine was never the fastest.
- `~` marks a ratio whose baseline (det or SOTA) or new latency has a
session spread above 5 % (|s1 - s2| / min of the per-session medians).
Such rows are noisy at this size.

**B200 (sm_100a): new non-deterministic Cake vs deterministic Cake vs
non-Cake SOTA, rows inside this PR's windows (T <= cut)**

GPU B200 sm_100a, 148 SMs, compute capability 10.0; driver 580.82.07;
CUDA toolkit Build cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0; torch
2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA runtime 13.0). NVML SM clock during timing 1965-1965
MHz (median 1965, 100% of samples at max) in each of s1-s4; memory
3996-3996 MHz; foreign GPU processes at start / end 0 / 0. Residual
bias: Cake gains somewhat more from the context than the other
non-compile libraries on small rows: SOTA/new vs the non-compile
candidates is up to about 1.10x higher (GB300) / 1.14x higher (B200) in
the one-process measurement than in a process without torch.compile;
large rows <= 1.02x. So small-row ratios may overstate the new kernel's
lead by up to about that much. Ratios vs det are unaffected. All rows
here are small rows (T <= 65), and the kernels run 2-8 us.

Rows: 12 forms at T1, T4, T16 and T64, x 3 ops = 144 rows.

**GB300 (sm_103a): new non-deterministic Cake vs deterministic Cake vs
non-Cake SOTA, rows inside this PR's windows (T <= cut)**

GPU GB300 sm_103a, 152 SMs, compute capability 10.3; driver 580.159.03;
CUDA toolkit Build cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0; torch
2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA runtime 13.0). NVML SM clock during timing 2070-2070
MHz (median 2070, 100% of samples at max) in each of s1-s4; memory
3996-3996 MHz; foreign GPU processes at start / end 0 / 0. Residual
bias: Cake gains somewhat more from the context than the other
non-compile libraries on small rows: SOTA/new vs the non-compile
candidates is up to about 1.10x higher (GB300) / 1.14x higher (B200) in
the one-process measurement than in a process without torch.compile;
large rows <= 1.02x. So small-row ratios may overstate the new kernel's
lead by up to about that much. Ratios vs det are unaffected. All rows
here are small rows (T <= 65), and the kernels run 2-8 us.

Rows: 12 forms at T1, T16 and the top of each window (T64, T32 or T48),
x 3 ops = 108 rows.

GPU R200 sm_107a, 212 SMs; CUDA [GAP: the CUDA toolkit and runtime of
this R200 run are not in the source; fill in before posting].

Backward-only timing: latencies are span medians in us, pooled over 4
sessions (CUDA graph, L2 flush, CUPTI span; balanced implementation
order).

- new = this PR's program.
- det = `deterministic=True`.
- FI main ND = the `deterministic=False` program that FlashInfer main
runs at that T, which this PR replaces.
- best torch.compile = the faster of the torch.compile default and
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs modes on the FP32 reference backward. It is
the only non-Cake baseline in this timing.

The measured programs are text-identical (CUDA and host code) to this
PR's. The R200 rows with det, SOTA from the full candidate set, and new
are pending. New is faster than det and than FI main ND on every row.

Rows: 12 forms at T 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 and 64, all inside
the R200 windows.

### [2b9ce0e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2b9ce0e9a5cf00670329ab845e96c4d957227808)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T20:54:52Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_dense_projection_gemm): two-split K1 for 4096 -> 128 FP32 weight gradients on 152-SM and 212-SM parts (#8680)

The K1 weight-gradient GEMM in
`flashinfer/experimental/dense_projection_gemm` (`deterministic=False`)
computes out[d_out, d_in] = G^T X over the tokens. It picks a split-K
program for each row, token count and SM count. This PR adds a K1 entry
for the FP32-output 4096 -> 128 weight gradient on 152-SM GB200
(sm_100a) and GB300 (sm_103a) parts, and the same entry on 212-SM R200
(sm_107a) parts. The row now runs a two-split program of 64-wide output
tiles when the token count spans an even number of 64-token K blocks.
That covers 1024 to 4096 tokens on GB200, 1024 to 6144 tokens on GB300
and 1024 to 7680 tokens on R200. At these block counts the output is
bitwise identical to the deterministic program's. The deterministic
program is the deterministic package's plan of the same GEMM, and this
package also runs it for rows without an entry. Before this PR, this row
ran it at every token count. Odd block counts, other token counts, BF16
output and SM counts other than 152 and 212 (148-SM B200 / B300
included) keep the deterministic program. There are two baselines: the
previous Cake route, which is the deterministic program, and the library
SOTA. This PR's own change is four commits (0f77bca7, 1897dbe4, 9196e63f
and e8b1c45d). The branch was stacked on #8671, which has merged, and
main is merged into it.

Compared with the deterministic program, this PR is faster in both eager
and graph modes. The speedup is 1.25-1.40x on GB200, 1.28-1.41x on GB300
and 1.32-1.38x on R200 for wgrad, 1.11-1.24x, 1.12-1.25x and 1.13-1.24x
for bwd, and 1.03-1.08x, 1.04-1.08x and 1.06-1.09x for ckpt. Graph wgrad
at 1024 tokens drops from 12.3 us to 8.8 us on GB200, from 12.2 us to
8.6 us on GB300 and from 10.1 us to 7.3 us on R200. The library SOTA is
still faster in every CUDA-graph cell except R200 wgrad at 7680 tokens,
where this PR is level with it (1.01 graph). For graph wgrad, SOTA /
this PR is 0.66-0.80 on GB200, 0.65-0.95 on GB300 and 0.60-1.01 on R200.
In eager mode the library also leads on wgrad, except R200 at 7680
tokens, where this PR is level with it (1.02). On GB200 and GB300 the
library's eager bwd and ckpt include host launch gaps between separate
launches, so this PR is faster there except for GB300 bwd at 4096 and
6144 tokens (0.98, 0.96). On R200 the library is also faster in eager
bwd (0.63-0.88) and eager ckpt (0.58-0.77).

- **Columns:** `deterministic us` and `previous route us` are the same
program here: the deterministic program, which this row ran before this
PR. The pair is an A/A check. `this PR us` is this package after this
PR, which runs the two-split program on these rows. `library SOTA us` is
the second baseline. Each time cell is eager / CUDA graph. In the ratio
columns, a value above 1 means this PR is faster.
- **op:** wgrad is the weight-gradient GEMM, the only op whose route
changes. bwd is input gradient + weight gradient. ckpt is 2 x forward +
input gradient + weight gradient (an activation-checkpointed step).
- **Library SOTA:** the fastest correct launch among `torch.mm` (cuBLAS
13.8.0) and the top 8 cuBLASLt 13.8.0 heuristic algorithms for the same
operands and output dtype, with FP32 compute. A launch is correct if its
FP64 relative Frobenius error is <= 1e-3 (FP32 output). In bwd and ckpt,
each op uses its own fastest library launch. It is the strongest
applicable baseline because it is the vendor library's own candidate set
for these exact shapes, with the fastest correct algorithm chosen per
shape on the measured GPU.
- **Timing:** CUPTI kernel timestamps. An op's time runs from the start
of the first kernel to the end of the last kernel across the launches in
the call. L2 is cold, flushed twice before every timed iteration. Each
cell uses 9 paired groups x 20 timed iterations, with arms interleaved
in a seeded random order, and takes the median per run. Each GPU type
ran 4 independent processes on separate GPUs of one node: two ran all
rows, and two ran one row per process. The reported value is the median
of the 4 run medians, for both eager and CUDA graph replay.
- **A/A noise:** Deterministic / previous route, which is the same
program run as two arms, is 0.992-1.007 over 18 cells on GB200,
0.996-1.008 over 24 cells on GB300 and 0.986-1.009 over 24 cells on
R200.
- **GPUs:** GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs, driver 580.126.20) and GB300
(sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03), with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA
13.0 runtime, CUDA 13.4 driver API and cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.8.0. R200
(sm_107a, 212 SMs, driver 620.43) used the CUDA 13.5 driver API, with
the same PyTorch, CUDA runtime and cuBLAS / cuBLASLt versions.
nvidia-smi showed no software power cap sample on any GPU in these runs.

The K1 program's other Cake variants cover BF16 and FP32 output, one to
four K splits, and transposed-store and row-major-store tiles of 64 to
256 columns, for d_in 4096 / 5120 / 6144 / 8192 and d_out 32 to 1024,
and the program ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [c325578](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c325578c2e7fcf76de3a82b2b469b4d4ce3ad3d6)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T20:29:24Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): plan the 5120 -> 17408 weight gradient with the half-tail TMA-store program at T 16231 / 16384 on sm_100a (#8703)

This PR adds row rules to the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package
in `flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM.
Most programs in the package are BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and
wgrad), and one is an FP32 router GEMM. The PR adds no new program,
kernel source or library. It adds 2 row rules, both for `sm_100a`. Each
rule applies at a single token count T, either 16231 or 16384. The rules
cover the 5120→17408 weight gradient (wgrad, BF16 output). Before this
PR, `sm_100a` had no rule for these rows, so they used the default
program. That is the plain register-store-epilogue program with 16-row
raster groups. `sm_103a` already has rules for the same rows at the same
two T. The new `sm_100a` rules match those `sm_103a` rules. They use the
half-tail program in 12-row raster groups, and its BF16 output tiles go
through a one-slot TMA-store epilogue. Its `sm_100a` library already
ships in the package. The K split stays the same, with the whole K per
output tile. The rule count goes from 382 to 384 (`sm_100a` from 150 to
152). The `sm_103a` and `sm_107a` rules are unchanged. The baseline is
the previous Cake version of the package on main. Against it, the
changed rows have a speedup of 1.042 on B200 at both T. On GB200 they
measure 1.009 at T 16231 and 1.008 at T 16384, which is a small gain.
The rules apply only to `sm_100a`, so these rows were measured on GB200
and B200 only. No changed row is slower on either GPU. The K split is
unchanged, so outputs on those rows are bitwise identical to main on
both. All other rows of the 294-row shape list plan the same programs as
main.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2,
BF16 output. Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1
mean this PR is faster.

| GPU (arch, SMs) | layer (in→out) | op | out | T | previous µs | this
PR µs | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 (sm_100a, 152) | 5120→17408 | weight gradient (wgrad) | BF16 |
16231 | 1595.8 | 1581.5 | 1.009 |
| GB200 (sm_100a, 152) | 5120→17408 | weight gradient (wgrad) | BF16 |
16384 | 1609.0 | 1595.5 | 1.008 |
| B200 (sm_100a, 148) | 5120→17408 | weight gradient (wgrad) | BF16 |
16231 | 1848.9 | 1774.5 | 1.042 |
| B200 (sm_100a, 148) | 5120→17408 | weight gradient (wgrad) | BF16 |
16384 | 1865.1 | 1790.6 | 1.042 |

The package also ships FP32-output forms, weight-gradient (wgrad)
programs and the FP32 router GEMM (run through BF16x3 emulation), on
`sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

### [f6fadc6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f6fadc62593238c98d5b09cec3bb5e7673897c29)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T20:28:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det): ticket scheduling on sm_107a, no fill kernel in eager entry (#8691)

`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk` is the Cake deterministic
DSA indexer top-k scan. It ships in the package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_dsa_indexer_det`. It uses BF16 queries and
keys, and FP32 head weights and scores. It returns the top-k key ids for
each query. The ids and scores do not depend on partition or chunking.
Ties go to the larger id. Cake ships one variant of this kernel. This PR
changes how the scan schedules work on sm_107a, and it removes a fill
kernel from the eager entry. On sm_107a, the scan programs gave each CTA
a fixed set of work units. If another CUDA stream keeps a kernel
resident on even one SM, some CTAs of the scan cannot run until a slot
frees. Their work units then run as a second wave, and the call becomes
about 1.3x to 1.8x slower. This is issue #7548.

- On sm_107a, every scan program except the l6 program now draws its
work units from a ticket word. The sm_100a and sm_103a programs already
do this. Each CTA that runs takes the next work unit, so the work units
spread over the CTAs that run. This removes the second wave.
- The ticket word is a kernel argument owned by the runner. The runner
zeroes it once when it prepares. Each call leaves it at zero again, so
no call pays for a reset.
- The l6 program on sm_107a keeps its fixed schedule, because tickets
made it slower.
- On sm_100a and sm_103a, program choice and schedule do not change. The
kernels get one extra, unused parameter.
- Each call through the eager entry with no causal query offsets used to
launch a small fill kernel before the scan. It now uses one cached
placeholder tensor per device, which is never read. The call therefore
launches only the scan's kernels.
- Most of the eager-entry speedup comes from this host-path change and
from host time that the measured span no longer contains. It does not
come from faster kernels. In prepared calls, kernel time is unchanged
within run-to-run noise.

| GPU | prepared calls (64 ratios: 32 shapes x sampling on/off) min /
median / max | eager entry (8 shapes) min / median / max |
|---|---|---|
| GB300 (sm_103a) | 0.986x / 1.004x / 1.046x | 1.047x / 1.123x / 2.098x
|
| GB200 (sm_100a) | 0.982x / 1.005x / 1.055x | 1.043x / 1.136x / 2.134x
|
| sm_107a (212 SMs) | 0.988x / 1.000x / 1.043x | 1.017x / 1.058x /
1.464x |

Side stream, sm_107a (212 SMs), 12 rows: 1.000x to 1.843x, median
1.442x. The I8 rows are 1.000x and 1.001x because their program is the
l6 program, which keeps the fixed schedule.

The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main: main
`eeed657f` on GB300 and GB200, and the #8355 build on sm_107a, whose
sm_107a dispatch plans equal main's on every row. Speedup is main time
divided by this PR time. Output bits match main on every row of every
table.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Improved work distribution across GPU scan operations, with scheduling
adapted to the operation and hardware.
* Workspace ticket storage is now cleared immediately before each scan
launch where needed, helping preserve correct results across repeated
runs, failed launches, graph replay, and eager calls.
  * Static scan operations avoid unnecessary ticket storage.

### [c1e72c0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c1e72c028a233fc1c8cece8dea908cfbc6c3f35f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T20:28:24Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_det): with grad, collapse pass reads the mapping-pass input from L2 on sm_107a (#8698)

FlashInfer's Cake deterministic mHC backend holds the four-stream mHC
kernels with grad. Main already has these variants:
- forward prepare / recompute and gradient routes at hidden sizes 4096,
5120 and 7168
- group-row token owner and reduction forms above 14927 tokens
- the dual-layout fn split on the activation-checkpoint route (#8312)
- `_xn` mapping-pass forms on sm_100a and sm_103a for 64 < T ≤ 6144
(#8582)

At hidden size 4096, forward prepare runs two passes. A mapping pass
loads the activations X with TMA, and then a collapse pass reads the
same X. The `_xn` forms differ from the existing forms in one way: the X
load uses the L2 hint EVICT_NORMAL instead of EVICT_FIRST. X therefore
stays in L2 for the collapse pass, both on the forward route and in the
activation-checkpoint recompute. This PR routes the `_xn` forms on
sm_107a for 64 < T ≤ 14928 and 15288 < T ≤ 65536. To do that, it adds
the sm_107a builds of three `_xn` mapping-pass forms, two of which are
new libraries. T ≤ 64, 14928 < T ≤ 15288 and T > 65536 keep the existing
forms. sm_100a and sm_103a are unchanged. Outputs are bitwise identical,
and the public API is unchanged.

The baseline, "previous", is the current Cake version of the same
kernels in FlashInfer main, which already includes #8582. Times are
CUPTI active GPU time (the union of kernel intervals) in microseconds.
L2 is flushed with a memset before every timed call. "Forward" is
forward prepare + finish. "Checkpoint" is the activation-checkpoint
recompute followed by the gradient route. Every shape uses 4 streams,
hidden 4096 and T tokens. Each session interleaves three arms in 6
ABC/CBA groups of 32 iterations: previous, this PR, and a second
previous run as a control. Each value is the mean of 2 independent
sessions on two different boards. Speedup = previous / this PR, and a
value above 1 means faster. At T = 15288 this PR runs the same kernels
as the previous version, so its "this PR" value is the control run of
those kernels.

2.14.1+cu130**

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): packed-triangular forward WY program at five CTAs per SM on R200 (#8695)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` is FlashInfer's
deterministic Gated DeltaNet chunked training kernel. Its outputs and
gradients are bitwise reproducible. #8615 added a forward WY program
that runs five CTAs per SM on sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300). That
program uses packed lower-triangular L^T / X tiles and 64 tensor-memory
columns, which brings each CTA to about 43.6 KB of shared memory and 87
registers. sm_107a (R200) kept the four-CTA program. This PR builds the
same program for sm_107a and uses it for every forward WY launch on
R200, both in the forward pass and in the backward recompute. On R200 it
also uses 87 registers and 43,648 B of shared memory per CTA and runs
five CTAs per SM. As a result, every row below changes its launches on
R200. Outputs and gradients are bitwise identical to the previous
version. The baseline is the previous version of this kernel on current
FlashInfer main (speedup = main / this PR, so >1 is faster; median over
56 interleaved clean-process cells). Forward + backward is 1.014x to
1.021x faster on 216 SMs, 1.011x to 1.019x faster on 212 SMs and 1.008x
to 1.022x faster on 208 SMs. The forward pass is 1.034x to 1.054x,
1.026x to 1.047x and 1.019x to 1.058x faster on those boards,
respectively. Every row is faster on all three boards in both f+b and
fwd, and every 95 % confidence interval excludes 1.0.

### [70d1add](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/70d1add9a392eef32514933384f7d9b6c5c86595)

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_cp): row-split sm_107a CP state fixup for 14 to 48 parallel states (up to 1.10x) (#8700)

The Cake Gated DeltaNet (GDN) context-parallel (CP) prefill kernel
family in FlashInfer has six variants: BF16 and FP16 I/O on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes only the CP state fixup stage of
the sm_107a variants. For sequences of one length, when the grid fits,
the fixup now splits each state over 5, 7, 8, 8, 8 and 10 rows per CTA
for 14, 22, 24, 26, 36 and 48 parallel states, instead of 4 rows. The
row splits already shipped for 4, 8, 16 and 32 parallel states are
unchanged. The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main.
This PR is faster on every one of the 14 FP16 shapes in the table: CUDA
graph geomean 1.059x (range 1.007x to 1.103x), eager geomean 1.057x
(range 1.007x to 1.099x). Shapes whose route does not change (other
state counts, or sequences of unequal length) stayed within 0.994x to
1.002x and are not in the table.

GPU: NVIDIA R200 (216 SMs), sm_107a, driver 615.71.10 (CUDA 13.4
driver), CUDA 13.4 toolkit for the kernel builds, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130
(CUDA runtime 13.0), SM clock 2412-2424 MHz during timing. Time = CUPTI
span of one whole public `chunk_gated_delta_rule` CP call (first kernel
start to last kernel end), with a cold L2 before each timed call. The
previous version and this PR were timed interleaved on the same board.
Each value is the median per seed, then the geomean of seeds 17 and 29.
eager = synchronized single calls; CUDA graph = graph replays. new =
this PR. speedup = previous Cake / this PR (above 1 = this PR faster).

public call picks. public call: auto =

are FP16 I/O because the automatic sm_107a CP route accepts FP16 calls
at these state counts. No BF16 call reached these state counts through
the public call in this measurement.

### [dfb2170](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dfb21707af79f987219833e8ebe9f3279d1e7c96)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T20:20:35Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train): L2-prefetching extra-long forward on SM107 (#8701)

This PR changes which module runs the sm_107a forward in the
non-deterministic package of Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` with `deterministic=False`).
From 1740 rows per SM, the sm_107a forward now runs
`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_7f014401d5cc855ab883`. This is the
L2-prefetching 256-thread forward with the packed gate, which PR #8673
added for sm_103a from 3000 rows per SM. On sm_107a, the new route takes
over the whole range the long forward used to serve, so the long forward
no longer runs on that architecture. All eight changed shapes in Table 1
are at or above 1740 rows per SM on the 212-SM R200.

The previous Cake baseline below is the long forward,
`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_7b7fac905aff1ddaa258`, which ran these
inputs on sm_107a before this PR. This PR adds no kernel source. It
builds the existing module for sm_107a and drops the long forward's
sm_107a build, which no sm_107a input reaches any more. The long forward
still ships on sm_100a and sm_103a. Every other module and route runs
the same code as before, including the backward, every sm_107a forward
below 1740 rows per SM, and every sm_100a and sm_103a route.

The PR is one commit on FlashInfer main after PR #8673. The A/B compared
two FlashInfer trees. In the first, the long forward serves sm_107a from
1740 rows per SM. The second is the same tree plus this PR's sm_107a
route. On sm_107a, this PR's routes, library entries and kernel sources
are identical to those of the measured second tree.

A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. The table gives ranges (min-max) over the eight changed shapes
of Table 1 on R200 (VR200 node; nvidia-smi name NVIDIA Graphics Device),
sm_107a, 212 SMs, CUDA 13.4.

| op | det Cake / new | strongest non-Cake / new | previous Cake / new
(A/B) |
|---|---|---|---|
| fwd | 1.096-1.201 | 1.054-1.116 | 1.019-1.059 |
| fwdg | 1.100-1.201 | 1.055-1.114 | 1.016-1.060 |
| bwdg | 1.028-1.109 | 1.038-1.107 | 0.9998-1.0003 |
| ckptg | 1.074-1.119 | 1.040-1.086 | 1.015-1.028 |
| stepg_f32 | 1.077-1.125 (A/B) | - | 1.016-1.028 |
| fwd + bwd | 1.060-1.114 (A/B) | - | 1.006-1.020 |

In the pre-registered A/B, the code changes in 32 cells (fwd, fwdg,
ckptg and stepg_f32 at the eight shapes), and new is faster than the
previous Cake route in all 32. bwdg and bwdg_f32 run the same code in
both trees. The strongest non-Cake kernel is not faster than new on any
row of Table 1. The deterministic Cake kernel is faster than new in one
cell: 1031x48 fwdg in Table 2 (det / new 0.996). That shape is below
1740 rows per SM, and this PR does not change its forward. Every cell
below 1x against the previous Cake route is in a cell that runs the same
code in both trees. "Cells below 1x" lists each one.

The kernel has two other Cake variants: the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`) and the FP32 weight-gradient output of the
non-deterministic package; both packages ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a, and this PR changes only the non-deterministic package's
forward on sm_107a from 1740 rows per SM.

## How the tables were measured

- Latency is CUPTI kernel time with a cold L2, taken with FlashInfer's
GPU timer in `flashinfer.testing`. Inputs are BF16, and all times are in
us.
- Table 1: the deterministic Cake kernel, the strongest non-Cake kernel
and new were measured in the same process. Each value is the median of
the per-round medians over 10 rounds.
- A/B values come from the pre-registered interleaved A/B, which ran 16
sequences and 160 processes. They are the previous Cake and new (A/B)
columns of Table 1 and all of Table 2, and each is a median.
- stepg_f32 has no same-process measurement, so its deterministic Cake
values also come from the A/B.
- The two new columns of Table 1 (new us and new us (A/B)) are two
separate measurements of the same code.
- Strongest non-Cake kernel per row: the fastest of the following, with
torch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0. On every measured row of Table 1,
the fastest was FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated`.
  - FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated` (`fla.modules.fused_norm_gate`).
  - mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn` (`layernorm_gated`).
- torch.compile in default and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs modes, best of
5 fresh compiles each.
- The inductor-generated persistent-reduction Triton kernel of the FP32
formula, launched directly (fwd and fwdg rows only).
- Deterministic Cake: `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`,
unchanged by this PR.
- Operations:
- `fwd` is one eager forward call, and `fwdg` is the forward replayed
from a CUDA graph.
- `bwdg` is the backward replayed from a CUDA graph, and `bwdg_f32` is
the same backward with an FP32 dw.
- `ckptg` is the checkpointed step (2 x forward + backward) in one CUDA
graph, and `stepg_f32` is the same step with an FP32 dw.
  - `fwd + bwd` is fwdg + bwdg, derived.
- In Table 2, the forward at the first eight shapes runs the new module.
1031x48, 3534x48, 6000x48 and 7684x48 are below 1740 rows per SM, so
they run the same code in both trees.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Performance Improvements**
- Updated forward-processing paths on supported hardware to better
handle larger workloads. The extra-long path is now available on
additional hardware, with its activation point aligned to the existing
long-path threshold.

- **Documentation**
- Clarified when forward processing prefetches the next block on
supported hardware.

- **Tests**
- Expanded coverage for routing behavior and inputs near the updated
processing threshold.

### [36f3099](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/36f3099171618dd08933753caf0d061e3510e980)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T20:17:43Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_fp8_projection): SM100a early first-stage loads in small-M decode programs (#8690)

### [f0cb73a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f0cb73aab31ff45e90008ab1a6fda87e34aa39bb)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T20:11:11Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8): masked BLOCK_N batch DeepGEMM FP8 on SM107a (#8688)

`flashinfer.gemm.batch_deepgemm_fp8_nt_groupwise(..., backend=...)`
still uses DeepGEMM by default. With `backend="cake"`, it runs the
generated Cake programs for the problems they own and raises for any
other problem. Before this PR, Cake covered SM100a/SM103a for eight `(n,
k)` pairs: (128, 512), (512, 128), (4096, 7168), (7168, 2048), (6144,
7168), (7168, 3072), (4096, 4096) and (4096, 2048). Those programs
accept float32 scales and native MN-major packed UE8M0 int32 scales for
the serving routes. They produce BF16 output and accumulate in FP32,
applying block scales in the same order as DeepGEMM. This PR adds SM107a
(compute capability 10.7) with masked BLOCK_N programs for (128, 512),
(512, 128), (4096, 7168) and (7168, 2048). On SM107a only float32 scales
are supported. Packed UE8M0 scales raise, so this PR doesn't cover the
serving-route shapes there. The SM107a programs use the K=64
block-scaled FP8 MMA on configs where it measured faster than the K=32
form and keep K=32 on the rest. Each problem's BLOCK_N comes from a
table measured on the 216-SM part. The SM100a/SM103a programs are
unchanged.

Results against FlashInfer's bundled DeepGEMM masked kernel
(`flashinfer.deep_gemm.m_grouped_fp8_gemm_nt_masked_sm10x`) are mixed.
The geomean over 56 shapes is 1.022, but the median is 0.986. Of the 56
rows, 18 are faster, 11 are at parity and 27 are slower. Speedups range
from 0.825 to 1.499. The gains come mostly from (128, 512), with a
geomean of 1.091 and 3 rows below 0.98. The geomean for (512, 128) is
1.024 with 8 rows below 0.98, and (7168, 2048) is roughly even at 1.002
with 7 rows below. (4096, 7168) is slower overall at 0.976, with 9 rows
below 0.98. At the extremes, `b128_m128_n128_k512` takes 19.34 µs on
Cake vs 28.99 µs on DeepGEMM (1.499), and `b1_m256_n4096_k7168` takes
18.16 µs vs 14.98 µs (0.825).

baseline is `m_grouped_fp8_gemm_nt_masked_sm10x`, timed as the kernel
only with its scale transform moved outside the timed region, on the
same GPU. Measured on NVIDIA R200 (`sm_107a`, 216 SMs), driver
615.71.10, CUDA 13.4. Each value is the median over paired timing
windows.*

Cake batch DeepGEMM FP8 now ships on sm_100a and sm_103a (float32 and
packed UE8M0 scales, 8 `(n, k)` pairs, unchanged by this PR) and on
sm_107a (float32 scales, 4 `(n, k)` pairs), and DeepGEMM remains the
default backend on every architecture.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added Cake batched FP8 matrix multiplication support for SM107a across
four supported `(N, K)` configurations, using float32 scales.
* Added architecture-specific geometry selection and dispatch while
preserving existing SM100a and SM103a routes.
* **Bug Fixes**
* Packed UE8M0 scales are now rejected on unsupported architectures,
with guidance to use float32 scales.
* **Tests**
* Expanded coverage for SM107a geometry support, dispatch boundaries,
repeated launches, and output comparisons.

### [7b23dee](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7b23deef3b118479a624956c1e7f7459cdd0de43)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T20:04:23Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion): deferred two-shot programs with a shared expert at world size 4 (#8697)

This PR adds 4 deferred two-shot shared programs to
`cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion` at world size 4 (2 data types x 2
epilogues). A deferred two-shot shared program uses the same protocol,
workspace, cross-rank exchange and summation order as the deferred
two-shot program. It produces the same outputs. In each token step, it
prefetches the shared-expert row into L2 before the route loop. It then
reads that row through the read-only non-coherent path. At world size 4,
a batch of 1536 tokens or more runs the deferred two-shot program. When
the call has a shared expert, that batch now runs the deferred two-shot
shared program. The choice depends only on the token count, the world
size and whether the call has a shared expert. `small_token_max` does
not change it. World sizes 2 and 8, and calls without a shared expert,
do not change.

The kernel fuses MoE finalize, the all-reduce across the ranks of one
NVLink node, the residual add and RMSNorm at hidden size 7168. MoE
finalize uses the top-k expert rows with their routing scale, plus an
optional shared-expert row. The entry point is
`flashinfer.comm.allreduce_fusion(..., moe_finalize_backend="cake")`.
The kernel has no other Cake variants. It ships only in this fused form
and covers sm_100a and sm_103a. With this PR, it has 56 programs per
architecture (52 before): 2 data types (fp16, bf16) x 2 epilogues
(BF16/FP16 output, packed NVFP4 output) x 14 program kinds. World size 2
has small-token, persistent, quad-route and large-token programs. World
size 4 has small-token, persistent, two-shot, two-shot early, deferred
two-shot and deferred two-shot shared programs. World size 8 has
small-token, two-shot, two-shot early and deferred two-shot programs.

The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main (PR #8503).
In the tables, this PR changes the program of the 16 shapes with 2048
tokens at world size 4 and a shared expert. These rows show the token
count in bold. Their geomean speedup is 1.028x on B300 (min 1.022x, max
1.037x) and 1.030x on B200 (min 1.023x, max 1.036x). The other 704
shapes run the same program in both versions. Their geomean is 1.001x on
B300 (min 0.976x, max 1.033x) and 1.000x on B200 (min 0.985x, max
1.016x). Over all 720 shapes in the tables, the geomean is 1.002x on
B300 and 1.001x on B200.

In the owner shape list, 2048 is the only token count at world size 4
that is 1536 or more. The data also include a second, independent
measurement of each of the 16 changed shapes. Over all 32 measurements
of changed shapes, the geomean speedup is 1.028x on B300 (min 1.022x)
and 1.030x on B200 (min 1.023x). None of them measures below 1.000 on
either GPU. Per program, the geomean speedup on B300 / B200 is 1.026x /
1.029x for bf16 with BF16 output, 1.025x / 1.028x for bf16 with NVFP4
output, 1.031x / 1.031x for fp16 with FP16 output and 1.029x / 1.031x
for fp16 with NVFP4 output.

The tables below give one row per shape of the owner shape list. The
measurements ran on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103a) and NVIDIA B200
(sm_100a) with CUDA 13.4 and the default `small_token_max` of 64. The
previous and this-PR columns give the median CUPTI kernel time in
microseconds, taking the minimum over ranks. Speedup is the median of
paired previous/this-PR ratios from interleaved runs, with its 95%
bootstrap confidence interval. So the speedup of some rows differs
slightly from the ratio of the two median times. Values above 1 mean
this PR is faster. In the flag columns (PDL, NVFP4 out, shared expert),
1 means yes and 0 means no. A token count in bold marks a shape whose
program this PR changes.

### [6b37c64](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6b37c64150419dba2f3582c18fc7726d20e70edb)

- **作者**: Vivian Chen NV
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T19:53:50Z
- **提交信息**: feat(quantization): validate-once launcher for the NVFP4 KV materializer (#8057)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`nvfp4_kv_materialize_fp8` (#6445) converts the active NVFP4 KV pages to
FP8 so that the FP8 context kernel can run at head_dim 512. Serving
frameworks call it once per layer per prefill step, eagerly, always with
the same layout. On every call, the function:

- binds its arguments and queries the compute capability
(`@backend_requirement`);
- runs about 30 shape, stride and alignment checks;
- allocates the output block table with `torch.zeros`.

That host time is several times the launch itself. It is paid on every
layer and adds to TTFT at small batch. Today the only way around it is
to call the private `_get_compiled_kernel` and `_BLOCKS_PER_SM`.

This PR adds `NVFP4KVMaterializer` in `flashinfer.quantization.kernels`:

- **Constructor:** validates the static layout (`num_kv_heads`,
`page_size`, `head_dim`, device, shared or separate K/V page indices),
checks the compute capability, and compiles or loads the kernel.
Compiling here means the first `run()` can already be graph-captured.
- **`run()`:** takes the per-step tensors plus caller-owned `out` and
`fp8_block_tables`, does three O(1) shape checks, and launches the same
cached kernel as the function.
- The compiled TVM-FFI launcher still rejects wrong dtypes, ranks, inner
strides, misalignment and mismatched shared extents. That covers wrong
heads, page size or head_dim, a CPU tensor, and a non-contiguous table.
- `run()` allocates nothing, never syncs, and launches on the current
stream, so it is CUDA-graph safe.
- `out` may be larger than the step needs (one workspace sized for the
largest step), so a captured graph can replay with new lengths, page ids
and `kv_page_indptr`. The kernel reads `kv_page_indptr[-1]` on the
device and stops there, so pages past it are neither written nor
visited.

`nvfp4_kv_materialize_fp8` is unchanged.

```python
from flashinfer.quantization.kernels import NVFP4KVMaterializer

materializer = NVFP4KVMaterializer(num_kv_heads, page_size, head_dim)  # once

# Per step: the same workspace and one zeroed table, shared by every layer.
fp8_block_tables.zero_()
for layer in layers:
    kv_fp8, tables = materializer.run(
        k_cache, v_cache, k_block_scales, v_block_scales,
        block_tables, seq_lens, kv_page_indptr,
        out=workspace, fp8_block_tables=fp8_block_tables,
    )
```

`run()` writes only each request's active block-table entries, as the
kernel already did. The function got zeros elsewhere from its own
`torch.zeros`. With `run()`, the caller zero-fills the table when it
needs zeros there: once per step is enough, because every layer writes
the same entries.

**Why a class rather than extending the function:** most of the cost is
the decorator and the body checks, not the allocation. The capability,
head_dim, page size and kernel lookup are fixed for the life of a model.
This matches FlashInfer's validate-once / run-many objects such as
`PrimsTSBatchDecodePlan` and the attention wrappers. Extending
`skip_check` to skip the body checks as well would still pay the
decorator, the kernel lookup and the default `kv_page_indptr` allocation
on every call.

**Host time per call** (B300, torch 2.13, page 64, kv_len 1024 per
request, compact `kv_page_indptr`, caller workspace). Each figure is the
median over 80 chunks of 25 back-to-back calls, with the clock stopped
before the sync.

| head_dim | KV heads | batch | function (µs) | function,
`skip_check=True` (µs) | `NVFP4KVMaterializer.run` (µs) | compiled
launcher alone (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 8 | 1 | 18.6 | 14.9 | 4.3 | 3.5 |
| 256 | 8 | 8 | 18.5 | 15.1 | 4.3 | 3.5 |
| 512 | 2 | 1 | 18.5 | 15.0 | 4.4 | 3.5 |
| 512 | 2 | 8 | 18.6 | 15.1 | 4.4 | 3.5 |

`run()` cuts the per-layer host time from about 18.5 µs to about 4.4 µs,
within about 1 µs of the bare compiled launcher. GPU work is unchanged:
it is the same kernel with the same grid.

**GPU time per call** (B300, page 64, compact `kv_page_indptr`; 20 calls
in one CUDA graph × 20 replays, median of 15 trials). An exact-size
`out` has `kv_page_indptr[-1] + 1` pages, just what the step needs. A
32k-page `out` is one 32768-page workspace sized for the largest step
and reused across steps. Exact-size times are the same before and after
this fix.

| head_dim / KV heads | kv_len | batch | live pages | exact-size `out`
(µs) | 32k-page `out`, before this fix (µs) | 32k-page `out`, with this
fix (µs) | with this fix vs exact-size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 / 8 | 1024 | 1 | 17 | 7.61 | 35.19 | 7.69 | 1.01x |
| 256 / 8 | 1024 | 8 | 129 | 8.40 | 102.78 | 14.13 | 1.68x |
| 256 / 8 | 1024 | 32 | 513 | 39.88 | 166.71 | 39.85 | 1.00x |
| 256 / 8 | 8192 | 1 | 129 | 8.00 | 41.17 | 13.69 | 1.71x |
| 256 / 8 | 8192 | 8 | 1025 | 74.82 | 159.27 | 75.45 | 1.01x |
| 256 / 8 | 8192 | 32 | 4097 | 273.06 | 382.81 | 273.80 | 1.00x |
| 512 / 2 | 1024 | 1 | 17 | 5.05 | 32.82 | 5.23 | 1.04x |
| 512 / 2 | 1024 | 8 | 129 | 5.64 | 97.42 | 8.63 | 1.53x |
| 512 / 2 | 1024 | 32 | 513 | 19.85 | 147.11 | 19.65 | 0.99x |
| 512 / 2 | 8192 | 1 | 129 | 5.23 | 35.80 | 8.20 | 1.57x |
| 512 / 2 | 8192 | 8 | 1025 | 38.76 | 123.58 | 38.73 | 1.00x |
| 512 / 2 | 8192 | 32 | 4097 | 137.70 | 248.69 | 137.58 | 1.00x |

The 129-page rows are still slower because a large `out` still launches
the full 296-CTA grid.

### [bb78b38](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/bb78b38f02354a4bb14f55ca22f3bd44295b264a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T19:51:24Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_grouped_fp8_gemm): earlier next-tile prefetch and two more small-block UE8M0 routes on SM100a/SM103a (#8694)

This PR changes only the block-scaled UE8M0 swap-AB small-M routes of
the Cake prepared contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM
(`flashinfer.gemm.prepare_group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise_contiguous`) on
SM100a and SM103a. The 64-row-block swap-AB programs now prefetch the
next tile's expert-index entries earlier, which affects the bm64 rows on
GB300. Two more layouts now use the small-block route:
`b3_a64_n1024_k512_p28` on SM100a and `b4_a32_n1024_k256_u6_g8` on
SM103a. Two existing programs are renamed, and their machine code is
byte-identical. Output bits do not change because every route applies
the same K order.

There are only a few gains, and they are small. Four of the 59 rows
improve, the other 55 show no real change, and no row is slower beyond
its noise. On B200, `b3_a64_n1024_k512_p28` goes from 4.896 to 4.767 µs
(1.027). `b3_a32_n4096_k4096_p48` (1.003) and `sw_a32_n1024_k256_u48`
(1.005) read slightly faster, but their machine code is identical, so
that difference is noise. On the faster-class GB300,
`b4_a32_n1024_k256_u6_g8` goes from 4.472 to 4.288 µs (1.037) and
`b4_a64_n1024_k1024_u12_g8` from 5.952 to 5.856 µs (1.016). On the
slower-class GB300, `sw_a64_n1024_k1024_u32` goes from 5.952 to 5.840 µs
(1.015). On that GPU, `b4_a32_n1024_k256_u6_g8` reads 1.022, which is
still within its noise.

### [5fa2397](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5fa2397f9a21bb13abe59ec2b62b77a975e20203)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T19:43:48Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_nvfp4_ptilemax_attention): add the SM103 NVFP4 per-tile-max attention as a separate API (#8693)

This PR adds the experimental package `cake_nvfp4_ptilemax_attention`
(entry point `flashinfer.prefill.prepare_nvfp4_ptilemax_attention`), the
dense NVFP4 attention forward (E2M1 Q, K and V, E4M3 scales per 16
values, BF16 output, head dimension 128) whose probability scales reuse
each score tile's maximum. Of the kernel's seven Cake builds
(per-tile-max or per-16-value probability scales, causal or noncausal,
with or without KV-tail masking, sm_100a or sm_103a), this PR delivers
the sm_103a (GB300) noncausal per-tile-max build without KV-tail
masking, for sequence lengths divisible by 512. The baseline is
`cake_nvfp4_attention_aeef857fb82e9e29a633`, the previous Cake SM103
program of this kernel, from #7328. GB300 speedup (baseline latency /
this PR's latency, same GPU) is 1.031x and 1.027x on the 512-token
shape, 1.003x to 1.006x on the 4096- and 8192-token shapes, 1.001x on
the 32768-token shape, and 1.006x on GPU 1 and parity on GPU 2 (1.001x;
2 of 8 groups not faster) on the 1024-token shape.

**NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4: two GPUs on two nodes;
latency = median of 8 interleaved groups of the CUPTI kernel time with a
cold L2**

| Shape | GPU 1: previous (µs) | GPU 1: this PR (µs) | GPU 1 speedup |
GPU 2: previous (µs) | GPU 2: this PR (µs) | GPU 2 speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| batch 4, 8 heads, 4096 tokens | 109.30 | 108.78 | 1.005x | 109.49 |
108.86 | 1.006x |
| batch 1, 8 heads, 32768 tokens | 1419.05 | 1417.72 | 1.001x | 1420.90
| 1419.02 | 1.001x |
| batch 8, 32 heads, 8192 tokens | 2754.54 | 2745.61 | 1.003x | 2759.49
| 2751.23 | 1.003x |
| batch 10, 16 heads, 512 tokens | 18.05 | 17.51 | 1.031x | 18.25 |
17.78 | 1.027x |
| batch 2, 40 heads, 1024 tokens | 26.67 | 26.50 | 1.006x | 26.97 |
26.94 | 1.001x |

Cake ships no other variant of this kernel in FlashInfer (the
per-16-value, causal, KV-tail and sm_100a builds are not exported), and
this family ships on sm_103a only.

### [74e87ce](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/74e87cef589c9c0523d1b481d37b0035f7e8313e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T19:41:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): per-architecture floor of the zero-gradient row skip, lighter log-prob backward host path (#8687)

Cake's chunked LM-head + loss training backend has a non-deterministic
(ND) form, `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss` with
`deterministic=False`. It serves cross-entropy loss and log-probability
with no temperature, a scalar temperature or a per-token FP32 `[T]`
temperature. On FlashInfer main (#8612), the ND log-probability backward
skips rows whose dlogp is zero in one-chunk calls only from 4097 valid
rows. This PR makes that threshold a per-architecture default
(`ZERO_DLOGP_MIN_ROWS_ARCH_DEFAULT`, resolved by
`zero_dlogp_min_rows(device)`). The skip now also covers one-chunk calls
from 1946 valid rows on sm_100a and from 3891 on sm_103a; sm_107a keeps
4097. Each backward call also does less host work: scratch slots are set
up only for bound names, and the backward reuses the forward problem.
The cells whose path changes are one-chunk calls at T = 2048 and 4096 on
B200 and T = 4096 on GB300, with no temperature and per-token
temperature, for bwd, fwd+bwd and ckpt. In those cells the new ND vs the
previous ND is 1.2168x-1.7700x on B200 / 1.2840x-1.7056x on GB300 at z =
0.5, 1.0364x-1.1546x / 1.0646x-1.1393x at z = 0.166, and 0.9904x-1.0088x
/ 0.9919x-1.0018x at z = 0 (no zero-dlogp valid rows). Every z > 0 cell
is ND faster (48 of 72 / 24 of 36), every z = 0 cell is at parity or
inconclusive, and none is ND slower. Vs deterministic Cake the same
cells are 1.2147x-1.7630x / 1.2800x-1.7112x at z = 0.5, 1.0346x-1.1563x
/ 1.0694x-1.1364x at z = 0.166 and 0.9828x-1.0059x / 0.9915x-1.0024x at
z = 0, with the same verdict pattern. Vs the strongest non-Cake
baseline, per-token temperature (PyTorch chunked + torch.compile) is
1.0685x-1.9307x / 1.0786x-1.8714x: ND faster in 35 of 36 / 18 of 18
cells, with 1 B200 cell inconclusive. With no temperature, vs Cut
Cross-Entropy on B200 the range is 0.7509x-1.3122x. The new ND is faster
in all 12 z = 0.5 cells and 1 z = 0.166 cell, slower in all 12 z = 0
cells (down to 0.7509x) and in 8 of 12 z = 0.166 cells, and inconclusive
in 3. On GB300 the range is 0.7661x-1.2918x and all 18 cells are
inconclusive, with point estimates below 1 in 10 of them; Cut
Cross-Entropy was timed on only 2 of the 3 steps there (†). This gap
already exists on main: the previous ND column is also slower than Cut
Cross-Entropy in the same cells. Cut Cross-Entropy keeps the full T x V
logits while the ND default bounds memory by chunks, and this PR does
not change that. Outside the changed range the code path is the same as
on main. The representative rows are at parity or inconclusive vs the
previous ND: 0.9958x-1.0094x on B200, 0.9933x-1.0153x on GB300 and
0.9932x-1.0103x on R200. R200 has no changed cell. The full sweep covers
293 cells on B200 and R200 and 188 on GB300 (plus 105 single-cluster
no-temperature cells there, ‡), including fwd cells (the threshold gates
only the backward) and scalar temperature. In it, no verdict vs the
previous ND or vs deterministic Cake is ND slower. Vs the non-Cake
baseline, the ND slower verdicts are 89 of 147 no-temperature cells on
B200 and 62 of 147 on R200, all vs Cut Cross-Entropy, plus, on GB300, 57
of the 105 single-cluster no-temperature cells (‡, all vs Cut
Cross-Entropy) and 2 of 119 per-token cells.

**B200 sm_100a.** NVIDIA B200, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07, CUDA 13.0
runtime (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130), kernels built with nvcc 13.4; H=6144,
V=154880, BF16; p 15 steps / 6 nodes, h 12 steps / 6 nodes, s 3 steps /
3 nodes. New ND floor 1946 valid rows (previous ND: 4097). Modes: p =
log-prob, h = log-prob with per-token temperature, s = log-prob with
scalar temperature 0.7. Operations: bwd = backward, fwd+bwd = forward +
backward, ckpt 2xfwd+bwd = checkpointed 2x forward + backward. States:
cooled, d1 = after an idle gap. z = fraction of valid rows whose dlogp
is 0. Latency = median over steps of the per-step median CUPTI GPU span,
L2 flushed; speedup = baseline latency / new ND latency (> 1: new ND
faster); CI95 = hierarchical bootstrap; 'ND faster' / 'ND slower' only
when the CI95 lies wholly outside 1 ± max(1 %, A/A floor) and every step
agrees, with >= 3 steps on >= 2 nodes. SOTA peers: b1c = PyTorch chunked
+ torch.compile; ccetc = Cut Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 (torch.compile path).

Cells whose code path this PR changes (one-chunk rows with 1946 <= valid
rows < 4097): 72

**GB300 sm_103a.** NVIDIA GB300, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03 /
580.167.08, CUDA 13.0 runtime (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130), kernels built with
nvcc 13.4; H=6144, V=154880, BF16; nodes from two clusters: p 3 steps /
3 nodes, h 12 steps / 3 nodes, s 3 steps / 3 nodes (p rows above T=4096:
4 steps / 2 nodes of one cluster, ‡). New ND floor 3891 valid rows
(previous ND: 4097); rows below 3891 valid rows show the path this PR
runs there (zero-gradient row skip off), rows at or above it the skip
on. The Cut Cross-Entropy (ccetc) timings in the p rows come from one
cluster's nodes only (†, ‡). Modes: p = log-prob, h = log-prob with
per-token temperature, s = log-prob with scalar temperature 0.7.
Operations: bwd = backward, fwd+bwd = forward + backward, ckpt 2xfwd+bwd
= checkpointed 2x forward + backward. States: cooled, d1 = after an idle
gap. z = fraction of valid rows whose dlogp is 0. Latency = median over
steps of the per-step median CUPTI GPU span, L2 flushed; speedup =
baseline latency / new ND latency (> 1: new ND faster); CI95 =
hierarchical bootstrap; 'ND faster' / 'ND slower' only when the CI95
lies wholly outside 1 ± max(1 %, A/A floor) and every step agrees, with
>= 3 steps on >= 2 nodes. SOTA peers: b1c = PyTorch chunked +
torch.compile; ccetc = Cut Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 (torch.compile path).

**R200 sm_107a.** R200 (device name 'NVIDIA Graphics Device'), 212 SMs,
driver 620.43, CUDA 13.0 runtime (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130), kernels built
with nvcc 13.4; H=6144, V=154880, BF16; p 20 steps / 2 nodes, h 16 steps
/ 2 nodes, s 4 steps / 2 nodes. ND floor 4097 valid rows, unchanged from
the previous ND. Modes: p = log-prob, h = log-prob with per-token
temperature, s = log-prob with scalar temperature 0.7. Operations: bwd =
backward, fwd+bwd = forward + backward, ckpt 2xfwd+bwd = checkpointed 2x
forward + backward. States: cooled, d1 = after an idle gap. z = fraction
of valid rows whose dlogp is 0. Latency = median over steps of the
per-step median CUPTI GPU span, L2 flushed; speedup = baseline latency /
new ND latency (> 1: new ND faster); CI95 = hierarchical bootstrap; 'ND
faster' / 'ND slower' only when the CI95 lies wholly outside 1 ± max(1
%, A/A floor) and every step agrees, with >= 3 steps on >= 2 nodes. SOTA
peers: b1c = PyTorch chunked + torch.compile; ccetc = Cut Cross-Entropy
25.1.1 (torch.compile path).

No cell changes its code path on R200 sm_107a: the head keeps the
previous floor 4097 here.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Zero-gradient log-probability backward skipping now uses
architecture-specific row thresholds: 1,946 rows on `sm_100a`, 3,891 on
`sm_103a`, and 4,097 on other architectures.
* You can set a custom threshold for all architectures or disable
skipping. Resetting the setting restores architecture-specific defaults;
querying without a device reports the generic 4,097-row threshold.
* **Documentation**
* Updated guidance describes the thresholds, one-chunk behavior,
potential gradient differences, and additional memory use.

### [0323b5d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0323b5dc9b3cc3704bf7b142de3f378febb0ff42)

- **作者**: Jonathan Dierksen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T19:30:11Z
- **提交信息**: ci(docker): split the CI image pip install into torch, deps and cuDNN layers (#7899)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Splits the single 4.8 GB pip layer of the `flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu*`
image into three layers, most stable first, by giving
`docker/install/install_python_packages.sh` a stage argument (`torch`,
`deps`, `cudnn`, default `all`) and running it once per stage in
`docker/Dockerfile.ci`:

1. `torch`: pip/setuptools, torch and the CUDA wheels it pulls in, plus
an early CUDA-version check.
2. `deps`: `requirements.txt`, test/build deps, cuda-python (incl. the
cu134 special case), nvshmem4py, `CI_IMAGE_DEPENDENCIES` pins, cuda-tile
compiler for cu13 < 13.4.
3. `cudnn`: the cuDNN override and the final version/backend assertions.

Why: a `cudnn_version` or requirements bump currently invalidates and
re-pulls the whole 4.8 GB layer, and the last big layer's unpack
dominates pull time on PR AOT runners (~3.5 of ~5 min in run
40929394275). All existing guarantees are kept: the `PIP_CONSTRAINT`
torch pin is rebuilt from the installed torch in each stage, and the
CUDA major/minor and cuDNN checks are unchanged.

Also sets `PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1` inside the script; the old script did not
disable the pip cache, so it was very likely baked into the layer (not
confirmed without an image).

Caveats:
- **Not built locally** (no Docker available); the three variants are
exercised only by this PR's `release-ci-docker` build.
- The `cudnn` layer duplicates the cuDNN 9.20 that torch pulls into
layer 1, so total size may grow by about one cuDNN wheel, partly offset
by dropping the pip cache.
- Whether unpack is gunzip-CPU or EBS bound is unverified; no pull-time
speedup is claimed. It must be measured on a runner after the next image
release.
- zstd layer compression is not enabled: the workflow uses `load: true`
plus `docker push`, and the runners' Docker version support is
unchecked. Follow-up.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
* CI image setup now installs PyTorch, other Python dependencies, and
cuDNN in separate stages. Stages can be selected individually or run
together, and invalid stage selections return an error.
* The PyTorch stage verifies that the installed CUDA version matches the
requested version. The cuDNN stage validates its configuration and the
final CUDA/cuDNN setup.
* CI checks now verify the stage order and the placement of build
inputs. These changes affect CI image builds; no end-user-facing changes
are included.

### [01e0531](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/01e05310d5b30a21b021e24afc9041afc481ad3d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T19:13:59Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dense_projection_gemm): route K1 entries that fail the accuracy rule to the deterministic program (#8671)

The K1 weight-gradient GEMM in
`flashinfer/experimental/dense_projection_gemm` (`deterministic=False`)
picks a split-K program for each row, token count and SM count. Every
entry must pass an accuracy rule against an FP64 reference. For each
seed, the entry's relative Frobenius error must be at most 1.02 times
the deterministic program's error. The deterministic program is the
deterministic package's plan of the same GEMM, and this package already
runs it for rows that have no entry. When both programs miss the BF16
error budget on BF16 output, the rule uses at least 10 seeds whose
outputs differ bitwise. Over those seeds, the pooled median of (entry
budget ratio / deterministic budget ratio) must be at most 1.02, and no
single ratio may exceed 1.30. Entries that fail the rule now run the
deterministic program. Every other entry passed and is unchanged. This
includes 5120 -> 1024 with BF16 output above 65536 tokens on sm_107a
parts with 216 or more SMs (measured with that plan on 212-SM parts),
whose output was bitwise identical to the deterministic program's on all
10 seeds.

### What failed and the new route

Each point was measured with 5 to 10 seeds.

- **sm_107a, FP32 output, one-split rows 4096 / 5120 -> 512 / 1024:**
from 961 tokens the deterministic plan splits K two ways, and the
one-split program's error is 2.0 to 2.4 times larger. These rows now run
the deterministic program from 961 tokens on parts with 216 or more SMs,
and at 16172 to 16384 tokens on 208 / 212 SMs.
- **sm_107a, FP32, 8192 -> 128 two-split at odd K-block counts (64-token
blocks), 1025 to 8192 tokens:** the error is 1.04 to 1.14 times the
deterministic program's. These rows now run the deterministic program on
212 SMs and on 216 or more SMs.
- **sm_100a and sm_103a, FP32, two-split rows at odd K-block counts:**
the error is 1.02 to 1.15 times the deterministic program's. The
deterministic plan halves K per tile, so at an odd block count its cut
differs from the two-split program's. Affected rows are 4096 -> 32 / 48
/ 64 on sm_100a and 4096 -> 32 / 48 on sm_103a from 1025 tokens, and
5120 -> 32 / 48 on sm_100a from 12289 tokens. Odd block counts now run
the deterministic program, listed in the new table
`K1_SPLIT_ODD_BLOCK_EXCLUDED_TOKENS`. Even block counts keep the
two-split program, whose output there is bitwise identical to the
deterministic program's.
- **BF16, large token counts (both programs miss the BF16 budget):** the
budget-ratio cap was exceeded, at 1.30 to 1.73 times. On sm_100a, 4096
-> 64 also had a pooled median of 1.04. Affected rows on sm_100a are
4096 -> 48 and 5120 -> 48 from 49153 tokens, 4096 -> 32 from 65536, 4096
-> 64 from 65536 on 152 SMs, and 5120 -> 32 from 65537. On sm_103a, 4096
-> 32 / 48 are affected on 152 SMs above 65536 tokens, for both BF16 and
FP32. All of these now run the deterministic program.

The docs said the forward has no cross-CTA reduction, but the
deterministic plan's automatic two-way split adds the partials in a
fixed order; the docs now say so.

### Cost

The new routes are slower than the previous (failing) entries. The rest
of this paragraph covers B200, B300, GB200 and GB300. The FP32 weight
gradient at 4097 tokens goes from 12.3-12.7 us to 17.8-19.7 us (40-60 %
slower on all four GPUs) and is 7-12 % slower at 16173 to 65537 tokens;
bwd is 22-34 % slower at 4097 tokens and 3-8 % slower at 16173 to 65537,
ckpt is 10-13 % and 1-4 % slower, and at 98304 tokens the difference is
within -1 % to +4 %. Against the library (CUDA graph), this PR is slower
at 4097 tokens (SOTA / this PR 0.55-0.59 wgrad, 0.64-0.68 bwd, 0.61-0.62
ckpt); at 16173 tokens and above it is faster in the weight gradient
(1.01-1.10) and within 0.98-1.06 on whole steps.

On R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), the times below are CUDA graph replay with
FP32 output; the table also has eager. Each factor is this PR's time
divided by the previous route's. The weight gradient for 4096 -> 512
goes from 36.7-37.1 us to 75.2-82.0 us (2.03-2.23x), and for 5120 -> 512
from 39.2-39.5 us to 76.0-83.2 us (1.92-2.12x). For 4096 -> 1024 it goes
from 54.9 us to 88.0 us at 16172 tokens (1.60x) and from 56.4 us to 59.4
us at 16384 tokens (1.05x). For 5120 -> 1024 it goes from 66.7-67.6 us
to 83.5-97.7 us (1.24-1.46x). For 8192 -> 128 it goes from 9.7 us to
15.3 us at 1025 tokens (1.58x), from 14.2 us to 20.3 us at 4097 (1.43x),
and from 20.1 us to 21.7 us at 8128 (1.08x). bwd takes 1.03-1.68x the
previous time and ckpt takes 1.01-1.35x. The largest increase is on 4096
-> 512 (1.56-1.68x bwd, 1.29-1.35x ckpt). The library (CUDA graph) is
faster than this PR on every R200 row: SOTA / this PR is 0.35-0.88
wgrad, 0.43-0.91 bwd and 0.44-0.94 ckpt.

- **Columns:** `deterministic us` is the deterministic program (first
baseline). `previous route us` is this package before this PR (the entry
that failed the rule). `this PR us` is this package after this PR, which
runs the deterministic program on these rows. `library SOTA us` is the
second baseline. Each time cell is eager / CUDA graph. In `det / this
PR` and `SOTA / this PR`, a value above 1 means this PR is faster.
- **op:** wgrad is the weight-gradient GEMM, the only op whose route
changes. bwd is input gradient + weight gradient. ckpt is 2 x forward +
input gradient + weight gradient (an activation-checkpointed step). The
forward and input-gradient GEMMs do not change.
- **Library SOTA:** the fastest correct launch among `torch.mm` (cuBLAS
13.8.0) and the top 8 cuBLASLt 13.8.0 heuristic algorithms for the same
operands and output dtype, with FP32 compute. A launch is correct if its
FP64 relative Frobenius error is <= 1e-3 (FP32 output) or <= 2e-2 (BF16
output). In bwd and ckpt, each op uses its own fastest library launch,
picked on the device by CUDA event timing (eager) or graph-replay timing
(graph). It is the strongest applicable baseline because it is the
vendor library's own candidate set for these exact shapes, with the
fastest correct algorithm chosen per shape on the measured GPU.
- **Timing:** CUPTI kernel timestamps. An op's time runs from when the
first kernel begins to when the last kernel ends across the launches in
the call. L2 is cold, flushed twice before every timed iteration. Each
cell uses 9 paired groups x 20 timed iterations, with arms interleaved
in a seeded random order, and takes the median per run. Each GPU type
ran 4 independent processes on separate GPUs of one node: two ran all
rows, and two ran one row per process. The reported value is the median
of the 4 run medians, for both eager and CUDA-graph replay.
- **A/A noise:** on these rows the deterministic arm and this PR run the
same program. det / this PR ranges from 0.970 to 1.014 over all 96 cells
(B200 0.984-1.014, B300 0.970-1.010, GB200 0.994-1.009, GB300
0.996-1.004). On R200 it ranges from 0.965 to 1.041 over 72 cells.
- **GPUs:** B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07), GB200 (sm_100a,
152 SMs, driver 580.126.20), B300 (sm_103a, 148 SMs, driver 580.126.09),
GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03), R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs,
driver 620.43). Software: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0 runtime, CUDA
13.4 driver API, cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.8.0. R200 uses the CUDA 13.5
driver API; its PyTorch, CUDA runtime and cuBLAS / cuBLASLt versions are
the same.
- **B200 and R200 power cap:** nvidia-smi showed the software power cap
active in about 10 % of 2-second samples on each B200. On each R200 it
was active in 8 to 11 of 109 samples (about 10 %, like the B200s). On
the other GPUs it was active in at most 1 sample.
- **GB200 / GB300 at 4097 tokens:** the library's eager bwd / ckpt times
include host launch gaps (eager ckpt 64-65 us, graph 34-35 us).

### [2c9bab5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2c9bab5e662b186840e8b02b129eb8c4898659f2)

- **作者**: Anerudhan Gopal
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T19:01:49Z
- **提交信息**: feat(prefill): teach the cuDNN ragged path sliding window, attention sinks and scalar scales (#5286)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Follow-up to #5133. cuDNN's SDPA supports sliding window, attention
sinks and fp8 scales; the wrapper's cuDNN branch simply never handed
them over, so `backend="auto"` was routing sliding-window and sink calls
*past* a backend that can serve them, and a scalar scale died on a type
mismatch.

**Sliding window** — mapped onto cuDNN's `diagonal_band_left_bound`. The
two libraries count the band differently and the conversion was
**measured, not assumed**: FlashInfer's `window_left = W` admits `W + 1`
keys including the diagonal, cuDNN's `diagonal_band_left_bound = L`
admits `L`. Calibrating `L` against a reference at `W-1 / W / W+1` shows
`W + 1` is the match:

| cuDNN bound | vs band `[qi-(L-1), qi]` | vs `[qi-L, qi]` | vs
`[qi-(L+1), qi]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| L=8 | **rel 0.0021** | 0.684 | 0.682 |
| L=32 | **rel 0.0021** | 0.354 | 0.352 |

Passing `W` through unchanged drops the oldest key of every window — an
error that survives a smoke test and quietly degrades quality, so it is
pinned by a test.

**Attention sinks** — bound to the SDPA `sink_token` input under a new
UID. The wrapper's cuDNN branch no longer refuses when `_sinks` is set
(vLLM's metadata builder stashes them there).

**Scalar scales** — `run()` advertises `q_scale: Optional[float]` and
forwards it unchanged to a cuDNN call typed `Optional[torch.Tensor]`, so
a float reached the variant pack and failed with `Object does not have
the __dlpack__() method`. Scalars are normalised to the 1×1×1×1 fp32
tensor cuDNN expects, memoised per `(value, device)` to keep the
conversion off the hot path.

`auto` eligibility splits accordingly: sliding window and sinks move out
of the universal disqualifier list into a per-backend test, because
cuDNN builds both into its graph while the CUTLASS run path receives
only `causal` and the scales and would silently drop them. The graph
cache keys on the window bound and on sink presence, so neither shares a
graph with a plain causal call.

**fp8 stays off `auto` deliberately.** The scale fix means an explicit
`backend="cudnn"` fp8 call now runs, but the output is not yet validated
against a reference, and cuDNN's `sdpa_fp8` graph compile does not
terminate for rectangular head dims — `d_qk=192, d_vo=128` was killed at
>240 s at *every* size tried, down to b1/s128/h4, while every square
head dim compiles in under 1 s. The stale "scale handling lives on the
paths after it" rationale in the eligibility comment is corrected to say
this.

The second commit fixes a CUDA-graph guard that was too strict in #5133:
`fmha_varlen_plan` reallocates its work-index buffers per call, so a
graph captured against plan N is stranded by plan N+1 — but planning
once and *then* capturing is fine. The guard now fires only on the
re-plan. This matters beyond theory: the blanket form broke
`benchmarks/routines/attention.py`, which enables CUDA graphs and plans
once, making every explicit-CUTLASS benchmark row fail.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #5133 (merged). No issue filed yet for the cuDNN `sdpa_fp8`
rectangular-head-dim compile hang; happy to open one — it reproduces at
the smallest constructible shape.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit`
(or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files`
and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

**174 passed, 1 xfailed** on B200 (cc 10.0), CUDA 13.4, cuDNN 9.26.0 /
frontend 1.29.0 — `tests/attention/test_auto_backend_upgrade.py` plus
`tests/attention/test_cudnn_prefill_token_indptr.py`.

FA2 in this wrapper consumes neither window nor sinks (only `fmha_v2`
reads `_sinks`), so there is no in-tree kernel to diff against; the new
numerics tests compare against a PyTorch reference written from the
definitions. All within ~0.5% relative:

| case | relative error |
|---|---|
| causal only (reference sanity) | 0.0018 |
| `window_left=16` | 0.0019 |
| `window_left=64` | 0.0018 |
| sinks | 0.0051 |
| window=32 + sinks | 0.0051 |

Plus: scalar scales accepted on the cuDNN path; CUTLASS
first-plan-under-capture resolves and the re-plan routes to fa2 /
raises. Four tests from #5133 asserted the old "auto declines
window/sinks" policy and now encode the new one, with CUTLASS still
required to stay out of both.

## Reviewer Notes

- The window off-by-one is the part most worth a second opinion — it is
a measured mapping, and getting it wrong is silent rather than loud.
- The `auto` eligibility split is deliberate: a condition belongs in the
per-backend branch when *some* backend can serve it, and in the
universal list only when none can. `logits_soft_cap` and custom masks
stay universal.
- Rebased onto current `main`; the `_build_prefill_graph` call collided
with the new `graph_kwargs()` helper, so `window_left`/`sinks` are
threaded through that helper rather than the call site, keeping the
graph build and the cache-key call from drifting.

### [a6e770e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a6e770e98d305ce169383d6d3229b5f4e99b3435)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T18:43:42Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): plan the 17408 -> 5120 forward in 12-column-tile raster groups at T 16231 / 16384 on sm_100a and sm_103a (#8686)

This PR adds row rules to the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package
in `flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM.
Most programs in the package are BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and
wgrad), and one is an FP32 router GEMM. The PR adds no new program,
kernel source or library. It adds 4 row rules: 2 for `sm_100a` and 2 for
`sm_103a`. Each rule applies at a single token count T, either 16231 or
16384. The rules cover the 17408→5120 forward (BF16 output). These rows
already run the overlapped half-tail program with a column-grouped
raster under the existing ragged rule on both architectures. That rule
puts 8 column tiles in each raster group. The new rules keep the same
program and the same K split, with the whole K per output tile. The only
change is the raster group size, which goes to 12 column tiles. The rule
count goes from 378 to 382 (`sm_100a` from 148 to 150, `sm_103a` from
105 to 107). The `sm_107a` rules are unchanged. The baseline is the
previous Cake version of the package on main. Against it, the changed
rows have a speedup of 1.008 on GB300 at both T. On GB200 they measure
1.005 at both T, which is a small gain. On B200 and B300 they measure
1.002 at both T, so they are essentially unchanged and within
measurement noise. No changed row is slower on any of the four GPUs.
Only the raster grouping changes, so outputs on those rows are bitwise
identical to main on all four. All other rows of the 294-row shape list
plan the same programs as main.

### [a2f011c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a2f011ccb75be84b976d19ee17b7cc3538915249)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T18:32:34Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_grouped_fp8_gemm): block-scaled contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM on SM107a (#8683)

Cake's prepared contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM is
`flashinfer.gemm.prepare_group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise_contiguous`, with
the same math contract as
`flashinfer.gemm.group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise_contiguous`. On SM100a and
SM103a it ships three variants: FP32-scale (promotion) programs,
block-scaled programs with packed UE8M0 scales, and a fused gate_up +
SwiGLU + FP8 quant form. This PR adds SM107a (compute capability 10.7)
with only the block-scaled UE8M0 variant. It uses four new generated
non-swapped routes: `bs_ue8m0_n128`, `bs_ue8m0_n256`,
`bs_ue8m0_n128_run32` and `bs_ue8m0_n256_run32`. These are built on the
SM107a K=64 block-scaled FP8 MMA, and one route keeps the K=32 form.
FP32 scales raise `NotImplementedError` on SM107a. The SM100a and SM103a
programs are unchanged.

The comparison baseline is FlashInfer's bundled DeepGEMM contiguous
grouped FP8 GEMM, and it does not run on SM107a for any of the 63 shapes
below. For some shapes its cubin is not registered for this
architecture. For others it hard-codes 128-row contiguous alignment, but
the shape uses 32-, 64- or 96-row alignment. FlashInfer main has no
SM107a path for this API, so there is no speedup ratio to report. The
table gives Cake's absolute times.

### [eafe29c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/eafe29c775df1ed115c5a18e502945528ef560c4)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T18:31:59Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP4 EP4 T512 / T1024 rank programs on sm_103a (#8682)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline for the 384-expert, top-6, hidden-5120 model with activation
clamp 10. A single kernel launch covers dispatch, FC1, clamped SwiGLU,
MXFP8 activation quantization, FC2 and weighted combine. The kernel has
four variants on main: single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8,
grouped-GEMM routes, and the TP/EP rank variant. The rank variant has 32
programs: TP4 EP1 (384 experts, width 640), TP8 EP1 (384 experts, width
384), TP4 EP4 (96 local experts, I2304) and TP8 EP8 (48 local experts,
I2304), each at 1 to 4096 tokens.

This PR updates the rank variant. It changes 2 of the 32 programs: TP4
EP4 at 512 and 1024 tokens. The combine walk now loads the next trip's
six token-to-permuted-row indices before it loads its own slots, so that
global-memory round trip overlaps the current chunk. Slot order, the
FP32 accumulation chain, the store slot and the stored bytes are
unchanged, and outputs are bitwise identical to the previous version.
The other 30 rank programs, the other variants' programs and every host
binding are byte-identical. The catalog closure hashes of the 2 changed
programs change.

Speedup over the previous Cake version (the rank variant on FlashInfer
main after #8669), for replicates a / b:

- TP4 EP4 at 512 tokens: 1.0005x / 1.0004x, saving 0.13 / 0.09 µs per
call. This is noise-level in this measurement.
- TP4 EP4 at 1024 tokens: 1.0013x / 1.0015x, saving 0.35 / 0.41 µs per
call.

The other 30 programs run 0.9992x to 1.0010x in replicate a and 0.9987x
to 1.0015x in replicate b.

Speedup over the issue baseline, autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`: this PR is faster on all 32 shapes
in both replicates. The range is 1.022x to 1.174x in replicate a and
1.017x to 1.172x in replicate b. On the two changed shapes it is 1.022x
/ 1.025x (512 tokens) and 1.031x / 1.031x (1024 tokens).

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.159.03, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. Columns 3-8 compare this PR with the previous Cake version
(FlashInfer main after #8669), with speedup = previous / this PR.
Per-call latency comes from CUDA-graph replays (20 calls per graph),
using the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous version and this
PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6 rounds. Each value is
the median of the 6 process medians. Columns a and b are two independent
replicates, each run alone on its own node. Speedups are computed from
the latencies before they were rounded to two decimals. They are shown
to 4 decimals for the 2 changed programs (bold) and to 3 decimals
elsewhere. The savings quoted above are the differences of the displayed
latencies. Each replicate also timed the previous version against itself
(an A/A control) to measure its noise band. The widest band is 0.13 % in
replicate a and 0.15 % in replicate b. The other 30 rank programs are
byte-identical between the two versions and compile to the same machine
code. Across both replicates, their ratios ranged from 0.9987 to 1.0015
and their latency moved by up to 0.31 µs. That is the run-to-run noise
envelope. Within it, TP8 EP1 at 1024 tokens (+0.056 / +0.033 µs) and TP4
EP4 at 16 tokens (+0.058 / +0.027 µs) read slower than their narrow A/A
bands in both replicates, and TP4 EP4 at 4096 tokens (-0.102 / -0.306
µs) reads faster in both. That is process-level noise, not a change. TP4
EP4 at 1024 tokens is outside the envelope in absolute time (0.35 / 0.41
µs saved) but not in ratio. TP4 EP4 at 512 tokens is inside the
envelope, so its 0.13 / 0.09 µs saving is noise-level in this
measurement. Columns 9-14 compare autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` with this PR, with speedup = TRT-LLM
/ this PR. They come from a separate run of the same kernel on the same
two nodes, so the this-PR latencies there differ slightly from columns 4
and 7.*

The other three variants (single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8
and grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a. The rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [658b1bd](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/658b1bd8ed37076b784d7ed3c7de5ba752872cda)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T18:26:23Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): SM107 short-query decode launches keep the K=64 uniform program past 128 rows (#8679)

The Cake backend of `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` has 49
programs: BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads
(several bodies per head count, picked per shape by the host route) and
an NVFP4-KV decode family. sm_107a ships six FP8 programs for the
DeepSeek-V4 decode route: the two 128-head persistent programs
(lane-issued gathers, uniform gathers), the K=64 sibling of the
uniform-gather program, the 64-head single-CTA M64 single-tile and
multi-tile programs, and the SWA low-head prefill program. This PR adds
no program. It changes only which existing sm_107a program the host
route picks. Before this PR, on sm_107a, FP8 128-head launches of at
least 128 query rows run the lane-issued gather program
`cake_dsv4_77fc7066e2ba5bebb062` (loader key
`fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent`). The uniform-gather route's K=64
program `cake_dsv4_7074d4c5b808db91fcba` (loader key
`fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent_uniform_k64`, added in #8668) runs
launches of 48 to 127 rows. With this PR, on sm_107a, decode launches of
at least 160 query rows keep the uniform-gather route when each request
holds one query row, or at most 2 from 256 rows, so the K=64 program
runs them. On calls that read the compress-ratio-4 cache (top-k 4x
layers, 64-row pages), the limit is at most 4 query rows per request, or
at most 8 from 256 rows. Every other launch of 128 rows or more keeps
the lane-issued program: prefill, longer requests, 128-159 rows, and
requests of 3 or more query rows on top-k 128x and SWA-only layers. The
window is bounded because outside it the K=64 program trailed the
lane-issued program (prefill, long requests, and some 4-query-row
launches on top-k 128x layers). sm_100a and sm_103a are unchanged.
