### [40f281b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/40f281b5c01a9133931c89d5f8f6d3c29367b63d)

- **作者**: Jonas Li
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T18:05:41Z
- **提交信息**: feat(kda): indexed state pool (ssm_state_indices) for the small-BH prefill backend (#8287)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`recurrent_kda(..., backend="small-bh")` now accepts
`ssm_state_indices`. It works the same way as the other prefill
backends' indexed-pool contract:

- `ssm_state_indices` is a contiguous CUDA int32 `[N_seq]` tensor.
- `initial_state` is a BF16 `(P, H, 128, 128)` state pool. It can hold
more slots than there are sequences, and its slot stride can be padded.
The pool is checked with the same `_is_state_pool_tensor` contract that
frozen prefill uses.
- Sequence `n` reads and updates `initial_state[ssm_state_indices[n]]`
in place. Unselected slots are left unchanged. With
`output_final_state=True`, the pool itself is returned.

Changes:

- **`kda_chunked_bt16_small_bh.py`**
- The K2 kernel takes an optional `mStateIndices` and looks up the slot
once per CTA. Without indices, the compiled specialization is the same
as before.
- For indexed state, the pool row stride is compiled as a 64-bit runtime
value (`cute.sym_int64`). This matters for serving engines, where the
state pool is often a strided view into a large KV-cache arena: a slot
can start more than 2**31 elements from the pool base, and a 32-bit
offset would wrap and fault.
  - `chunk_kda_fwd` / `chunk_kda_fwd_k2` gain a `state_indices` keyword.
- **`kda_prefill_cute_small_bh.py`**: the eligibility check now accepts
indexed state and forwards it to the kernel.
- **`kda.py`**: `backend="auto"` does not route indexed calls to
small-BH, so `auto` routing for indexed state is unchanged. Only the
explicit `backend="small-bh"` opts in. The docstrings are updated to
match.

Motivation: TensorRT-LLM vendors this kernel for Kimi K3 serving and has
been carrying the indexed-state support as a local patch
(NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#21342). Upstreaming it lets that patch be dropped
once the vendored copy is bumped.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#21342 (downstream fix for the 32-bit pool-offset
wrap in the patched kernel)

### [6a78963](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6a789639f788af11c8e1007f5248dc3bf5b95f9a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:53:43Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fused_moe): Kimi-K3 NVFP4 SiTU experts SM103 2048- and 4096-token rows: fused quantization + reset and per-CTA privatized routing (#8674)

The Cake-generated Kimi-K3 NVFP4 SiTU expert MoE path behind
`cutlass_fused_moe(backend="cake")` uses NVFP4 weights and activations,
FP32 accumulation and BF16 output, with a single model contract (H=3584,
I=384, E=896, top_k=16). It ships 44 programs on main and 46 with this
PR, organized as per-token-count routes of quant, route, FC1, FC2 and
finalize stages. This PR adds two new sm_103a-only routing programs,
`route_histogram:n128_p256f` and `route_scatter:n128_p256fh2`. At 256
routed pairs per CTA, they keep the expert histogram private in per-CTA
shared memory and reserve a block of rows for each CTA. The existing
sm_100a 8192-token program that fuses quantization with the
routing-table reset now also ships for sm_103a, because its kernel does
not depend on routing pairs per CTA. On SM103, the 2048-token route
changes from `mid_work5fd` to `mid_work5fd_p256fh2qr`, and the
4096-token route changes from `mid_q8i` to `mid_q8i_p256fh2qr`. Each
route drops from eight launches to seven because quantization and the
routing-table reset now share one launch. FC1, FC2 and finalize are
unchanged on both rows. `mid_q8i` served only the sm_103a 4096-token
row, so this PR removes it. Compared with the previous Cake version of
these routes, the whole call is 1.004x to 1.020x faster. Compared with
freshly autotuned trtllm-gen, it is 1.023x to 1.063x faster.

*Whole-call median latency for the full MoE expert layer on NVIDIA B300
(sm_103a) with CUDA 13.3.1, cold L2. Baselines: the previous Cake
version of each route (the route FlashInfer ships today for these rows)
and FlashInfer `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` (trtllm-gen), freshly
autotuned. All columns use the same timer.*

vs previous | trtllm-gen (us) | Speedup vs trtllm-gen |

| 2048 | uniform | 441.476 | 439.684 | 1.004x | 449.859 | 1.023x |

All other Cake variants of this kernel are unchanged: sm_100a keeps

### [725a39e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/725a39ed6599121320e80e5ba05372a033ab613a)

- **作者**: Sam
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:51:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(quantization): select the NVFP4 TMA quantize kernel by input size (#6691)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

This follows up on the second suggestion in the #6276 review: FP8 inputs
with `m >= 1024` always take the TMA kernel, and that kernel is slower
on several `m <= 4096` shapes.

The CUDA backend sends every NVFP4 quantize call (FP8, FP16 or BF16
input) with `m >= 1024` to the TMA kernel. The TMA kernel has a higher
steady-state bandwidth, but filling and draining its producer/consumer
pipeline costs about 2 µs more than the vectorized kernel's launch. At
`m = 1024–4096` that fixed cost dominates. On B200 the TMA kernel is up
to 1.6× slower there: BF16 1024 × 7168 with the linear layout takes 10.4
µs vs 6.6 µs.

The TMA kernel is now taken only when the input is at least 32 MiB,
batch included, and when its grid gives every SM a work tile: `b ×
ceil(padded rows / TMA_ROW_TILE) >= multiProcessorCount`, where the
padded rows are the rows the SF layout pads to (`m` for linear). The
launcher sizes the grid from the same count. `m >= 1024` and the
column-chunk condition from #6276 are unchanged.

**Why the work-tile condition** (suggested in review). `m >= 1024` does
not keep wide inputs with few rows off the TMA kernel. Since #6207, the
TMA grid spans `b × row tiles`, so BF16 1024 × 32768 runs on 64 CTAs,
and on B200 it takes 34.4 µs on TMA against 19.8 µs on the vectorized
kernel. The review suggested exempting batched input. That was measured
before this branch picked up #6207, when the grid ignored `b`. With the
current grid, batched input has the same problem: BF16 2 × 1024 × n has
128 work tiles on 148 SMs, and the vectorized kernel is 15–17% faster
there. So the condition counts `b × row tiles` for every input instead
of special-casing `b > 1`.

**Why 32 MiB.** I forced each path and swept FP8/BF16 × three SF layouts
× m ∈ [512, 32768] × n ∈ {2048, 4096, 7168}.
- On B200, the TMA kernel starts to win between 16 and 32 MiB for both
dtypes. The three SF layouts agree within a few percent, so one
threshold covers all of them.
- On RTX 5080, the crossover is also about 32 MiB for FP8. For BF16, the
TMA kernel never clearly wins: it is 7–12% slower at 16 MiB and within
5% from 32 MiB up.
- BF16 with n = 7168 crosses later, at 50 MiB or above. A lower
threshold would make BF16 2048 × 7168 (28 MiB) 17–21% slower. With 32
MiB, the worst cell is FP8 4096 × 7168 (28 MiB), which is 5–9% slower
than with TMA.

**Ablation.** Disabling the TMA loads brings the TMA kernel's fixed cost
down to the vectorized kernel's level, so the extra cost sits in the
load pipeline's startup and drain. Doubling the pipeline stages does not
reduce it.

**Related design.** CuTe-DSL `nvfp4_quantize` reached a similar
conclusion in #3905 / #3977: the vectorized kernel by default, TMA only
where it was measured to win. I kept the CUDA backend on TMA above the
threshold, because on B200 the TMA kernel is 1.2–1.5× faster than the
vectorized kernel at 64 MiB and above. The exception is BF16 with n =
7168, where it is about 1.05× faster.

**Known losses.** FP8 with n = 1024 at 2–8 MiB took the TMA kernel under
`m >= 1024` and now takes the vectorized kernel, which is slower there:
5–19% on B200 and B300 (4096 × 1024: 5.7 → 6.7 µs) and 8–18% on RTX PRO
6000, as measured in the review comments. Above the threshold, the
vectorized kernel is still up to 9% faster on B200 in some cells that
have enough work tiles: about 1.3 waves (BF16 3 × 1024 × n, with 192
tiles), and wide rows (FP8 m = 2048 with n ≥ 16384, BF16 n = 32768).
Those come from the TMA kernel's per-column-chunk cost, not from
routing, and would need a kernel change.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #6276 (review suggestion 2). Related: #3905, #3977 (the
same question for the CuTe-DSL backend).

Under the new threshold, most of the FP8 TMA test shapes from #6276 no
longer reach the TMA kernel. They are moved to inputs of 32 MiB and
above, and keep the same edge cases: m not a multiple of 128, a
single-row last tile, and an odd number of column chunks. Two shapes
check routing: one below the size threshold, and one with n an odd
multiple of 512. In the batched cases, each batch alone is below 32 MiB
and the whole input is not, so the batch-inclusive size is also tested.
The references still run in 512-row blocks, which stay on the vectorized
kernel through `m >= 1024`.

To check that the new shapes really reach the TMA kernel, I reverted the
#6276 OOB-fill fix. Exactly the 17 TMA cases then failed with `Failed to
encode TMA tensor map`, and the 6 routing cases passed.

`tests/utils/test_fp4_quantize.py`: 1188 passed on RTX 5080 (SM120,
driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.3).

With the 32 MiB rule, the small FP16/BF16 shapes no longer reach the TMA
kernel, so the FP8 parity test now also runs FP16 and BF16 over the same
shapes, with one BF16 32 MiB case for the 4over6 recipe. After the
rebase onto `main`, the scale-buffer guard test from #6278 moves to
inputs of 32 MiB and above for the same reason.

With the work-tile condition, the TMA shapes move to m ≥ 4096, which
gives a work tile per SM on every supported GPU, and they keep their
edge cases. (1024, 32768) now guards the new condition. A temporary
print in the TMA launcher confirmed that on RTX 5080 every case reaches
the kernel it is meant to.

The scale-buffer guard test also gains FP8 input, as asked in the #6278
review: (4097, 8192) and (4103, 8192), with m % 8 of 1 and 7. FP8 walks
rows in tiles of 8, so only the linear layout leaves a partial last
tile. On RTX 5080 the guard test passes all 24 cases; with #6278's row
bound removed, 14 fail, and the FP8 cases fail in linear only.

After the rebase: `tests/utils/test_fp4_quantize.py`: 1560 passed on RTX
5080 (SM120, driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0, `flashinfer-ci-cu130` image)
and on B200 (driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0).

### Performance

B200 (driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.9.1). CUPTI kernel time, cold
L2, median, `enable_pdl` default, 128x4 layout. Rows with m ≥ 8192 are
omitted: they take the same kernel before and after, and all are within
0.98–1.03×.

| input | m × n | MiB | `main` (µs) | this PR (µs) | speedup |

| FP8 | 1024 × 2048 | 2 | 4.4 | 3.6 | 1.21× |
| FP8 | 2048 × 2048 | 4 | 5.4 | 4.9 | 1.10× |
| FP8 | 4096 × 2048 | 8 | 7.6 | 6.9 | 1.11× |

| FP8 | 4096 × 7168 | 28 | 16.0 | 17.4 | 0.92× |
| BF16 | 1024 × 2048 | 4 | 5.7 | 4.4 | 1.30× |
| BF16 | 2048 × 2048 | 8 | 6.3 | 5.8 | 1.09× |
| BF16 | 4096 × 2048 | 16 | 8.4 | 8.2 | 1.01× |

Across all 36 shapes, the geomean speedup is 1.06× for the 128x4 layout
(range 0.92–1.47×) and 1.08× for the linear layout (range 0.94–1.57×).
The 8x4 layout was swept with the forced paths and behaves like 128x4.

I also checked the B200 numbers with a second method. It times a CUDA
graph of up to 200 back-to-back launches with CUDA events, cycling
through input buffers 3× the L2 size, with PDL off. The absolute times
are 0.5–1 µs lower than CUPTI for both kernels, but the TMA/vectorized
ratios match within ~0.05, and the crossover sits at the same sizes.

On RTX 5080 I used only the graph method. CUPTI there inflated every
kernel by about 4 µs, which hid the difference between the two kernels.
With the graph method, the FP8 TMA kernel is 1.2–1.4× slower below 4 MiB
and reaches parity at about 32 MiB.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script (CUPTI)</summary>

```python
import statistics, torch
from flashinfer import nvfp4_quantize, SfLayout
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time

torch.set_default_device("cuda")
global_scale = torch.tensor([1.0])
for dtype in (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.bfloat16):
    for layout in (SfLayout.layout_128x4, SfLayout.layout_linear):
        for n in (2048, 4096, 7168):
            for m in (1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768):
                x = torch.randn(m, n).to(dtype)
                fn = lambda: nvfp4_quantize(x, global_scale, sfLayout=layout, backend="cuda")
                times = bench_gpu_time(fn, enable_cupti=True, cold_l2_cache=True)
                print(dtype, layout, m, n, f"{statistics.median(times) * 1000:.2f} us")
```

</details>

#### Work-tile condition

B200 (driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0), CUPTI kernel time,
cold L2, median, 128x4 layout (batched: `nvfp4_batched_quantize`).
"Before" is this PR without the work-tile condition, which routes these
cells the same as `main`.

| input | b × m × n | work tiles | before (µs) | after (µs) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 | 1 × 1024 × 32768 | 128 | 21.3 | 17.2 | 1.24× |
| FP8 | 1 × 1024 × 65536 | 128 | 38.0 | 30.6 | 1.24× |
| BF16 | 1 × 1024 × 16384 | 64 | 19.1 | 11.1 | 1.73× |
| BF16 | 1 × 1024 × 32768 | 64 | 34.4 | 19.8 | 1.74× |
| BF16 | 1 × 1024 × 65536 | 64 | 64.5 | 35.8 | 1.80× |
| BF16 | 1 × 2048 × 8192 | 128 | 13.4 | 11.6 | 1.16× |
| BF16 | 1 × 2048 × 32768 | 128 | 41.1 | 35.7 | 1.15× |
| BF16 | 2 × 1024 × 8192 | 128 | 13.5 | 11.7 | 1.15× |
| BF16 | 2 × 1024 × 32768 | 128 | 41.2 | 35.2 | 1.17× |
| BF16 | 4 × 1024 × 8192 (unchanged) | 256 | 19.8 | 19.8 | 1.00× |
| BF16 | 1 × 4096 × 16384 (unchanged) | 256 | 33.1 | 33.0 | 1.00× |

The linear and 8x4 layouts move the same way: 1.80–1.98× for BF16 m =
1024 and 1.24–1.27× for m = 2048. Cells with enough work tiles stay
within 1%. Over 49 batched cells, the slowdown against the faster of the
two kernels is 1.016× by geomean (1.088× worst) with this condition,
against 1.024× (1.167× worst) with batched input exempted.

On RTX 5080 (84 SMs; CUDA graphs with CUDA events, PDL off, 54 cells of
32–128 MiB), the condition moves only unbatched BF16 m = 1024, by
1.00–1.05×. Every batched cell already has at least 128 work tiles. The
two kernels are within 9% of each other on that card, and the rules tie
at 1.02× by geomean.

### [9281863](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/92818633632e1cb89f2ef5f546450d3db9d3f601)

- **作者**: Tian Zheng
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:47:48Z
- **提交信息**: feat(gdn): add SM120 cuteDSL ReplaySSM GDN MTP decode kernels (#7536)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

Extend GDN ReplaySSM speculative decoding (#5314) to SM120. #5314 added
frozen-checkpoint verify (`gated_delta_rule_mtp(...,
cache_replayssm=True)`) and accepted-prefix commit
(`gated_delta_rule_replayssm_commit`), but restricted both to
SM100/SM103 because its fast paths use tcgen05. SM120 has no tcgen05, so
this PR adds a TF32 warp-MMA (`mma.sync`) verify specialization and
enables the existing portable paths on SM120.

- Allow `cache_replayssm=True` and `gated_delta_rule_replayssm_commit`
on SM120 (compute capability 12.0). The verify/commit API, buffer
layouts and lifecycle are unchanged.
- Add `gdn_decode_mtp_replayssm_hmma.py`, an SM120 frozen-state verify
kernel. Each CTA computes `state[rows, 128] @ [K_0..K_{T-1},
Q_0..Q_{T-1}]^T` with `mma.sync.m16n8k8` TF32 (one warp per 16-row state
tile) while another warp computes the small K/Q Gram matrix. Outputs are
then reconstructed from these base products and the rank-one update
coefficients with an O(T²) per-row recurrence, so no per-token state is
materialized. It writes the same raw K/V, log-decay and beta windows as
the other verify paths.
- Split each head's V rows across 2 CTAs (4 when `B * HV <= 128`) so
enough state loads are in flight at small grids; only the cheap Q/K
normalization and Gram work repeat per slice.
- Permute K consistently within each 64-wide group so that each lane's
TF32 A-fragment elements are 16 contiguous state columns, loaded with
128-bit loads. State/K, state/Q and Gram products are invariant under
the shared permutation.
- Commit on SM120 uses the existing FP32 SIMT fold kernel:
`backend="auto"` never selects tcgen05 there, and an explicit
`backend="tcgen05"` raises `ValueError`.

Dispatch: the SM120 TF32 verify requires contiguous FP32 checkpoints,
K=V=128, T=4..8, B=1..256, normalized Q/K, int32 indices and BF16 output
(any HV/H ratio). Among those, it is selected when `B * HV <= 128` or `T
>= 7`; for `T <= 6` with `B * HV > 128` the FP32 MTP path is as fast or
faster (up to ~16% at T=4) and remains in use, as do all other supported
inputs. TF32 outputs are not bitwise identical to the FP32 path.

SM121 and other SM12x variants are not enabled; they have not been
validated.

### Performance

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), H=8, HV=32 (Qwen3.5-397B
TP=2), K=V=128, BF16 inputs, FP32 state, same methodology as #5314. All
values are microseconds. Verify columns are per layer; commit and total
columns cover four layers. All benchmarks make sure L2 is cold for each
iteration. Full acceptance (4/4 or 8/8):

| B | T | Upstream verify + snapshots | ReplaySSM verify | Upstream
total | ReplaySSM total | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4 | 5.06 | 2.91 | 26.13 | 18.35 | 1.42x |
| 8 | 4 | 59.92 | 12.41 | 284.07 | 77.64 | 3.66x |
| 16 | 4 | 119.41 | 22.01 | 661.36 | 215.26 | 3.07x |
| 32 | 4 | 237.68 | 53.06 | 1317.85 | 586.36 | 2.25x |
| 64 | 4 | 474.03 | 100.70 | 2630.99 | 1149.97 | 2.29x |
| 128 | 4 | 946.01 | 196.55 | 5252.02 | 2285.59 | 2.30x |
| 256 | 4 | 1890.14 | 388.44 | 10497.97 | 4548.93 | 2.31x |
| 1 | 8 | 7.57 | 3.52 | 35.56 | 22.86 | 1.56x |
| 8 | 8 | 109.97 | 7.67 | 501.00 | 72.63 | 6.90x |
| 16 | 8 | 216.98 | 24.77 | 1051.55 | 259.07 | 4.06x |
| 32 | 8 | 433.99 | 54.56 | 2103.32 | 597.27 | 3.52x |
| 64 | 8 | 861.89 | 105.21 | 4181.93 | 1175.06 | 3.56x |
| 128 | 8 | 1720.48 | 206.22 | 8350.18 | 2332.70 | 3.58x |
| 256 | 8 | 3441.32 | 407.59 | 16702.39 | 4645.40 | 3.60x |

The full-acceptance total improves **1.42–6.90x**. Upstream total is `4
* (verify + full FP32 snapshot per token) + one copy of the accepted
snapshot`; ReplaySSM total is `4 * ReplaySSM verify + one all-layer
commit` (SIMT on SM120). On SM120 the commit is DRAM-bound and close to
the snapshot copy, so the gain comes from verify: it no longer writes
per-token snapshots, and for T=8 (and B=1) it uses the TF32 warp-MMA
kernel, which is faster than plain MTP verify without snapshots (e.g.
B=8/T=8: 22.2 → 7.7 µs; B=256/T=8: 502 → 408 µs).

Timing uses CUDA graphs with ten calls per graph, ten warmup and fifty
timed replays, three rounds, reporting the median of the three medians;
no explicit L2 flush, four distinct layers visited in sequence. Before
timing, each shape checks that ReplaySSM outputs match the snapshot path
(max abs error 1.2e-4) and that the committed checkpoint matches the
accepted snapshot (max abs error 1.5e-8).

<!-- Optional: anything you'd like reviewers to focus on, concerns, etc.

### How to review

The ReplaySSM contract from #5314 is unchanged: verify reads a frozen
checkpoint and writes raw K/V plus gate windows by state-pool slot;
commit replays the accepted prefix. This PR only adds an SM120
implementation of verify and routes SM120 commit to the existing SIMT
kernel.

| File (suggested reading order) | What changed and why | Review focus |
|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer/gdn_decode.py` | Opens the ReplaySSM architecture gate to
SM120 (12.0) and documents the SM120 verify/commit behavior. | The gate
admits exactly SM100-family and SM120; docs match the dispatch. |
| `flashinfer/gdn_kernels/gdn_replayssm_spec_fold.py` | Admits SM120 for
commit; `auto` considers tcgen05 only on SM100-family, and explicit
`tcgen05` raises elsewhere. | SM100 dispatch is unchanged; the
explicit-backend error is raised after the shared validation. |
| `flashinfer/gdn_kernels/gdn_decode_mtp.py` | Adds the SM120 dispatch
ahead of the SM100 tcgen05 dispatch in `run_mtp_decode`, with the
eligibility conditions and selection policy described above. |
Eligibility mirrors the tcgen05 path minus the HV/H parity requirement;
ineligible inputs fall through to the existing MTP kernels. |
| `flashinfer/gdn_kernels/gdn_decode_mtp_replayssm_hmma.py` | New SM120
verify kernel and launcher. Phase 1: one warp per timestep normalizes
Q/K into SMEM at permuted MMA columns (`_operand_column`), stages V,
computes decay/beta and writes the raw windows (raw K, log-g and beta
from slice 0 only; raw V per slice for its own rows). Phase 2: state
warps compute base products with 128-bit state loads into the TF32 A
fragment; warp 4 computes the Gram matrix. Phase 3: one thread per V row
runs the low-rank recurrence. The launcher follows the tcgen05
launcher's compile-target, persistent-cache and layout-key conventions.
| The K permutation must be applied identically to state loads and K/Q
stores; padding rows `[2T, 16)` of the operand tile are zeroed for T<8;
window-write ownership across V slices; padding rows (negative indices)
write nothing. |
| `tests/gdn/test_replayssm_spec_fold.py` | See Tests. | Routing tests
check selection separately from numerics. |

### Validation scope

Validated on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) and B300 (SM103). SM121 is not enabled
and not validated. compute-sanitizer (memcheck/racecheck) was clean on
the pre-port version of this kernel; it has not been re-run on this
branch. Performance measured with FlashInfer commit `c65c9d839` (this
branch, based on `47e64b0e9`) in `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.08-py3`,

### [b08f407](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b08f40719a7d946d113a0a6ba4a056163b7d6217)

- **作者**: Zupeng Wang
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:46:48Z
- **提交信息**: fix(sampling): isolate softmax partial reductions across streams (#4692)

## 📌 Description

The split-vocabulary `OnlineSoftmax` path used a module-global 1 MiB
workspace for partial reductions. Calls on different CUDA streams
therefore aliased the same storage: one call's phase-1 kernels could
overwrite another call's partials before its phase-2 reduction consumed
them.

This change stores each row's partial reductions in the beginning of
that invocation's output row. Phase 2 loads all partials before its
block synchronization and only then writes normalized values, so the row
can safely double as scratch. The existing external workspace argument
is preserved for ABI compatibility, and the hot path adds no allocation
or stream lookup.

A regression test interleaves large-vocabulary softmax calls on two CUDA
streams through both `flashinfer.sampling.softmax` and the compiled
`LogitsPipe([Temperature(), Softmax()])` path.

Base: `2f519edced8b027f8aee960bc622346e510e2cfa`

Head: `4a04a72ead82f652f912147cfd04023746743e84`

### Reproduction and performance check

Environment: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (SM86), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch
`2.13.0+cu130`, one GPU.

Before the fix, a two-stream stress run at `(batch_size=128,
vocab_size=131072)` produced 17 incorrect outputs out of 80 calls. The
worst row-sum error was `0.9897358`. The added pytest regression also
failed on the original kernel with 21.7% mismatched elements in an
affected output.

After the fix, both API variants pass 10 interleaved calls per stream,
and both variants pass CUDA Graph capture/replay.

Serial no-regression benchmark: 20 warmups, 10 rounds, 200 calls/round
for `1x32000` and 100 calls/round for `128x131072`. Values are wall-time
median in microseconds with `[p10, p90]`:

| Shape | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `1x32000` | `13.239 [12.856, 13.400]` | `12.736 [12.426, 13.369]` |
| `128x131072` | `252.476 [247.567, 255.461]` | `247.885 [247.624,
249.330]` |

The intervals overlap; this is a no-regression check rather than a
speedup claim.

## 🔍 Related Issues

No matching open issue or PR was found for the softmax workspace race.
The active top-k stream-safety work does not touch `OnlineSoftmax` or
this workspace.

### [b54e546](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b54e546b41c92912ae951eb83bb0bea9dc4083c8)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:46:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_attn_res): L2 first-chunk prefetch and CLC token-broadcast programs for two B200 and five B300 shapes (#8676)

This PR changes routes of the Cake AttnRes operator,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kimi_k3_attn_res`, which is exposed as
`flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res` and
`kimi_k3_attn_res`. One launch does residual add, an optional snapshot
write, K+1 candidate scoring, softmax, mix and output RMSNorm. It takes
BF16 inputs with hidden size 7168 and K in [0, 8]. It has one data type,
one layout and two fused forms: dense and snapshot write. This PR
changes routes on B300 and B200, at both PDL modes. No GB300 route
changes. Among the measured shapes, 5 change on B300 and 2 on B200. This
PR adds three build options. All are off by default and ship only in
programs that a route uses.

- **New first-chunk L2 prefetch options (B300):** Each of these shapes
moves to a build of its previous program with a first-chunk L2 prefetch
option that this PR adds. The kernel issues the K+2 first-chunk row
prefetches from lanes or warps that are not on the setup path, so the
prefetches overlap the barrier setup. With `_fpl`, a lane group issues
the prefetches. With `_fpw`, each warp issues one row.
- On B300 (sm_103a): serving_m384_k2 moves from
`persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f011010000000000_fm_crfnone` to
`persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f011010000000000_fm_crfnone_fpw`.
- On B300 (sm_103a): serving_m768_k1 moves from
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f111010000000000_fm` to
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f111010000000000_fm_fpl`.
- On B300 (sm_103a): serving_m768_k2 moves from
`persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f111010000000000_fm` to
`persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f111010000000000_fm_fpl`.
- On B300 (sm_103a): serving_m512_k3 moves from
`persistent:k3_nc4_d2_f111000000000000_fm_rcp` to
`persistent:k3_nc4_d2_f111000000000000_fm_rcp_fpl`.
- On B300 (sm_103a): write_m1024_k1_write1 moves from
`persistent:k1_nc4_d3_f010000000000010_crheld_write` to
`persistent:k1_nc4_d3_f010000000000010_crheld_write_fpl` with PDL off,
and from `persistent:k1_nc4_d3_f010000000100000_crheld_write` to
`persistent:k1_nc4_d3_f010000000100000_crheld_write_fpl` with PDL on.
- **New token-queue builds with CLC token broadcast (B200):** Both
shapes move from a static persistent program (grid = SM count) to a
token-queue (`_clc`) build (grid = M) with CLC token broadcast
(`_tokb`), which this PR adds. With `_tokb`, only the producer warp
takes the next token from cluster launch control. It passes the token to
the consumer warps through shared memory, so the consumers no longer
touch the CLC response ring.
- On B200 (sm_100a): serving_m16384_k7 moves from
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000` to
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_clc_tokb`.
- On B200 (sm_100a): serving_m12288_k4 moves from
`persistent:k4_nc3_d3_f110000000000000` to
`persistent:k4_nc3_d3_f110000000000000_clc_tokb`.

The program set goes from 195 to 200 programs. This PR adds 8 programs:
2 `_clc_tokb` programs for sm_100a, and 1 `_fpw` program and 5 `_fpl`
programs for sm_103a. It removes 3 programs that serve no other shape:
`persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f011010000000000_fm_crfnone`,
`persistent:k1_nc4_d3_f010000000000010_crheld_write` and
`persistent:k1_nc4_d3_f010000000100000_crheld_write`. The other previous
programs stay because they still serve other shapes.

All changed shapes are faster. On B300, serving_m384_k2 measures 1.050x,
serving_m768_k1 1.037x and serving_m768_k2 1.026x, each at both PDL
modes. On B300, serving_m512_k3 measures 1.032x with PDL off and 1.030x
with PDL on, and write_m1024_k1_write1 measures 1.037x with PDL off and
1.031x with PDL on. On B200, serving_m16384_k7 measures 1.014x with PDL
off and 1.010x with PDL on, and serving_m12288_k4 measures 1.021x with
PDL off and 1.019x with PDL on. For shapes not in the tables below, see
the timings in PRs #6980, #7014, #7338, #7374, #7411, #7453, #7540,
#7737, #8120, #8143, #8155, #8171, #8207, #8291, #8351, #8428, #8489,
#8554 and #8609.

### [51f704d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/51f704d0d2ebfd0b73d26c5c2ec68fd18c03c605)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:45:27Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn): run the split adjoint scan beside the group-of-three tail on B200 and GB300 (#8675)

Cake ships four GDN training variants in FlashInfer: a non-deterministic
and a deterministic form, each as a single-rank package and a
context-parallel (KCP) package. This PR changes only the
non-deterministic single-rank package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gdn_train` (packed variable-length
sequences, head dim 128, chunk 64, grouped Q/K heads). On sm_100a (B200)
and sm_103a (GB300), group-of-three rows (HV = 3H, shown as H/HV 2/6 in
the tables) now use a different backward. The adjoint scan is split into
two groups, and the second group runs on a high-priority side stream
beside the group-of-three tail. Before this PR, one serial scan ran
beside that tail. The deterministic package already uses this backward
form on these rows. All other rows keep the previous schedule, and so
does every row on sm_107a (R200). On every measured row, the output and
all gradients are bitwise identical to the previous non-deterministic
package and to the deterministic package.

Ratios are baseline ms / this PR ms, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. ckpt is the checkpointed step. Before this PR, four cells were
slower than deterministic Cake beyond run-to-run noise: B200 FP32-beta 6
seqs, 241817 tokens fwd+bwd; B200 FP32-beta 64 x 4096 fwd+bwd and ckpt;
and GB300 FP32-beta 64 x 4096 ckpt. All four are now at parity with
deterministic Cake (0.998x-1.004x). Compared with the previous
non-deterministic package, they are 1.007x-1.019x. Two of them (B200 64
x 4096 fwd+bwd and GB300 64 x 4096 ckpt) are classed faster, and the
other two are at parity.

The bwd rows show where this PR costs time. On the four group-of-three
rows, the isolated backward is 0.977x-0.991x of the previous
non-deterministic package on both GPUs (0.9-2.4 % more time), which is
the same time as the deterministic package (0.999x-1.002x). On those
rows, fwd+bwd and ckpt are at parity with the previous package or
faster. Two BF16-beta fwd+bwd cells are still slower than deterministic
Cake beyond run-to-run noise, both at 7 x ~4.3k (real pack), H/HV 8/16:
0.985x on B200 and 0.992x on GB300. This PR does not change the schedule
of those rows, and they are at parity with the previous package.

The tables use three baselines:
- Deterministic Cake (`cake_gdn_det_train` at FlashInfer main).
- The previous non-deterministic Cake package (FlashInfer main before
this PR).
- Per cell, the strongest applicable non-Cake implementation among cuDNN
frontend 1.32.1 FROST (chunk 0 and chunk 64) and FLA 0.6.0 (Triton).
Where the fastest non-Cake implementation drifted by more than 2 %, the
cell is marked "unstable (not published)".

All timings are eager, on NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) and NVIDIA
GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), with CUDA 13.0 and torch 2.14.1+cu130.

of 16 samples (L2 flushed before each sample); speedup = baseline ms /
this PR ms; bwd = the backward pass alone (its forward runs outside the
timed region), fwd+bwd = one training step, ckpt = forward, recomputed
forward and backward of a checkpointed step.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [8cb3a60](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8cb3a6010be73fd79697255d12a6b8c9456a2662)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:43:00Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train): L2-prefetching extra-long forward on SM103 (#8673)

This PR adds an extra-long forward tier on sm_103a to the
non-deterministic package of Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` with `deterministic=False`).
From 3000 rows per SM, the sm_103a forward now runs
`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_7f014401d5cc855ab883`, and this route is
tried before the long forward's. The new module is a 256-thread forward
with the packed gate. In it, thread 0 also warms the CTA's next row
block in L2, the same way the mid forward warms its later blocks: one
bulk prefetch per tensor wherever the inputs x and z hold their rows
packed. All nine changed shapes in Table 1 are at or above 3000 rows per
SM on the 152-SM GB300.

The previous Cake baseline below is the long forward,
`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_7b7fac905aff1ddaa258`. It ran these inputs
before this PR, and it still runs sm_103a inputs from 2400 up to 3000
rows per SM. This PR removes no module. Every other module and route
runs the same code as before, including the backward, the short, mid and
long forwards, and every sm_100a and sm_107a route.

The PR is one commit on FlashInfer main after PR #8656. The A/B compared
two FlashInfer trees. In the first, there is no extra-long route, so the
long forward also serves 3000 rows per SM and up. The second is the same
tree plus this PR's sm_103a route. Both trees predate PR #8656, which
changed only the sm_107a mid forward. In the measured tree, the new
module's sources are byte-identical to this PR's.

A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. The table gives ranges (min-max) over the nine changed shapes of
Table 1 on GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4.

| op | det Cake / new | strongest non-Cake / new | previous Cake / new
(A/B) |
|---|---|---|---|
| fwd | 1.134-1.164 | 1.061-1.133 | 1.039-1.050 |
| fwdg | 1.134-1.165 | 1.053-1.134 | 1.039-1.049 |
| bwdg | 1.114-1.147 | 1.091-1.115 | 0.9999-1.0002 |
| ckptg | 1.123-1.144 | 1.093-1.121 | 1.017-1.022 |
| stepg_f32 | 1.125-1.145 (A/B) | - | 1.017-1.021 |
| fwd + bwd | 1.129-1.143 (A/B) | - | 1.014-1.018 |

In the pre-registered A/B, the code changes in 36 cells (fwd, fwdg,
ckptg and stepg_f32 at the nine shapes), and new is faster than the
previous Cake route in all 36. bwdg and bwdg_f32 run the same code in
both trees. Neither the strongest non-Cake kernel (Table 1) nor the
deterministic Cake kernel (Tables 1 and 2) is faster than new on any
row. Every cell below 1x is a same-code cell against the previous Cake
route and is within 0.1 % of parity. "Cells below 1x" lists each one.

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`) and the FP32 weight-gradient output of the
non-deterministic package; both packages ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a, and this PR changes only the non-deterministic package's
forward on sm_103a from 3000 rows per SM.

## How the tables were measured

- Latency: CUPTI kernel time with cold L2, taken with FlashInfer's GPU
timer in `flashinfer.testing`. Inputs are BF16, and all times are in us.
- Table 1: the deterministic Cake kernel, the strongest non-Cake kernel
and new were measured in the same process. Each value is the median of
the per-round medians over 10 rounds.
- A/B values: the previous Cake and new (A/B) columns and all of Table 2
are medians of the pre-registered interleaved A/B, which ran 16
sequences and 160 processes. stepg_f32 has no same-process measurement,
so its deterministic Cake values also come from the A/B.
- Strongest non-Cake kernel per row: the fastest of the following, with
torch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0.
  - FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated` (`fla.modules.fused_norm_gate`).
  - mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn` (`layernorm_gated`).
- torch.compile in default and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs modes, best of
5 fresh compiles each. `#k` names the fastest compile.
- The inductor-generated persistent-reduction Triton kernel of the FP32
formula, launched directly.
- Deterministic Cake: `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`,
unchanged by this PR.
- Operations:
- `fwd` is one eager forward call, and `fwdg` is the forward replayed
from a CUDA graph.
- `bwdg` is the backward replayed from a CUDA graph, and `bwdg_f32` is
the same backward with an FP32 dw.
- `ckptg` is the checkpointed step (2 x forward + backward) in one CUDA
graph, and `stepg_f32` is the same step with an FP32 dw.
  - `fwd + bwd` is fwdg + bwdg, derived.
- In Table 2, the forward at the first nine shapes runs the new module.
7600x48, 9120x48 and 9499x48 are below 3000 rows per SM and run the same
code in both trees.

## Cells below 1x

- vs the strongest non-Cake kernel (Table 1): none.
- vs the deterministic Cake kernel (Tables 1 and 2): none.
- vs the previous Cake route (A/B), only at cells that run the same code
in both trees:
  - Table 1, bwdg: 9500x48 0.99996, 9975x48 0.9999
- Table 2, changed shapes (backward cells): 9500x48 bwdg 0.99996,
9975x48 bwdg 0.9999, 9975x48 bwdg_f32 0.9998, 19000x48 bwdg_f32 0.99996
- Table 2, same-code shapes: 7600x48 fwd 0.9999, 7600x48 ckptg 0.9995,
7600x48 bwdg_f32 0.9998, 7600x48 stepg_f32 0.9998, 9120x48 fwd 0.9999,
9120x48 ckptg 0.99996, 9120x48 stepg_f32 0.9998, 9499x48 fwdg 0.99999,
9499x48 bwdg_f32 0.9999
- The same-process run behind Table 1 also timed the previous Cake
route. Those times are not in the tables. Its bwdg previous / new, where
both routes run the same backward module, is below 1 at 9975x48 0.9997
(107.361 / 107.392 us), 11400x48 0.999 (118.688 / 118.752 us), 14250x48
0.9998 (146.497 / 146.529 us), 19000x48 0.999 (189.217 / 189.312 us) and
32737x48 0.9999 (316.057 / 316.097 us).

### [6d1ee9e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6d1ee9e16be51031f4f24c6d795a1cdcf5c3c805)

- **作者**: Feanor
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:41:43Z
- **提交信息**: fix(norm): mixed-architecture dispatch compatibility guard (#8474)

Follow-up to #5355

Fixes the norm dispatch issue diagnosed in #5355 by @kahyunnam and
@kerry0520.

## Problem

CuTe DSL compile target is process-global (device 0 only). On
mixed-architecture hosts (e.g., sm_86 + sm_89), launching on a different
device gives cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice (209).

The existing _use_cuda_norm() guard only checks whether the DSL's Arch
enum knows the target architecture, not whether the DSL is actually
compiling for it.

## Root Cause

The CuTe DSL's captured compile target (_dsl_captured_arch()) reflects
device 0's architecture did not validate thiscompatibility with the
target device.
## Fix                                                                
Compare the DSL's captured target against the target device's compute
capability using CUDA bcubin for sm_X.Y runs on sm_X.Z when Z >= Y), and
fall back to the CUDA JIT path when they are incompatible.

## Changes

- Add _is_arch_compatib binary compatibilityrules
- Modify _use_cuda_norm vs target devicecapability
- Import _dsl_captured_.availability withgraceful fallback

## Impact

Fixes all norm operations that use _use_cuda_norm() for dispatch:
rmsnorm,
fused_add_rmsnorm, gemm operations.

## Testing

- Unit tests for archit
- Dispatch tests for mixed-architecture fallback
- Validates forward comr minor)
- Validates cross-major incompatibility fallback

Fixes the norm dispatch issue diagnosed in #5355.

-->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* Improved normalization backend selection on systems with GPUs of
different architectures. Devices that cannot use the alternative backend
now use the CUDA path, while compatible devices can continue using the
alternative.
* Architecture variants are considered during compatibility checks, and
invalid or mismatched targets fall back to CUDA.
* Explicit selection of CUDA normalization remains supported. When
architecture information is unavailable, supported devices can still use
the alternative backend.

### [46ea00d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/46ea00d3ed7b7ad858ab8d9bf62fdf58f93415ec)

- **作者**: Julien Debache
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T17:18:58Z
- **提交信息**: feat(moe_ep): post-FC2 routing weights in the SM107 NVFP4 MegaMoE tuner (#8013)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The SM107 NVFP4 MegaMoE backend already supports routing weights applied
after FC2, and its knob cache keys entries by that placement, but
`flashinfer.moe_ep.tune` rejected
`--no-apply-routing-weights-before-fc2` on SM107 (and ignored it with
GenPhase), so the tuner never produced knobs for that placement. This PR
accepts the flag for SM107 NVFP4 and passes the placement to the SM107
tuner's symmetric buffer and schedule-sweep base, so it times the
post-FC2 kernels and records the winners under that placement. Caller
finalization (`--no-do-finalize`) stays SM100-only, and SM107 still
rejects post-FC2 weights with MXFP8 or with `--allow-nondeterministic`,
whose in-kernel FC2 reduce needs weights applied before FC2.
`tests/cpu/moe_ep/test_tuning_dispatch.py` now checks that the SM107
flag reaches the tuner and that those combinations are rejected; it
passes on current main (`5d6081143`), CPU only, with 71 passed (two new
tests).

In addition, we note that tuned selection is not necessary, as the
heuristics already choose optimal kernels

### [beeb23b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/beeb23bc0ac24effce80b23aec4a84ae8848df56)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T16:17:59Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_msa): blackwell_msa paged BF16 8-token decode at 64/4 heads, batch 64/128 on the GQA-16 union program (#8672)

The blackwell_msa sparse attention family still has 51 routes backed by
48 programs at this PR, the same as main. This PR adds no route or
program and removes none. The routes cover BF16, FP16 and FP8 (E4M3)
data types and flat and paged KV layouts. They span decode
(`decode_m16`, `decode_uniform_fp8`, `decode_fp8_q1`), prefill
(`prefill_union`, `kmaj_p`, `kmaj_p_fused`, `long_bf16_reverse`) and
four top-k selection routes. This PR changes one dispatch case: a paged
causal BF16 decode call now runs on the existing folded GQA-16
`prefill_union` program (`prefill_union` bf16 paged gqa16 causal_mask64)
instead of `decode_m16` when it has eight query tokens per request, 64
query heads, 4 KV heads, 64 or 128 requests, top-k 16, no explicit
`q_offset` and a page table of at most 10 pages. Every other decode call
keeps its route.

Compared with the previous Cake version on main (#8574), the main/PR
latency ratios are 1.95 to 1.96 on GB300 and 1.91 to 1.92 on B200. A
ratio above 1 means this PR is faster. Latencies are pooled geometric
means over 3 repetitions in µs, measured with a cold L2.

**NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, CUDA 13.3**

| shape | route | main (µs) | this PR (µs) | speedup (main / PR) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `decode_bf16_paged_b64_q8_kvr750-1250_hq64_hkv4_k16` | `decode_m16` →
`prefill_union` gqa16 | 96.37 | 49.17 | 1.9600 |
| `decode_bf16_paged_b128_q8_kvr752-1248_hq64_hkv4_k16` | `decode_m16` →
`prefill_union` gqa16 | 179.15 | 91.76 | 1.9524 |

**NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, CUDA 13.3**

| shape | route | main (µs) | this PR (µs) | speedup (main / PR) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `decode_bf16_paged_b64_q8_kvr750-1250_hq64_hkv4_k16` | `decode_m16` →
`prefill_union` gqa16 | 104.96 | 54.78 | 1.9159 |
| `decode_bf16_paged_b128_q8_kvr752-1248_hq64_hkv4_k16` | `decode_m16` →
`prefill_union` gqa16 | 197.62 | 103.71 | 1.9054 |

This PR leaves the family's other BF16, FP16 and FP8 decode, prefill and
top-k routes unchanged, and the family ships on sm_100a and sm_103a.

### [90fdb2b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/90fdb2b3a7071aeb674fb376daa6f18128c058d6)

- **作者**: Jaeyeon Kim(김재연)
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T16:16:02Z
- **提交信息**: fix(quantization): preserve signed zero in E2M1 fallback (#8397)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Fix signed-zero decoding in the pure-PyTorch E2M1 dequantization
fallback: Python's integer `-0` becomes positive zero, so use `-0.0` for
code `0x8`. For example, packed `0x88` with E4M3 scale 1.0 should decode
to two negative zeros.

Add bit-exact tests using an independent arithmetic reference for all
256 packed bytes × 254 finite E4M3FN scales, with block-varying scales.
Coverage includes both nibble positions, signed scale zeros, global
scales 1 and -2 (and the fallback default), and the native host
decoder's linear, 128x4 and 8x4 layouts. NaN scale encodings are
excluded from logical inputs.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Related context: #7504, #7501 and #7196 cover quantization/MoE
exactness. This PR targets the separate Python fallback LUT and host
decode API. Existing roundtrip tests in
`tests/utils/test_fp4_quantize.py` do not directly assert the fallback's
signed-zero storage bits. No issue is claimed as fixed.

- **作者**: Brandon Zhang

- **提交信息**: [test] KDA decode call-shape equivalence + kernel-census + fp32-rejection tests (#6560) (#8052)

## 📌 Description

Adds `tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_decode_call_shapes.py`, the
call-shape pinning test from the #6560 measurement discussion, opened as
a PR per [kahyunnam's
request](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/6560#issuecomment-6530371304).
It pins the H=64, K=V=128 single-token `recurrent_kda` decode geometry:

- **Call-form equivalence:** the packed `[1, B]` + `cu_seqlens` +
`ssm_state_indices` form, the batched `[B, 1]` + `ssm_state_indices`
form, and the batched contiguous-state-slice form must produce
bit-identical outputs and final states (B in {1, 8}).
- **Full kernel census (as requested):** every device launch per call is
counted via `torch.profiler` — kernels and memcpys, not a single kernel
name — so the host-side gather/scatter around the batched indexed form
is visible. The packed and batched-contiguous forms assert exactly one
launch per call. The batched `[B, 1]` + `ssm_state_indices` case asserts
the same and is marked `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=False)`: it fails today
(5 launches: the state-pool gather/scatter around the same decode
kernel) and flips to passing once that form is routed onto the packed
kernel path (task 4 in #6560).
- **fp32 state rejection:** a float32 state pool (the serving
frameworks' contract) must raise `TypeError` on the CuTe decode path,
per #6893, for both layouts. A future fp32-state decode variant flips
this fixture to a passing path.

Guards match the neighboring `tests/kda` tests (`is_sm100a_supported` +
`_RECURRENT_KDA_AVAILABLE` autouse skip).

Validated on **GB300 (SM103)** against current main (`fca88978`), torch
2.13.0 / CUDA 13.3:

### [0a9a30d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0a9a30dd517e8acb9934c528ea37f0c83e0bb632)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T15:16:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): issue the sm_107a FP8 low-head prefill MMAs at K=64 (#8670)

Cake's DSv4 sparse MLA kernel (`trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4(...,
backend="cake")`) has 48 BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128
query heads, plus an NVFP4-KV decode family. On sm_107a it ships five
FP8 programs: two 128-head and two 64-head persistent prefill programs,
and the FP8 low-head prefill program (`fp8_lowhead_prefill`), which this
PR updates. FlashInfer sends FP8 rows to this program in three cases.
The first is 8, 16 or 32 query heads with sliding-window-only KV and
`max_q_len < 257`. The second is the same with 64 heads when 2 × query
tokens ≤ SM count. The third is 8 heads with `max_q_len ≥ 257` at any
sparse width. On sm_107a the program now issues its QK and PV
tensor-core MMAs with the K=64 FP8 instruction, so each 128-wide K slice
takes two MMAs instead of four K=32 MMAs. The program keeps its name,
and other architectures are unchanged. Speedups are measured against the
previous Cake program, which is the shipped K=32 version of this program
on sm_107a.

NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs), CUDA 13.4. Latency is kernel time
(CUPTI) with a cold L2 and back-to-back launches, the median of 6 paired
rounds; speedup is the median of the 6 per-round previous / this PR
ratios. T is the total number of query tokens. Every row uses the
128-token sliding window; the cache column gives request 0's SWA cache
length, and each later request's cache is longer by the stated step.

The kernel's other Cake variants are the BF16 and FP8 programs with a
split reducer on sm_100a and sm_103a (28 per architecture, 13 of them
shared by both), the NVFP4-KV decode family (seven decode forms and a
merge on each of sm_100a and sm_103a) and the other four FP8 programs on
sm_107a; the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and Cake's
separate SM120 DSv4 programs (NVFP4 and DSv4.1 mixed-cache sparse MLA)
ship on sm_120a.

### [098d8eb](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/098d8eb527b47fa576108ed4b623bee7f4d0027a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T15:11:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): sum the router's split-K partials with a fixed-order program in the bound launch chain (#8664)

The Cake dense projection GEMM package (the non-deterministic one,
`deterministic=False`) ships two GEMM families. The first is the BF16
weight-gradient GEMM (BF16 or FP32 output, several tile widths). The
second is the FP32 router GEMM (forward, input gradient and weight
gradient, 256 experts, hidden 4096 / 5120 / 6144). The router has BF16x3
split-precision stream-K and head/tail programs, and exact-FP32 FFMA
(SIMT) programs at few tokens. For the router launches none of these
serve, it runs the deterministic router program through this package's
bound launch. That program writes split-K partials (4 in the forward, 6
in the weight gradient), and the package reduced them with torch.sum
after the launch. This PR adds a Cake program that adds the partials in
torch.sum's order: four FP32 accumulators, partial s into accumulator s
% 4, combined left to right. It runs right after the router program in
the same bound launch chain, for 2 to 8 splits. The saving is host time
per call. On GB200 the forward entry point takes 18 to 21 us of host
time per call instead of 28 to 32 us (median host time per call over 200
back-to-back calls). GPU time is unchanged, so CUDA graph replays keep
their latency (parity). In eager mode the checkpointed step is 1.27x to
1.40x faster than before on GB200 and 1.22x to 1.41x faster on GB300 at
64 to 1024 tokens, and 1.03x to 1.06x faster at 4096 tokens. Graph
replays are at parity with the previous version (0.98x to 1.02x). Router
launches that run another program (the input gradient, SIMT or this
package's own stream-K programs) are unchanged. Its speedup:

Latency is in microseconds. Each run takes the median of 15 paired
groups of 20 timed iterations (CUPTI kernel spans, cold L2, eager
launches of the router entry points and CUDA graph replays of them). The
table shows the median over runs: four runs of each Cake program, and
two runs of each library route per cuBLAS build. Shapes are hidden (H) x
tokens (T), with 256 experts in FP32. The checkpointed step is 2 forward
+ backward. Deterministic Cake is the deterministic package's router
entry points. Previous is this package before this PR. New is this PR.
Non-Cake SOTA is, per operation, the fastest FP32 library route within
the router accuracy budget (relative Frobenius error at most 2e-6
against FP64). The candidates are cublasSgemm, cuBLASLt FP32 (best of
the heuristic's top 8), torch.mm FP32 without TF32, cuBLAS FP32 in
BF16x9 emulation, and the fastest of these per GEMM, on cuBLAS 13.8 and
13.1. SOTA route names the winning route and its cuBLAS build. Each
speedup is that baseline's latency divided by the new latency. GB200 is
NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs). GB300 is NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152
SMs). The runtime is CUDA 13.0 (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130), and kernels are
built with CUDA 13.4. Outputs are bit for bit the same as before this
PR, also with CUDA graph replay and checkpoint recompute.

The package's other Cake programs (the BF16 weight-gradient GEMM and the
router's stream-K, head/tail and SIMT programs) are unchanged, and the
package ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [02fa872](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/02fa872444d6e529e1ca10cef05873b7b4463024)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T15:02:55Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): projection entry points go from their key to the bound launch (#8650)

The Cake dense projection GEMM package has two GEMM families for MoE
layers behind its non-deterministic entry points
(`deterministic=False`). The first is the BF16 projection GEMM: forward,
input gradient and weight gradient, with the weight gradient in BF16 or
FP32 output and several tile widths. The second is the FP32 router GEMM:
forward, input gradient and weight gradient in BF16x3 split precision
with stream-K and head/tail schedules, plus exact-FP32 FFMA programs for
the router gradients at few tokens. This PR changes only the host path
of the projection GEMM entry points (forward, input gradient, weight
gradient) called with `deterministic=False`. Once a call's key has a
bound program, later calls with that key launch it directly from the
key. They skip re-planning and DLPack conversion and use one stream
context per thread for each device and stream. Kernels, plans and
outputs are unchanged, so CUDA-graph replay time stays the same and only
the eager host time per call drops.

All ratios are baseline/new, so a value above 1 means this PR is faster.
Against the previous version (previous/new), the host-bound rows get
faster on GB200 and GB300. These are the eager backward and the eager
checkpointed step of the three smaller shapes (4096 -> 32 T1024, 4096 ->
128 T1024 and 4096 -> 512 T4096), 6 rows per GPU. On GB200 the median of
the 4 per-run ratios is 1.068-1.136x over these six rows. Every row is
above its A/A band (the bands reach at most 1.052). The single per-run
ratios are 1.053-1.185x. On GB300 the medians are 1.082-1.129x. Every
row is above its A/A band (the bands reach at most 1.029). The single
per-run ratios are 1.065-1.139x. On R200 the same rows are 0.999-1.002x
(medians; single per-run ratios 0.995-1.010x). Five of the six rows are
inside their A/A band. The sixth is the eager checkpointed step of 4096
-> 512 (1.000 against band 1.001-1.003), which is 0.001 below it. On
R200 the host already keeps ahead of these kernels, so the change
neither speeds up nor slows down R200.

Graph rows are at parity on every GPU, with the same kernels:
previous/new is 0.981-1.015x (GB200 0.989-1.015, GB300 0.993-1.013, R200
0.981-1.011). The remaining eager rows are at parity too (0.987-1.018x):
forward and weight gradient alone, and every operation of 5120 -> 1024,
T16231.

A/A outliers are cells whose previous/new lies outside its A/A band or
on its edge. All are within 0.013 of the band and run the same plans and
kernels as before. They are listed as GPU, mode, shape, operation,
previous/new (band):

- Above the band (in favor of this PR): GB200 graph 4096 -> 32 forward
1.013 (band 0.999-1.013, on the edge); GB200 graph 4096 -> 32 backward
1.015 (1.013-1.015, on the edge); GB200 eager 4096 -> 512 weight
gradient 1.004 (0.998-1.001); GB200 eager 5120 -> 1024 checkpointed step
1.011 (0.974-0.998, power-capped row); GB300 eager 4096 -> 128 forward
1.001 (0.998-1.000); GB300 eager 4096 -> 512 weight gradient 1.002
(0.999-1.001); GB300 graph 4096 -> 512 weight gradient 1.000
(0.998-1.000, on the edge); GB300 graph 4096 -> 512 backward 1.002
(0.997-1.001); GB300 graph 5120 -> 1024 backward 1.006 (0.989-1.005);
R200 graph 4096 -> 32 checkpointed step 0.997 (0.994-0.997, on the
edge); R200 graph 4096 -> 128 backward 1.011 (1.003-1.010); R200 eager
5120 -> 1024 forward 1.018 (0.981-1.015); R200 eager 5120 -> 1024 weight
gradient 1.012 (0.991-1.005).
- Below the band (against this PR): GB200 eager 5120 -> 1024 forward
1.002 (1.004-1.019); GB200 eager 5120 -> 1024 backward 0.991
(0.994-1.009); R200 graph 4096 -> 128 forward 0.999 (1.000-1.003); R200
eager 4096 -> 512 checkpointed step 1.000 (1.001-1.003, the host-bound
row above); R200 eager 5120 -> 1024 checkpointed step 0.998
(1.005-1.029).

Against the deterministic Cake entry points (det/new), this PR is at:

- eager: 0.99-1.90x on GB200, 1.00-1.92x on GB300 and 0.97-2.33x on R200
- graph: 0.99-1.47x on GB200, 0.98-1.47x on GB300 and 0.99-1.26x on R200

The strongest non-Cake library GEMM (SOTA: torch.mm or the cuBLASLt
algorithm search, defined below) is faster than this package on 91 of
the 96 rows. SOTA/new is:

- eager: 0.48-0.99x on GB200, 0.48-1.02x on GB300 and 0.36-0.98x on R200
- graph: 0.46-1.01x on GB200, 0.46-1.01x on GB300 and 0.35-0.99x on R200

This package is faster or equal (SOTA/new >= 1.00) on 5 rows, all of
5120 -> 1024, T16231: the GB200 graph weight gradient (1.01), the GB300
weight gradient (eager 1.02, graph 1.01) and the GB300 backward (eager
1.00, graph 1.00). Compared with torch.mm alone, the cuBLASLt search
makes the SOTA column up to 25% faster on GB200, 7% on GB300 and 14% on
R200 (SOTA us / torch.mm us down to 0.745, 0.926 and 0.859).

All values are operation time in us (lower is better) for BF16 inputs
with FP32 weight-gradient output. In the mode column, eager means the
entry points and graph means prepared launches replayed in a CUDA graph.

- **GPUs:** GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs, driver 580.126.20), GB300 (sm_103a,
152 SMs, driver 580.167.08) and R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs, driver 620.43).
torch 2.14.1+cu130; CUDA 13.4 toolkit (nvcc 13.4.92) for the JIT builds.
- **previous:** this package before this PR (same kernels and plans),
`deterministic=False`.
- **deterministic Cake:** the same entry points with
`deterministic=True` (eager) or the deterministic package's prepared
launches (graph).
- **SOTA:** per row and run, the fastest correct library launch among
torch.mm and the top 8 algorithms of the cuBLASLt heuristic. It uses
cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.8.0, the same BF16 operands and the row's output
dtype (BF16 forward and input gradient, FP32 weight gradient via
`out_dtype=torch.float32` for torch.mm). It runs on the same GPU in the
same process as the other arms. "Correct" means within 2e-2 (BF16
output) or 1e-3 (FP32 output) relative Frobenius error of an FP64
reference. Every algorithm the heuristic returned passed (8 per
operation; 7 for the R200 4096 -> 128 input gradient, where the
heuristic returns only 7). For the backward and the checkpointed step,
the library is chosen per operation before timing (by CUDA-event timing
of eager calls and of CUDA-graph replays). The faster of that sequence
and the all-torch.mm sequence is taken. Each us value is the median over
the 4 runs of the per-run fastest launch. This is the strongest
applicable non-Cake baseline. It is the vendor library GEMM that a
training stack without Cake calls (torch.mm), plus the vendor library's
own algorithm search for the same layout and output dtype (cuBLASLt top
8). cuBLAS 13.8.0 is the newest cuBLAS available on these systems. The
cuBLAS 13.1.1 that ships with the PyTorch wheel was also measured on
GB200 and GB300 and was not faster (graph rows: 13.1.1 / 13.8.0 time
ratio 0.985-1.061 on GB200 and 0.986-1.068 on GB300).
- **SOTA library column:** the library of the fastest launch in most of
the 4 runs (with the count when it is not all 4). "cuBLASLt + torch.mm"
means a per-operation mix.
- **Timer:** CUPTI kernel-only time of each operation, from the
beginning of its first kernel to the end of its last kernel. L2 is cold
(two L2 flushes before every iteration). Each cell takes the median of
15 paired groups x 20 timed iterations.
- **Runs:** 4 runs per cell: one process for all rows and one process
per row in reverse order, each twice, one GPU per run. Every us value is
the median of the 4 runs, and previous/new is the median of the 4
per-run ratios. On GB200 and GB300 the eager host-bound rows vary
between runs because the host time varies (for example GB200 4096 -> 128
backward, new 41.3 to 58.4 us). Each ratio is paired within its run.
- **A/A band:** min-max of previous/new over 4 runs of the same protocol
with both arms running this PR's code, which is the timer noise.
- **Power cap:** the 5120 -> 1024, T16231 rows run into the software
power cap on all three GPUs (the cap flag is set after their timing in 2
to 4 of the 4 runs of each pass). The lowest SM clock sampled during
timing was 1312 of 2062 MHz on GB200, 1590 of 2070 MHz on GB300 and 2064
of 2424 MHz on R200.

### [73953fc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/73953fcee68c234b2c45ecc5de06172561e27f1c)

- **作者**: Jimmy Zhou
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T14:58:35Z
- **提交信息**: fix(rope): stop near-tie grid splits on large prefill; test the forced schedules (#7831)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Follow-up to #6794 (merged), addressing the review raised there by
@kahyunnam.

**Problem.** #6794 sizes the token-parallel RoPE grids in whole waves.
On 2048-thread GPUs it keeps the unsplit kernel unless the head-split
kernel *models* cheaper. On large prefill the unsplit grid is many waves
long, so the model's saving is just the last partial wave, and near-ties
went to the split kernel. For example, 40/8 heads at 262k tokens scored
1125 for `g = 2` vs 1127 for `g = 1`. On B200 that split launch runs
0.94-0.98x of the pre-#6794 kernel for `apply_rope_pos_ids`,
`apply_llama31_rope_pos_ids` and `apply_rope_with_cos_sin_cache` at
65k-262k tokens. A forced-`g` sweep shows that no split beats the
unsplit kernel there, and even `g = 1` of the strided kernel is slower.

### Changes

- **Split margin past one wave.** When the unsplit grid exceeds one wave
of resident blocks, the one-head-per-step launchers keep the unsplit
kernel unless the split models **more than 1.1x** cheaper. Below one
wave the previous rule stays, because there a split fills idle SMs and
wins (e.g. `apply_llama31_rope_pos_ids` with 16/2 heads at 8k tokens,
which a flat margin would have lost).
  - All large-token near-ties model at most 1.044x.
  - All measured wins model at least 1.11x.
  - The two-heads path (SM107) is untouched.
- **Two heads per step is gated on SM107 (compute capability 10.7).**
The old `<= 1024 threads/SM` check also matched SM75 (T4), where this
schedule was never measured.
- **Test-only launch override.**
`flashinfer.rope._set_rope_launch_override(two_heads=..., split=...)`
(backed by `rope_set_launch_override` in `csrc/rope.cu`) forces the
token-parallel schedule on any GPU: one or two heads per step, any
`gridDim.y`. With no arguments it restores the automatic choice. It is a
process-wide static read at launch, with no per-launch CUDA queries.

## 📊 Performance

B200, bf16, head_dim 128, neox, random positions. CUPTI kernel time with
cold L2, median of 5 rounds that interleave the three builds in one
container. "pre-#6794" is `51a2fde6c`; "#6794" is the merged code
(current `main`).

| kernel | heads (q/kv) | tokens | #6794 µs | this PR µs | #6794 vs
pre-#6794 | this PR vs pre-#6794 |

## Reviewer Notes

- **The 1.1x bar comes from B200 data.** All three kernels allocate 48
registers there, so both kernels fit 10 blocks/SM (1480 resident
blocks). B300 was not re-measured. The one-wave boundary is computed per
device, so it moves with SM count, but the bar itself is not re-tuned
per arch.
- **SM107 is unchanged by construction.** The margin applies only to the
one-head path, and GR100 is compute capability 10.7, so it keeps two
heads per step. It was not re-run for this PR.
- **The override is test-only and process-wide.** It is a private
underscore function, not a public API; the test resets it in `finally`.
- **Out of scope:** CodeRabbit's note on #6794 that the one-head step
count is modelled as `ceil((q + kv) / g)` rather than `ceil(q / g) +
ceil(kv / g)`. That undercount biases toward splitting, the direction
the margin now guards. Replaying the model, the fix changes no pick at
any multi-wave shape measured here. It does move `g` at decode sizes
(e.g. 40 to 32 at 64 tokens for 32/8 heads), so it is left for a
separately measured change.
- #6794 is in `release-v0.7.2` (0.7.2.post1), so this should be picked
there too.

### [1ce8f91](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1ce8f915659e308195cc44fe1bd8563bfff522ba)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T14:53:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP8 EP1 T32 / T128 / T512 / T1024 rank programs on sm_103a (#8669)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline for the 384-expert, top-6, hidden-5120 model with activation
clamp 10. A single kernel launch covers dispatch, FC1, clamped SwiGLU,
MXFP8 activation quantization, FC2 and weighted combine. The kernel has
four variants on main: single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8,
grouped-GEMM routes, and the TP/EP rank variant. The rank variant has 32
programs: TP4 EP1 (384 experts, width 640), TP8 EP1 (384 experts, width
384), TP4 EP4 (96 local experts) and TP8 EP8 (48 local experts), each at
1 to 4096 tokens.

This PR updates the rank variant. It changes 4 of the 32 programs, all
TP8 EP1, at 32, 128, 512 and 1024 tokens. Each FC2 ring task now covers
all four N clusters of a claimed group, so the scheduler publishes one
FC2 task per group instead of two. Every role runs its task body once
per N cluster on the same two TMEM accumulator buffers.

Outputs are bitwise identical to the previous version. The other 28 rank
programs, the other variants' programs and every host binding are
byte-identical. The catalog closure hashes of the 4 changed programs
change.

Speedup over the previous Cake version (the rank variant on FlashInfer
main after #8627), for replicates a / b:

- TP8 EP1 at 32 tokens: 1.010x / 1.009x, saving 0.90 / 0.80 µs per call
- TP8 EP1 at 128 tokens: 1.009x / 1.010x, saving 1.61 / 1.66 µs per call
- TP8 EP1 at 512 tokens: 1.006x / 1.006x, saving 1.18 / 1.07 µs per call
- TP8 EP1 at 1024 tokens: 1.004x / 1.005x, saving 0.76 / 0.91 µs per
call

All four changes are faster than the A/A noise band in both replicates.
The other 28 programs run 0.998x to 1.001x in replicate a and 0.998x to
1.003x in replicate b.

Speedup over the issue baseline, autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`: this PR is faster on all 32 shapes
in both replicates. The range is 1.021x to 1.174x in replicate a and
1.023x to 1.172x in replicate b. On the four changed shapes it is 1.173x
/ 1.167x (32 tokens), 1.160x / 1.156x (128 tokens), 1.168x / 1.163x (512
tokens) and 1.143x / 1.138x (1024 tokens).

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.159.03, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. Columns 3-8 compare this PR with the previous Cake version
(FlashInfer main after #8627), with speedup = previous / this PR.
Per-call latency comes from CUDA-graph replays (20 calls per graph),
using the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous version and this
PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6 rounds. Each value is
the median of the 6 process medians. Speedups are computed from the
latencies before they are rounded to two decimals. The savings quoted
above are the differences of the displayed latencies. Columns a and b
are two independent replicates, each run alone on its own node. Each
replicate also timed the previous version against itself (an A/A
control) to measure its noise band. The widest band is 0.18 % in
replicate a and 0.28 % in replicate b. Columns 9-14 compare autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` with this PR, with speedup = TRT-LLM
/ this PR. They come from a separate run of the same commit on the same
two nodes, so the this-PR latencies there differ slightly from columns 4
and 7. The kernels and host bindings of the 28 unchanged programs are
byte-identical to the previous version and compile to the same machine
code. One of them, TP4 EP1 at 1024 tokens (+0.016 / +0.119 µs), reads
slower than its narrow A/A band in both replicates. That is
process-level noise, not a regression.*

and grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a. The rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [c2f7cf8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c2f7cf877abd17e856569b9a1453861f24bbe4d1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T14:52:36Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dense_projection_gemm): plan cached router launches again after a router-table change (#8663)

This follow-up to #8618 fixes three review findings
([1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8618#discussion_r4467092725),
[2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8618#discussion_r4467092979),
[3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8618#discussion_r4467093185))
and builds on the #8618 head; that commit shows in the diff until #8618
merges.

**Finding 1.** With `deterministic=False`, the cache key of a planned
router (K2) launch does not record the router tables (`ROUTER_RULES`,
`ROUTER_RULES_BY_SM`). A change to a router table, or a rebind to a
plain dict, left `router_forward`, `router_dgrad`, `router_wgrad` and
`router_fp32_gemm` on the old program; outputs stayed correct.

A launch planned without a split count now keeps its router-table memo,
and a call with another memo plans the launch again. Launches with an
explicit split count read no router table and stay cached; the cached
call path adds one identity comparison per call.

**Finding 2.** The README K2 numerics rows "operands and accumulation"
and "subnormals" now describe the SIMT windows of the input and weight
gradient.

**Finding 3.** In the benchmark `plan_record`, the `kn` rule key is now
`(hidden, experts)` as in `ROUTER_RULES`, and SIMT plans report `tiles`
as `m_tiles * n_tiles`.

A CPU test changes a router-table verdict between two calls through the
entry points and `router_fp32_gemm`; the second call must run the new
plan. With the #8618 head's `cake_backend.py` the test fails in all 12
cases (stale launch); with this PR's it passes in all 12. A GPU test
checks by kernel name that the new program runs, and a dump of every K1
and router plan matches the #8618 head.

## Host-path parity

This checks that the cached call path did not get slower. Each cell
times a host-bound eager entry-point call (`deterministic=False`), with
previous (#8618 head, f7b1cd3c) and new (this PR, e84deee1) paired in
one process on an NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs; driver 580.126.20;
CUDA 13.4, nvcc 13.4.92; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130; SM clock 2062 MHz on all
4 GPUs for the whole run, no power capping). The timer is the CUPTI op
span (first kernel start to last kernel end of the call), with cold L2
before every iteration, 15 paired groups x 20 iterations and a median
per run. The previous and new times are medians over 8 runs (2 sessions
x 4 processes). The previous/new column is the median over the 8 runs of
each run's previous/new ratio (above 1 = new faster). The A/A band is
the min-max of that ratio over 8 A/A runs in which both arms are the new
code.

| shape (in -> out, tokens) | operation | previous us | new us |
previous/new | A/A band |

38.20 | 1.009 | 0.979-1.032 |

12 of 14 cells, including all 8 router cells, are inside the A/A band
and none is below it. The 4096 -> 128 and 4096 -> 512 checkpointed steps

### [8e7be5e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8e7be5e3a832fdf5d872cb01b05d6d3c5906b974)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T14:23:23Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn): packed-triangular forward WY program at five CTAs per SM on B200 and GB300 (#8665)

Cake ships four GDN training variants in FlashInfer: a non-deterministic
and a deterministic form, each as a single-rank package and a
context-parallel (KCP) package. This PR changes the non-deterministic
single-rank package `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gdn_train`. On
sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300), its forward WY stage now runs the
packed-triangular WY program at five CTAs per SM (`wy_tc2`). The
deterministic package `flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train`
already runs this program (#8615). On sm_107a (R200), the package keeps
the previous WY program. In every timed configuration, the output and
the gradients of q, k, v, g and beta are bitwise equal to the previous
version.

Every ratio is baseline ms / this PR ms, so a value above 1 means this
PR is faster. ckpt is the checkpointed step. The tables use three
baselines:
- "Deterministic Cake" is the deterministic package at FlashInfer main
4046a863.
- "Non-Cake SOTA" is chosen per cell. It is the fastest
accuracy-qualified implementation among FLA 0.6.0 (Triton) and the GDN
from cuDNN frontend 1.32.1 (FROST) in two modes: states recomputed
("cuDNN FROST" in the tables) or states stored every 64 tokens ("cuDNN
FROST (chunk 64)"). FlashQLA 0.1.3, timed earlier on one shape on B200
and GB300, was slower than both cuDNN FROST modes there, so it is not
among the candidates. In the published cells, it is cuDNN FROST in fwd
and cuDNN FROST (chunk 64) in fwd+bwd and ckpt. Where this comparison
was not stable enough to publish, the table shows "unstable (not
published)" and no ratio.
- "Previous" is this package at the same main commit.

Against deterministic Cake and the previous version, a cell counts as
faster or slower only when both opposite-order runs fall outside the
spread of an A/A run of this PR against itself. Where a longer sustained
run exists, that run decides. All other cells are at parity. Each cell's
class (faster, parity or slower) comes from that cell's own A/A spread,
so a ratio below 1 can be parity in one cell and slower in another.
Non-Cake SOTA results are plain ratios with no class.

On B200, the forward is 1.005-1.045 against the previous version with
FP32 beta and 1.028-1.043 with BF16 beta. With FP32 beta, fwd+bwd is
0.987-1.024 and ckpt is 0.991-1.031. With BF16 beta, fwd+bwd is
1.001-1.032 and ckpt is 0.983-1.058. Against deterministic Cake, the
FP32-beta ranges are 0.998-1.012 (fwd), 0.992-1.112 (fwd+bwd) and
0.988-1.077 (ckpt). The BF16-beta ranges are 0.997-1.004, 0.987-1.114
and 0.986-1.057. Against non-Cake SOTA, the ratio is above 1 in every
published fwd+bwd cell: 1.076-1.559 in 7 FP32-beta cells and 1.058-1.695
in 4 BF16-beta cells. In ckpt, it is above 1 in 6 of 7 FP32-beta cells
(1.148-1.418) and 3 of 4 BF16-beta cells (1.083-1.459). In the remaining
ckpt cell of each set (16 x 4096, H/HV 16/32) it is below 1, at 0.938
and 0.917. In fwd, it is below 1 in 7 of 9 published FP32-beta cells
(0.489-0.970) and 8 of 10 BF16-beta cells (0.481-0.952). It is above 1
in the other 2 fwd cells of each set (1.172-1.297 and 1.143-1.268).

On GB300, the forward is 1.013-1.039 against the previous version with
FP32 beta and 1.022-1.039 with BF16 beta. With FP32 beta, fwd+bwd is
0.985-1.017 and ckpt is 0.986-1.021. With BF16 beta, fwd+bwd is
1.005-1.019 and ckpt is 0.997-1.020. Against deterministic Cake, the
FP32-beta ranges are 0.993-1.043 (fwd), 0.990-1.111 (fwd+bwd) and
0.992-1.080 (ckpt). The BF16-beta ranges are 0.996-1.007, 0.993-1.175
and 0.999-1.109. Against non-Cake SOTA, the ratio is above 1 in every
published fwd+bwd cell: 1.053-2.013 in 12 FP32-beta cells and
1.164-1.984 in 4 BF16-beta cells. It is also above 1 in all 9 published
FP32-beta ckpt cells (1.002-1.699), but three of them are only
1.002-1.018. No BF16-beta ckpt cell has a published non-Cake timing. In
fwd, it is below 1 in all 5 published cells: 0.570-0.832 in 4 FP32-beta
cells and 0.620 in 1 BF16-beta cell.

On B200 and GB300, no cell is slower than the previous version. The
fwd+bwd and ckpt cells below 1.000 are at parity. The lowest is B200
BF16-beta 4 x 4096, H/HV 8/16 ckpt, at 0.983.

Five cells are still slower than deterministic Cake:
- B200, FP32 beta, 6 seqs, 241817 tokens, H/HV 2/6, fwd+bwd: 0.992
- B200, FP32 beta, 64 x 4096, H/HV 2/6, fwd+bwd: 0.992
- B200, FP32 beta, 64 x 4096, H/HV 2/6, ckpt: 0.988
- GB300, FP32 beta, 64 x 4096, H/HV 2/6, ckpt: 0.992
- GB300, BF16 beta, 7 x ~4.3k (real pack), H/HV 8/16, fwd+bwd: 0.993

On B200, the first three of these cells are slower in the sustained run
at the board power limit; the short runs shown in the table are within
the A/A spread. On these workloads, the forward now launches the same
programs as the deterministic package and is at parity with it
(0.998-1.000). The deterministic package uses different backward forms
there. The other cells below 1.000 against deterministic Cake on B200
and GB300 (0.986-0.999) are at parity.

R200 was timed with FP32 beta only; this PR does not change the R200
program. On R200 (sm_107a), the package keeps the previous WY program,
and every cell is at parity with the previous version (0.994-1.001).
Against deterministic Cake, it is 1.000-1.186. Against non-Cake SOTA,
the ratio is above 1 in all 19 fwd+bwd cells (1.258-2.527) and all 14
published ckpt cells (1.106-2.066). In fwd, it is below 1 in 12 of 16
published cells (0.452-0.860) and above 1 in the other 4 (1.155-1.291).

### [a8e34e4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a8e34e4863344639dc7e49ff01e37e1a832c5c24)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T14:19:24Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): K=64 FP8 MMA program for the SM107 128-head uniform-gather persistent route (#8668)

The Cake backend of `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` has 49
programs with this PR: BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128
query heads (several bodies per head count, picked per shape by the host
route) and an NVFP4-KV decode family. With this PR, sm_107a ships six
FP8 programs for the DeepSeek-V4 decode route: the two 128-head
persistent programs (lane-issued gathers, uniform gathers), the new K=64
program, the 64-head single-CTA M64 single-tile and multi-tile programs,
and the SWA low-head prefill program. This PR adds a K=64 sibling of the
sm_107a FP8 128-head uniform-gather persistent program
(`cake_dsv4_7074d4c5b808db91fcba`, loader key
`fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent_uniform_k64`). Every MMA in the new
program is a one-CTA M128 tile that uses the K=64 FP8 instruction. The
existing program's two-CTA M128 MMAs run at K=32 on sm_107a. On sm_107a,
launches of the uniform-gather persistent route with at least 48 query
rows run the new program. Shorter launches keep the existing K=32
program, because below 48 rows the new program was slower when calls run
back to back. The FP8 64-head rows that FlashInfer sends to this route
follow the same rule. Launches of 128 rows and more (the lane-issued
program) are unchanged, and so are sm_100a and sm_103a. Speedups are
measured against the previous Cake program, the K=32 uniform-gather
program `cake_dsv4_4a6718b7a2ca825d8800` (FlashInfer main bc4e12b3).

VR200 (sm_107a, 208 SMs), CUDA 13.4. The shapes come from the
DeepSeek-V4 decode tests' input helpers with an FP8 query and KV cache
and a 32768-token context, where rows = batch x q_len and q_len is 4
except in the 1- and 8-row rows (q_len 1). Each time is per call, from
eight back-to-back calls with `enable_pdl=True` in one CUDA graph with
L2 flushed before each graph launch, taking the median of 4 alternating
rounds; speedup = previous / this PR. The "program" column says which
program the row runs, rows below 48 run the unchanged program, and
outputs are bitwise equal to the previous program's on every row.
