### [576e064](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/576e0649a8128c7294282f404630936fd782f09f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T14:10:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): store the 5120 -> 17408 input gradient's overlapped tiles through the TMA store at T 16231 and 16384 on sm_103a (#8667)

This PR adds row rules to the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package
in `flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM.
Most programs in the package are BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and
wgrad), and one is an FP32 router GEMM. The PR adds no new program,
kernel source or library. It adds 2 row rules for `sm_103a`. Each rule
applies at a single token count T, either 16231 or 16384. The rules move
the 5120→17408 input gradient (dgrad, BF16 output) to the overlapped
half-tail program with the same K split. That program uses a
column-grouped raster with groups of 12 column tiles, and its BF16
output tiles go through a one-slot TMA-store epilogue. Before this PR,
these rows used the existing ragged rule's row-half program. The package
already has the `sm_103a` library for the overlapped half-tail program.
It was added for the `sm_100a` rules of the same rows, but until now no
rule selected it on `sm_103a`. The rule count goes from 376 to 378. The
`sm_100a` and `sm_107a` rules are unchanged. The baseline is the
previous Cake version of the package on main. Against it, the changed
rows have a speedup of 1.010–1.011 on GB300. On B300 they measure
1.007–1.008, which is below the run-to-run noise threshold of that
measurement. No changed row is slower on either GPU, and outputs on
those rows are bitwise identical to main. All other rows of the 294-row
shape list plan the same programs as main on `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and
`sm_107a`.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB300
(`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), B300 (`sm_103a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2,
BF16 output. Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1
mean this PR is faster.

| layer (in→out) | op | out | T | GB300 previous µs | GB300 this PR µs |
GB300 speedup | B300 previous µs | B300 this PR µs | B300 speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5120→17408 | dgrad (input gradient) | bf16 | 16231 | 1427.4 | 1413.3 |
1.010 | 1612.5 | 1601.5 | 1.007 |
| 5120→17408 | dgrad (input gradient) | bf16 | 16384 | 1431.1 | 1415.6 |
1.011 | 1618.4 | 1606.3 | 1.008 |

The package also ships FP32-output forms, weight-gradient (wgrad)
programs and the FP32 router GEMM (run through BF16x3 emulation), on
`sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

### [eeed657](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/eeed657f157b0803ffe61df56ffe5ccf1196d2a1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T13:30:17Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det): glm_bwd_prep v11_g8 runs the KCP saved-rstd backward's replay prep on sm_100a / sm_103a (#8652)

`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train` is the deterministic Cake KDA (Kimi
Delta Attention) chunked training package. It has four variants. The Q/K
L2 norm is either done by the caller or fused in the kernel
(`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`). Each of these comes with either the g
gate or the raw gate (`use_gate_in_kernel`). Every variant has forward,
backward and checkpoint entries, and the package also has a
context-parallel (KCP) form. This PR changes one path: the fused
in-kernel Q/K L2 norm variant with the g gate, in the KCP backward that
reads the saved per-row rstd. In that path, the replay prep stage now
runs glm_bwd_prep v11_g8 (`bwd_prep_g8_replay_saved_l2n`) on sm_100a and
sm_103a. It replaces glm_bwd_prep v8_g8 (`bwd_prep_g8_replay_l2n`).
Against FlashInfer main, the stage is 1.081x to 1.147x faster.
Single-rank calls never select the new record, so single-rank timing
does not change.

ABBA order, median per call. The ratio column is the median of per-pair
after/before ratios, with its min and max. ckpt = forward + recomputed
forward + backward. Two rows differ from 1.000 by more than their pair
range: T=16384, 1 sequence bwd (1.0023) and T=16384, 4 sequences fwd
(0.9972). They point in opposite directions on code paths that did not
change, so they are run-to-run variance.*

The family also includes the non-deterministic `cake_kda_train` package
and the KCP form of both packages, and it ships on sm_100a (B200,
GB200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a (R200), while v11_g8 ships on
sm_100a and sm_103a only and sm_107a keeps v8_g8.

Follow-up to #7817

* **New Features**
* Added support for saved-statistics Q/K normalization during replay
preparation on select GPU architectures.
* Launch reporting now identifies when this specialized preparation
variant is used.

architecture-specific support is available; otherwise, preparation
continues to use the existing variant.

### [212d236](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/212d236dabfd9591160d1b42376e1fa649434515)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T13:17:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): two-split K1 weight gradient for the wide FP32 rows on 212-SM sm_107a (#8657)

The Cake dense projection GEMM package
(`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`, the non-deterministic
schedule) has two GEMM families. The first is a BF16 weight-gradient
GEMM. It has BF16 or FP32 output, tile widths 64, 128, 192 and 256, and
one or more K splits whose partial sums are added in arrival order. The
second is an FP32 router GEMM for the forward pass, input gradient and
weight gradient. It uses BF16x3 split-precision stream-K and head/tail
programs, plus an exact-FP32 CUDA-core program for the router weight
gradient at few tokens. This PR changes the FP32-output weight gradient
of four projection rows on 212-SM sm_107a parts: 4096 -> 512, 5120 ->
512, 4096 -> 1024 and 5120 -> 1024 (BF16 in, FP32 out). Before this PR,
these rows ran the deterministic program at these token counts on 212
SMs. The new planner table `K1_SPLIT_EVEN_BLOCK_RANGES_BY_SM` routes
them to two K splits with the row's tile width. Rows 4096 -> 512 and
5120 -> 512 use tile width 128 at 1024 to 8192 tokens and 32768 to 65536
tokens. Row 4096 -> 1024 uses tile width 192 at 2048 to 8192 tokens and
32768 to 65536 tokens. Row 5120 -> 1024 uses tile width 256 at 1024 to
8192 tokens. The route applies only when the token count covers an even
number of 64-token K blocks (ceil(T / 64) even). Odd block counts, token
counts outside these ranges, other SM counts and other rows keep their
previous plan, which here is the deterministic program. At every
measured even block count from 1024 tokens up, the two-split output is
bit-for-bit equal to the deterministic program's output. Across the 21
routed points in eager and graph modes, the speedup against the
deterministic Cake program is x1.06-1.70 on the weight gradient. It is
x1.04-1.53 on the backward pass (input gradient + weight gradient) and
x1.02-1.27 on the checkpointed step (2 forward + input gradient + weight
gradient). Against the non-Cake SOTA, the fastest accurate library
route, the same ratios are x0.41-0.91, x0.51-0.95 and x0.51-0.96. The
non-Cake library routes are faster than the new program on every row.

Latencies are in microseconds. Timing uses CUPTI kernel timings, with
the L2 cache flushed before every timed iteration (cold L2), for both
eager launches and CUDA graph replays. Each run takes the median of 15
paired groups of 20 timed iterations for the weight gradient, and of 9
paired groups for the backward pass and the checkpointed step. Each
table cell is the median over eight runs: four GPUs on each of two R200
nodes. "Deterministic Cake" is the deterministic Cake dense projection
package, with its current programs, for every GEMM of the operation. The
new program's backward pass and checkpointed step use this package's
forward and input-gradient plans plus the new weight gradient. For the
weight gradient, "non-Cake SOTA" is the fastest library launch in each
mode. The candidates are torch.mm (cuBLAS heuristic) and the cuBLASLt
heuristic's top 8 algorithms whose output is within 1e-3 relative
Frobenius error of FP64. For the backward pass and the checkpointed
step, each GEMM of the step uses its fastest such library launch, chosen
by CUDA-event pre-timing. The library is cuBLAS 13.8. Each speedup is
the baseline latency divided by the new program's latency, so a value
below 1 means the baseline is faster. As a noise check, the
deterministic weight gradient was measured against a second copy of
itself (A/A), giving x0.984-1.010 per point (time ratio, both modes). As
a previous-plan check, the step was run with the deterministic weight
gradient, which is this package's plan before this PR. The backward pass
measured x0.987-1.014 and the checkpointed step x0.988-1.047 of the
deterministic package's time (time ratio; values above 1 are slower).
Programmatic dependent launch is enabled in every Cake launch, which is
the sm_107a default. GPU: R200, sm_107a, 212 SMs, driver 620.43. CUDA
13.0 runtime with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130; kernels built with CUDA 13.4.
The GPUs ran at the default power limit of 2300 W per GPU, and the SM
clock was not locked (maximum 2424 MHz). nvidia-smi was sampled every 2
seconds during the runs. The mean busy SM clock was 2337-2384 MHz per
node run (minimum 1032 MHz), and the software power-cap throttle reason
was set in 229 of 2668 samples.

This PR leaves the BF16-output weight gradients, the other FP32
weight-gradient rows and SM counts, and the FP32 router programs
unchanged; the package ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [3bd4dbd](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3bd4dbdbb5658e260b102816efe0c6edc2693c99)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T13:16:08Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm): blocked FP32 dw sums for the large-T GB300 and R200 backward (#8655)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). The two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`, use the same forward and differ only in the
backward. Both modes support these forms on sm_100a (B200), sm_103a
(GB300) and sm_107a (R200):

- [T, H] rows with BF16 weight, or FP32 weight (`w32`)
- fused residual add (`res`, H6144)
- per-head views [T,24,256] (strided) and [T,4,256] (contiguous), with a
shared w[256]

This follow-up to #8577 and #8626 changes only the `deterministic=False`
backward at large T, on sm_103a and sm_107a. The bounds of the windows
below are unchanged. In each one, the backward now runs a new
single-kernel program (kblock pipe, blocked FP32 dw sums) in place of
the previous non-deterministic program:

- GB300 (sm_103a): H4096 with BF16 weight, T > 50176; H4096 `w32`, T >
9216; H5120 with either weight dtype, T > 61952.
- R200 (sm_107a): H5120 with either weight dtype, T > 49152.

This PR does not change the sm_100a (B200) routes or programs, so it has
no B200 table. The forward and the deterministic package are also
unchanged.

Speedup = baseline latency / new latency. A value > 1 means the new
kernel is faster. Geomeans over the shapes of the changed windows, vs
deterministic / vs SOTA:

- GB300 (12 shapes): fwd 0.999x / 0.994x, bwd 0.996x / 1.124x, 2xfwd+bwd
1.000x / 1.069x
- R200 (8 shapes): fwd 1.001x / 0.930x, bwd 0.951x / 1.371x, 2xfwd+bwd
0.978x / 1.207x

Against the program each window replaces, for the GB300 H4096 and R200
H5120 windows. These numbers come from a separate route screen on
another node of the same type: 4 sessions, with s2 and s4 in reverse
order. Compare its ratios with the tables below, not its latencies.
Values are previous -> new bwd latency (previous/new):

- GB300 H4096, BF16 weight: 257.4245 -> 254.2535 us at T65536 (1.0125x),
376.5300 -> 373.1205 us at T98304 (1.0091x), 498.1615 -> 494.3530 us at
T131072 (1.0077x)
- GB300 H4096 `w32`: 76.6405 -> 72.9120 us at T16384 (1.0511x), 136.0490
-> 131.6020 us at T32768 (1.0338x), 258.7055 -> 253.8730 us at T65536
(1.0190x)
- R200 H5120, BF16 weight: 301.4755 -> 170.1305 us at T65536 (1.7720x),
447.5260 -> 242.9000 us at T98304 (1.8424x), 594.8560 -> 323.3485 us at
T131072 (1.8397x)
- R200 H5120 `w32`: 297.7805 -> 175.9865 us at T65536 (1.6921x),
441.5740 -> 251.1555 us at T98304 (1.7582x), 586.7600 -> 334.8205 us at
T131072 (1.7525x)
- The new program was faster in every session. Per-session ratios were
1.00738 to 1.05222 on GB300 and 1.68171 to 1.85670 on R200.
- The R200 screen did not include T55296. At T53248 and T57344, the
per-session ratios were 1.75861 to 1.80047 with BF16 weight and 1.68194
to 1.72597 with `w32`.

Notable rows:

- Rows slower than det. In these windows det runs faster programs, but
at some T in these windows those programs do not meet the per-element dw
accuracy bar that the non-deterministic mode requires of its own
programs: the worst dw element must stay within 0.85 of the per-element
dw budget defined below. The non-deterministic mode therefore cannot
route to them. This PR narrows the gap to det but does not close it.
Latencies are new vs det:
- GB300 H4096, BF16 weight, bwd: 254.69 vs 249.97 us at T65536, 374.91
vs 368.90 us at T98304 and 494.75 vs 487.06 us at T131072 (0.98x each).
H4096 `w32` T65536 bwd: 254.27 vs 250.19 us (0.98x). On these four rows
new is slower in all 4 sessions. The other GB300 bwd rows read 0.99x to
1.01x. Of these, only H5120 `w32` T65536 bwd (314.69 vs 312.58 us,
0.99x) is also slower in all 4 sessions. All GB300 2xfwd+bwd rows read
0.99x to 1.02x.
- R200: every bwd row is slower, 0.96x to 0.97x with BF16 weight and
0.93x to 0.95x with `w32`. The 2xfwd+bwd rows read 0.97x to 0.99x. The
largest gap is H5120 T65536 `w32` bwd: 175.71 vs 163.52 us (0.93x).
- Rows below SOTA:
- GB300 H4096 T65536 bwd (BF16 weight): 254.69 vs 246.38 us (QuACK
autotuned, 0.97x).
- GB300 H4096 T131072 bwd (BF16 weight): 494.75 vs 490.08 us
(torch.compile, 0.99x).
  - The 2xfwd+bwd rows of these two shapes read 0.99x.
- Every other bwd and 2xfwd+bwd row is at or above 1.00x vs SOTA. GB300
reaches up to 1.22x on bwd and 1.12x on 2xfwd+bwd. R200 reads 1.31x to
1.45x on bwd and 1.12x to 1.32x on 2xfwd+bwd.
- The forward, which this PR does not change, is below SOTA on 9 of 12
GB300 shapes (lowest 0.985x) and on 8 of 8 R200 shapes (0.903x to
1.000x).
- R200 candidates outside the budget. QuACK autotuned is faster than new
on the four `w32` bwd rows and on all eight 2xfwd+bwd rows. Its dw is
outside the budget there (dw err/tol 1.108 to 2.476 over 5 seeds), so it
is not SOTA. All 16 R200 bwd and 2xfwd+bwd rows are marked `o`. On the
four BF16 bwd rows, the out-of-budget candidates beat the SOTA shown but
not new. The candidates are listed below the R200 table.

Baselines and measurement. Every row has two baselines:

- det: the deterministic Cake kernel (`deterministic=True`). On every
row here it launches the same GPU programs as current FlashInfer main.
- SOTA: per row, the fastest non-Cake candidate that has the same
outputs (BF16 y / dx, FP32 rstd / dw) and meets the accuracy budget.
Every applicable candidate is timed on every row. Configurations that
return dw in the weight dtype (the public PyTorch, Liger, QuACK and TE
APIs on BF16-weight rows) do not have matched outputs and are never
chosen.

new = the non-deterministic Cake kernel (`deterministic=False`) with
this PR's programs. The accuracy budget takes the worst of 5 seeds: dx
atol = rtol = 1e-2, and dw per element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64.

Latency = median of the CUPTI spans pooled over 4 sessions (s1 to s4) on
the 4 GPUs of one node. One span is one CUDA-graph replay after an L2
flush (cold L2), and it includes the implementation's own setup,
reduction, cast and copy kernels. eps = 1e-6. Latencies print to 0.01 us
and per-row ratios to 0.01x. The summary geomeans use the unrounded
medians. On GB300, s1 and s3 run the rows in order and s2 and s4 run
them in reverse, each in 3 interleaved rounds. The implementation order
rotates so that every implementation takes every position equally often,
so no implementation gets a better or worse slot from a fixed order. On
the fwd rows, where both modes launch the same programs, det/new reads
0.993 to 1.002 on GB300 and 1.000 to 1.002 on R200.

torch.compile in the process. All implementations of a row run in one
process that also loads every non-Cake candidate, including
torch.compile. The check reported in #8577 (B200 and GB300) found that a
torch.compile function in the process makes every non-compile
implementation run faster. On small rows, the Cake kernels gain somewhat
more than the other non-compile libraries, so the ratio vs those
libraries reads up to about 1.10x (GB300) and 1.14x (B200) higher than
in a process without torch.compile. On large rows this difference is at
most 1.02x, and every row here is large (T >= 16384). Ratios vs det are
not affected, because both are Cake kernels in the same process.

Key:

- Shapes: x [T, H] is BF16, and w is BF16 or FP32 (`w32`). `plain` = no
residual. y / dx are BF16, and rstd / dw are FP32.
- op: `2xfwd+bwd (checkpointed)` = two forwards and one backward.
- `=` after the op: det and new launch the same GPU programs (every fwd
row). The printed ratios are measured values; none is set to 1.00x.
- SOTA:
- torch.compile = torch.compile (torch 2.14.1+cu130, inductor
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, emulate_precision_casts=True) of an explicit
FP32-statistics reference. In the R200 table it is labelled
torch.compile (inductor).
- torch.compile (default mode) = the same in torch.compile default mode.
In the R200 table it is labelled torch.compile default mode (inductor).
  - QuACK = QuACK 0.6.5 (nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1), heuristic config.
- QuACK autotuned = QuACK 0.6.5 exhaustive per-shape autotune
(rmsnorm_fwd_tuned / rmsnorm_bwd_tuned, cached before timing).
- Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton 3.8.0, casting_mode gemma) and Transformer
Engine 2.20.2 (run as the FP32 problem, with the casts inside its span)
were never fastest.
- PyTorch's fused rms_norm cannot run this form (BF16 x with FP32 w).
Apex FusedRMSNorm has no wheel. FlashInfer's inference rmsnorm is
forward only.
- `o` (R200): a non-Cake candidate faster than the SOTA shown fails the
dw budget on this row. These candidates are listed below the R200 table.

- **作者**: eigen

### [d56cbcf](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d56cbcf649a4483020cef8df2f2c88aa8985cee6)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T13:07:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): FFMA router input gradient up to 64-128 tokens on sm_100a/sm_107a (#8618)

The Cake dense projection GEMM package has two GEMM families for MoE
layers. The first is the BF16 weight-gradient GEMM, with BF16 or FP32
output and several tile widths. The second is the FP32 router GEMM,
which covers forward, input gradient and weight gradient using BF16x3
split precision with stream-K and head/tail schedules. The previous PR
added an exact-FP32 FFMA program on the CUDA cores for the router weight
gradient. This PR adds an exact-FP32 FFMA program on the CUDA cores for
the router input gradient. It covers FP32, 256 experts and hidden 4096,
5120 or 6144. The planner routes to it on 152-SM sm_100a parts and
212-SM sm_107a parts. On both, it covers hidden 4096 and 5120 from 1 to
128 tokens and hidden 6144 from 1 to 64 tokens. Other parts, including
sm_103a, and other token counts keep their previous plan. On GB200, the
measured token counts are 1, 17, 32, 64, 96 and 128 at hidden 4096 and
5120. At hidden 6144, they are 1, 17, 32 and 64. Over all measured GB200
rows, eager and graph, the speedup against the deterministic Cake router
program is x1.09-1.97 on the input gradient. It is x1.43-3.25 on the
full backward (input + weight gradient) and x1.11-1.30 on a checkpointed
step (2 forward + backward). Against the fastest accurate non-Cake
library route, the same ratios are x0.72-1.35, x0.66-1.63 and
x0.26-0.92. Against this package's previous plan, they are x1.09-1.97,
x1.04-1.58 and x1.01-1.08. On the input gradient alone, the library
route is faster at 1 token (x0.72-0.76). The new program is faster at 17
and 32 tokens (x1.14-1.35). On R200, the measured token counts are the
same as on GB200. Over all 96 measured R200 rows, eager and graph, the
speedup against the deterministic Cake router program is x1.41-2.60 on
the input gradient. It is x1.63-3.32 on the full backward and x1.13-1.34
on a checkpointed step. Against the fastest accurate non-Cake library
route, the same ratios are x0.85-1.68, x0.77-1.36 and x0.28-0.74.
Against this package's previous plan, they are x1.41-2.60, x1.17-1.88
and x1.03-1.13. On R200, the library route is faster only at 1 token on
the input gradient (x0.85-0.87) and the full backward (x0.77-0.81). As
on GB200, it is faster on every checkpointed-step row.

Latencies are in microseconds. Each run takes the median of 15 paired
groups of 20 timed iterations. It uses CUPTI kernel spans, a cold L2,
and both eager launches and CUDA graph replays. Each cell is the median
over runs: four runs of each Cake program and two runs of each library
route per cuBLAS build. "Deterministic Cake" is this package's
deterministic router program for both GEMMs of the backward. "Previous
plan" is this package's plan before this PR at the same shape and token
count. It already includes the previous PR's weight-gradient program.
"Non-Cake SOTA" is, for each operation, the fastest FP32 library route
within the router accuracy budget. That budget is a relative Frobenius
error of at most 2e-6 against FP64 over 5 seeds. The candidate routes
are cublasSgemm, cuBLASLt FP32 (best of the heuristic's top 8), torch.mm
FP32 without TF32 and cuBLAS FP32 in BF16x9 emulation. On GB200, each
route runs with cuBLAS 13.8 and 13.1. On R200, both library builds load
cuBLAS 13.8, so every library route runs with cuBLAS 13.8. The SOTA
route column names the winning route, and "fastest per GEMM" means the
fastest route is chosen per GEMM. Each speedup is the baseline latency
divided by the new program's latency, so a value below 1 means the
baseline is faster. The forward and weight-gradient GEMMs run the same
programs in the previous plan and in this PR. That A/A comparison varied
by x0.980-1.027 per run and cell on GB200 (256 cells). On GB200, across
the four runs, the fastest library route's eager latency on the full
backward and the checkpointed step varied by up to x2.57 per cell. This
ratio is the slowest run divided by the fastest run. Every other GB200
library cell, the input gradient and all graph rows, varied by at most
x1.20. GB200 is NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs). The runs used the CUDA
13.0 runtime with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, and the kernels were built with
CUDA 13.4. R200 is NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs). The R200 runs used
the same CUDA 13.0 runtime, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and CUDA 13.4 kernel
build. On R200, the A/A comparison varied by x0.967-1.033 per run and
cell (256 cells). The fastest library route's latency varied by at most
x1.06 per cell across R200 runs. The new program's input gradient meets
the same accuracy budget.

The other Cake programs (the BF16 weight-gradient GEMM, the BF16x3
router programs and the FFMA router weight-gradient program) are
unchanged; the package ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [e58f187](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e58f1872388b2c9c89573878a56dd965b45157ef)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T12:38:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): store the 12288 -> 4096 forward's overlapped tiles through the TMA store at T 16231 and 16384 on sm_100a (#8660)

This PR adds a program and row rules to the Cake
`dense_projection_det_gemm` package in `flashinfer.experimental`, the
deterministic dense projection GEMM. Most programs in the package are
BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and wgrad), and one is an FP32 router
GEMM. The new program is an overlapped half-tail forward program with
K-major B. It uses a column-grouped raster with groups of 8 column
tiles, and its BF16 output tiles go through a one-slot TMA-store
epilogue. It is the K-major-B twin of the overlapped TMA-store program
that the package already ships for the 5120→17408 input gradient. It
comes from one new kernel source, compiled for `sm_100a` only. With it,
the package's kernel sources go from 108 to 109 and its compiled
libraries from 272 to 273. The PR adds 2 row rules for `sm_100a`. Each
rule applies at a single token count T, either 16231 or 16384. The rules
move the 12288→4096 forward (BF16 output) to the new program with the
same K split. Before this PR, these rows used the existing ragged rule's
program, which is the same overlapped half-tail column-grouped program
without the TMA store. The rule count goes from 374 to 376. The
`sm_103a` and `sm_107a` rules are unchanged. The baseline is the
previous Cake version of the package on main. Against it, the changed
rows have a speedup of 1.009–1.010 on GB200 and 1.008 on B200. No
changed row is slower on either GPU, and outputs on those rows are
bitwise identical to main. All other rows of the 294-row shape list plan
the same programs as main on `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2,
BF16 output. Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1
mean this PR is faster.

| shape (K→N) | op | out | T | GB200 previous µs | GB200 this PR µs |
GB200 speedup | B200 previous µs | B200 this PR µs | B200 speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12288→4096 | forward | bf16 | 16231 | 921.7 | 913.0 | 1.010 | 986.8 |
979.3 | 1.008 |
| 12288→4096 | forward | bf16 | 16384 | 933.9 | 925.9 | 1.009 | 1000.4 |
992.0 | 1.008 |

The package also ships FP32-output forms, weight-gradient (wgrad)
programs and the FP32 router GEMM (run through BF16x3 emulation), on
`sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

### [f266f13](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f266f1335f008214bf81639c9b62508ff8952a16)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T12:35:06Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_kcp): with grad, full-save forward writes the output and the tapes in one walk (#8644)

Cake ships four GDN training variants in FlashInfer. Each comes in a
non-deterministic and a deterministic form, and each form has a
single-rank package and a context-parallel (KCP) package. This PR
changes the non-deterministic KCP package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp`. With `save_mode="full"`, a
forward with grad now runs one fused walk. That walk writes the output
and also the h and v_new tapes that the backward reads. Before, the
forward ran a tape walk and then a separate output pass. The light save
mode is unchanged, and outputs and every input gradient stay bitwise
equal to the previous version.

"Previous" is this package at FlashInfer main f2926f20. Ratios are
previous / this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is faster. In table
A, no cell is slower than previous on any GPU. On B200 and GB300, 23 of
27 cells are faster and 4 are at parity. On a 212-SM R200, all 27 cells
are faster. The parity cells are all contiguous-layout cells of shapes H
and I, at CP8 on B200 and CP4 on GB300. The forward gains the most:
1.004-1.104 on B200, 1.011-1.111 on GB300 and 1.024-1.103 on R200. On
every GPU the best cell is shape G at CP1: 5.899 -> 5.344 ms on B200,
5.522 -> 4.972 ms on GB300 and 3.252 -> 2.947 ms on R200. fwd+bwd gains
1.003-1.042 on B200, 1.002-1.043 on GB300 and 1.011-1.038 on R200. The
checkpointed step (ckpt) gains 1.004-1.041, 1.001-1.032 and 1.007-1.030
on the same three GPUs.

det(main) is the deterministic KCP package of the same main, and this PR
does not change it. In table A this PR is faster than or equal to
det(main) in every cell. The det(main) / this PR ratio runs from 1.000
to 1.645 (R200 shape I CP4 C fwd+bwd, 2.913 -> 1.771 ms). In table B,
det(main) is faster in one cell: B200 shape H CP8 C fwd, at 1.542 ms vs
1.552 ms for this PR (0.994). In table A the same cell is 1.530 ms on
both sides.

Table B also compares this PR with the strongest accuracy-qualified
non-Cake arm. Its ratios are non-Cake / this PR, so a value below 1
means the non-Cake arm is faster. At CP1, that arm is a head split
around the cuDNN frontend GDN (FROST) in every published cell, and it
runs in the same process as this PR. Table B has nine B200 CP1 cells for
shapes A, G and M, and seven of them were measured under the sustained
protocol. In those nine cells, det(main) / this PR is 1.015-1.123, and
FROST is faster than this PR in all nine, at 0.348-0.832. Across the
three GPUs, FROST is faster than this PR in 24 of the 26 published CP1
cells, at 0.283-0.933. The widest gap is R200 shape A fwd: 1.885 ms for
FROST vs 6.663 ms for this PR. At CP1 this PR is ahead only in R200
fwd+bwd on shapes G and M (1.019 and 1.026).

At CP > 1, the strongest applicable non-Cake arm is FlashQLA 0.1.3 with
dual context parallelism (inter- and intra-rank), in the contiguous
layout. It was measured on B200 at CP8 and on GB300 at CP4. In the
forward at CP > 1, this PR trails FlashQLA in every measured cell.
FlashQLA / this PR is 0.736-0.849 on B200 CP8 and 0.738-0.888 on GB300
CP4. The widest gap is at shape H: 1.142 ms vs 1.552 ms on B200 CP8, and
1.883 ms vs 2.552 ms on GB300 CP4. This PR is faster in fwd+bwd, where
FlashQLA / this PR is 1.043-1.124 on B200 CP8 and 1.084-1.208 on GB300
CP4. It is also faster in ckpt, at 1.034-1.040 and 1.008-1.128. Layout D
(per-document zigzag) cells are not claimed because FlashQLA has no
zigzag layout. The R200 CP4 non-Cake cells are not claimed because
FlashQLA has no sm_107a build. For both of these groups, table B shows
the best in-process arm as a note only.

# Non-deterministic GDN training (KCP), save_mode="full": one fused walk
writes the output and the tapes, performance

this PR = the non-deterministic KCP package of this PR (a
save_mode="full" forward that keeps its saved set runs one walk that
writes the output and the h / v_new tapes); previous = the
non-deterministic KCP package before this PR (tape walk, then the output
program); A/A = a second copy of previous (noise control); det(main) =
the deterministic KCP package of main (unchanged by this PR). All Cake
arms of a run share one process. Outputs and every input gradient of
this PR are bitwise equal to previous in every timed configuration.

Workloads: BF16 q / k / v, head dim 128, save_mode="full", in-kernel Q /
K L2 norm (use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True), eager, GDN layer only (no
conv1d); layouts C = contiguous, D = per-document zigzag; CPn = context
parallel over n GPUs. Time = median over 5 groups x 12 samples (10
warm-up calls, L2 flushed before each call) of the slowest rank, ms.
Operations: fwd = forward with autograd recording; fwd+bwd = forward +
backward; ckpt = torch.utils.checkpoint(use_reentrant=False): forward +
recompute + backward (2 x fwd + bwd).

## B. Two baselines (det(main), this PR and the in-process non-Cake arms
in one run; ‡ = FlashQLA in its own process)

Strongest non-Cake = the fastest arm that passes the accuracy check:
FLA-CP = flash-linear-attention 0.6.0's own context parallelism; FLA-HS
= head split (all-to-all) around FLA's single-GPU kernels; FROST-ck0 /
-ck64 = the same head split around cuDNN frontend 1.32.1's GDN (states
recomputed / stored every 64 tokens). A non-Cake cell is published when
this PR's arm and the shown arm drift <= 2 % between groups and every
arm with drift > 2 % is slower than the shown arm in every group. At CP
> 1 the strongest applicable non-Cake arm is FlashQLA 0.1.3 dual-CP
(inter + intra rank context parallelism, contiguous layout): it runs in
its own process and environment, paired with FLA-CP there and checked
against it (relative RMS <= 1e-2, max abs <= 2e-2 of the reference max);
'‡' = a FlashQLA value, its ratio divides by this PR's ms of the same
table-B run, and the FLA-CP anchor of both processes is listed under the
table. A CP > 1 cell without a FlashQLA value (layout D: FlashQLA has no
per-document zigzag layout; a GPU without a FlashQLA build) is not
claimed; the best in-process arm is shown as a note only.

### [9e97780](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9e97780a2ab94fbf9621aeecf5643ac52d75786d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T12:26:23Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate): L2-prefetching mid forward on SM107 (#8656)

This PR switches the sm_107a mid forward of the non-deterministic
package of Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` with `deterministic=False`)
to `cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_87f0173e9583ad4fdd2a`. That is the
L2-prefetching module sm_100a and sm_103a already run. In it, thread 0
also warms two later row blocks in L2, with one bulk prefetch per
tensor, wherever the inputs x and z hold their rows packed. The two
blocks are the CTA's next block and the CTA's first block one resident
wave later. The sm_107a routing thresholds and grid do not change: the
mid forward serves inputs from 800 rows per SM up to the long forward's
1740. The five shapes in Table 1 fall in that range.

The module this replaces,
`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_b0eb3df9844d5b734850`, is the same
128-thread build without the prefetch. Nothing routes to it anymore, so
this PR removes it. It is the "previous Cake" baseline below. Every
other module and route is FlashInfer main's code: the backward, the
short and long forwards, and every sm_100a and sm_103a route run the
same code as before.

The PR is one commit on FlashInfer main after PR #8622. The A/B compared
two FlashInfer trees: one whose sm_107a mid forward runs without the
prefetch, and the same tree plus this PR's sm_107a route. In the
measured tree, the new module's sources are byte-identical to this PR's.

A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. The table gives ranges (min-max) over the five shapes of Table 1
on R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), CUDA 13.4. For stepg_f32 and fwd + bwd, the
ranges cover the twelve shapes of Table 2: those five, plus seven shapes
that run the same code in both trees.

| op | det Cake / new | strongest non-Cake / new | previous Cake / new
(A/B) |
|---|---|---|---|
| fwd | 1.119-1.141 | 1.071-1.080 | 1.113-1.136 |
| fwdg | 1.131-1.142 | 1.047-1.077 | 1.111-1.136 |
| bwdg | 1.081-1.163 | 1.097-1.119 | 0.9998-1.0002 |
| ckptg | 1.115-1.151 | 1.070-1.084 | 1.046-1.060 |
| stepg_f32 (12 shapes) | 1.068-1.218 | - | 0.9996-1.061 |
| fwd + bwd (12 shapes) | 1.062-1.197 | - | 0.998-1.045 |

In the pre-registered A/B, all 20 cells whose code changes (fwd, fwdg,
ckptg and stepg_f32 at the five shapes) are faster than the previous
Cake route. bwdg runs the same code in both trees. Neither the strongest
non-Cake kernel (Table 1) nor the deterministic Cake kernel (Tables 1
and 2) is faster than new on any row. Every cell below 1x is a same-code
cell against the previous Cake route, each by less than 0.3 %, and every
one is listed under "Cells below 1x".

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`) and the FP32 weight-gradient output of the
non-deterministic package. Both packages ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a. sm_100a and sm_103a have run this mid forward since PR #8622,
and this PR changes only the non-deterministic package's mid forward on
sm_107a.

## How the tables were measured

- Latency: CUPTI kernel time with cold L2, taken with FlashInfer's GPU
timer in `flashinfer.testing`. Inputs are BF16, and all times are in us.
- Table 1: the deterministic Cake kernel, the strongest non-Cake kernel
and new were measured in the same process. Each value is the median of
the per-round medians over 10 rounds.
- A/B values: the previous Cake and new (A/B) columns and all of Table 2
are medians of the pre-registered interleaved A/B, which ran 16
sequences and 160 processes. stepg_f32 has no same-process measurement,
so its deterministic Cake values also come from the A/B.
- Strongest non-Cake kernel per row: the fastest of the following, with
torch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0.
  - FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated` (`fla.modules.fused_norm_gate`).
  - mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn` (`layernorm_gated`).
- torch.compile in default and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs modes, best of
5 fresh compiles each. `#k` names the fastest compile.
- The inductor-generated persistent-reduction Triton kernel of the FP32
formula, launched directly.
- Deterministic Cake: `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`,
unchanged by this PR.
- Operations:
- `fwd` is one eager forward call, and `fwdg` is the forward replayed
from a CUDA graph.
  - `bwdg` is the backward replayed from a CUDA graph.
- `ckptg` is the checkpointed step (2 x forward + backward) in one CUDA
graph, and `stepg_f32` is the same step with an FP32 dw.
  - `fwd + bwd` is fwdg + bwdg, derived.
- In Table 2, the first five shapes run the new module. 260x48, 1031x48,
2048x48, 3533x48, 7685x48, 10600x48 and 16384x48 run the same code in
both trees.

## Cells below 1x

- vs the strongest non-Cake kernel (Table 1): none.
- vs the deterministic Cake kernel: none.
- vs the previous Cake route (A/B), only at cells that run the same code
in both trees:
  - bwdg (Table 1): 8192x32 0.9998, 7684x48 0.99999
- Table 2: 1031x48 stepg_f32 0.9997, 1031x48 fwd + bwd 0.998, 2048x48
stepg_f32 0.9996, 3533x48 ckptg 0.9996, 3533x48 stepg_f32 0.9999,
7685x48 stepg_f32 0.9999, 7685x48 fwd + bwd 0.9998, 10600x48 stepg_f32
0.99996, 16384x48 fwd + bwd 0.9999

### [13d3749](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/13d37493695df1b78ea38c937a44e24e526327d4)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T12:19:52Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm_mega_mhc): weight-staging routes for the 16-split two-wave non-deterministic band on sm_107a (#8651)

`flashinfer.mega_mhc` (`prepare_mega_mhc`) runs the fused
manifold-constrained hyper-connection (mHC) inference step. FlashInfer
main ships 45 per-arch programs for it:

- 14 hidden-5120 FP8-E4M3-output programs on sm_100a and sm_103a.
- For hidden 4096, five programs on each of sm_107a, sm_100a and
sm_103a: BF16 output, its tailpipe twin, its weight-staging tailpipe
twin, FP8 group-128 output and NVFP4 output.
- Four sm_107a-only tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe forms of the
FP8 group-128 and NVFP4 variants.
- Three sm_107a-only FP8 group-128 UE8M0-scale-mode programs (plain,
tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe).
- One sm_107a-only fast-division form of the plain FP8 group-128
program.
- Six sm_107a-only fast-chain forms: one each of the BF16-output
tailpipe program, the plain FP8 group-128 program (raw scale mode), the
plain FP8 group-128 program (UE8M0 scale mode), the FP8 group-128
weight-staging tailpipe program (raw scale mode), the FP8 group-128
UE8M0 tailpipe program and the NVFP4 tailpipe program.
- Two sm_107a-only chain-packing forms: one of the FP8 group-128
tailpipe program (raw scale mode) and one of the plain FP8 group-128
UE8M0 program.

Routes on main can already carry an optional SM-count key.

This PR adds no program and changes no program. It adds three routes,
and each route is keyed to one SM count (208 or 216). Each route moves
non-deterministic launches in the 2-wave 16-split band to the existing
weight-staging tailpipe program with the same output layout and scale
mode. The previous round already sends non-deterministic launches above
this band to this program (for NVFP4 on 216 SMs, from T = 2113). The
weight-staging tailpipe program keeps the split count and the grid of
the program it replaces. It also stages the RMSNorm weight in shared
memory. Outputs are bitwise identical. Every other SM count, and a call
with no SM count, dispatch exactly as on main. No sm_100a or sm_103a
launch changes, and no deterministic launch changes.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the kernel, which is what
FlashInfer main dispatches today. A is the program main dispatches, and
B is the program this PR dispatches. Speedup = A / B. Both sides run
through FlashInfer's loader on the same GPU, with the same inputs, in
one process. Both use programmatic dependent launch, as main already
does. The tables show medians. Each table lists the owner shapes first,
then the changed rows. The GPU is an NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a), with 208-SM
and 216-SM devices. Non-deterministic launches use 16 splits over two
waves for T = 1281–1664 on 208 SMs and T = 1345–1728 on 216 SMs. Below
that they use one wave with fewer splits. Above it they use 13 splits.
The tables show the split count per row.

- **FP8 group-128 output, UE8M0 scales, non-deterministic** (UE8M0
tailpipe program → UE8M0 weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T =
1472–1664 (1.026–1.045×). 216 SMs: T = 1536–1728 (1.024–1.039×). On
both, the new range ends where the previous round's range starts.
- **NVFP4 output, non-deterministic** (NVFP4 tailpipe program → NVFP4
weight-staging tailpipe program). 216 SMs only: T = 1664–1728
(1.010–1.013×). 208-SM NVFP4 launches are unchanged.
- **FP8 group-128 output, raw scales.** Launches are unchanged on both
SM counts.
- **Owner shapes.** No owner shape (T = 1, 4, …, 8192) lies in a changed
range. Owner-shape rows measure 0.996–1.004× on the 208-SM GPU and
0.993–1.005× on the 216-SM GPU; those rows are all within noise.

### [1b4c25b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1b4c25b58804be6eab04ac5ae51c68d590844196)

- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dense_projection_gemm): run 4096 -> 64 BF16 output deterministic from 65536 tokens on 148-SM sm_100a parts (#8636)

`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` provides BF16-input
dense and batched projection GEMMs with BF16 or FP32 output, and an FP32
router GEMM. The default, `deterministic=True`, calls
`dense_projection_det_gemm`. With `deterministic=False`, the package
runs its split-K / stream-K programs on the rows that its measured
routing tables select. Every other row runs the deterministic program.
This PR changes one variant: the weight gradient (wgrad) with
`deterministic=False`, `4096 -> 64` with BF16 output, on B200 `sm_100a`
parts with exactly 148 SMs. This row now runs the deterministic program
at all token counts from 65536 up. Before this PR, it ran the 2-split
program above 65536 tokens, and 65536 itself already ran the
deterministic program. The same row with FP32 output on `sm_100a`
already runs the deterministic program from 65536 tokens up. So does
`4096 -> 32` (BF16 and FP32 output) on 148-SM B300 `sm_103a` parts. All
other token counts, rows, parts and SM counts keep their current
programs.

Columns: "det" is the deterministic Cake program. "SOTA" is the
strongest non-Cake library GEMM. "previous" is the program that the row
ran before this PR, which is the 2-split program. "new" is the program
that it runs now, which is the deterministic program, so det/new is
1.000 by definition. Ratio = baseline us / new us. Above 1.00 means the
new routing is faster, and below 1.00 means it is slower. wgrad is the
weight-gradient op alone. bwd is the whole backward (input gradient +
weight gradient). ckpt is the checkpointed step (2 forward + input
gradient + weight gradient). In the lists below, graph means CUDA graph
replay and eager means eager launches.

**Timing conditions.** Part: B200 `sm_100a`, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07.
Software: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), nvcc 13.4, cuBLAS 13.8.0.4.
Each time is the CUPTI span of all launches of the op. L2 is cold before
every iteration: a 2x-L2 buffer is cleared. Single op: median of 9
paired groups of 20 timed iterations. Whole backward and checkpointed
step: cold L2 before every sequence, median of 9 paired groups. Each
table value is the median of two runs on two GPUs of the same node. With
two runs, this is their mean. CUDA graph replay and eager launches, PDL
on. SOTA is, per row, the fastest correct library launch among
`torch.mm` (cuBLAS 13.8.0.4) and the top 8 algorithms of the cuBLASLt
heuristic. It uses the same BF16 operands and output dtype, and is
chosen on the same GPU in the same process. For the whole steps, it is
chosen per op. This is the strongest non-Cake GEMM available for this
layout and output dtype on this part. During timing, 2 to 5 of the 15
clock samples per GPU and phase showed a software power cap, and the
lowest sampled SM clock was 1462 MHz.

**A/A noise** (a second, independently prepared launch of the
deterministic program, aa/det, same statistic): wgrad 0.997 to 1.002,
bwd 0.978 to 1.012, ckpt 0.993 to 1.019.

The split programs of this package ship for `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and
`sm_107a`, and this PR does not change the other variants: forward,
input gradient, batched projections, the router GEMM, other shapes, FP32
output, other SM counts and `deterministic=True`.

### [174fc7c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/174fc7c9b395f1ab26386a5d88fb4c605a63f76d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T11:47:13Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): with grad, reduce the raw gate's parameter gradients in FP64 in the non-deterministic packages on sm_100a and sm_103a (#8620)

Cake's KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training kernels come in two
kinds of package: deterministic and non-deterministic (ND). Each kind
has a single-rank package and a KCP context-parallel package. There are
two forget-gate modes. In precomputed `g` mode the gate is an input. In
raw mode the kernel computes the gate from `A_log`, `dt_bias` and
`lower_bound` (`use_gate_in_kernel=True`). This PR changes one variant:
raw mode with grad, in the ND single-rank package
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_train`) and the ND KCP package
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train_kcp`), on sm_100a and sm_103a.

Before this PR, ND raw mode ran the deterministic programs. The
gate-gradient kernel wrote per-chunk FP32 partials of the `A_log` /
`dt_bias` gradients, and a second program merged them in a fixed order.
Now the gate-gradient kernel adds the partials into FP64 accumulators:
`glm_intra_v20c`, or `glm_intra_v20c_r8` with 8 accumulator stripes.
Then `param_finalize_cast` (or `param_finalize_cast_r8`) rounds the sum
to FP32 once. On sm_100a the kernel uses 8 stripes from 32 heads and 1
stripe below that. On sm_103a it uses 1 stripe. sm_107a keeps the
deterministic programs.

Every output stays bitwise equal to the deterministic package's output,
with one exception: `dA_log` / `ddt_bias` on sm_100a / sm_103a. Each of
these is the FP64 sum of the deterministic partials, rounded to FP32
once. The result is within half an FP32 ulp of the exact sum, plus the
FP64 error. The measured run-to-run spread is 0 ulp.

Baselines:
- (a) The deterministic Cake packages at FlashInfer main c0d987da. This
PR does not change them, and ND raw mode ran their programs before this
PR.
- (b) FLA `chunk_kda` 0.6.0 with `use_gate_in_kernel=True`,
`safe_gate=True` and `lower_bound=-5`. This is the strongest non-Cake
KDA implementation with an in-kernel gate.

A row counts as faster or slower only when det/ND is outside the A/A
noise band in both build orders. On every GPU, no row is slower than the
deterministic packages in both build orders.

| GPU | arch | single-rank det/ND geomean | KCP det/ND geomean |
faster/parity, single-rank | faster/parity, KCP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | sm_100a | 1.0446 | 1.0245 | 22/29 | 36/0 |
| B200 | sm_100a | 1.0083 | 1.0150 | 16/41 | 32/4 |
| GB300 | sm_103a | 1.0326 | 1.0280 | 13/41 | 46/2 |
| B300 | sm_103a | 1.0195 | 1.0171 | 16/20 | 35/0 |
| VR200 | sm_107a | 1.0052 | 1.0196 | 4/47 | 26/10 |

- **GB200 totals:** 87 rows, 58 faster and 29 at parity.
- **B300 build-order rows:** 15 single-rank rows and 1 KCP row are
outside the band in only one build order.
- **Lowest cells:** 0.9994 (GB200 P1 fwd), 0.9946 (B200 P11 ckpt),
0.9960 (GB300 P9 fwd), 0.9992 (B300 P1 fwd) and 0.9997 (VR200 P1 fwd).
- **Nominally slower rows:** ND is nominally slower in both orders on 3
B200 rows, 5 GB300 rows and 2 B300 rows. None of them is outside the
band in both orders.
- **Largest single-rank ratios:** these are on the T=16384, H=4 rows R1
and R2, from 1.1133 (VR200) to 1.6239 (GB200 R2 bwd). These rows are
host/launch-bound and several have wide A/A bands, so the exact size of
these speedups is uncertain.
- **Rows the change does not touch:** the new programs run only in the
backward and never on sm_107a. det/ND on the fwd rows and on all VR200
rows is therefore not from this change.

ND is faster than FLA on every single-rank row. FLA/ND ranges from 1.830
to 10.280 (GB200), 1.788 to 9.885 (B200), 2.152 to 10.466 (GB300), 1.700
to 9.103 (B300) and 1.858 to 13.775 (VR200).

How to read the tables:
- det/ND = deterministic Cake latency / ND latency.
- FLA/ND = FLA latency / ND latency.
- A ratio above 1 means ND is faster.
- Each ratio is the mean of the det-first and nd-first paired medians,
so it can differ slightly from the ratio of the listed latencies.
- ckpt = one `torch.utils.checkpoint` step (2 x forward + backward),
timed as one span.
- Latencies are in microseconds (us).
- FLA has no context-parallel KDA path, so KCP rows have no FLA
baseline.

Other Cake variants in this family: precomputed-`g` mode in all four
packages, raw mode in the two deterministic packages, and the in-kernel
Q/K L2-norm option. The family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Raw-gate training now uses an architecture-specific parameter-gradient
reduction path on supported GPUs, with updated workspace sizing and
memory reporting.
* Benchmark tools can compare execution with different build orders and
report numerical differences, memory use, and performance across those
orders.

* **Documentation**
* Clarified where raw-gate parameter gradients may vary slightly between
runs and how behavior differs by GPU architecture.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

---------

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [6b3c261](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6b3c261566f8f653f0683f8dd0c1f9ad000fdd4c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T11:40:14Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det): with grad, cached FFI entry and raw-stream launch in the deterministic single-rank package (#8630)

Follow-up to #7817. The Cake KDA chunked training (with grad) family
ships four packages: deterministic single-rank, deterministic
context-parallel, non-deterministic single-rank and non-deterministic
context-parallel. This PR changes only the host launch of the
deterministic single-rank package (`cake_kda_det_train`) for every
record. It now caches each record's FFI entry and launches on the raw
stream, as the non-deterministic package has done since #8455. Host
issue time per step falls by 47-62 µs (forward), 78-128 µs (backward),
121-179 µs (forward + backward) and 156-249 µs (checkpointed). Wall time
falls by 9-49 µs (0.3-2.7 %). The baseline is the same package with the
previous launcher on FlashInfer main, run in the same process with the
same inputs.

GB200 and B200 (sm_100a), GB300 (sm_103a); PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA
13.0); causal conv1d -> KDA with in-kernel Q/K L2 norm; one GPU on an
idle node, paired in one process, medians of 5 blocks x 20 iterations;
speedup = before / after; parity = wall 95% CI crosses 1.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
- Improved CUDA stream handling during execution, including support for
environments where the preferred stream lookup is unavailable.
- CUDA operations now run using the current PyTorch stream, helping
maintain consistent execution across supported configurations.

### [bc4e12b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/bc4e12b39aff7285dc8bdf39aee8208433b5c0a6)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T10:29:42Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): FFMA router weight gradient up to 192-256 tokens on sm_100a/sm_107a (#8578)

The Cake dense projection GEMM package has two GEMM families for MoE
layers. The first is the BF16 weight-gradient GEMM, with BF16 or FP32
output and several tile widths. The second is the FP32 router GEMM,
which covers forward, input gradient and weight gradient using BF16x3
split precision with stream-K and head/tail schedules. This PR adds a
third program for the router weight gradient at FP32, 256 experts and
hidden 4096, 5120 or 6144. It is an exact-FP32 FFMA program that runs on
the CUDA cores. On 152-SM sm_100a parts, the planner routes to it at
hidden 4096 from 1 to 224 tokens and at hidden 5120 and 6144 from 1 to
256 tokens. On 212-SM sm_107a parts, it routes to it at hidden 4096 and
5120 from 1 to 256 tokens and at hidden 6144 from 1 to 192 tokens. Other
parts and token counts keep their previous plan. At the measured token
counts (64, 128, 192 and 256), the speedup against the deterministic
Cake router program is x1.17-3.64 on the weight gradient, x1.09-1.82 on
the full backward (input + weight gradient) and x1.01-1.20 on a
checkpointed step. Against the fastest accurate non-Cake library route,
the same ratios are x0.88-1.09, x0.83-1.18 and x0.53-0.98.

Latencies are in microseconds. Each run takes the median of 15 paired
groups of 20 timed iterations, using CUPTI kernel spans, a cold L2, and
both eager launches and CUDA graph replays. Each cell is the median over
runs: four runs of each Cake program and two runs of each library route
per cuBLAS build. "Deterministic Cake" is this package's deterministic
router program. "Previous plan" is this package's plan before this PR at
the same shape and token count. "Non-Cake SOTA" is, for each operation,
the fastest FP32 library route within the router accuracy budget, which
is a relative Frobenius error of at most 2e-6 against FP64 over 5 seeds.
The candidate routes are cublasSgemm, cuBLASLt FP32 (best of the
heuristic's top 8), torch.mm FP32 without TF32 and cuBLAS FP32 in BF16x9
emulation, with cuBLAS 13.8 and 13.1 on GB200 and cuBLAS 13.8 on R200.
The SOTA route column names the winning route. Each speedup is the
baseline latency divided by the new program's latency, so a value below
1 means the baseline is faster. An A/A comparison of the same program
against itself varied by x0.967-1.053 per cell on GB200 (672 cells) and
x0.938-1.039 on R200 (288 cells). GB200 is NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100a, 152
SMs), and R200 is sm_107a with 212 SMs. The runs used the CUDA 13.0
runtime with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, and the kernels were built with CUDA
13.4. The new program's results differ from the deterministic program's
in the last bits and repeat bit for bit.

The package's other Cake programs, the BF16 weight-gradient GEMM and the
BF16x3 router programs, are unchanged; the package ships on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [4046a86](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4046a8635810e77174ae7553224dbaa24ad9ba9e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T10:02:58Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d_det): with grad, 32-vector channel tiles for narrow single-tile rows (#8611)

`cake_causal_conv1d_det_train` is the deterministic, packed, width-4
depthwise causal convolution + SiLU for training. It has 8 variants: 3
forward (`fwd`, `fwd_dt`, `fwd_bias`) and 5 backward (`bwd`, `bwd_dt`,
`bwd_bias`, `bwd_fp32g`, `bwd_bias_fp32g`). This PR changes only the
host-side channel tile plan at 128 threads per CTA. It applies to `bwd`
and `bwd_bias` for C = 520 to 768 and C = 224, and to `fwd` and
`fwd_bias` for C = 576 to 768. These rows used to run as one channel
tile, which left many lanes in each CTA idle. They now run as 32-vector
channel tiles. The kernel programs are unchanged, and y and dx are
bitwise unchanged. All other variants and channel counts keep the
previous plan. The results below are median paired ratios against
FlashInfer main on the 30 changed rows per GPU. On B200 (sm_100a),
backward is 1.199x to 1.437x faster, forward is 1.114x to 1.130x faster,
and forward + backward is 1.123x to 1.311x faster. On GB300 (sm_103a),
backward is 1.135x to 1.484x faster, forward is 1.092x to 1.143x faster,
and forward + backward is 1.094x to 1.349x faster. On VR200 (sm_107a),
backward is 1.077x to 1.394x faster, forward is 1.018x to 1.139x faster,
and forward + backward is 1.103x to 1.290x faster. The 19 unchanged rows
per GPU run the same plan on both sides and stay within 0.995x to
1.001x, which is measurement noise.

cold L2, taken as the median per copy and averaged over two separate
copies of each package. Speedup is the median of 48 paired per-call
ratios (FlashInfer main / this PR), with a 95% bootstrap CI.*

### [9873f95](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9873f954ae6abe355bd6e35f70161e63d9ebc990)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T09:55:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): add the sm_107a 4096 -> 1024 fp32 weight-gradient key at T 16384 (#8635)

This PR adds a row rule to the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package
in `flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM.
Most programs in the package are BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and
wgrad), and one is an FP32 router GEMM. The PR adds no new program, and
the kernel sources and compiled libraries are unchanged. It adds 1 row
rule for `sm_107a` (Rubin), and the rule applies at a single token
count, T 16384. It covers the 4096→1024 weight gradient (wgrad, FP32
output). At this token count the rule moves that row from the existing
256-column tile program `nn_n256_m256_f32_tma1_pro7` to the program the
row already uses at T 16231. That program,
`nn_n160_m256_bz64_f32_v8_ef_pro15`, uses a 160-column tile with a
64-byte B swizzle and 8-wide FP32 stores. The new rule is a copy of the
row's existing T 16231 rule. It keeps the K split that the row would get
without the rule, so outputs are bitwise identical to main. The rule
count goes from 373 to 374, and the `sm_107a` rule count goes from 124
to 125. The `sm_100a` and `sm_103a` rules are unchanged. The baseline is
the previous Cake version of the package on main. Against it, the
changed row has a speedup of 1.414 on the 216-SM Rubin part (77.1 µs to
54.6 µs) and 1.380 on the 212-SM Rubin part (78.8 µs to 57.1 µs). No
changed row is slower on either part. All other rows of the 294-row
shape list plan the same programs as main on `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and
`sm_107a`.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** Rubin
(`sm_107a`, 216 SMs and 212 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2, FP32 output.
Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1 mean this PR
is faster.

| shape (K→N) | op | out | T | GPU | previous µs | this PR µs | speedup
|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096→1024 | wgrad | fp32 | 16384 | Rubin (`sm_107a`, 216 SMs) | 77.1 |
54.6 | 1.414 |
| 4096→1024 | wgrad | fp32 | 16384 | Rubin (`sm_107a`, 212 SMs) | 78.8 |
57.1 | 1.380 |

The package also ships BF16-output forms, forward and input-gradient
(dgrad) programs and the FP32 router GEMM (run through BF16x3
emulation), on `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

### [80affe9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/80affe99787f5c5b9e3f88b0ceac8ed6033ccbb9)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T09:48:29Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kda_det): with grad, zero the next group's qn / kn rows before the batched l2n replay (#8629)

Follow-up to #7817.

With `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`, a batched arena
(`KdaDetArena(batch_tokens=...)`) and the replay backward
(`saved=None`), groups on the serial route (more than eight heads on
sm_100a, 32 or more on every architecture) run the plain intra program
after their prep. It reads 64-row boxes of the per-call `qn` / `kn` from
each chunk start, so a group's last chunk can read up to 63 rows of the
next group before that group's prep writes them. Uninitialized NaN bytes
in those rows reached every gradient through `0 * NaN`. The backward now
zeroes those rows of `qn` / `kn` before the groups run.

The new test
`test_l2n_batched_replay_reads_no_unwritten_row_of_the_next_group` fills
every per-call float tensor and the arena with NaN. It fails on main for
the overhanging group boundary (lengths 100, 126, 50 at
`batch_tokens=226`, H 16 and 32, `g` and raw gate) and passes here; the
chunk-aligned control passes on both.

The batched replay backward time does not change (GB200, docs 23496 /
88510 / 114974 / 34413, H32, `batch_tokens=149387`, median of 6 x 30
calls): `g` 34.76 ms on main vs 34.80 ms here, raw gate 37.92 ms vs
37.94 ms.

### [fdb862f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/fdb862f5e5d7733d6d7bfd7f05ac7c3ccb40565e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:39:46Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_alpha_moe): NVFP4 fused batch kernel quantizes its activation per lane (#8632)

The AlphaMoE Cake kernels in FlashInfer have three sets: NVFP4 MoE, W8A8
MoE and the fused router. This PR changes one NVFP4 kernel, the fused
batch kernel of the word-scale path. Each lane now quantizes its own
activation value to e2m1, and the kernel no longer gathers the values
through lane 0. The 8 lanes of a 32-bit word combine their 4-bit codes
with xor shuffles. The per-element math and the stored activation bytes
stay the same, so each route's contribution is bitwise identical to the
previous version. Of the 10 NVFP4 shapes below, only M=128, N=256,
K=7168, block_m=16 runs this kernel. On that shape, this PR is faster
than the previous version (the Cake AlphaMoE NVFP4 kernels on FlashInfer
main, from #8353). The speedup is 1.011x (memset) and 1.013x (read) on
B200, and 1.009x (memset) and 1.013x (read) on GB300.

The tables give kernel time per MoE call in microseconds. This is the
sum of the MoE kernels of one call, measured with CUPTI. We timed the
previous version and this PR in paired, interleaved runs on the same
GPU. "memset" means a cold L2: we clear a large buffer with memset.
"read" means we flush L2 by reading a large buffer. Speedup = previous /
this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is faster. The other 9 shapes
run the same machine code on both sides. Their ratios are 0.999x to
1.001x, which is inside the same-node noise band. We measured that band
by running the previous code against itself.

#### B200 (sm_100a)

CUDA 13.3 (nvcc 13.3), PyTorch 2.13, driver 580.82.07. Each node median
covers 16 values (8 GPUs x 2 repetitions). The M=8/N=256, M=128/N=256,
M=8/N=1024 and M=128/N=1024 rows are the mean of two node medians. The
other 6 rows come from one node.

### [3064b3e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3064b3ec6f8d03d91a565c2dab69cf4b380b6ab6)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:39:06Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_moe_grouped_gemm): fuse the fp32 weight-gradient accumulate into main_grad on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a (#8602)

The Cake ragged BF16 grouped GEMM for MoE expert training has two
variants: deterministic
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_moe_grouped_det_gemm` and
non-deterministic `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_moe_grouped_gemm`
(selected with `deterministic=False`). Both use FP32 accumulation. Each
has forward (`Y = X W^T`), data-gradient (`dX = G W`) and
weight-gradient (`dW = G^T X`, BF16 or FP32 output) programs. The facade
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.grouped_mm` reaches the kernel, and its
default stays deterministic.

This PR adds weight-gradient accumulation into an existing buffer,
`out[e] += G_e^T X_e`. It is opt-in and applies to the non-deterministic
variant only. These are the semantics of Megatron's
`gradient_accumulation_fusion` and Transformer Engine's
`fuse_wgrad_accumulation`. The public surface is
`grouped_gemm_wgrad(..., out=out, accumulate=True)`,
`prepare_grouped_gemm_wgrad(..., accumulate=True)` and
`cake_grouped_mm(x, w, offs, deterministic=False,
fuse_wgrad_accumulation=True)`. The last one adds into `w.main_grad` in
the backward and supports Megatron's `grad_added_to_main_grad`.
`accumulate` and `fuse_wgrad_accumulation` both default to off. With the
defaults, the routes, programs, plans and bits are unchanged. For an
fp32 `out` or `main_grad`, the add is fused into the epilogue of the
k512 half-release weight-gradient programs. On sm_100a and sm_103a these
are forms `main_halves` and `main_wave_halves`; on sm_107a they are
`main_halves` and `main_halves_k256t`. This adds six fp32 accumulate
builds that need CUDA toolkit 13.4 or newer. Every other case runs
composed (the dW, then one add): a bf16 `main_grad`, the 256-wide k
tile, other forms, a misaligned `out`, or an accumulate library that
cannot load. `plan["accumulate"]` reports `"fused"` or `"composed"`. As
before for this variant, the summation order of a split tail tile can
differ between runs. Against an fp32 dW followed by `main_grad.add_`,
the fused route with `grad_added_to_main_grad` saves `2 * S` bytes of
peak memory (S = E * N * K elements).

**Results** (point estimates, new non-deterministic Cake against each
baseline):

- **wgrad accumulate:** At or above 1.0 against deterministic Cake on
every row: GB300 1.033-1.255x, B200 1.022-1.241x, R200 1.024-1.318x.
Against non-Cake SOTA the range is 0.931-1.060x on GB300, 0.945-1.058x
on B200 and 0.961-1.036x on R200. The standalone call is slower than
non-Cake SOTA on 9 of 20 rows on GB300 (lowest 0.931x), 8 of 20 on B200
(lowest 0.945x) and 11 of 20 on R200 (lowest 0.961x). On those rows the
fastest baseline is mostly TE GroupedLinear. It takes host-side
`m_splits`, so it needs the group sizes on the host. This kernel reads
device offsets with no host sync. Closing the standalone wgrad
accumulate gap to TE is follow-up work.
- **full backward:** Against deterministic Cake the range is
0.989-1.174x on GB300 (3 rows below 1.0, each with a CI that includes 1)
and 0.912-1.142x on B200 (9 rows below 1.0; one has a CI entirely below
1). On R200 it is 1.022-1.220x. Against non-Cake SOTA the range is
0.965-1.052x on GB300 (6 rows below 1.0), 0.910-1.046x on B200 (13 rows
below 1.0) and 1.002-1.089x on R200.
- **checkpointed 2×fwd + bwd:** At or above 1.0 on every row against
both baselines. Against deterministic Cake: GB300 1.007-1.071x, B200
1.006-1.071x, R200 1.005-1.075x. Against non-Cake SOTA: GB300
1.010-1.054x, B200 1.000-1.044x, R200 1.010-1.069x.

**Baselines and measurement.** Speedup = baseline latency / new latency,
so a value above 1 means the new kernel is faster. Brackets are
bootstrap 95% CIs of the paired per-group median ratio.

- "new non-deterministic Cake" is this PR's fused route.
- "deterministic Cake" is the deterministic variant's fp32 dW followed
by `main_grad.add_`. In full backward and checkpointed 2×fwd + bwd, it
is the deterministic autograd plus the add.
- "non-Cake SOTA" is the fastest fp32-accumulate non-Cake implementation
measured for each row. The table names it in parentheses. This choice
favors the baseline. The candidates are:
- "TE GroupedLinear": Transformer Engine 2.20.2
`GroupedLinear(fuse_wgrad_accumulation=True)` on the legacy per-expert
cuBLAS path with host `m_splits`.
- "TE grouped tensor": the TE grouped-tensor path with device `m_splits`
(cuBLASLt grouped GEMM).
- "cuBLAS per expert": per-expert `cublasGemmEx` with beta=1 into
`main_grad`.
- "cuBLASLt grouped": cuBLASLt grouped matmul with beta=1 (wgrad
accumulate only).
- "DeepGEMM": DeepGEMM 2.8.2 k-grouped BF16 GEMM with C accumulation
(wgrad accumulate only). It does not run on sm_107a, so it is absent on
R200.
- "per-op best composite" (full backward and checkpointed 2×fwd + bwd
only): the fastest deterministic-matching forward and data-gradient
(per-expert cuBLAS, torch, cuDNN or FlashInfer mm), plus the fastest
fp32 accumulate weight-gradient.
- `torch._grouped_mm` with fp32 output is unsupported in torch 2.14.1.
- Operations:
- "wgrad accumulate `main_grad += dW`" is the accumulate call alone
(CUPTI cold-L2 span, 12 groups).
- "full backward" is data-gradient + wgrad accumulate, with the forward
untimed (cold-L2 CUDA events, 16 groups × 4 sequences).
- "checkpointed 2×fwd + bwd" is one checkpointed micro-step (CUPTI
cold-L2 span).
  - All runs use eager execution and cold L2.
- Shapes are gate_up and down projections. E is the number of experts
and M is the total token count. balanced, one_empty, skewed and short16
are group-size patterns. Inputs are bf16 and `main_grad` is fp32.
- Environments:
  - GB300 sm_103a: 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03, power limit 1400 W.
  - B200 sm_100a: 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07, power limit 1000 W.
- R200 sm_107a: 208 SMs, driver 615.71.10, power limit 2300 W, measured
on one timing-admitted board (n=1, not decision-grade).
- On all three, kernels were built with CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4), with
torch 2.14.1+cu130 and cuBLAS 13.8.0.4.
- Non-Cake arms ran on one GPU per row. On GB300 and B200, the Cake arms
also ran on replica GPUs for some rows.

### [c22374d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c22374d3e3fd5806fdf7e2990e305d18f407d254)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:34:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det_train): glm_intra v30 runs the fused Q/K L2 norm's GLM intra stage on sm_103a (#8625)

The deterministic Cake KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training
package, `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train`, has four variants. In two of
them the caller does the Q/K L2 norm. In the other two it is fused in
the kernel (`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`). Each of these comes with
either the g gate or the raw gate (`use_gate_in_kernel`). Every variant
has forward, backward and checkpoint entries. This PR changes only one:
the fused in-kernel Q/K L2 norm variant with the g gate, on sm_103a
(GB300). Its backward GLM intra stage now runs glm_intra v30 (record
`glm_intra_v30_l2n`) in place of glm_intra v27. v30 lays out the L2 norm
pullback eight lanes per row. Every output and gradient is bit-identical
to v27. Backward is 1.012x to 1.013x faster, about 50 us per call.
fwd+bwd is 1.007x to 1.008x faster and ckpt is 1.002x to 1.007x faster.
The forward code is unchanged, so the forward does not change. Its
0.995x to 0.998x is run-to-run noise.

GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs), driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92) JIT
build, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, one GPU of an otherwise idle node. 4 before
and 4 after processes in ABBA order, median per call. Both sides use
`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`. ckpt = forward + recomputed forward +
backward. Speedup = before / after.

| GPU | shape (H=64, D=128, BF16) | timed operation | before: FlashInfer
main (glm_intra v27), ms | after: this PR (glm_intra v30), ms | speedup
(before/after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs) | T=16384, 1 sequence | fwd | 1.5683 | 1.5769
| 0.995x |
| GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs) | T=16384, 1 sequence | bwd | 4.1044 | 4.0548
| 1.012x |
| GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs) | T=16384, 1 sequence | fwd+bwd | 5.4766 |
5.4305 | 1.008x |
| GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs) | T=16384, 1 sequence | ckpt | 6.9779 | 6.9289
| 1.007x |
| GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs) | T=16384, 4 sequences (8192/4096/3072/1024) |
fwd | 1.5780 | 1.5804 | 0.998x |
| GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs) | T=16384, 4 sequences (8192/4096/3072/1024) |
bwd | 3.9638 | 3.9133 | 1.013x |
| GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs) | T=16384, 4 sequences (8192/4096/3072/1024) |
fwd+bwd | 5.3330 | 5.2985 | 1.007x |
| GB300 (SM103a, 152 SMs) | T=16384, 4 sequences (8192/4096/3072/1024) |
ckpt | 6.8202 | 6.8049 | 1.002x |

The family also includes the non-deterministic `cake_kda_train` package
and a context-parallel (KCP) form of the deterministic package, and it
ships on sm_100a (B200, GB200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a (R200), but
glm_intra v30 is sm_103a only, so sm_100a and sm_107a keep v27.

Follow-up to #7817

### [2b3a7a3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2b3a7a36ca45f53f1f9dcc2eaec38d4a11fe203e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:32:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16): CuTe-DSL programs on the CUDA backend's cross-rank protocol (#8631)

`cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16` is the fused MoE kernel with BF16 activations
and MXFP8 weights for 16-way expert parallelism (EP16). It has a CUDA
backend and a CuTe-DSL backend. Each backend has three programs per
architecture: the fused kernel, the fused kernel with the return-all-CTA
config, and the top-k reduce. This PR regenerates the nine CuTe-DSL
programs (3 programs × 3 architectures) so they use the CUDA backend's
cross-rank protocol and workspace. The fused kernel now arms the route
terms on every forward, and the top-k reduce no longer re-arms them.

Compared with the CuTe-DSL backend on current `main`, EP16 runs
1.050–1.065× faster on GB300 and 1.074–1.103× faster on R200.

**Table 1.** NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), 16 GPUs (4 nodes × 4
GPUs in one NVLink domain), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CuTe-DSL
(nvidia-cutlass-dsl) 4.7.0. Latency is one eager EP16 forward with a
cold L2, timed with CUDA events. Each value is the maximum over ranks of
the per-rank median, over 12 rounds × 40 iterations, with sessions
recreated each round in alternating order. Baseline is the CuTe-DSL
backend on current `main`, and Speedup = baseline / this PR. In
"Pre-sleep" mode, a GPU sleep of 1e6 cycles precedes each launch. In
"Back-to-back" mode, launches run with no sleep. T is tokens per rank.
`balanced` routing spreads routes evenly across experts, and `hotset50`
sends half of the routes to a hot set of experts. Every row has a
one-sided Mann-Whitney p = 3.7e-07 (this PR faster).

| Launch mode | T | Routing | Baseline (µs) | This PR (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pre-sleep | 16 | balanced | 301.73 | 284.04 | 1.062× |
| Pre-sleep | 16 | hotset50 | 304.26 | 285.58 | 1.065× |
| Pre-sleep | 32 | balanced | 302.37 | 284.29 | 1.064× |
| Pre-sleep | 32 | hotset50 | 301.70 | 284.55 | 1.060× |
| Pre-sleep | 64 | balanced | 302.98 | 287.63 | 1.053× |
| Pre-sleep | 64 | hotset50 | 303.80 | 289.41 | 1.050× |
| Back-to-back | 16 | balanced | 301.71 | 285.31 | 1.057× |
| Back-to-back | 16 | hotset50 | 302.48 | 285.84 | 1.058× |
| Back-to-back | 32 | balanced | 302.72 | 285.06 | 1.062× |
| Back-to-back | 32 | hotset50 | 302.47 | 285.31 | 1.060× |
| Back-to-back | 64 | balanced | 302.92 | 287.36 | 1.054× |
| Back-to-back | 64 | hotset50 | 303.78 | 289.42 | 1.050× |

**Table 2.** NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), 16 GPUs (4 nodes × 4 GPUs),
CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CuTe-DSL (nvidia-cutlass-dsl) 4.8.1.
The timing method, baseline, launch modes and routings are the same as
in Table 1. Every row has a one-sided Mann-Whitney p = 3.7e-07 (this PR

sm_100a (B200) EP16 is not measured because the available B200 systems
have 8-GPU NVLink domains, so EP16 cannot run on them (`main` fails the

sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [cddf9ae](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cddf9ae39905151da2924fa69940955ada7b46fc)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:30:17Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): measured K1 token coverage on 148-, 212- and 216-SM parts (#8595)

`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` provides BF16-input
dense and batched projection GEMMs with BF16 or FP32 output, and an FP32
router GEMM. The default, `deterministic=True`, calls
`dense_projection_det_gemm`. With `deterministic=False`, the package
runs its split-K / stream-K programs on the rows that its measured
routing tables select. Every other row runs the deterministic program.

This PR changes one variant: the weight gradient (wgrad) with
`deterministic=False`, at measured token counts on three part types. All
other token counts, rows and SM counts keep their current programs.

- R200 `sm_107a`, 212 SMs: `5120 -> 1024` with BF16 output now runs the
256-wide one-split program from 512 to 12288 tokens. Before this PR, it
ran the deterministic program there.
- B200 `sm_100a` and B300 `sm_103a`, parts with exactly 148 SMs: 17
(`sm_100a`) and 34 (`sm_103a`) measured token counts now run the
deterministic program instead of the split program. This includes the
token counts between consecutive measured counts of a row. The same
change applies to all token counts from 65536 up for `4096 -> 64` with
FP32 output on `sm_100a`, and for `4096 -> 32` (BF16 and FP32 output) on
`sm_103a`.
- R200 `sm_107a`, 216 SMs and more: 12 single token counts now run the
deterministic program.

Columns: "det" is the deterministic Cake program. "SOTA" is the
strongest non-Cake library GEMM. "previous" is the program that the row
ran before this PR. "new" is the program that it runs now. Ratio =
baseline us / new us; above 1.00 means the new routing is faster. Where
the new program is the deterministic one, det/new is 1.000 by
definition. In the lists below, graph means CUDA graph replay and eager
means eager launches. wgrad is the weight-gradient op alone, bwd is the
whole backward, and ckpt is the checkpointed step.

**Timing conditions.** Each time is the CUPTI span of all launches of
the op. L2 is cold before every iteration: a 2x-L2 buffer is cleared.
Single op: median of paired groups of 20 timed iterations, with 15
groups on 212 and 216 SMs and 9 groups on 148 SMs. Whole backward (input
gradient + weight gradient) and checkpointed step (2 forward + input
gradient + weight gradient): cold L2 before every sequence, median of 9
paired groups. CUDA graph replay and eager launches, PDL on. SOTA is,
per row, the fastest correct library launch among `torch.mm` (cuBLAS
13.8.0.4) and the top 8 algorithms of the cuBLASLt heuristic. It uses
the same BF16 operands and output dtype, and is chosen on the same GPU
in the same process; for the whole steps, it is chosen per op. This is
the strongest non-Cake GEMM available for these layouts and output
dtypes on these parts.

0.972 to 1.030, ckpt 0.992 to 1.032 (above 65536 tokens: 0.998 to 1.002,
0.998 to 1.013, 1.000 to 1.007); 216 SMs part 1 wgrad 0.995 to 1.008,
bwd 0.988 to 1.016, ckpt 0.989 to 1.039; part 2 wgrad 0.982 to 1.005,
bwd 0.986 to 1.006, ckpt 0.983 to 1.041.

**Software** on every part: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), nvcc 13.4,
cuBLAS 13.8.0.4. Drivers: R200 `sm_107a` 212 SMs 620.43, 216 SMs
615.71.10; B200 `sm_100a` 580.82.07; B300 `sm_103a` 580.126.09.

The 212-SM table below lists run 1 in graph and eager mode (run 2 is
only in the ranges above), and the other tables list the graph-mode
rows, with absolute us for every column. The eager ranges are in the
bullets above.

The split programs of this package ship for `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and
`sm_107a`. This PR does not change the other variants: input gradient,
forward, batched projections, the router GEMM, BF16 vs FP32 output, and
`deterministic=True`.
