### [7b78bd4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7b78bd40eed6cabb755edfb0b9beee61ad3511b1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:26:11Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): per-warp TMA final-state store for short many-task turnover launches on sm_100a in BF16 KDA prefill (#8628)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. They come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes only the prepared BF16-input path with FP32 state
(`flashinfer.prepare_bf16_kda_prefill`), and only on sm_100a. It changes
the binned turnover launches of the direct route that are short and have
many tasks. A launch qualifies when its longest task has at most two
32-token chunks (64 tokens or fewer) and it has at least 4 tasks per SM.
These launches now use the turnover program that stores the final FP32
state with a per-warp TMA store. sm_103a has shipped this program since
the previous version. A new short-task table, used only on sm_100a,
selects these launches. Every other sm_100a turnover launch keeps the
stock program and does no extra host work. An architecture with an empty
table skips the check, so the sm_103a programs and routes do not change.
The PR also re-renders one other prefill program with the current
generator. Its SASS is identical on both arches. Outputs are
bit-identical.

The tables compare this PR with the previous Cake version on FlashInfer
main. They report the median latency per call in microseconds, with a
cold L2. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or
-5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. TIE means no difference beyond the
measurement band. Both B200 gains are at BS64 x T64 with no gate lower
bound. With 12 heads, latency drops from 58.75 to 56.09 us (1.05x) on
the fast path and from 59.07 to 56.51 us (1.05x) in serving. With 16
heads, it drops from 69.12 to 66.59 us (1.04x) on the fast path and from
69.54 to 67.01 us (1.04x) in serving. The other 54 B200 rows are TIE in
both tables, including the 0.99x rows. GB300 has no program change, and
every counted GB300 row is a TIE. One GB300 fast-path row is marked †
and is not counted: 16 heads, gate lower bound -5, 2x(8128+64). In that
row, the timing of both sides drifted beyond the measurement guard
within one run. This also happens when FlashInfer main is timed against
itself.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. GB300: NVIDIA
GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.167.08. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

### [9b79151](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9b79151945d3f0aec8c71aed421c4f1c3fe7ba24)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:17:40Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_softmax): issue register-tile loads before the CTA barrier in the 8-CTA low-latency kernels (#8617)

The Cake Blackwell FP32 softmax behind `flashinfer.sampling.softmax`
sends each shape to one of several kernels. This PR changes only the
8-CTA low-latency shared-tile kernel `c8_t4_s4_lat` and its PDL twin.
Each thread now issues its four register-tile global loads before the
CTA barrier and the elected-thread shared-tile TMA / mbarrier setup, so
the loads overlap that setup. The arithmetic is unchanged, and the
outputs are bitwise identical to main. The 16-CTA low-latency kernel
`c16_t4_s4_lat` is unchanged, because the same reordering slowed small
batches on B200. The low-latency forms serve sm_100 (B200) at every
batch size. On other architectures they serve only grids of at most two
waves. On B200, shapes routed to `c8_t4_s4_lat` run 1.009x to 1.023x
faster than main. Shapes routed to other kernels (the cached-cluster row
kernel and the persistent cached-cluster kernel) are unchanged and
measure at parity, 0.998x to 1.005x. On GB300 (sm_103a), 14 shapes of at
most two waves measured 0.997x to 1.004x vs main, which is parity.

**B200 (sm_100a)**, FP32 logits, temperature 1.0, CUDA 13.4, median of
12 cold-L2 runs (µs).

| batch x vocab | kernel | main | this PR | speedup vs main |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 x 100000 | 16-CTA cached-cluster row (unchanged) | 5.760 | 5.760 |
1.000x |
| 32 x 100000 | 16-CTA cached-cluster row (unchanged) | 8.240 | 8.248 |
0.999x |
| 64 x 100000 | persistent cached-cluster (unchanged) | 11.616 | 11.624
| 0.999x |
| 128 x 100000 | persistent cached-cluster (unchanged) | 19.056 | 19.016
| 1.002x |
| 256 x 100000 | persistent cached-cluster (unchanged) | 35.240 | 35.312
| 0.998x |
| 403 x 100000 | `c8_t4_s4_lat` | 53.079 | 51.896 | 1.023x |
| 1024 x 100000 | `c8_t4_s4_lat` | 124.063 | 122.935 | 1.009x |
| 128 x 81928 | persistent cached-cluster (unchanged) | 16.800 | 16.832
| 0.998x |
| 403 x 81928 | `c8_t4_s4_lat` | 44.544 | 44.064 | 1.011x |
| 96 x 128000 | persistent cached-cluster (unchanged) | 17.552 | 17.472

The other kernels in the family are unchanged: the 16-CTA low-latency
shared-tile kernel, the multi-wave shared-tile kernels, the warp kernel,
the row-wise kernel, the cached-cluster row kernels (1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 12
or 16 CTAs per row) and the persistent cached-cluster kernel; the family
covers sm_100a (B200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a.

### [7cec832](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7cec8325f678be0c6d2d09de4e05ea464167797e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:15:42Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det_kcp): shorter host prologue of the in-kernel q/k L2 norm backward (#8552)

## 📌 Description

With `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`, the KCP backward spent about 100 us
more host time before its first kernel launch than the flag-off
backward. This PR shortens that host prologue. It changes two files in
`flashinfer/experimental/cake_kda_det_train_kcp/`: `cake_kcp.py` and
`cake_kcp_plan.py`.

- In the fused form with saved mode, `dv` and `dbeta` are now allocated
after the first local stage is launched, because that stage's record
binds none of them. In raw gate mode, the parameter partials and the
finalize scratch also move after that launch.
- The moved arena views are built with one `as_strided` view. The view
namespace is copied through its dict.
- The workspace's capability check keeps the CUDA device it is passed
and imports its backend modules once.

Outputs and the order of refusal errors are unchanged.

### Performance

GB200 (sm_100a), 4 GPUs, torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0).

Workload: the KCP W4 row of the KDA training benchmark (T_r = 16384
tokens per rank, `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`, persistent workspace,
12 seeds). Each value is the median over all iterations. main and this
PR ran back to back on the same node.

| mode | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | this PR / main |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| forward | 3.273 | 3.268 | 0.9986 |
| backward | 5.844 | 5.824 | 0.9966 |
| forward + backward | 8.837 | 8.816 | 0.9976 |
| checkpointed forward + backward | 11.277 | 11.228 | 0.9957 |

The end-to-end effect is small. The unchanged flag-off arm of the same
runs moved by up to 0.4% between the two runs, so these differences are
within run-to-run variation. Peak memory is identical in every mode.

The host profile of the flag-on backward call shows a clearer change:

- Time from the KCP backward entry to its first stage launch drops from
196.0 us (main) to 181.0 us (this PR).
- The capability check `WorkspaceDetKcp._require_l2n` drops from 9.9 us
to 1.4 us.

GB300 (sm_103a), 4 GPUs, torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0). Same workload
as above. main (commit cbb7d408) and this PR (head f59cb9b5) ran back to
back on the same node; each value is the median over all iterations.

| mode | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | this PR / main |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| forward | 3.245 | 3.250 | 1.0014 |
| backward | 5.686 | 5.663 | 0.9959 |
| forward + backward | 8.563 | 8.594 | 1.0037 |
| checkpointed forward + backward | 10.949 | 10.915 | 0.9969 |

The unchanged flag-off arm of the same runs moved by up to 0.41% between
the two runs. For forward + backward, the flag-off arm moved +0.34%,
which matches the +0.37% of the flag-on arm. Within each run, the
flag-on / flag-off backward ratio drops from 1.0411 (main) to 1.0378
(this PR). Their 95% confidence intervals do not overlap ([1.0405,
1.0417] vs [1.0372, 1.0385]). The ratios of the other three modes change
by at most 0.001. Peak memory is identical in every mode.

Host profile of the flag-on backward call on GB300 (rank 0 medians over
40 iterations):

- Time from the KCP backward entry to its first stage launch drops from
185.9 us (main) to 174.2 us (this PR).
- The capability check `WorkspaceDetKcp._require_l2n` drops from 9.8 us
to 1.3 us.
- The deferred outputs are allocated right after the backward's first
local stage is launched. So most of the host time removed before the
first launch moves to after it, where it overlaps that stage's device
work. The capability-check saving is removed outright.

The total host time of the backward call shows no difference beyond
process-to-process variation on either GPU. In the same process, the
flag-on backward call minus the flag-off backward call is -170.1 us
(main) vs -194.1 us (this PR) on GB200, and -165.0 us (main) vs -133.0
us (this PR) on GB300. But the flag-off backward call, which this PR
leaves unchanged, differed between the two processes by 85 us on GB200
(2185.2 us vs 2270.5 us) and by 38 us on GB300 (2107.0 us vs 2145.2 us).
The first-launch and capability-check numbers above remain the clear
changes.

### [cd745dc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cd745dc27999bf61a0ab897c369904b75bc09287)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:04:52Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_train): run the deterministic package's pairs in more backward windows (#8626)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). The two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`, use the same forward and differ only in the
backward. Both modes support these forms:

- [T, H] rows with BF16 weight, or FP32 weight (`w32`)
- fused residual add (`res`, H6144)
- per-head views [T,24,256] (strided) and [T,4,256] (contiguous), with a
shared w[256]

This follow-up to #8577 changes only the `deterministic=False` backward,
and only on sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300). In the windows below,
that backward now runs a pair from the deterministic package (main
kernel + fixed-order dw reduce) in place of the #8577 programs. In this
list, rows = T for [T, H], 24T for [T,24,256] and 4T for [T,4,256]:

- B200: H256 problems with 92160 < rows <= 524288 (both weight dtypes);
H6144 `w32` with 1168 < T <= 1408.
- GB300: H256 problems with 1080 < rows <= 5120 or 12288 < rows <=
720896 (both weight dtypes); H6144 `res` with 56 < T <= 304 or 1920 < T
<= 2304; H6144 `res w32` with 1824 < T <= 2304.

In most of these windows, the pair is the same one that
`deterministic=True` launches for the same rows (`=` in the tables). The
GB300 H256 windows 1080 < rows <= 2048 and 97280 < rows <= 99840 use a
different pair from the same package; the [T,24,256] T4096 rows measure
the second of these. sm_107a (R200) routes are unchanged from #8577, so
this PR has no R200 table.

Speedup = baseline latency / new latency. A value > 1 means the new
kernel is faster. Geomeans, vs deterministic / vs SOTA:

- Shapes whose backward changes in this PR (`^`):
- B200 (6 shapes): fwd 1.000x / 1.025x, bwd 0.997x / 1.131x, 2xfwd+bwd
1.001x / 1.086x

Notable rows:

- Changed shapes vs det. Some bwd and 2xfwd+bwd rows launch the same
programs in both modes (`=`). These read det/new 0.986 to 1.003 on B200
(12 rows) and 0.969 to 1.011 on GB300 (36 rows), which is inside the
order band described below. The printed ratios are measured values; none
is set to 1.00x. GB300 [T,24,256] T4096 runs a different pair from det:
bwd 33.15 vs 32.42 us (0.98x), 2xfwd+bwd 62.59 vs 61.70 us (0.99x).
- Changed shapes vs SOTA. Every bwd and 2xfwd+bwd row is faster than
SOTA: 1.04x to 1.25x on B200 and 1.05x to 1.64x on GB300. The forward is
unchanged, and the fwd rows of these shapes are below SOTA on 4 of 6
shapes (B200) and 15 of 19 (GB300). The lowest is GB300 [T,4,256] T4096
fwd: 4.96 vs 4.61 us (tcd, 0.93x).
- Rows below 0.95x vs det. This PR does not change the programs of any
of these shapes. Latencies are new vs det:
- B200: H256 T1048576 bwd 292.89 vs 262.27 us (0.90x), and its `w32`
form 295.13 vs 259.25 us (0.88x; 2xfwd+bwd 0.94x). [T,24,256] T65536 bwd
427.66 vs 384.77 us (0.90x, `!`). H1536 T1024 bwd 7.78 vs 7.33 us
(0.94x), although both modes launch the same programs there; this is the
low end of the order band.
- GB300: H1536 T56320 bwd 112.38 vs 88.67 us (0.79x; `w32` 0.78x). H1536
T65536 bwd 128.48 vs 101.63 us (0.79x). H2048 T65536 bwd 144.90 vs
128.51 us (0.89x). H5120 T65536 bwd 363.25 vs 313.50 us (0.86x; `w32`
0.85x). H6144 T65536 w32 bwd 391.07 vs 366.11 us (0.94x). The 2xfwd+bwd
rows of the H1536 and H5120 shapes read 0.91x to 0.93x.
- Lowest bwd vs SOTA. None of these shapes changes in this PR:
  - B200 H256 T1048576 w32: 295.13 vs 271.57 us (tc, 0.92x)
  - GB300 H1536 T56320 w32: 112.96 vs 93.89 us (qa, 0.83x)
  - GB300 H1536 T56320 and T65536: 0.85x (qa)

Baselines and measurement. Every row has two baselines:

- det: the deterministic Cake kernel (`deterministic=True`). Its GPU
programs are those of FlashInfer main at 59432d00, the same as in #8577.
This PR does not change the deterministic package. #8512, merged after
these runs, changes the deterministic backward at small T; of the rows
here, it changes only the det programs of B200 H2048 T256 (bwd and
2xfwd+bwd).
- SOTA: per row, the fastest non-Cake candidate that has the same
outputs (BF16 y / dx / h_new, FP32 rstd / dw) and meets the accuracy
budget. Every candidate is timed on every row, except torch.compile
max-autotune on the B200 `p` rows. Configurations that return dw in the
weight dtype (the public PyTorch, Liger, QuACK and TE APIs on
BF16-weight rows) do not have matched outputs and are never chosen.

new = the non-deterministic Cake kernel of this PR
(`deterministic=False`). The accuracy budget takes the worst of 5 seeds:
dx atol = rtol = 1e-2, and dw per element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64.

Latency = median of 804 CUPTI spans per implementation per row. There
are 1608 spans for the two GB300 shapes timed twice, and 402 or 603 for
the SOTA implementation on `h` rows. One span is one CUDA-graph replay
after an L2 flush (cold L2), and it includes the implementation's own
setup, reduction, cast and copy kernels. For each GPU type, 4 sessions
ran in parallel on 4 GPUs of one node. Each session ran 3 interleaved
rounds x 67 replays. eps = 1e-6. Latencies print to 0.01 us and per-row
ratios to 0.01x. The geomeans use unrounded values.

Two caveats apply to all ratios:

- Fixed implementation order. Implementations run in a fixed list order:
det first, the non-Cake candidates, then new. Two of the four sessions
use the reversed list, and alternate rounds replay the list reversed.
The check reported in #8577 found that this fixed order alone moves an
implementation's latency by up to about 5 %. In this run, bwd and
2xfwd+bwd rows where det and new launch the same programs read det/new
0.942 to 1.041 on B200 (62 rows) and 0.947 to 1.051 on GB300 (136 rows).
The fwd rows (same forward in both modes) read 0.978 to 1.038 on B200
and 0.972 to 1.046 on GB300. A ratio within about 5 % of 1.00x is
therefore not a measured difference.
- torch.compile in the process. All implementations of a row run in one
process that also loads every non-Cake candidate, including
torch.compile. The check reported in #8577 found that a torch.compile
function in the process makes every non-compile implementation run
faster. On small rows, the Cake kernels and the other libraries (QuACK,
TE, torch, Liger) run up to about 30 % shorter than in a process without
torch.compile; torch.compile itself runs within about 3 % of the same
speed in both. So the table compares all implementations in the same
state. On small rows, the Cake kernels gain somewhat more than the other
non-compile libraries. The ratio vs those libraries reads up to about
1.10x (GB300) and 1.14x (B200) higher than in a process without
torch.compile, so these small-row ratios may overstate the new kernel's
lead by up to that factor. On large rows, this difference is at most
1.02x. Ratios vs det are not affected, because both are Cake kernels in
the same process.

Key:

- Shapes: H = hidden size, T = tokens. x / y / dx are BF16, rstd / dw
are FP32, and w is BF16 unless marked `w32`. `res` adds the BF16 output
h_new. `[T,24,256]` has strides (12288, 512, 1), and `[T,4,256]` is
contiguous. Both share w[256].
- op: `step` = 2xfwd+bwd (checkpointed).
- SOTA:
- tc = torch.compile of an explicit FP32-statistics reference (torch
2.14.1+cu130, inductor max-autotune-no-cudagraphs,
emulate_precision_casts=True)
  - tcd = the same in torch.compile default mode
  - q = QuACK 0.6.5 (nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1) heuristic config
- qa = QuACK 0.6.5 exhaustive per-shape autotune (rmsnorm_fwd_tuned /
rmsnorm_bwd_tuned, cached before timing)
  - on `res` rows, QuACK is torch add + QuACK
  - lg = Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton 3.8.0, casting_mode gemma)
- Transformer Engine 2.20.2 runs only as the FP32 problem, with the
casts inside its span. It was never fastest.
- PyTorch's fused rms_norm cannot run this form (BF16 x with FP32 w).
Apex FusedRMSNorm has no wheel. FlashInfer's inference rmsnorm is
forward only.
- Marks:
- `^`: the backward programs of this shape change in this PR (bwd and
2xfwd+bwd rows).
- `=`: det and new launch the same GPU programs for this op (bwd and
2xfwd+bwd rows). Every fwd row launches the same forward programs in
both modes.
- `~`: for det, SOTA or new, (max - min) / min of the 4 session medians
is above 5.0 %.
- `!`: no matched candidate meets the dw budget. The fastest matched one
is shown, and the row is left out of the vs-SOTA statistics.
- `p`: torch.compile max-autotune did not run on this row (disk-quota
error in that run), so SOTA is the fastest of the other candidates.
- `h`: the SOTA implementation ran in only 2 or 3 of the 4 sessions (402
or 603 spans instead of 804).

**B200 (sm_100a)**

B200, 148 SMs, sm_100a, compute capability 10.0, driver 580.82.07, CUDA
13.4 (nvcc cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0), torch 2.14.1+cu130. SM
clock median 1965 MHz (98-99 % of samples at max), memory clock 3996
MHz, 4 GPUs of one node, no foreign GPU processes.

Rows: 86 shapes x 3 ops = 258 rows. These are the 78-shape list plus
H256 T49152, T262144 and T1048576 (both weight dtypes), H4096 T1536 w32
and H6144 T1280 w32.

The 3 H4096 T1536 w32 rows come from a second run on another B200 node
with the same software (SM clock 100 % at max). The first run timed a
backward pair that this PR does not ship; that window keeps the #8577
programs. Because these 3 rows come from a different node, compare their
ratios with the other rows, not their latencies.

- `!`: 2 rows, [T,24,256] T65536 bwd and 2xfwd+bwd.
- `p`: 39 rows, none on a changed shape. They cover H1536 T65536, plus
T256, T1024 and T4096 of H5120 w32, H6144 w32, H6144 res and H6144 res
w32.
- `h`: 7 rows.

**GB300 (sm_103a)**

GB300, 152 SMs, sm_103a, compute capability 10.3, driver 580.159.03,
CUDA 13.4 (same nvcc as B200), torch 2.14.1+cu130. SM clock 2070 MHz
(100 % of samples at max), memory clock 3996 MHz, 4 GPUs of one node, no
foreign GPU processes.

Rows: 93 shapes x 3 ops = 279 rows. These are the 78-shape list plus:

- H256 T3000, T26624, T65536, T262144 and T1048576, and H1536 T56320
(both weight dtypes)
- H6144 T200 res, H6144 T2048 res and H6144 T2048 res w32

H6144 T1024 res and H6144 T1024 res w32 are in both row lists and were
timed twice (1608 spans). There are no `!`, `p` or `h` rows.

### [9340cb3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9340cb34c7fdfb0fda2812b7bfacef0edd15e9f1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T08:04:24Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP4 / TP8 EP1, TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8 T4096 rank programs on sm_103a (#8627)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline for the 384-expert, top-6, hidden-5120 model with activation
clamp 10. A single kernel launch covers dispatch, FC1, clamped SwiGLU,
MXFP8 activation quantization, FC2 and weighted combine. The kernel has
four variants on main: single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8,
grouped-GEMM routes, and the TP/EP rank variant. The rank variant has 32
programs: TP4 EP1 (384 experts, width 640), TP8 EP1 (384 experts, width
384), TP4 EP4 (96 local experts) and TP8 EP8 (48 local experts), each at
1 to 4096 tokens.

This PR updates the rank variant. It changes 4 of the 32 programs, all
at 4096 tokens: TP4 EP1, TP8 EP1, TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8. Only L2
cache-policy hints change:
- The dispatch bulk stores use evict_last on TP4 EP1, TP8 EP1 and TP4
EP4.
- The FC2 partial stores use evict_last on TP4 EP1, TP8 EP1 and TP8 EP8.
- The weight and weight scale-factor loads use evict_first on TP8 EP8.

The outputs are bitwise identical to the previous version. The other 28
rank programs and every host binding are unchanged. The catalog closure
hashes of the 4 changed programs change.

Speedup over the previous Cake version (the rank variant on FlashInfer
main after #8594), for replicates a / b:

- TP4 EP1 at 4096 tokens: 1.009x / 1.009x, saving 3.67 / 3.76 µs per
call
- TP8 EP1 at 4096 tokens: 1.016x / 1.015x, saving 4.65 / 4.56 µs per
call
- TP4 EP4 at 4096 tokens: 1.010x / 1.010x, saving 3.19 / 3.29 µs per
call
- TP8 EP8 at 4096 tokens: 1.029x / 1.026x, saving 5.10 / 4.72 µs per
call

All four changes are faster than the A/A noise band in both replicates.
The other 28 programs run 0.999x to 1.001x in replicate a and 0.997x to
1.003x in replicate b.

Speedup over the issue baseline, autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`: this PR is faster on all 32 shapes
in both replicates. The range is 1.023x to 1.172x in replicate a and
1.018x to 1.178x in replicate b. On the four changed shapes it is 1.068x
/ 1.069x (TP4 EP1), 1.070x / 1.076x (TP8 EP1), 1.118x / 1.125x (TP4 EP4)
and 1.172x / 1.178x (TP8 EP8).

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.159.03, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. Columns 3-8 compare this PR with the previous Cake version
(FlashInfer main after #8594), with speedup = previous / this PR.
Per-call latency comes from CUDA-graph replays (20 calls per graph),
taking the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous version and this
PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6 rounds. Each value is
the median of the 6 process medians. Speedups are computed from the
latencies before rounding to two decimals. Columns a and b are two
independent replicates, each run alone on its own node. Each replicate
also timed the previous version against itself (an A/A control) to
measure its noise band. The widest band is 0.20 % in replicate a and
0.58 % in replicate b. Columns 9-14 compare autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` with this PR, with speedup = TRT-LLM
/ this PR. They come from a separate run of the same commit on the same
two nodes, so the this-PR latencies there differ slightly from columns 4
and 7. The kernels and host bindings of the 28 unchanged programs are
byte-identical to the previous version and compile to the same machine
code. Two of them, TP8 EP1 at 128 tokens (+0.040 / +0.034 µs) and TP8
EP8 at 128 tokens (+0.027 / +0.020 µs), read slower than their narrow
A/A band in both replicates. That is process-level noise, not a
regression.*

The other three variants (single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8
and grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a; the rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [b791f51](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b791f51454ac1b7e84f03882c3ac51e6a105a89b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:54:09Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train): L2-prefetching mid forward on SM100 and SM103 (#8622)

This PR adds an L2-prefetching build of the mid forward to the
non-deterministic package of Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` with `deterministic=False`).
On sm_100a and sm_103a, the mid forward now routes to that build. In the
new module, `cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_87f0173e9583ad4fdd2a`, thread
0 also warms two later row blocks in L2, with one bulk prefetch per
tensor, wherever the inputs x and z hold their rows packed. The two
blocks are the CTA's next block and the CTA's first block one resident
wave later. The routing thresholds do not change: on these two
architectures, the mid forward serves inputs from 976 rows per SM up to
the long forward's 2400. The six shapes per GPU in Table 1 fall in that
range.

Every other module is FlashInfer main's code. The backward, the short
and long forwards, and every sm_107a route run the same code as before.
The forward modules' build settings now include the two prefetch
settings, so the long, mid (sm_107a) and short forward modules shipped
before get new names; the renamed modules are the same code under new
names.

| forward | name on FlashInfer main | name in this PR | architectures |
|---|---|---|---|
| long | `cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_e0672c312c57421abe21` |
`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_7b7fac905aff1ddaa258` | sm_100a, sm_103a,
sm_107a |
| mid | `cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_8bd481246a4b97382250` |
`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_b0eb3df9844d5b734850` | sm_107a |
| short | `cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_55ff8a9d0ba6d83285b5` |
`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train_de5df3c9a4a5a804fcf2` | sm_100a, sm_103a,
sm_107a |

The PR is one commit on FlashInfer main after PR #8556 (merge commit
7b20619a9c26f017826109e6c7b59bc1ba0c0d27). The "previous Cake" baseline
below is FlashInfer main's route, where the mid forward runs without the
prefetch. The A/B compared FlashInfer main at
61bc8b6dd7049a44d614b2a0cd4a036cb3c46ad0 with the same tree plus this
PR's mid forward and routes. That commit predates PR #8556, which
changes no sm_100a or sm_103a route. In the measured tree, the new
module's sources are byte-identical to this PR's, and the unchanged
modules keep their old names.

A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. The table gives ranges (min-max) over the six shapes of Table 1.
For stepg_f32 and fwd + bwd, the ranges cover the ten shapes of Table 2:
those six, plus four shapes that run the same code in both trees.

In the pre-registered A/B, all 24 cells per GPU whose code changes (fwd,

torch.compile is faster than the new forward at 5 of the 12 B200 forward
rows and at 1 of the 12 GB300 forward rows, each time by 1 % or less.
Every cell below 1x is listed under "Cells below 1x".

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`) and the FP32 weight-gradient output of the
non-deterministic package. Both packages ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a. This PR changes only the non-deterministic package's mid
forward on sm_100a and sm_103a, and sm_107a keeps its code.

## How the tables were measured

- Latency: CUPTI kernel time with cold L2 (FlashInfer's
`bench_gpu_time`), BF16 inputs. All times are in us.
- Table 1: the deterministic Cake kernel, the strongest non-Cake kernel
and new were measured in the same process. Each value is the median of
the per-round medians over 10 rounds.
- A/B values: the previous Cake and new (A/B) columns and all of Table 2
are medians of the pre-registered interleaved A/B, with 16 sequences and
160 processes per GPU model. The deterministic Cake values in the
stepg_f32 rows also come from the A/B.
- Strongest non-Cake kernel per row: the fastest of the following, with
torch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0.
  - FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated` (`fla.modules.fused_norm_gate`).
  - mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn` (`layernorm_gated`).
- torch.compile in default and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs modes, best of
5 fresh compiles each. `#k` names the fastest compile.
- The inductor-generated persistent-reduction Triton kernel of the FP32
formula, launched directly.
- Deterministic Cake: `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`,
unchanged by this PR.
- Operations:
- `fwd` is one eager forward call, and `fwdg` is the forward replayed
from a CUDA graph.
  - `bwdg` is the backward replayed from a CUDA graph.
- `ckptg` is the checkpointed step (2 x forward + backward) in one CUDA
graph, and `stepg_f32` is the same step with an FP32 dw.
  - `fwd + bwd` is fwdg + bwdg, derived.
- In Table 2, the first six shapes run the new module. 2048x48, 3009x48
(B200) / 3090x48 (GB300), 7400x48 (B200) / 7600x48 (GB300) and 16384x48
run the same code in both trees.

### [d89f45c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d89f45cd8a9d4ca03c691b810e425697bc1baeb0)

- **作者**: Perkz Zheng
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:52:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(prims-ts): faster D576 and D512 (DSv4) sparse MLA decode on SM103/SM107 (#8322)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Faster sparse MLA decode for D576 (top-k 2048) and D512 (DSv4: SWA128 +
top-k 512/1024). Scheduling, data movement and pipeline depth only;
attention math is unchanged.

**D576**
- **SM107: third retained NVFP4 K/V tile** in the 2CTA kernel (279 KiB
of SM107's 327 KiB SMEM). NVFP4 grids that would split only twice now
run one unsplit wave instead.
- **Split reducers (all GPUs):** the reducers synchronize on barrier 1
instead of barrier 4, so more reducer CTAs fit on an SM. On SM107 that
goes from 3 to 8 resident CTAs.
- **H12/H16 native FP8, rows > SM/4, q <= 8 (all GPUs):** these grids
now use the eight-issuer Swap-AB. The split is SM/rows up to one wave, 2
below 1.5 waves, and 1 with CLC persistence above that.
- **SM107: two-slot NVFP4 raw record ring** for persistent 1CTA grids
(264 KB). The 1CTA SMEM check uses the compile target's capacity.
- **SM107: third V stage** for the native FP8 2CTA wave grid.

**D512 (DSv4)**
- **NVFP4:** the whole-tile Keep-AB schedule now covers capacity >= 512,
and small grids take one KV tile per split (Swap-AB keeps at least two).
H128 uses it up to 16 KV tiles per split and keeps the 2CTA split above
that.
- **Native FP8 H64, 16 rows up to one wave:** padded to 128 heads on the
2CTA kernel, with no KV split.
- **Persistent 1CTA NVFP4:** two-slot raw record ring.
- **FP8 2CTA H128 wave grids:** BF16 output goes through SMEM and a TMA
store; short-Q grids get a third V stage.

Kernel time (us, CUDA graph, cold L2, same GPU, before -> after):

| GPU | Case | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VR200 | D576 NVFP4 H96, 4 x 8 (3 splits) | 25.70 | 21.28 | 1.21x |
| VR200 | D576 NVFP4 H96, 256 x 4 | 226.0 | 205.5 | 1.10x |
| VR200 | D576 NVFP4 H96, prefill 8192 | 1687 | 1494 | 1.13x |
| GB300 | D576 FP8 H12, 128 rows | 65.6 | 56.5 | 1.16x |
| VR200 | D576 FP8 H12, 107 rows | 44.4 | 36.7 | 1.21x |
| Rubin, 216 SMs | D576 NVFP4 H12, 832 rows | 124.8 | 114.8 | 1.09x |
| Rubin, 216 SMs | D576 NVFP4 H64, 832 rows | 144.3 | 131.4 | 1.10x |
| Rubin, 216 SMs | D576 FP8 H128, 1024 rows | 130.5 | 127.8 | 1.02x |
| GB300 | D512 NVFP4 H64, 64 rows, top-k 512 | 70.9 | 18.4 | 3.87x |
| GB300 | D512 FP8 H64, 64 rows, top-k 1024 | 25.4 | 17.4 | 1.46x |

Ranges and unchanged cases:
- H12/H16 FP8 wave fill: 1.05-1.22x on GB300 and VR200.
- D512 NVFP4: geomean 0.784 of the old time over 96 shapes.
- SM107 ring: 1.06-1.12x; SM107 third V stage: 1.01-1.02x.
- Unchanged:
  - shapes outside these rules, within 0.3-1%;
  - B300 for the first three items, geomean 1.00x;
- the D576 shapes across the D512 commit, geomean 1.000-1.002x on GB300
and VR200.
- Outputs stay within the FP64 reference bound.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #8186.

an sm_100f build on SM107 plans generically.

### [2982836](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/298283694f5a0cff2635f58e564d5e0d6cfe9a5c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:46:59Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): add NVFP4-KV runtime-size paged context programs for sm_100a and sm_103a (#8619)

The Cake NVFP4-KV paged context family ships exact Q511 programs. Until
now, every other causal page-16 NVFP4 call ran a JIT-compiled module.
This PR adds 18 runtime-size programs: GQA packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12
and 16 on both sm_100a and sm_103a. Each of these calls, with host or
device scales, now runs the program for its JIT pack. Calls whose pack
has no program keep the JIT module, and so do toolkits older than CUDA
13.4. Outputs are bitwise equal to the JIT module. The baseline below is
the previous Cake path for these calls, which is the JIT module, and
trtllm-gen is shown as a second column. On B200, this PR is
1.279x-2.156x faster than the previous path across 28 shapes. On GB300,
it is 1.285x-3.958x faster across 28 shapes. Against trtllm-gen, this PR
is slower on 6 of 28 B200 shapes and 9 of 28 GB300 shapes. The worst
case is 1-32-32768-32-4-16 on GB300: 401.89 µs for this PR vs 277.25 µs
for trtllm-gen.

### [f2a5262](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f2a5262ca2e1f366e6fb3d5414b3cf0b83d519c7)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:40:39Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): counted temperature dz recompute under the zero-gradient row skip (#8612)

Cake's chunked LM-head + loss training backend has a deterministic form
(the default) and a non-deterministic (ND) form
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`), measured via
`chunked_lm_head_logprob(..., deterministic=False)` with a scalar or
per-token FP32 `[T]` temperature (#8436). On FlashInfer main (#8514),
its backward skips rows whose log-probability gradient (dlogp) is zero
in dX and dW but recomputes the tempered logit gradient dz over all
rows. This PR adds counted tempered dz programs, on by default when
`deterministic=False`, that run only the work items of rows with
non-zero dlogp on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a: two new kernel programs
(one for sm_100a, one for sm_103a that sm_107a also uses) and 3 new
package entries; the 172 existing entries are unchanged.

This PR's own gain is the ratio vs ND #8514 (on B200/GB300 from a
separate run); ratios vs deterministic Cake and non-Cake SOTA also
include the dX/dW row skip already on main. Per-token temperature, at
least 4097 valid rows, each range B200 / GB300 / R200, vs ND #8514: z =
0.5 bwd 1.186x-1.354x / 1.268x-1.338x / 1.233x-1.375x, ckpt
1.094x-1.142x / 1.124x-1.144x / 1.118x-1.170x; z = 0.166 bwd
1.039x-1.066x / 1.052x-1.067x / 1.050x-1.073x, ckpt 1.025x-1.037x /
1.030x-1.038x / 1.024x-1.040x (z = 0.166 ckpt: 2 of 7 B200 cells and 1
of 7 R200 cells inconclusive; every other cell in these ranges ND
faster). Vs deterministic Cake these cells are all ND faster; vs
non-Cake SOTA (R200: cross-run ratios without CI95 or verdict, 5 of
these 7 shapes; n/a at T = 16231 chunk 2048/8192), so are all B200 and
GB300 ones. At z = 0.5 bwd they are 1.315x-1.926x / 1.639x-1.907x /
1.514x-2.041x vs deterministic Cake and 1.403x-2.048x / 1.789x-2.034x /
1.723x-2.181x vs non-Cake SOTA. Every fwd cell, every z = 0 cell and
every cell below 4097 valid rows is at parity or inconclusive vs ND
#8514 and deterministic Cake, so z = 0 gains vs non-Cake SOTA are not
from this PR. Verdicts per GPU over 108 cells (ND faster / parity /
inconclusive):

- **B200**: vs ND #8514 38 / 49 / 21; vs deterministic Cake 40 / 53 /
15; vs non-Cake SOTA 108 / 0 / 0.
- **GB300**: vs ND #8514 40 / 65 / 3; vs deterministic Cake 40 / 65 / 3;
vs non-Cake SOTA 107 / 0 / 1.
- **R200**: vs ND #8514 39 / 57 / 12; vs deterministic Cake 40 / 51 /
17; vs non-Cake SOTA no verdicts (cross-run).
- No verdict on any GPU is 'ND slower'; every R200 cross-run SOTA ratio
is above 1 (minimum 1.063x).

**Method (all GPUs).** H = 6144, V = 154880, BF16, 5 % ignored rows,
state cooled. Per-token temperature at T = 2048, 4096, 8117, 16172,
16231, 32463, 65031 (chunk 4096; T = 16231 also 2048, 8192); scalar 0.7
at T = 8117, 16231, 65031. z = fraction of valid rows whose dlogp is
zero: 0, 0.166, 0.5 (random rows). Below 4097 valid rows (T = 2048,
4096) both ND arms run with the row skip off by design. Arms: new ND =
this PR (counted tempered dz on); ND #8514 = this build with the counted
tempered dz switched off (the dz path main runs today); deterministic
Cake (same build); non-Cake SOTA = per cell the fastest exact-semantics
PyTorch implementation: (c) chunked + torch.compile, (e) chunked eager,
(u) unchunked autograd. (e) and (u) were timed at z = 0 only (their work
does not depend on z), (u) not above T = 32463 on B200 and GB300; (c)
was fastest in every timed cell. Cut Cross-Entropy has no temperature
argument. Latency = median over steps (timing passes) of the per-step
median CUPTI GPU span; speedup = baseline latency / new ND latency (> 1:
new ND faster); CI95 = hierarchical bootstrap. Verdict 'ND faster' / 'ND
slower' only when the CI95 lies wholly outside 1 ± band (band = max(1 %,
A/A floor), A/A = new ND timed twice) and every step agrees; 'parity'
when wholly inside; else 'inconclusive'. Kernels built with CUDA 13.4;
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0 runtime); timed kernels and Python files
are byte-identical to the PR head. B200 and GB300 have two runs: run A
times deterministic Cake, non-Cake SOTA and new ND together, run B new
ND and ND #8514 (‡ columns). ‡ ratio = ND #8514 / run B's new ND, which
no column shows and which differs from run A's (see ‡ footnote); do not
divide ND #8514 (ms) by new ND (ms). R200 has only run B, which also
times deterministic Cake; only non-Cake SOTA comes from the #8514 PR's
run of the same cell (†: cross-run, no CI95 or verdict; n/a = per-token
T = 16231 chunk 2048/8192, scalar T = 8117/65031). Deterministic Cake
latency, this run / that run, is 0.938-1.043 (median 1.015) over the 72
matched cells, so † ratios can carry drift of that order.

**B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, driver
580.82.07.** Run A: one node, one timing process, 2 steps per cell; the
18 per-token T = 16231 chunk 2048/8192 cells were re-timed with all arms
in 2 later steps (fresh processes, same node) after (c) hit its
recompile limit. Run B: another node, one timing process; per-token 2
steps, scalar 1 step (scalar ‡ verdicts rest on one step).

### [b88169f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b88169f8f24d886fe128a64bb6a99e69cf191142)

- **作者**: Brian K. Ryu
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:31:41Z
- **提交信息**: feat(batch_invariant): batch-invariant quantizers: `mxfp8_quantize`, `mxfp4_quantize` and `nvfp4_quantize(batch_invariant=True)` (#8565)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

Adds batch invariant (and numerics alined with Transformer Engine) mode
to `flashinfer.mxfp8_quantize(input, ..., batch_invariant=True)`,
`flashinfer.mxfp4_quantize(a, ..., batch_invariant=True)` and
`flashinfer.nvfp4_quantize(a, a_global_sf, ..., batch_invariant=True)`.
They run a specified, fingerprinted quantization in place of the
backends.

The three operators gain `backend="auto"` as their default: 
- without the `batch_invariant=True` flag `"auto"` runs the CUDA kernel
exactly as before
- with the flag it runs the batch invariant class.

### Performance

FlashInfer's quantizers take 16-bit inputs only (the MXFP8 CuTe-DSL one
also fp32), so the fp32 slices have no
baseline except that one. Speedup = FlashInfer time / ours (geomean per
regime; > 1 = the class is faster).

Performance overall is roughly on par.

### [f2926f2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f2926f204d1c648d4399c838abc15d5d1842d967)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:29:26Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_gdn_kcp): byte queries of the non-deterministic KCP GDN package match what the calls bind (#8623)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` is the non-deterministic
GDN training package with key-context parallelism. Callers use its byte
queries (`gdn_workspace_layout_kcp`, `gdn_workspace_bytes_kcp`,
`gdn_saved_layout_kcp`, `gdn_comm_bytes_kcp`) to size a caller-held
`WorkspaceKcp` and to budget memory. These queries did not match what
the calls bind. On two ranks of a five-document pack at HV = 6 and P = 2
with crossing fragments, `gdn_workspace_layout_kcp` reported up to
2,162,688 B less than the workspace actually bound in the backward, and
up to 589,824 B less in the forward; in other contexts the queries
counted buffers the call never binds. The queries also did not model
several documented call contexts. This PR adds the missing terms and
contexts, removes the extra ones, and new tests check the queries
against the real host path at exact bytes.

The queries now report:

- At P > 1, the M_f^T tiles of crossing-out fragments in the c1 send
pool (new term `c1_send_mf`).
- With the fused walks at P > 1, `max(n_in, n_out)` more carry-plane
slots (new keyword `fused_walks`, the call's test knob; 1 is the shipped
form).
- The b1 pools at the larger of their two split forms, as the host sizes
them.
- For a saved backward on a caller-held workspace, the forward exchange
pools again until its adjoint exchange is done.
- The `P=` override in the workspace staging term.
- New `graph="replay"`: a captured call releases no buffer, so the
forward and backward figures count every pool and tape the call binds.
Like the call, the query refuses it with `reuse_recompute_tapes=True` /
`"auto"`.
- New `save_for_backward=`: a forward without a saved set, and the
backward that then replays the forward. After a fused forward, the
replayed forward binds the eight tapes `#1` re-writes, not ten, before
its c1 release.
- `boundary_mode="replay"`: S_in as a fresh tensor, and the replayed
forward's moment before the c1 release as `bwd.phase.replay_forward`.
- Kept-tape form (`reuse_recompute_tapes`) at P > 1 without
`save_transfer`: one backward staging plane, with the handed-over
M_seg^T plane counted in `bwd.kept_tapes` and `backward_transient`.
- The forward as the larger of `fwd.phase.prep` (`#1`) and
`fwd.phase.walk`.

The figures are for a workspace's first forward and backward. The docs
explain how later steps on a reused workspace compare with the
`graph="replay"` figure: equal for the replay form, and at most that
figure in the cases they name. The docs list `exchange="ring"` and the
`schedule="overlap"` test knob as not covered and give their extra terms
as bounds. `graph=`, `save_for_backward=` and `fused_walks=` exist only
on this package's query. Through the facade they need
`deterministic=False`.

The README's byte-query block now states the same rules. Its formula
cells use the padded state size: S_in is `n_in * s_pad`, and the owner's
summary pairs are `2 * s_owner * N_out`. The `gdn_comm_bytes_kcp`
formulas use `s_pad` / `s_owner` and the group totals. The validator
does not check a workspace's size, and the README no longer says it
does.

Tests (all CPU):

- An arena test runs the real host path with a recording workspace and
checks the query at tolerance 0. It covers two- and four-rank groups
with fragments that cross in and out, `graph="replay"`, forward-only
calls and their `saved=None` backward, the replay boundary, the
in-kernel L2 norm, and per-pool sizes. It also records the bytes bound
just before the replayed forward releases the c1 send pool, and checks
them against `bwd.phase.replay_forward` on every rank of a group that
exchanges.
- A measured kept-form checkpoint test at P = 2 (with and without
`save_transfer`, and with the norm) checks the pool sizes, the hand-off
bytes, the backward figure and `backward_transient`.
- A three-step reuse test checks what the docs say about later steps.
- A README tie test checks the saved-set table, including a padded owner
(HV = 48 on five ranks).
- An API test checks the facade route and the remaining differences
between the two packages' saved queries.
- Package suite: 435 passed, 115 skipped. Deterministic package suite:
289 passed, 85 skipped. Each of 49 mutations of the queries, each
reverting or breaking one modelled term, makes at least one new test
fail.

Query, documentation and test changes only (5 files, +1526 / -244); the
runtime, the kernels and the deterministic package are unchanged, so
there is no timing.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai
-->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Workspace and saved-memory queries now account for graph modes, fused
or split execution, replay boundaries, saved-tensor choices, and segment
overrides.
* Workspace queries include additional staging, exchange, and
normalization buffers in their estimates.
* **Documentation**
* Clarified workspace sizing, saved-data behavior, replay details,
segment planning, and per-rank memory calculations.
  * Expanded guidance on byte-query options and graph-mode coverage.

### [1786148](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1786148798cf1862df4e20a1cfb5b37fc1bac2be)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:28:49Z
- **提交信息**: msa_ops ICP indexer: short prefill windows up to 384 tokens on B200 TP2 page 128 (#8624)

Part of #8170.

The CAKE MSA ICP indexer
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake_msa_icp_indexer`) scores sparse-attention
indices for MiniMax-M3 (MSA) with indexer context parallelism. Each
prefill layout (page size 128 or 256, at TP2 or TP4) has two variants.
The materialized variant writes the FP32 score matrix and then selects
the per-rank Top-16. The fused variant keeps local Top-16 lists and
builds the cross-rank exchange carrier directly. A threshold for each
combination of architecture, page size and TP sends windows of at most N
query tokens to the materialized variant, and longer windows take the
fused variant. Both variants produce byte-identical outputs. This PR
changes one threshold: on sm_100a (B200) at page size 128 and TP2, it
drops from 512 to 384 query tokens. Windows of 385-512 tokens on that
layout now take the fused variant. The baseline is the previous version,
current FlashInfer main, where the threshold is 512 and these windows
ran the materialized variant. Over windows of 256-1024 tokens and
histories of 8192-204800 tokens, the worst loss against the faster
variant drops from 4.5 to 2.9 us, and the summed loss drops from 24.9 to
10.8 us (three rounds). One row gets slower: 512 query tokens at a
history of 32768 runs at 0.94x.

Kernel-only time per prefill indexer call (one layer, one rank) on
NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), driver 580.82.07, kernels built with
CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14 (cu130). Each call is timed with CUDA events
during CUDA graph replay with a cold L2, and each value is the median
over 8 sessions of the per-session mean of 256 iterations, averaged over
3 rounds on the same GPU. "History" is the number of tokens already in
the KV cache, and speedup = previous / this PR (>1 is faster).

| query tokens | history | previous us | this PR us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 448 | 8192 | 30.21 | 30.19 | 1.00x |
| 448 | 32768 | 32.78 | 32.87 | 1.00x |
| 448 | 122880 | 47.08 | 46.41 | 1.01x |
| 448 | 163840 | 55.36 | 51.25 | 1.08x |
| 448 | 204800 | 59.51 | 57.37 | 1.04x |
| 512 | 8192 | 30.73 | 30.67 | 1.00x |
| 512 | 32768 | 32.80 | 34.84 | 0.94x |
| 512 | 122880 | 49.16 | 48.18 | 1.02x |
| 512 | 163840 | 59.40 | 55.62 | 1.07x |
| 512 | 204800 | 65.65 | 61.17 | 1.07x |

Decode kernels and all other thresholds are unchanged (512 at page size
128 and 1024 at page size 256, except 512 for sm_100a TP4 at page size
256), and the indexer covers page size 128 or 256 at TP2 or TP4 on
sm_100a (B200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a (VR200).

### [9eb1b86](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9eb1b866044e0e27c719093f0769b6d521a719a3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:24:41Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm): faster SM120 paged FP8 MQA logits routes for 4 RTX 5090 and 12 RTX PRO 6000 shapes (#8621)

The SM120 paged FP8 MQA logits kernel picks its program from a route
catalog. Each heads/page/next_n configuration has a default route.
Device routes choose a static, `_par` or dynamic-scheduler (`dynv28`)
variant per shape. FlashInfer main (2a79e302) already ships the previous
version of this kernel. This PR moves 4 RTX 5090 shapes and 12 RTX PRO
6000 shapes from their default route to faster variants. On the changed
shapes, the geomean speedup over FlashInfer main is 1.0236× (seed 760)
and 1.0304× (seed 52021) on RTX 5090, and 1.2519× and 1.2495× on RTX PRO
6000. The PR adds one used route and its static sibling, which no shape
selects. No routes or programs are deleted. Every other shape keeps its
current route.

RTX 5090:
- h32/p128/next_n 5 moves from the default route to the new
`bta_ha_wr_ef` par route for four shapes: batch 32 at context 65536,
batch 64 at context 16384, batch 128 at context 16384, and batch 256 at
context 4096.
- The PR also adds the static `bta_ha_wr_ef` sibling of that route. No
shape selects it.

RTX PRO 6000 (all 12 shapes move from the default route to an existing
route):
- h32/p64/next_n 6 and h32/p128/next_n 6 at batch 128, context 65536
move to `a6:mpf_bta_ha_k2q_ef`.
- h64/p64/next_n 3 at batch 256, context 16384 moves to `a3:par`.
- h64/p64/next_n 4 at batch 128 and batch 256 (context 16384), and at
batch 32 (context 65536), moves to `a4:mpf_bta_ha_k2q_ef`.
- h64/p64/next_n 5 at batch 128 (context 16384 and 65536) and at batch
32 (context 65536) moves to `a5:atom5_mpf_bta_ha_k2q_ef`.
- h64/p64/next_n 6 at batch 128 (context 16384 and 65536) and at batch
256 (context 16384) moves to `a6:atom6_mpf_bta_ha_ef`.

### RTX 5090

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (170 SMs, sm_120a), driver 620.62, CUDA 13.0
runtime (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130), JIT toolchain CUDA 13.4.92. Baseline:
FlashInfer main (2a79e302). Latency: median µs of the paged FP8 MQA
logits call (CUPTI, L2 flushed before each launch, 5 interleaved
baseline/new groups). Each seed (760, 52021) runs on its own GPU.
Speedup = baseline µs / new µs. The table covers all 216 shapes. The 4
changed shapes have a geomean speedup of 1.0236× (seed 760) and 1.0304×
(seed 52021), with a range of 1.011× to 1.052×. On unchanged shapes both
sides run the same program. ² = clock-gate miss: the SM clock gate (min
≥ 2500 MHz, spread ≤ 250 MHz) failed after one re-time, and the numbers
are shown as recorded. No row-seed has this mark.

only.

### [35f52e0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/35f52e08c412e2490d6e03346da5f23432a1e230)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T07:00:22Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): packed-triangular forward WY program at five CTAs per SM on B200 and GB300 (#8615)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` is FlashInfer's
deterministic Gated DeltaNet chunked training kernel. Its outputs and
gradients are bitwise reproducible. The forward WY stage builds the
per-chunk WY representation (w and u). The forward pass uses it, and the
backward pass recomputes it. This PR adds a new compiled program for
that stage on sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300) that runs five CTAs per
SM instead of four. It keeps the triangular L^T / X tiles in a packed
lower-triangular layout and uses 64 tensor-memory columns, so each CTA
needs about 43.6 KB of shared memory and 87 registers. On B200 and
GB300, every launch of this stage uses the new program, both in the
forward pass and in the backward recompute. As a result, every row below
changes its launches. sm_107a (R200) is unchanged: its compiled programs
and launches are identical to FlashInfer main. All other stages are
unchanged, and outputs and gradients are bitwise identical to the
previous version. The baseline is the previous version of this kernel on
current FlashInfer main (speedup = main / this PR, so >1 is faster;
median over 56 interleaved clean-process cells). The forward pass is
faster on every row on both GPUs: 1.028x to 1.044x on B200 and 1.025x to
1.046x on GB300. For forward + backward, B200 measures 1.007x to 1.015x
on 14 rows and 1.000x on 3 x ~4.25k 8 / 16. GB300 measures 1.008x to
1.018x on 14 rows and 0.990x on 1 x 16384 8 / 16. In this run, the 95 %
confidence interval of the f+b ratio includes 1.0 on seven B200 rows and
two GB300 rows, so those rows are within measurement noise here. The
B200 rows are 4 x 4096 8 / 16, 3 x ~4.25k 8 / 16, 15 x ~4.3k 8 / 16, 1 x
16384 8 / 16, 16 x 4096 16 / 32, 11000 + 12000 + 9768 16 / 48, and 2
seqs 259174 tokens 2 / 6. The GB300 rows are 4 x 4096 8 / 16 and 1 x
16384 8 / 16. A repeat measurement of exactly those rows, shown in the
last table, finds f+b faster on both GB300 rows and on four of the seven
B200 rows. The other three B200 rows remain within noise. No row in
either run was slower beyond measurement noise.

### [a8284b0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a8284b03e1150d6ab8835599e07ca84f0e7dd5dd)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:49:39Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): store the 5120 -> 17408 input gradient's overlapped tiles through the TMA store at T 16231 / 16384 on sm_100a (#8614)

This PR adds a program and row rules to the Cake
`dense_projection_det_gemm` package in `flashinfer.experimental`, the
deterministic dense projection GEMM. Most programs in the package are
BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and wgrad), and one is an FP32 router
GEMM. The new program is an overlapped half-tail input-gradient (dgrad)
program. It uses a column-grouped raster with groups of 12 column tiles,
and its BF16 output tiles go through a one-slot TMA-store epilogue. It
comes from one new kernel source, compiled for `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`.
With it, the package's kernel sources go from 107 to 108 and its
compiled libraries from 270 to 272. The PR adds 2 row rules for
`sm_100a`. Each rule applies at a single token count T, either 16231 or
16384. The rules move the 5120→17408 input gradient (dgrad, BF16 output)
from the existing ragged rule's row-half program to the new program with
the same K split. The rule count goes from 371 to 373. The `sm_103a` and
`sm_107a` rules are unchanged, so no rule selects the new `sm_103a`
library. The baseline is the previous Cake version of the package on
main. Against it, the changed rows have a speedup of 1.012 on GB200 and
1.011–1.012 on B200. No changed row is slower on either GPU, and outputs
on those rows are bitwise identical to main. All other rows of the
294-row shape list plan the same programs as main on `sm_100a`,
`sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2,
BF16 output. Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1
mean this PR is faster.

| shape (K→N) | op | out | T | GB200 previous µs | GB200 this PR µs |
GB200 speedup | B200 previous µs | B200 this PR µs | B200 speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5120→17408 | dgrad (input gradient) | bf16 | 16231 | 1595.7 | 1576.5 |
1.012 | 1795.3 | 1775.6 | 1.011 |
| 5120→17408 | dgrad (input gradient) | bf16 | 16384 | 1599.8 | 1580.0 |
1.012 | 1799.6 | 1777.4 | 1.012 |

The package also ships FP32-output forms, weight-gradient (wgrad)
programs and the FP32 router GEMM (run through BF16x3 emulation), on
`sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

### [2b5018b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2b5018be222307c435bab22f5f0ad770170b4407)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:48:12Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_softmax): issue register-tile loads before the CTA barrier in the shared-tile kernels (#8597)

The Cake Blackwell FP32 softmax behind `flashinfer.sampling.softmax`
sends each shape to one of several kernels. This PR changes the 8- and
16-CTA shared-tile kernels `c8_t4_s4` and `c16_t4_s4`, along with their
PDL twins. Each thread now issues its four register-tile global loads
before the CTA barrier and the shared-tile TMA setup, so the loads
overlap that setup. The arithmetic is unchanged, and the outputs are
bitwise identical to main. Since #8449 and #8513, the low-latency forms
`c8_t4_s4_lat` / `c16_t4_s4_lat` serve sm_100 at every batch size. On
other architectures they serve grids of at most two waves. So the
changed kernels run on sm_103 (GB300) and sm_107 when the batch exceeds
two waves of resident shared-tile clusters. B200 kernel choice and
outputs are unchanged. On GB300 the multi-wave shapes run 1.005x to
1.035x faster than main. The 64 x 151936 shape uses the unchanged
low-latency kernel and stays at parity.

**GB300 (sm_103a)**, FP32 logits, temperature 1.0, CUDA 13.4, median of
12 runs (µs).

| batch x vocab | main | this PR | speedup vs main |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 x 151936 | 17.344 | 17.336 | 1.000x (low-latency kernel, unchanged
path) |
| 96 x 151936 | 24.384 | 23.552 | 1.035x |
| 128 x 151936 | 30.312 | 29.368 | 1.032x |
| 180 x 151936 | 39.584 | 38.712 | 1.023x |
| 256 x 151936 | 52.784 | 51.704 | 1.021x |
| 512 x 151936 | 96.912 | 95.504 | 1.015x |
| 1024 x 151936 | 185.656 | 183.728 | 1.010x |
| 180 x 202048 | 49.392 | 48.024 | 1.028x |
| 1024 x 202048 | 238.472 | 236.928 | 1.007x |
| 403 x 100000 | 52.256 | 51.191 | 1.021x |
| 512 x 256000 | 153.969 | 153.168 | 1.005x |

The other kernels in the family are unchanged: the low-latency
shared-tile kernels, the warp kernel, the row-wise kernel, the
cached-cluster row kernels (1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 12 or 16 CTAs per row) and
the persistent cached-cluster kernel; the family covers sm_100a (B200),
sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a.

### [5ea69e3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5ea69e3429d81e5f889e98564e9117c0104ec0e2)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:37:55Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): run the split program at measured token ranges on 212-SM sm_107a parts (#8530)

`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` has BF16-input dense and
batched projection GEMMs with BF16 or FP32 output, and an FP32 router
GEMM. The default, `deterministic=True`, calls
`dense_projection_det_gemm`. With `deterministic=False`, this package
runs its split-K / stream-K programs on the rows its measured rules
select. Every other row runs the deterministic program.

This PR changes one variant: the weight gradient with
`deterministic=False` on `sm_107a` parts with 212 SMs. Before this PR,
the split programs of the 212-SM table ran on these parts only from
16172 to 16384 tokens. Every other token count ran the deterministic
program. With this PR, the split programs also run in these measured
token ranges:

- FP32-output `4096 -> 32`, `4096 -> 48`, `4096 -> 64`, `5120 -> 32`,
`5120 -> 48` and `5120 -> 64`: from 1024 to 65536 tokens.
- `8192 -> 128` with BF16 output and with FP32 output: from 1024 to
32768 tokens.
- FP32-output `4096 -> 512`, `4096 -> 1024`, `5120 -> 512` and `5120 ->
1024`: at 512 tokens.

All other token counts, all other rows, and parts with other SM counts
keep their current programs.

Before this PR, `deterministic=False` ran the deterministic program at
these points. Compared with `deterministic=True`, det/new is:

- Weight gradient: 1.016 to 2.037 (graph) and 1.014 to 2.083 (eager).
- Whole backward: 1.003 to 1.498 (graph) and 1.004 to 1.482 (eager).
- Checkpointed step: 1.000 to 1.174 (graph) and 1.001 to 1.176 (eager).

Compared with cuBLAS / cuBLASLt, the results are mixed:

- Weight gradient: SOTA/new is 0.515 to 1.116 (graph). SOTA is faster in
31 of 50 graph rows and 29 of 50 eager rows. One eager row is at 1.000.
- Whole backward: SOTA/new is 0.408 to 1.050 (graph). SOTA is faster in
37 of 50 graph rows and 32 of 50 eager rows. One row in each mode is at
1.000.
- Checkpointed step: SOTA/new is 0.447 to 0.976 (graph). SOTA is faster
in all 50 graph rows and in 40 of 50 eager rows.

In eager mode, the library checkpointed step takes 1.16 to 20.60 us
longer than in graph mode (median 3.42 us). This PR takes 0.98 to 2.79
us longer, and the deterministic program 0.72 to 2.98 us longer. So the
10 eager checkpointed rows with SOTA/new above 1 come from host launch
gaps of the library calls: in graph mode, SOTA is faster in all 10.

This PR is faster than SOTA on the weight gradient in 17 of the 36 graph
rows of the six thin FP32 rows. SOTA is faster in every row of the four
wide FP32 rows at 512 tokens.

*R200 (`sm_107a`), 212 SMs. The table lists the 50 measured shape /
token-count points that this PR adds. Each point has the weight
gradient, the whole backward and the checkpointed step, in graph and
eager mode. The weight gradient is `dW[d_out, d_in] = G[T, d_out]^T X[T,
d_in]` with BF16 inputs and the listed output dtype. T is the number of
tokens. For wgrad rows, each value is the median over 4 runs, one on
each of the 4 GPUs of one node. Each run value is the median over 15
paired groups x 20 timed steps per arm. Time is the GPU span from the
beginning of the first kernel to the end of the last kernel of the call.
L2 is flushed before every launch. bwd is the input gradient plus the
weight gradient. ckpt is 2 forward + input gradient + weight gradient,
which is the checkpointed step. The forward and the input gradient have
BF16 output. For bwd and ckpt, each value is the median over the 4 runs
of each run's median over 9 paired groups x 20 timed steps. L2 is
flushed before every sequence. In both arms, the forward and the input
gradient run the deterministic program. Thus bwd and ckpt differ only in
the weight gradient. graph is CUDA graph replay. eager is eager launch.
det Cake is `deterministic=True`. new is `deterministic=False` with this
PR. For wgrad, SOTA is the faster of two library baselines. The first is
`torch.mm` with the cuBLAS heuristic and `out_dtype=torch.float32` for
FP32 output. The second is a cuBLASLt sweep of the top 8 heuristic
algorithms. Both use BF16 inputs, FP32 accumulation and the row's output
dtype. TF32 does not apply because the inputs are BF16. This is the
strongest applicable library baseline. It is the vendor GEMM on the same
inputs and output dtype, at the best of its heuristic choice and 8
alternatives. For bwd and ckpt, SOTA uses the fastest of these library
launches for each op. Each selected launch meets the accuracy check. A/A
noise comes from a second, independently prepared launch of the
deterministic program, measured like a candidate. The A/A ratios are
0.994 to 1.014 (wgrad, graph), 0.987 to 1.012 (wgrad, eager), 0.980 to
1.014 (bwd, graph), 0.992 to 1.010 (bwd, eager), 0.987 to 1.009 (ckpt,
graph) and 0.993 to 1.005 (ckpt, eager). The software is PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), nvcc 13.4, cuBLAS 13.8 and driver 620.43.
Ratio = baseline us / new us. A ratio above 1.00 means this PR is
faster.*

The family's other Cake variants (the split-K weight gradients of the
other measured rows with BF16 and FP32 output, the batched MLA head
projections and the FP32 router GEMM, plus the deterministic default)
are unchanged, and both packages ship on `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and
`sm_107a`.

execution, while excluded token counts continue to take precedence.

device configurations.

### [4c083b4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4c083b49c7da0a224baeb41bcd061219d0908b3b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:21:24Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_hopper_msa): exact signed-zero tie-break in the top-k block-select programs (#8606)

`flashinfer.msa_ops.msa_topk_select` on Hopper (SM90) uses 32 Cake top-k
block-select programs, chosen by route. Routes differ in plain or masked
(non-visible-prefix) selection, 1 / 2 / 8 / 16 / 32 chunks per block, 4
/ 16 / 32 / 128-wide tiles and 6 / 9 / 11 merge levels, and some are
latency-oriented forms for the long-query shapes. This PR regenerates 22
of these programs to fix a signed-zero tie in the second-pass block
select. These programs compared a candidate block's class by its float
value, so a class of -0.0 tied with +0.0. A tile in the +0 class could
then get key 0 and decode to index -1. The regenerated programs break
this tie exactly with an integer compare on the class bits. Seven of
them used to share a kernel source with another program and now compile
their own, which adds 4 kernel sources. The other 10 top-k programs and
the package's 57 attention / proxy-score programs are byte-identical to
the shipped version. The baseline is the previous Cake version of the
same programs, already shipped in FlashInfer, timed in the same process.
20 of the 28 shapes run on the regenerated programs. On these shapes,
previous / this PR ranges from 0.99x to 1.01x. The other 8 shapes run
byte-identical programs and land at 1.00x to 1.03x, which is measurement
noise. The fix makes the select correct at the signed-zero boundary at
no measurable cost.

Median kernel time (CUPTI, cold L2) on NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (132 SMs,
sm_90a), CUDA 13.4.92, driver 535.216.03. Speedup = Previous / This PR.
`nvp_forced` = masked selection with the non-visible prefix forced on.

The Hopper family (`cake_hopper_msa`) ships on `sm_90a` only. Cake's
other MSA top-k select programs ship in the Blackwell MSA family

### [d0e4047](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d0e40479abb4c46078e4210159d6c66e4f473b04)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:21:15Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_kcp): cheaper eager host path for non-deterministic KCP GDN autograd (#8600)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` is the non-deterministic
KCP (context-parallel) GDN training package. Its q, k, v and output o
are BF16; g, beta and their gradients dg and dbeta are FP32. It supports
contiguous, zigzag and per-document zigzag layouts and explicit
`fragments` partitions. It has an optional in-kernel q/k L2 norm and
forward, backward and checkpointed calls. This PR makes its eager host
path cheaper. "Previous" is this package at the timing base (FlashInfer
main 61bc8b6d), byte-copied and imported in the same process as this PR.
The launch stream is bound through `tvm_ffi.use_raw_stream` with a
cached device. This is the same stream that `tvm_ffi.use_torch_stream()`
binds. When torch exposes `_cuda_getCurrentRawStream`, no
`torch.cuda.Stream` is built per entry body or per unscoped launch. The
registry answers (in-kernel L2 norm records and fused-output records)
are derived once per registry identity and per architecture. The chunk
table's token count is kept with the context. An options dict whose
values are hashable is validated once per distinct content (bounded
64-entry cache; keyword overrides are part of the key). The launch-key
and public-argument builds are trimmed. Launches, records, grids, every
non-pointer argument, plans and numerics are unchanged. On B200 and
R200, host time per eager step is lower in all 27 measured rows
(previous / this PR 1.032-1.404). For one fwd+bwd step, it drops from
1407.3 to 1325.2 us on B200 workload N CP1 (1.062x) and from 1641.1 to
1417.6 us on B200 workload A CP1 (1.158x). On R200 workload N CP1, it
drops from 502.8 to 454.6 us (1.106x). In the device-timed comparison
with previous, all 20 classified rows (of 27; 7 rows have a cell that is
not published) are WIN. GB300 timing is pending.

This PR does not change the other Cake GDN training variants, namely the
single-rank packages `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gdn_train`
(non-deterministic) and `flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train`
(deterministic) and the deterministic KCP package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`; architecture coverage
stays sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

**Correctness**

Unless a bullet names the rebased head, these checks ran on this patch
applied to the timing base 61bc8b6d.

- Launch logs of this PR and previous are identical; rows that raise an
error raise the same error in both packages. A launch log holds the
kernel records, grids, every non-pointer argument value (tensors as
dtype, shape, stride and storage offset) and the plan records.
- Launch-log coverage: CPU at 1, 2 and 4 ranks (no ring, no graph
capture), B200 at 1, 2 and 4 ranks, GB300 at 1 and 2 ranks, and R200 at
1 rank.
- On B200, the launch-log check also ran with an A/A control at 2 and 4
ranks and with the arm order reversed at 4 ranks.
- Only the GPU runs at 2 and 4 ranks cover the ring exchange: B200 at 2
and 4 ranks, and GB300 at 2 ranks.
- One extra call ran per run, workload, CP and operation (host-time runs
and det-first device-timed runs). In each, the output and every input
gradient of this PR are bitwise equal to previous on every rank (54 of
54).
- In the reversed-order device-timed runs, A/A is bitwise equal to
previous (27 of 27).
- The single-GPU suites pass on B200, GB300 and R200 (429 passed and 9
skipped on each).
- The distributed suite passes on B200 with 8 GPUs and on R200 with 4
GPUs (212-SM node), with 33 passed and 20 skipped on each. It did not
run on GB300 (pending) or at the rebased head.
- 5 new tests (plus 2 updated stream-binding tests) pin the caches and
the stream binding. Each of 7 single-line mutations of the cache keys
and the binding makes its target test fail.
- The PR head 69c6c2fc149523d3a78954be512b5e3c0510622a is the same patch
rebased on main 533500214888b57a99a3914a8167b25c776c9833. The timings
were taken at the timing base 61bc8b6d. At the rebased head, compared
with main's package: the CPU suites pass (this package 390 passed and
115 skipped, the deterministic package 276 passed and 83 skipped), the
CPU launch logs at 1, 2 and 4 ranks are identical, the B200 single-GPU
suites pass (443 passed and 9 skipped), and the B200 launch logs at 1, 2
and 4 ranks are identical.

**Conventions**

- Ratio = baseline / this PR. Above 1 means this PR is faster. The
tables print it as previous / this PR, or as speedup vs the named
baseline. A/A / previous is the noise control.
- Workloads, with heads given as (H_qk, HV):
  - N: 8192 tokens, documents 2049/3001/3142, heads (2, 6).
- M: 32768 tokens, documents 12000/9000/6000/3768/2000, heads (16, 48).
  - A: 262144 tokens, documents 98304/65536/57344/40960, heads (16, 48).
- CPn = context parallel over n GPUs. Every timed row uses the
contiguous layout. Operations: fwd, fwd+bwd and ckpt (2 x fwd + bwd).
- Host time: host wall time of one step (the whole fwd, fwd+bwd or ckpt
operation), measured with perf_counter and no profiler. A device
synchronize runs before each step. At CP > 1, a barrier also runs before
each step. At CP > 1 the table shows the slowest rank's median. The host
table is not classified.
- Device-timed cells (tables A and B) are in ms. Each cell is the median
over timed iterations of the per-iteration slowest-rank time (the
maximum over ranks for each iteration).
- Each (GPU, workload, CP, operation) row is printed as two lines. One
run has the det(main) arm first ("det first"). The other run reverses
the whole arm order ("reversed").
- drift = |last group median - first group median| / median of the group
medians.
- Publication rule:
- Table A needs the drift of this PR, previous and A/A each <= 2 %. "max
drift" is the largest of the three.
- Table B needs the drift of this PR and the compared baseline each <= 2
%.
- Otherwise the paired-ratio test applies: at least 5 groups, and every
per-group paired ratio within ±1 % of their median. A per-group paired
ratio is the baseline's group median divided by this PR's group median
in the same group (the baseline is previous in table A and the compared
baseline in table B). Both tests use unrounded values, so a bracket
printed to 3 decimals can look slightly inside or outside ±1 %.
- If both tests fail, the comparison is not published: table A prints
"not published (unstable)", table B prints "not published".
- Power-cap share: the share of NVML samples (every 50 ms) joined to an
arm's timed block that show the software power-cap reason, on the GPUs
the run used.
- If any arm of either run has a power-cap share >= 5 %, the row is not
published in both arm orders and is not classified (table A prints "not
published (power cap)", table B prints "not published"). This includes
det(main) and the non-Cake arms.
- Classes cover table A rows whose two runs are both published. WIN
means every per-group paired ratio is above 1 in both arm orders.
REGRESSION means every ratio is below 1 in both orders and the fwd+bwd
and ckpt rows agree. Everything else is PARITY.
- The row counts use (GPU, workload, CP, operation) rows, which table A
prints as 54 lines. Table A has 20 classified rows (of 27): 20 WIN, 0
REGRESSION, 0 PARITY.
- Published speedups vs previous range from 1.005 (B200 workload M CP1
ckpt) to 1.104 (B200 workload N CP1 fwd).
- Ten cells are not published:
- 4 unstable: B200 workload N CP4 fwd+bwd, CP8 fwd+bwd and CP8 ckpt in
the det-first order, and R200 workload N CP1 fwd in the reversed order.
- 6 power-capped: B200 workload A CP1 fwd, fwd+bwd and ckpt, in both arm
orders. For fwd, only the non-Cake head-sharded arms triggered the flag.
This PR, previous, A/A and det(main) had 0.0 %. For fwd+bwd and ckpt,
this PR's own arm was capped: 16.7 / 10.9 % and 25.0 / 15.5 % (det first
/ reversed).
  - The 7 rows with these cells are not classified.

**Baselines**

- Previous = this package on FlashInfer main
61bc8b6dd7049a44d614b2a0cd4a036cb3c46ad0, the timing base. A/A is a
second byte copy of the same base package, imported in the same process.
- det(main) = `flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` at the
timing base 61bc8b6d, not at the rebased main.
- Table B counts each arm order as a separate line. Against det(main),
this PR is faster on all 40 published lines of 54 (1.060-1.676).
- Four non-Cake arms run in the same process as this PR:
  - FLA chunk (KCP form): FLA 0.6.0 chunk kernels in a KCP form.
- FLA chunk (head-sharded CP): FLA single-rank varlen kernels, with
heads split across ranks.
- cuDNN FROST (head-sharded CP): `checkpoint_every_n_tokens` 0, so the
backward recomputes the states.
- cuDNN FROST ck64 (head-sharded CP): `checkpoint_every_n_tokens` 64, so
the states are stored.
- Versions: fla-core and flash-linear-attention 0.6.0, FLA_FLASH_QLA 0,
triton 3.8.0, nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.32.1 and nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1.
- Head-sharded CP needs CP to divide H_qk and HV. Workload N has heads
(2, 6), so at workload N CP4 and CP8 only FLA chunk (KCP form) applies.
- Accuracy filter: an arm qualifies only if its output and every input
gradient are finite and agree with this PR's tensors. The limits are
rel-RMS <= 1e-2 and max-abs <= 2e-2 x max|ref|, with ref = this PR's
tensor.
- Table B shows the fastest qualified non-Cake arm that meets the
publication rule. The cell is shown only if every non-Cake arm that
misses the rule is slower than the shown arm in every group. Otherwise
it reads "not published".
- Against the non-Cake arm, this PR's ratio is 0.422-1.562. This PR is
faster on 17 of 29 published lines.
- 9 of the 17 wins are against FLA chunk (KCP form) at workload N CP4
and CP8. 8 are against cuDNN FROST (5) or FROST ck64 (3).
- All 12 lines below 1 are CP1 lines against cuDNN FROST (5) or FROST
ck64 (7): B200 workload N (3), B200 workload M (4) and R200 workload M
(5).
- For workload M (B200 and R200), the CP1 gap to cuDNN FROST is mostly
kernel time (forward-type kernels). This host-path change does not
address it.
- For workload N on B200, the gap is mostly eager host time. This PR
reduces it but does not close it: in the det-first run, B200 workload N
CP1 fwd+bwd goes from 1.488 ms (previous) to 1.413 ms.

**Setup**

- Timed GPUs:
- B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs): CP1, CP2, CP4 and CP8 on workload N; CP1 and
CP8 on workload M; CP1 on workload A.
  - R200 (sm_107a, 208 SMs): CP1 on workloads N and M.
- GB300 (sm_103a): the single-GPU suites and the launch-log identity at
1 and 2 ranks passed. The GB300 distributed suite and GB300 timing are
pending. The tables have no GB300 rows, and no GB300 timing is claimed.
- Software: torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA runtime 13.0) in a CUDA 13.4
development container, NCCL 2.30.7, and Python 3.14.9 on B200 and 3.14.8
on R200. All timings are eager.
- Timed boundary: one KCP GDN call with no convolution. Every arm,
including the non-Cake arms, uses the in-kernel q/k L2 norm.
- Device-timed protocol (tables A and B):
- The protocol has 5 groups. In each group, the arms run in palindromic
order (a1 .. an, an .. a1).
- Each arm visit runs 2 untimed and 12 timed iterations. One iteration
is one call.
- Each iteration runs after an L2 flush. CUDA events time it on every
rank.
- This gives 120 samples per arm. Each sample is the slowest rank's time
for that iteration.
- Host protocol: each arm gets 5 untimed warm-up steps. Then 4 groups
visit the 4 arms (this PR, previous, A/A, det(main)) in palindromic
order (a1 .. a4, a4 .. a1). Each visit runs 30 steps (240 per arm).
- Power-cap share reached up to 77.1 % on B200 (cuDNN FROST ck64,
workload A CP1 ckpt, det first) and 0.0 % on R200 (96 entries).
- A/A / previous is 0.997-1.008 in the host table (27 rows) and
0.993-1.017 over the 44 published table A cells.
- The B200 and R200 rows timed this patch applied to the timing base
61bc8b6d, in a package tree that differs from the patch only in typing:
in this PR, the launch scope's `__exit__` is annotated `-> None` and has
no `return False`, and one local variable has an annotation. Runtime
behavior is the same. The rebase onto main also brings in main's own
change to this package since the timing base (#8542: the full saved set
keeps the segment transfer plane), which these tables did not time.
