### [8a0a21d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8a0a21ddf78874a434e7b82eea1f6e0ac431c15a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:16:38Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_attn_res): CLC lookahead token-queue programs for one B200 and one GB300 shape (#8609)

This PR changes routes of the Cake AttnRes operator,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kimi_k3_attn_res`, which is exposed as
`flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res` and
`kimi_k3_attn_res`. One launch does residual add, an optional snapshot
write, K+1 candidate scoring, softmax, mix and output RMSNorm. It takes
BF16 inputs with hidden size 7168 and K in [0, 8]. It has one data type,
one layout and two fused forms: dense and snapshot write. This PR
changes routes on GB300 and B200, at both PDL modes. No B300 route
changes. Among the measured shapes, 1 changes on GB300 and 1 on B200.

- **New token-queue builds with CLC lookahead (GB300, B200):** Both
shapes move from a static persistent program to a token-queue (`_clc`)
build that this PR adds. A token-queue build launches one CTA per token
(grid M) and uses cluster launch control. Each running CTA processes its
own token and then the tokens of the CTAs it cancels, so tokens are
spread over the SMs dynamically instead of by a static stride. This PR
adds two options to these builds. With CLC lookahead (`_cla`), each CTA
requests its next token from cluster launch control one trip ahead. With
first-chunk L2 prefetch (`_fpf`), the kernel issues an L2 bulk prefetch
of the first chunk at entry.
- On GB300 (sm_103a): serving_m384_k2 moves from
`persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f011010000000000_fm_crfnone` to
`persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f011010000000000_fm_crfnone_clc_cla_fpf`.
- On B200 (sm_100a): serving_m12288_k5 moves from
`persistent:k5_nc4_d3_f110000000000000` to
`persistent:k5_nc4_d3_f110000000000000_clc_cla`.

The program set goes from 193 to 195 programs. This PR adds 2 programs:
`persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f011010000000000_fm_crfnone_clc_cla_fpf` for
sm_103a and `persistent:k5_nc4_d3_f110000000000000_clc_cla` for sm_100a.
It removes none, because both previous programs still serve other
shapes.

Both changed shapes are faster. GB300 serving_m384_k2 measures 1.021x at
both PDL modes. B200 serving_m12288_k5 measures 1.036x with PDL off and
1.017x with PDL on. For shapes not in the tables below, see the timings
in PRs #6980, #7014, #7338, #7374, #7411, #7453, #7540, #7737, #8120,
#8143, #8155, #8171, #8207, #8291, #8351, #8428, #8489 and #8554.

NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.4, torch
2.14.1+cu130. Baseline: the previous Cake version of this kernel shipped
in FlashInfer (PR #8554).

| Shape | M | K | Previous µs (PDL off) | New µs (PDL off) | Speedup |
Previous µs (PDL on) | New µs (PDL on) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| serving_m384_k2 | 384 | 2 | 9.184 | 8.992 | 1.021x | 9.184 | 8.992 |
1.021x |

NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), driver 580.82.07, CUDA 13.4, torch
2.14.1+cu130. Baseline: the previous Cake version of this kernel shipped
in FlashInfer (PR #8554).

| Shape | M | K | Previous µs (PDL off) | New µs (PDL off) | Speedup |
Previous µs (PDL on) | New µs (PDL on) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| serving_m12288_k5 | 12288 | 5 | 239.3745 | 232.063 | 1.036x | 237.631
| 235.151 | 1.017x |

Cake ships no other data types or layouts for this operator, since the
dense and snapshot-write forms are the whole family, and 195 programs
cover B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), B300 (sm_103a, 148 SMs) and GB300
(sm_103a, 152 SMs).

### [3ded62b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3ded62b988e2557f9313b4acd8bc22920f39a840)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:11:42Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): vectorized MXFP8 dispatch quantize in the sm_107a recompute (#7821) (#8604)

`cake_mok_bf16` is FlashInfer's MoK mixture-of-experts training kernel
family. It covers forward, full-forward checkpoint recompute and
backward, and has four variants: BF16 or MXFP8 routed experts, each with
plain or clamped SwiGLU. This PR speeds up the MXFP8 context-only
recompute kernel on sm_107a (for #7821). This is the kernel behind
`recompute_forward_context`, which rebuilds the saved forward context
for backward without producing the output. The change covers plain and
clamped SwiGLU, which are the two rendered sm_107a recompute MXFP8
kernels. It brings the same vectorized shared-memory MXFP8 dispatch
quantize that #8506 added to the forward and #8546 added to the
backward. The recompute kernel's communication CTAs quantize each
dispatched 128x128 BF16 token tile to MXFP8, once row-major and once
transposed. They now read shared memory in 128-bit chunks and write the
MXFP8 words with 64-bit and 128-bit vector stores. Outputs and the saved
context are bitwise identical to before. The forward and backward code
is unchanged.

**Kernel phases** (ms, before → after, speedup)

| Workload | Forward | Recompute (`recompute_forward_context`) |
Backward |
|---|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 3.828 → 3.838 (0.997x) | 2.820 → 2.749
(1.026x) | 6.733 → 6.753 (0.997x) |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 5.160 → 5.166 (0.999x) | 3.260 → 3.179
(1.025x) | 8.738 → 8.716 (1.002x) |

returns the windows of `ROUTER_RULES` on every SM count. Those windows
hold only on `ROUTER_SM_COUNT` SMs (152 for sm_103a) or on an SM count

### [5f47f21](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5f47f216b44471cdb9bf2a945009033938d924c5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:08:52Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): keep power-of-two query lengths on the JIT module for long causal BF16 context on sm_100a (#8608)

The Cake BF16 paged context family
(`trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache(..., backend="cake")`) picks an
exact program first (Q8192, B128, Q511, Q257). Other causal calls
without LSE or sinks go to a runtime-size program, and the JIT-compiled
module is the fallback. The JIT module is compiled for the call's sizes
and runs power-of-two query lengths faster than neighbouring lengths.
For example, with 32/4 heads, pack 8 and 16384 keys, it takes 1335.8 µs
at q 8192 against 1355.2 µs for the program, but 1407.5 µs against
1346.0 µs at q 8064. On sm_100a, this PR sends calls to the JIT module
when the pack is above 1, the max query length is a power of two of at
least 4096 and the max KV length is at least 14336. Pack 1, every other
query length and all sm_103a calls keep the runtime-size program.
Outputs are bitwise unchanged. The baseline is the previous Cake path
for these calls, the runtime-size program. trtllm-gen is shown as a
second comparison column. On the 19 measured shapes that move, this PR
is up to 1.022x faster than the previous path. On 4 of them the JIT
module is slower by up to 0.9% (ratios 0.991 to 0.999). This PR is
1.096x to 1.155x faster than trtllm-gen on all 19.

B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4. Cold L2; each µs value is the median
over 10 seeded memory layouts x 4 rotating rounds. A ratio above 1 means
this PR is faster.

### [3ade982](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3ade982f15126245aebd78b0abc8f191662f6653)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T06:00:50Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_fp8_rowwise_gemm_allreduce): SM103 fused FP8 GEMM + all-reduce for TP2/4/8 (#8605)

`flashinfer.comm.fp8_rowwise_gemm_allreduce` with `backend="cake"` runs
a row-wise scaled FP8 (e4m3) GEMM and the all-reduce over 2, 4 or 8
ranks on one node in one fused kernel per call, and returns a BF16
output on every rank. It supports one data type combination: FP8 e4m3
inputs with per-row and per-column scales, and BF16 output. On sm_103a,
Cake has three variants of this family, one per world size. At 2 and 4
ranks, a peer-to-peer NVLink pull/reduce carrier is used, and both world
sizes share one new generated program built for sm_103a. At 8 ranks,
Cake uses the NVLink multicast (NVLS) program that already ships for
sm_100a, and this PR also builds it for sm_103a. This PR adds sm_103a
support for all three world sizes and leaves the sm_100a programs
unchanged. The fused kernel is faster than the PyTorch baseline at 2
ranks (geomean 1.104x). At 4 ranks (0.959x) and 8 ranks (0.890x) it is
slower on most shapes.

### 2 ranks

Cake has no previous version on sm_103a, so the baseline for all three
world sizes is `torch._scaled_mm` row-wise FP8 GEMM (cuBLASLt, BF16
output) followed by `torch.distributed.all_reduce` in BF16 (NCCL default
algorithm). It runs on one node of 8 NVIDIA B300 SXM6 GPUs (sm_103a,
Blackwell Ultra) with CUDA 13.0 and driver 580.126.09. The timed value
is the CUPTI GPU time of one call (median over iterations of the slowest
rank). Cake and the baseline alternate in the same session (A/B/B/A
order), over two independent passes, each in a separate allocation.
Speedup = baseline / this PR (> 1 means this PR is faster), and the last
column is the geometric mean of the two passes' speedups. Geomean
1.104x, 33 of 48 shapes at or above 1.0x, range 0.685x to 1.613x.

### [94caa58](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/94caa58ef0e40a40e3306b80af27424126f69e5e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T05:54:30Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_rmsnorm_det): fixed-order dw for the smallest token counts of the SM100/SM103 backward (#8512)

This PR changes the small-row backward pass of the deterministic Cake
RMSNorm training package (`cake_rmsnorm_det_train`) on sm_100a and
sm_103a. The package covers BF16 and FP32 weights, residual and
non-residual inputs, row widths H 256 (per-head view) / 512 / 1536 /
2048 / 4096 / 5120 / 6144, and both forward and backward passes. This PR
changes only the backward pass (residual and non-residual, BF16 and FP32
weight) for row counts T up to a per-width limit. Above that limit, the
previous kernels are kept. The limits on sm_100a are H 256: 87, H 512:
227, H 1536: 109, H 2048: 288, H 4096: 203, H 5120: 121, H 6144: 20 and
residual H 6144: 32. The limits on sm_103a are H 256: 1680, H 512: 227,
H 1536: 214, H 2048: 171, H 4096: 152, H 5120: 25, H 6144: 20 and
residual H 6144: 32. For every width except H 256, one kernel now
replaces the main backward kernel and the separate dw reduction kernel.
It computes dx bit-identically to before. It sums each dw column in a
fixed row order with exact products and compensated (TwoSum) summation.
A fixed-order FP64 fold follows, then one final rounding to FP32. The dw
result does not depend on the grid size or SM count. For H 256, the main
kernel accumulates with TwoSum, and the dw column reduction also uses
TwoSum. The package already uses this form for larger H 256 row counts.
The new form makes dw more accurate at these row counts, so some rows
are slower than the previous Cake package. torch.compile is faster than
Cake on many of these small rows. Each Cake launch has a floor of a few
microseconds, and the previous Cake package had the same floor. Speedups
against the previous Cake package and torch.compile (listed in that
order):
- B200 (sm_100a): 0.888x-1.685x vs previous Cake (16 of 140 rows slower,
at most +0.631 us); 0.270x-1.866x vs torch.compile (Cake faster on 67
rows).
- GB300 (sm_103a): 0.859x-1.397x vs previous Cake (31 of 144 rows
slower, at most +0.968 us); 0.307x-1.991x vs torch.compile (Cake faster
on 41 rows).

**NVIDIA B200 (148 SMs), sm_100a**; CUDA 13.4 (kernels built with nvcc
13.4), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Backward pass (dx and dw in
one call). Latency = CUPTI kernel-active time per call, cold L2, median
of 4 x 20 calls per process. Previous Cake = the previously shipped Cake
package; Cake = this package; both through the package's public backward
entry point in the same processes (counterbalanced). Each Cake and
previous Cake value = fastest valid process over the row's formal
sessions (at least 2 sessions; each session a fresh process set with
fresh caches, one GPU per session; a process is valid when its repeated
Cake control run agrees within 1 %). Each baseline value = fastest
process that timed it. Fastest non-Cake = the fastest of torch.compile
(per-shape static compile of the FP32 formula, dynamic=False),
F.rms_norm, Liger and eager FP32, named when it is not torch.compile.
Residual rows: in the forward, Cake and every baseline return h = x +
residual and y = RMSNorm(h); the backward takes the gradients of y and h
and returns the gradient of h (which is that of x and of residual) and
dw (torch.compile compiles the add and the norm as one graph; Liger =
the faster of its RMSNorm and its fused add RMSNorm). Speedup = baseline
/ Cake.

**NVIDIA GB300 (152 SMs), sm_103a**; CUDA 13.4 (kernels built with nvcc
13.4), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Backward pass (dx and dw in
one call). Latency = CUPTI kernel-active time per call, cold L2, median
of 4 x 20 calls per process. Previous Cake = the previously shipped Cake
package; Cake = this package; both through the package's public backward
entry point in the same processes (counterbalanced). Each Cake and
previous Cake value = fastest valid process over the row's formal
sessions (at least 2 sessions; each session a fresh process set with
fresh caches, one GPU per session; a process is valid when its repeated
Cake control run agrees within 1 %). Each baseline value = fastest
process that timed it. Fastest non-Cake = the fastest of torch.compile
(per-shape static compile of the FP32 formula, dynamic=False),
F.rms_norm, Liger and eager FP32, named when it is not torch.compile.
Residual rows: in the forward, Cake and every baseline return h = x +
residual and y = RMSNorm(h); the backward takes the gradients of y and h
and returns the gradient of h (which is that of x and of residual) and
dw (torch.compile compiles the add and the norm as one graph; Liger =
the faster of its RMSNorm and its fused add RMSNorm). Speedup = baseline
/ Cake.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added deterministic RMSNorm training support for SM100 and SM103 GPUs,
including backward computation for BF16 inputs.
* Added additional backward execution paths for small token counts, with
route selection varying by workload.
* **Improvements**
* Reduced workspace requirements for certain backward paths by using
counters without partial-sum storage.
* Updated route selection for residual-fused backward cases to account
for token count.

### [59432d0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/59432d00b9e3be44b455f977c2bcf2aae8223353)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T05:33:06Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_nvfp4_mla_decode): two-split combine for short GB300 decodes (#8596)

`cake_nvfp4_mla_decode`
(`flashinfer.mla.prepare_nvfp4_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`,
experimental) is the MLA decode with NVFP4 queries and KV cache, and the
baseline is its previous Cake version in `main`. The kernel has one
variant (one data type, one layout, no fused forms), and this PR changes
that variant. On GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), short decodes whose split
requests have exactly two pieces and whose work units hold at most 32
pipeline tiles (128 keys each) now use the two-split combine program,
under the same rule that `main` already applies on B200 and GB200
(sm_100a). Every other plan, including every B200, GB200 and 148-SM
sm_103a plan, is unchanged, and every other program compiles to the same
machine code as in `main`. Rows marked unchanged run the same programs
with the same launch arguments as `main`, and their two latencies differ
by at most 0.6%. Rows use per-head attention sinks unless marked "no
attention sink". Each latency is the median over two GPUs of the median
CUDA graph replay time with a cold L2, and each speedup is the median
over the same two GPUs of each GPU's paired ratio of the `main` time to
this PR's time, so it can differ slightly from the quotient of the two
latency columns.

These are the four shapes whose plans change, with their speedups on
GB300. They are: batch 2 (256 and 300 keys), 64 heads, 6 query tokens,
KV split every 256 keys at 1.027x; batch 2 (256 and 384 keys), 64 heads,
6 query tokens, KV split every 256 keys at 1.024x; batch 3 (200, 300 and
450 keys), 8 heads, 6 query tokens, KV split every 256 keys at 1.014x;
and batch 2 (64 and 260 keys), 64 heads, 1 query token, KV split every
256 keys, no attention sink at 1.045x.

### [8e67d9c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8e67d9c44ce12e45424482a216bc04dd4308cf5f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T05:26:42Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_det): with grad, collapse pass reads the mapping-pass input from L2 on sm_100a / sm_103a (#8582)

FlashInfer's Cake deterministic mHC backend holds the four-stream mHC
kernels with grad. Main already has these variants:
- forward prepare / recompute and gradient routes at hidden sizes 4096,
5120 and 7168
- group-row token owner and reduction forms above 14927 tokens
- the dual-layout fn split on the activation-checkpoint route (#8312)

At hidden size 4096, forward prepare runs two passes. A mapping pass
loads the activations X with TMA, then a collapse pass reads the same X.
In main, the mapping pass loads X with the L2 hint EVICT_FIRST. So the
collapse pass reads X from DRAM again, both on the forward route and in
the activation-checkpoint recompute. This PR adds `_xn` variants of the
mapping-pass forms: five libraries and six kernel configurations. Their
only difference is the EVICT_NORMAL hint on the X load, so the collapse
pass reads X from L2. In ncu at T = 1024, the collapse-pass DRAM read
falls by about 32 MB. A control that flushes L2 between the two passes
removes the gain. The `_xn` forms run for 64 < T ≤ 6144 on sm_100a and
sm_103a. T ≤ 64, T > 6144 and sm_107a keep the existing forms. Outputs
are bitwise identical, and the public API is unchanged.

The baseline, "previous", is the current Cake version of the same
kernels in FlashInfer main. Times are CUPTI active GPU time (the union
of kernel intervals) in microseconds. L2 is flushed with a memset before
every timed call. "Forward" is forward prepare + finish. "Checkpoint" is
the activation-checkpoint recompute followed by the gradient route.
Every shape uses 4 streams, hidden 4096 and T tokens. Each session
interleaves three arms in 6 ABC/CBA groups of 32 iterations: previous,
this PR, and a second previous run as a control. Each value is the mean
of 2 independent sessions on separate allocations and different nodes.
The T = 128 and 256 rows come from a second pair of sessions run the
same way. Speedup = previous / this PR, and a value above 1 means
faster. Above T = 6144 both versions run the same kernels, so those rows
show run-to-run variation.

### [4b018c2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4b018c2783aa3a528fa49d300b453ad964ce3345)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T05:12:00Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_vsa): per-architecture block-64 balanced route on SM100/SM103 (#8588)

`flashinfer.cake_vsa` (`BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="cake")`)
handles block-64 BF16 head_dim-128 selections with two Cake per-head
programs: a persistent program and an M64N256 warp-specialized program.
Since #8525 it also has a balanced persistent program for selections
shared by every head. In that program, one CTA per SM takes (query
block, head) tiles in descending selection size. Before this PR, the
plan sent a shared selection to the balanced program only under two
conditions: at least 8 selected blocks per query block on average, and
at least 0.8 (query block, head) tiles per SM. Where the per-head plan
is the WS program, bucket and wave limits also applied. Those bounds
were measured on B200 only. This PR sets the route per architecture,
based on new measurements on B200 and GB300. The balanced program now
serves a shared selection with at least 7 selected blocks per query
block on average over at least 8 (query block, head) tiles. On sm_100a,
where the per-head plan is the M64N256 WS program, the previous limits
still apply. Those limits are at least 0.8 tiles per SM, plus either
rows of at most 64 blocks in one group-count bucket or rows in several
buckets over at least 1.05 waves. On sm_103a the balanced program also
takes those WS rows. The plan still makes this choice on the host at
plan time, and the kernels' code paths do not change. The baseline T_fi
is the previous Cake version. That is the Cake route served on
FlashInfer main for these shapes, which is the per-head block-64
persistent program. "served" is the route this PR serves, and it uses
the balanced program on every row below. On B200, served runs at
1.055–1.265× against T_fi in eager mode and 1.043–1.264× under
CUDA-graph replay. On GB300, served runs at 1.052–1.198× in eager mode
and 1.039–1.198× under CUDA-graph replay. It is faster on all 8 rows in
both modes on both GPUs.

### [203cc3c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/203cc3c299139b9eea1c0d5417275a779ae38e6e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T04:56:11Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_gdn_det_kcp): keep M_seg in the full saved set at P > 1 and count the whole plane in the saved byte query (#8585)

With `save_mode="full"` and `save_transfer=False` on a rank whose
fragments run in P > 1 segments, gradients were wrong; `out` was not
affected. This includes `exchange="ring"`, because the ring requires
`save_transfer=False`. The backward merges read the per-segment transfer
plane `M_seg`, but the forward drops that buffer and the full saved set
kept `M_seg` only under `save_transfer`, so the merges read memory that
no program of the call had written. The fix is host-only, with no kernel
or launch change. The full saved set now keeps `M_seg` at P > 1 for
either `save_transfer` value, and a full saved set without it is
refused. `gdn_det_saved_bytes_kcp` / `gdn_det_saved_layout_kcp` now
count `M_seg` as `P * n_frag` states, which is the whole `n_frag * P`
plane that is kept, instead of `(P - 1) * n_frag`. Defaults
(`save_mode="light"`, `save_transfer=True`) are unaffected, and the
light rows are bitwise equal to main in the tables below.

8 GPUs (2 nodes x 4), context parallel 8; four documents of 98,304 /
65,536 / 57,344 / 40,960 tokens, 32,768 tokens per rank; (H_qk, HV) =
(16, 48); median ms of the slowest rank over interleaved main/fix
visits; CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

fix/main |

On the contiguous layout, P = 3 on every rank, so main's gradients are
wrong in the `save_mode="full"`, `save_transfer=False` rows. The main
time in those rows is only a cost reference.

Cake also ships these separately: a non-deterministic variant of this
kernel, single-GPU GDN training packages without context parallelism
(deterministic and non-deterministic), GDN inference kernels for chunked
prefill and decode, and the KDA deterministic context-parallel training
sibling, which covers the per-channel-gate form; this kernel ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [cb16ec2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cb16ec24085b7816b53a8f8365849b92aeb201d7)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T04:50:53Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_cp): row-split sm_107a CP state fixup for 4, 8, 16 and 32 parallel states (up to 1.08x) (#8572)

The Cake Gated DeltaNet (GDN) context-parallel (CP) prefill kernel
family in FlashInfer has six variants: BF16 and FP16 I/O on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes only the CP state fixup stage of
the sm_107a BF16 and FP16 variants, for 4, 8, 16 and 32 parallel states.
For these cases, the fixup now splits each state over 3, 5 or 10 rows
per CTA instead of 4. The baseline is the previous Cake version on
FlashInfer main. On the 72 shapes in the table (48 BF16, 24 FP16), this
PR is faster on every shape: eager geomean 1.041x (range 1.007x to
1.079x), CUDA graph geomean 1.042x (range 1.007x to 1.079x).

GPU: NVIDIA R200 (216 SMs), sm_107a, driver 615.71.10, CUDA 13.4,
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Time = CUPTI span of one whole public
`chunk_gated_delta_rule` CP call (first kernel start to last kernel end)
with a cold L2. Each value is the median per seed, then the geomean of
seeds 17 and 29. eager = synchronized single calls; CUDA graph = graph
replays. new = this PR. speedup = previous Cake / this PR (above 1 =
this PR faster). parallel states = sequences x Hv. CP chunk = the chunk
that the public call picks. public call: auto =
`chunk_gated_delta_rule(backend="cake_gdn")`; use_cp=True =
`backend="cake_gdn", use_cp=True`. The FP16 rows use int32 `cu_seqlens`
and were timed in both columns on a FlashInfer main without #8523, which
speeds up their Stage-1.

### [cc032bb](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cc032bb85e17c523135c2c54dd7537b502be33b7)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T04:48:34Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8 T4096 rank programs on sm_103a (#8594)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline for the 384-expert, top-6, hidden-5120 model with activation
clamp 10. A single kernel launch covers dispatch, FC1, clamped SwiGLU,
MXFP8 activation quantization, FC2 and weighted combine. The kernel has
four variants on main, and this PR updates one of them: the TP/EP rank
variant. It changes 2 of the variant's 32 programs: TP4 EP4 (96 local
experts) at 4096 tokens and TP8 EP8 (48 local experts) at 4096 tokens.

In both programs, the combine stage now gives more of each CTA's token
chunks to the eight epilogue warps and fewer to the four dispatch warps,
which walk their chunks more slowly. The epilogue warps take the CTA's
first 76 chunks and the dispatch warps take the rest. At 4096 tokens,
that is 9-10 chunks per epilogue warp and 7-8 per dispatch warp,
compared with 9 per warp before. On each loop trip, a warp also reads
the permuted-row indices for its next trip.

The outputs are bitwise identical to the previous version. No host
binding changes. The catalog closure hashes of the 2 changed programs
change. The baseline is the previous Cake version on main, which is the
rank variant as last updated by #8553. For replicates a / b, the
speedups for the changed programs are:

- TP4 EP4 at 4096 tokens: 1.006x / 1.006x, saving 1.96 / 2.02 µs per
call
- TP8 EP8 at 4096 tokens: 1.011x / 1.011x, saving 2.04 / 1.93 µs per
call

Both changes are faster than the A/A noise band in both replicates. The
other 30 programs run 0.998x to 1.002x in replicate a and 0.998x to
1.003x in replicate b.

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.159.03, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. Per-call latency comes from CUDA-graph replays (20 calls
per graph), taking the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous
version and this PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6
rounds. Each value is the median of the 6 process medians. Speedup =
previous / this PR, computed from the latencies before rounding to two
decimals. Columns a and b are two independent replicates, each run alone
on its own node. Each replicate also timed the previous version against
itself (an A/A control) to measure its noise band. The widest band is
0.24 % in replicate a and 0.26 % in replicate b. The kernels and host
bindings of the other 30 programs are byte-identical to the previous
version, and they compile to the same machine code. Two of them, TP8 EP8
at 128 tokens (+0.015 / +0.044 µs) and at 512 tokens (+0.061 / +0.034
µs), read slower than their narrow A/A band in both replicates, which is
process-level noise, not a regression.*

The other three variants (single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8
and grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a; the rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [8c959ef](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8c959ef3c6e3c65fd309b31f56a45b78c51b9aa0)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T04:32:08Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_msa_icp_indexer): faster prefill list-to-carrier merge (#8593)

Part of #8170.

The CAKE MSA ICP indexer
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake_msa_icp_indexer`) scores the
sparse-attention index for MiniMax-M3 (MSA) with indexer context
parallelism. Its prefill path has two variants, each for four layouts
(page size 128 or 256 at TP2 or TP4). The materialized variant writes
the FP32 score matrix and then selects the Top-16 per rank. The fused
variant keeps local Top-16 lists and builds the cross-rank exchange
carrier directly. Windows of at most 512 query tokens (page 128) or 1024
(page 256; 512 on sm_100a at TP4 page 256) keep the materialized score
and select. This PR changes only the fused variant's list-to-carrier
merge kernel. The kernel now uses 88 registers instead of 134 (96 on
sm_107a), so a long chunk runs in fewer waves, and its final merge steps
keep 8, then 4, then 2 keys per lane. Outputs are byte-identical. The
baseline is the previous CAKE version, which FlashInfer ships today. On
rows that run the fused path (windows above the short-window threshold),
the speedup is 1.00x-1.02x on all three GPUs. Rows at or below the
threshold run the unchanged materialized path, so their 0.98x-1.03x
ratios are run-to-run variation. The full-model step time is unchanged
within measurement noise.

Kernel-only time per prefill indexer call (one layer, one rank, serving
dispatch path) on GB300 (sm_103a, CUPTI), B200 (sm_100a, CUDA events)
and VR200 (sm_107a, CUDA events), built with CUDA 13.4. Both sides ran
on the same GPU in alternating order with CUDA graph replay and cold L2;
each time is the median of 6 sessions x 32 iterations, averaged over 2
rounds; speedup = previous / this PR. "8192 + 14 decode" query tokens
means an 8192-token prefill chunk plus 14 decode requests in one call,
and history is the number of tokens already in the KV cache.

### [3119588](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3119588d1b68eb5ee3462d3a954c83eaa8ce6713)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T04:18:48Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dcp): run the fold-free planner program for near-grid E4M3 head_dim-128 launches (#8586)

The E4M3 head_dim-128 family of `flashinfer.cake_dcp` uses BF16 query
and output with an FP8 E4M3 paged KV cache. It has three programs, and
the host picks one from launch metadata:

- Program 0 is the persistent planner program without the idle-CTA
eight-slice fold.
- Program 1 is the same planner program with that fold.
- Program 2 is the plan-free static one-wave program.

Before this PR, every launch below the grid ran program 1 unless it used
the static one-wave program. With this PR, some of those launches run
program 0 instead. The launch must have at least 8 query rows per
request, and `num_kv_heads * (batch_size + 10)` must be greater than the
SM count. No request can be split in that range, so the fold never runs.
Every other launch keeps its program. The baseline is the previous Cake
version of the kernel, which runs program 1 here. FlashInfer main also
uses program 1 for this shape. On the measured shape, this PR is 1.0008x
to 1.0047x faster than the baseline.

| GPU | Mode | Previous Cake (µs) | This PR (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) | Eager | 209.82 | 209.07 | 1.0034x |
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) | CUDA-graph replay | 210.19 | 209.22 |
1.0047x |
| NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) | Eager | 199.41 | 199.22 | 1.0008x |
| NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) | CUDA-graph replay | 199.78 | 199.31
| 1.0022x |

*Shape: 16 requests with 8 query tokens each (speculative decode), 8 KV
heads with 8 query heads per KV head, head_dim 128 and page size 64. The
context-parallel world size is 4 and the measured shard is rank 3.
Context lengths are long and ragged, taken from an agentic trace.
Software: CUDA 13.0 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Each value is kernel time
from FlashInfer `bench_gpu_time` (CUPTI) with FlashInfer's L2 flush
(cold L2). Each value is the median of 3 independent runs. Speedup =
previous / this PR.*

This module also ships the BF16 head_dim-128 and E4M3 head_dim-256
balanced DCP families from Cake, and these programs ship on sm_100a and
sm_103a.

### [c92fdaa](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c92fdaa3b153b393a651e63f72b67539beb499a1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T04:12:50Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): store the indexer_q weight gradient's stream-K tiles through the TMA store at T 16172 / 16231 (#8584)

This PR adds a program and row rules to the Cake
`dense_projection_det_gemm` package in `flashinfer.experimental`, the
deterministic dense projection GEMM. Most programs in the package are
BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and wgrad), and one is an FP32 router
GEMM. The new program is a synchronised two-partial stream-K
weight-gradient (wgrad) program with a TMA-store epilogue. It comes from
one new kernel source, compiled for `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`. With it,
the package's kernel sources go from 106 to 107 and its compiled
libraries from 268 to 270. The PR adds 4 row rules for `sm_100a` and
`sm_103a`. Each rule applies at a single token count T, either 16172 or
16231. The rules move the indexer_q weight gradient (2048→4096, BF16
output) from the existing stream-K program to the new program with the
same K split. The rule count goes from 367 to 371, and `sm_107a` is
unchanged. The baseline is the previous Cake version of the package on
main. Against it, the changed rows have a speedup of 1.014–1.019 on
GB200, 1.012–1.016 on GB300, 1.014–1.017 on B200 and 1.010–1.015 on
B300. No changed row is slower on any of the four GPUs, and outputs on
those rows are bitwise identical to main. All other rows of the 294-row
shape list plan the same programs as main.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), GB300 (`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148
SMs), B300 (`sm_103a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2, BF16 output.
Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1 mean this PR
is faster.

| shape (K→N) | op | out | T | GB200 previous µs | GB200 this PR µs |
GB200 speedup | GB300 previous µs | GB300 this PR µs | GB300 speedup |
B200 previous µs | B200 this PR µs | B200 speedup | B300 previous µs |
B300 this PR µs | B300 speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| indexer_q (2048→4096) | wgrad | bf16 | 16172 | 183.9 | 180.5 | 1.019 |
147.0 | 144.7 | 1.016 | 167.4 | 164.6 | 1.017 | 154.5 | 152.2 | 1.015 |
| indexer_q (2048→4096) | wgrad | bf16 | 16231 | 184.1 | 181.6 | 1.014 |
146.9 | 145.2 | 1.012 | 167.0 | 164.6 | 1.014 | 154.0 | 152.4 | 1.010 |

The package also ships FP32-output forms, weight-gradient (wgrad)
programs and the FP32 router GEMM (run through BF16x3 emulation), on
`sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

### [6ed3b15](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6ed3b1503d9827e303dddc07cb4c18bd4a005721)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T04:11:14Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): batch-of-eight elected wavefront release for the dhu scan on R200 (#8587)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` is FlashInfer's
deterministic Gated DeltaNet chunked training kernel. Its outputs and
gradients are bitwise reproducible. The backward can run the reverse
state-adjoint scan (dhu) and the fused BF16-beta tail_g2 backward tail
concurrently as a wavefront pair. The scan publishes per-chunk ready
counts, and the tail, on a side stream, begins each chunk as soon as its
counts arrive. Two publish forms already exist: a per-thread release
every second chunk (w2) and an elected single-thread release every
fourth chunk (e4). This PR adds a third form, e8, on sm_107a (R200). In
e8, one elected store thread publishes every eighth chunk and at the
walk's last chunk. The PR also enables the wavefront pair on sm_107a for
plans that have a host-built table, one scan round (2 x segments x value
heads <= SM count) and the BF16-beta fused tail of a value-head group of
two. Fewer, larger releases cut the scan's publish overhead, and the
tail still overlaps the scan. The PR adds one compiled program for
sm_107a. Every other program, and every launch on sm_100a (B200) and
sm_103a (GB300), is unchanged. Outputs and gradients are bitwise
identical to the previous version. The baseline is the previous version
of this kernel on current FlashInfer main (speedup = main / this PR, so
>1 is faster; median over 56 interleaved cells). Of the measured shapes,
only 1 x 16384 with H / HV 8 / 16 and 1 x 16384 with H / HV 16 / 32
change their launches, on all three R200 boards measured. For these two
rows, forward + backward drops:
- 216 SMs: from 0.4125 to 0.3916 ms (1.053x) and from 0.7252 to 0.6798
ms (1.067x)
- 212 SMs: from 0.4052 to 0.3811 ms (1.063x) and from 0.6895 to 0.6332
ms (1.089x)
- 208 SMs: from 0.4186 to 0.4018 ms (1.042x) and from 0.7465 to 0.7035
ms (1.061x)

Every other row runs the same launches as before, so the spread in its
ratios is measurement noise. The forward pass is unchanged on every row.
Its ratios of 0.998x to 1.001x are noise; for example, on 216 SMs, 1 x
16384 16 / 32 shows 0.998x with an unchanged forward launch.

### [e27eacf](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e27eacf157254ecada7723d8a6bb5234c937fd55)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T04:04:42Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dense_projection_gemm): run the deterministic program for four FP32 sm_107a K1 rows at large token counts on 216-SM parts (#8509)

The `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` family has
BF16-input dense and batched projection GEMMs with BF16 or FP32 output,
and an FP32 router GEMM. `deterministic=True` (the default) calls
`dense_projection_det_gemm`. `deterministic=False` runs this package's
split-K / stream-K programs on the rows its measured rules take; every
other row runs the deterministic program.

This PR changes one variant: the FP32-output weight gradient of `4096 ->
512`, `4096 -> 1024`, `5120 -> 512` and `5120 -> 1024` on `sm_107a`
parts with 216 SMs or more, from 40961 tokens up. These rows now run the
deterministic program there, whose FP32 error is half that of the
one-split program it replaces; this keeps them within the FP32 error
budget up to at least 65536 tokens (at 131072 tokens both programs
exceed it). Smaller token counts and parts with fewer SMs are unchanged.

At these token counts `deterministic=False` therefore runs the same
program as `deterministic=True`
(`dense_proj_det_gemm_nn_n256_m256_f32_tma1_pro7`, the same grid):
det/new is 0.98 to 1.03, the run-to-run variation of one launch, so this
change is not a speedup. The one-split program it replaces took 89.04,
147.14, 92.72 and 149.22 us at 40961 tokens and 137.94, 228.10, 143.58
and 232.35 us at 65536 tokens (graph; the four rows in the order of the
tables). cuBLAS stays faster on the weight gradient: SOTA/new is 0.392
to 0.794; on the checkpointed step it is 0.722 to 1.017.

*R200 (`sm_107a`, 216 SMs). Weight gradient `dW[d_out, d_in] = G[T,
d_out]^T X[T, d_in]`, BF16 inputs, FP32 output; checkpointed step = 2 x
forward + input gradient + weight gradient of the same projection (the
forward recomputed under activation checkpointing). Each value is the
median over 9 paired groups of the group's median over 20 timed steps
per arm, with L2 flushed before every launch; graph = CUDA graph replay,
eager = eager launch. det Cake = `deterministic=True` (the
`dense_projection_det_gemm` package). new = `deterministic=False` with
this PR, the same deterministic program. SOTA = the faster of
`torch.mm(..., out_dtype=torch.float32)` (cuBLAS heuristic) and a
cuBLASLt sweep of the top heuristic algorithms (BF16 inputs, FP32
compute and output); for the checkpointed step, `torch.matmul` per
operation. PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), nvcc 13.4, cuBLAS 13.8,
driver 615.71.10. Ratio = baseline us / new us; above 1.00 means this PR
is faster.*

The family's other Cake variants (the split-K weight gradients of the
other measured rows with BF16 and FP32 output, the batched MLA head
projections and the FP32 router GEMM, plus the deterministic default)
are unchanged, and both packages ship on `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and
`sm_107a`.

### [d3c28c5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d3c28c5a02d3ad74aa744a23331013a7f65f9c04)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T03:34:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_msa): blackwell_msa fused K-major prefill, qpair BF16 decode, FP8 fuseq8 (#8574)

The blackwell_msa sparse attention family has 51 routes backed by 48
programs at this PR. Main has 47 routes and 44 programs. The routes
cover BF16, FP16 and FP8 (E4M3) data types and flat and paged KV
layouts. Some routes are fused; others split into main and reduce
stages. They span decode (`decode_m16`, `decode_uniform_fp8`,
`decode_fp8_q1`), prefill (`prefill_union`, `kmaj_p`, `kmaj_p_fused`,
`long_bf16_reverse`) and four top-k selection routes.

This PR adds four routes and removes none:
- three fused K-major BF16 prefill routes: `kmaj_p_fused` flat gqa16,
paged gqa16 and paged gqa8
- one paired-ticket BF16 paged decode route: `decode_m16` bf16/bf16
paged `qpair`

It also replaces the program behind all 10 `decode_uniform_fp8` routes,
including the FP8 fused decode route `fuseq8`.

Compared with the previous Cake version on main (#8264), the main/PR
latency ratios are:
- **GB300:** 2.1311 and 2.5827 for `kmaj_p_fused`, 0.9867 to 1.6172 for
`qpair`, and 1.4910 for `fuseq8`.
- **B200:** 0.9795 for `kmaj_p_fused` (one shape), 1.0176 to 1.6728 for
`qpair`, and 1.9547 for `fuseq8`.

A ratio above 1 means this PR is faster. Latencies are pooled medians in
µs.

`decode_fp8_q1`, the other seven `decode_m16` routes, `kmaj_p`,
`long_bf16_reverse`, `prefill_union` and the top-k selection routes. All
48 blackwell_msa programs build for `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`, and compute
capability 10.7 is allowed only for the separate packed-NVFP4 paged-KV
modules.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [b7b1f7b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b7b1f7bc485ee82d036671250f36b60181e195db)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T03:23:07Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm_mega_mhc): weight-staging tail routes at two and three waves on sm_107a (#8571)

`flashinfer.mega_mhc` (`prepare_mega_mhc`) runs the fused
manifold-constrained hyper-connection (mHC) inference step. FlashInfer
main ships 45 per-arch programs for it:

- 14 hidden-5120 FP8-E4M3-output programs on sm_100a and sm_103a.
- For hidden 4096, five programs on each of sm_107a, sm_100a and
sm_103a: BF16 output, its tailpipe twin, its weight-staging tailpipe
twin, FP8 group-128 output and NVFP4 output.
- Four sm_107a-only tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe forms of the
FP8 group-128 and NVFP4 variants.
- Three sm_107a-only FP8 group-128 UE8M0-scale-mode programs (plain,
tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe).
- One sm_107a-only fast-division form of the plain FP8 group-128
program.
- Six sm_107a-only fast-chain forms: one each of the BF16-output
tailpipe program, the plain FP8 group-128 program (raw scale mode), the
plain FP8 group-128 program (UE8M0 scale mode), the FP8 group-128
weight-staging tailpipe program (raw scale mode), the FP8 group-128
UE8M0 tailpipe program and the NVFP4 tailpipe program.
- Two sm_107a-only chain-packing forms: one of the FP8 group-128
tailpipe program (raw scale mode) and one of the plain FP8 group-128
UE8M0 program.

Routes on main can already carry an optional SM-count key.

This PR adds no program and changes no program. It adds routes, and each
route is keyed to one SM count (208 or 216). Each route moves launches
to the existing weight-staging tailpipe program with the same output
layout and scale mode. The previous round already sends the 3-wave and
4-wave 16-split tail bands of several modes to this program. This PR
extends the routes to the 2-wave deterministic band. It also extends
them to the 2-wave (13 splits) and 3-wave (16 splits) non-deterministic
bands. The weight-staging tailpipe program keeps the split count and the
grid of the program it replaces. It also stages the RMSNorm weight in
shared memory. Outputs are bitwise identical, and the deterministic
launches stay batch invariant. Every other SM count, and a call with no
SM count, dispatch exactly as on main. No sm_100a or sm_103a launch
changes.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the kernel, which is what
FlashInfer main dispatches today. A is the program main dispatches, and
B is the program this PR dispatches. Speedup = A / B. Both sides run
through FlashInfer's loader on the same GPU, with the same inputs, in
one process. Both use programmatic dependent launch, as main already
does. The tables show medians. Each table lists the owner shapes first,
then the changed rows. The GPU is an NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a), with 208-SM
and 216-SM devices. Deterministic launches use 16 splits.
Non-deterministic launches use 13 splits for two waves: T = 1665–2048 on
208 SMs and T = 1729–2112 on 216 SMs. Above that they use 16 splits
(three waves). The tables show the split count per row.

- **NVFP4 output, deterministic** (plain NVFP4 program → NVFP4
weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T = 1536–1664 (1.023–1.030×).
216 SMs: T = 1536–1728 (1.021–1.033×).
- **NVFP4 output, non-deterministic** (NVFP4 tailpipe program → NVFP4
weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T = 1665–2496 (1.007–1.017×).
216 SMs: T = 2113–2560 (1.009–1.021×). On both, the new range ends where
the previous round's range starts.
- **FP8 group-128 output, UE8M0 scales, deterministic** (UE8M0 tailpipe
program → UE8M0 weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T = 1472–1664
(1.022–1.030×). 216 SMs: T = 1536–1728 (1.019–1.043×).
- **FP8 group-128 output, UE8M0 scales, non-deterministic** (UE8M0
tailpipe program → UE8M0 weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T =
1665–2496 (1.014–1.031×). 216 SMs: T = 1729–2560 (1.011–1.034×).
- **FP8 group-128 output, raw scales, deterministic** (fast-division
form of the plain FP8 group-128 program → FP8 group-128 weight-staging
tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T = 1472–1664 (1.027–1.033×). 216 SMs: T =
1408–1728 (1.018–1.029×).
- **FP8 group-128 output, raw scales, non-deterministic** (FP8 group-128
tailpipe program → FP8 group-128 weight-staging tailpipe program). 208
SMs: T = 1665–2496 (1.006–1.031×). 216 SMs: T = 2113–2560
(1.014–1.032×).
- **Owner shapes.** T = 2048 is a changed row in four tables, all
non-deterministic: NVFP4 on 208 SMs (1.008×), UE8M0 on 208 SMs (1.027×)
and 216 SMs (1.022×), and raw on 208 SMs (1.009×). The owner-shape rows
that keep their program measure 0.997–1.004× on the 208-SM GPU and
0.994–1.004× on the 216-SM GPU; those rows are all within noise.

### [c5db8d3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c5db8d3ccd3fa3842812280f7f208718dc0b8610)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T02:45:56Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm): launch the non-deterministic column tasks at once and run the deterministic pair in two GB300 backward windows (#8577)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). The two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`, use the same forward and differ only in the
backward. The family ships for sm_100a (B200), sm_103a (GB300) and
sm_107a (R200). The tables cover these forms in both modes:

- [T, H] rows with BF16 weight (H512 to H6144)
- FP32 weight (`w32`): H5120 and H6144, plus H2048 and H4096 in the B200
small-T rows
- fused residual add (`res`, H6144) with BF16 or FP32 weight
- per-head views [T,24,256] (strided) and [T,4,256] (contiguous), with a
shared w[256]

This follow-up to #8208 and #8253 changes only the `deterministic=False`
backward. It makes two changes:

- Column-task launch (all three GPUs): the column-task programs (H2048,
H4096, H5120, H6144, the `res` H6144 route and their FP32-weight twins)
now launch one CTA per row chunk plus one per column task, capped at the
slot count, as the deterministic column-task programs already do; the
grid changes only at small T, where a few CTAs used to run every column
task in turn.
- Two GB300 windows: at H6144 from T449 to T1152 (both weight dtypes)
and at H5120 (BF16 weight) from T321 to T896, the backward now runs the
deterministic pair instead of its single kernel, because the pair is
faster there (the pair is the main kernel + fixed-order dw reduce,
programs the package already ships).

Speedup = baseline latency / new latency. A value > 1 means the new
kernel is faster. Geomeans over the 78-shape list, vs deterministic / vs
SOTA:

- fwd (same forward in both modes): B200 1.001x / 1.015x, GB300 1.001x /
1.017x, R200 0.999x / 1.012x
- bwd: B200 1.048x / 1.157x, GB300 0.991x / 1.146x, R200 0.942x / 1.080x
- 2xfwd+bwd: B200 1.022x / 1.120x, GB300 0.998x / 1.138x, R200 0.971x /
1.096x

The B200 vs-SOTA geomeans leave out the two B200 `!` rows.

Added rows, vs deterministic / vs SOTA (small T = T1, T4, T16 and T64):

- B200 small-T (36): fwd 1.003x / 0.940x, bwd 1.537x / 1.029x, 2xfwd+bwd
1.220x / 0.999x
- GB300 small-T (20): fwd 1.000x / 0.888x, bwd 1.173x / 1.055x,
2xfwd+bwd 1.073x / 1.195x
- GB300 window rows (9): fwd 0.999x / 1.026x, bwd 0.971x / 1.219x,
2xfwd+bwd 0.998x / 1.242x
- R200 small-T (8): fwd 0.994x / 0.903x, bwd 1.005x / 0.758x, 2xfwd+bwd
0.991x / 0.884x

Notable rows:

- Small T vs deterministic: B200 small-T bwd runs at 1.26x to 1.76x, and
all 36 rows are faster. GB300 small-T bwd reaches 1.46x (geomean 1.173).
R200 small-T rows are at parity (bwd 0.983x to 1.019x).
- In a separate earlier run on B200 and GB300, T = 1 backward took
87-212 us with the previous non-deterministic programs and 3.8-4.5 us
with this PR's programs.
- torch.compile still beats the new kernel at T = 1 backward on all
three GPUs. The exception is GB300 `res` and `res w32`. Example, B200
H2048 T1 bwd: det 5.98 us, SOTA 2.08 us (tcd), new 3.87 us. On R200,
SOTA is faster on all 8 small-T bwd rows (0.518x to 0.936x vs SOTA).
- The rows below are slower than deterministic. This is pre-existing:
this PR does not change their GPU programs or launch. Latencies are new
vs det:
- R200 at large T. The lowest is H5120 T65536 bwd at 300.86 vs 161.73 us
(0.54x). Others: H6144 T32768 bwd 162.40 vs 101.82 us (0.63x) and H6144
T65536 bwd 311.11 vs 192.77 us (0.62x). The full list is every R200 row
below 0.95x vs det.
- GB300: H1536 T65536 bwd 128.45 vs 101.47 us (0.79x); [T,4,256] T1024
bwd 9.70 vs 7.94 us (0.82x); H5120 T65536 and H5120 T65536 w32 bwd 0.85x
to 0.87x; H6144 T64 res bwd 8.03 vs 7.36 us (0.92x).
  - B200: [T,24,256] T65536 bwd 427.77 vs 384.89 us (0.90x, `!`).
- GB300 window rows: both modes launch the same GPU programs here. The
new mode measures 0.962x to 0.996x of det on bwd (geomean 0.971). This
gap comes from the timing order (see below), not from the GPU programs.

Baselines and measurement. Every row has two baselines:

- det: the deterministic Cake kernel (`deterministic=True`). Its GPU
programs are those of FlashInfer main at a1b4ed39. This PR does not
touch the deterministic package.
- SOTA: per row, the fastest non-Cake candidate that has the same
outputs (BF16 y / dx / h_new, FP32 rstd / dw) and meets the accuracy
budget. This is the strongest applicable comparison: every listed
candidate is timed on every row, and the fastest in-budget one is taken.
APIs that return dw in the weight dtype (Liger, QuACK, TE) do not have
matched outputs and are never chosen. Apex FusedRMSNorm has no wheel.

new = the non-deterministic Cake kernel of this PR
(`deterministic=False`). The accuracy budget takes the worst of 5 seeds:
y and dx atol = rtol = 1e-2; rstd rel. error <= 1e-4; dw per element
atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64. New and det meet it on every row on all
three GPUs.

Latency = median of 804 CUPTI spans per implementation per row. One span
is one CUDA-graph replay after an L2 flush (cold L2). It includes the
implementation's own setup, reduction, cast and copy kernels. For each
GPU type, 4 sessions ran in parallel on 4 GPUs of one node (2 in row
order, 2 in reverse). Each session ran 3 interleaved passes x 67
replays. eps = 1e-6. Latencies print to 0.01 us and per-row ratios to
0.01x.

In each session the implementations run in a fixed order: det first,
then the non-Cake candidates, then new. A later check on B200 and GB300
found that this order alone moves an implementation's latency by up to
about 5 %: rows where both modes launch the same GPU programs read 0.95x
to 1.05x instead of 1.00x. A ratio within about 5 % of 1.00x is
therefore not a measured difference. All implementations of a row run in
one process that also loads every non-Cake candidate, including
torch.compile. A later check found that loading torch.compile into the
process makes the Cake kernels faster on small rows (B200 H1536 T1024:
bwd 8.40 to 7.45 us, fwd 3.33 to 2.61 us; GB300 H6144 T449: bwd about
10.9 to 9.70 us, fwd about 4.1 to 3.15 us), while the non-Cake
candidates gain about 3.5-5 %. On small rows the ratios vs SOTA can
therefore overstate the new kernel's lead; the size per row is being
measured. Ratios vs det are not affected (both are Cake kernels in the
same process).

Key:

- Shapes: H = hidden size, T = tokens. x / y / dx are BF16, rstd / dw
are FP32, and w is BF16 unless marked `w32`. `res` adds the BF16 output
h_new. `[T,24,256]` has strides (12288, 512, 1), and `[T,4,256]` is
contiguous. Both share w[256].
- SOTA:
- tc = torch.compile of an explicit FP32-statistics reference (torch
2.14.1+cu130, inductor max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, static shape,
emulate_precision_casts=True)
  - tcd = the same in torch.compile default mode
  - q = QuACK 0.6.5 heuristic config
- qa = QuACK 0.6.5 exhaustive per-shape autotune (rmsnorm_fwd_tuned /
rmsnorm_bwd_tuned, cached before timing)
  - on `res` rows, QuACK is torch add + QuACK
  - lg = Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton 3.8.0, casting_mode gemma)
- Transformer Engine 2.20.2 was never fastest. PyTorch's fused rms_norm
cannot run this form (BF16 x with FP32 w).
- `~`: for det, SOTA or new, (max - min) / min of the 4 session medians
is above 5.0 % (compared at 0.1 % resolution).
- `*`: a faster non-Cake candidate fails the dw budget. These candidates
are listed below the table.
- `!`: no matched candidate meets the dw budget. The fastest matched one
is shown, and the row is left out of the vs-SOTA summary.

**B200 (sm_100a)**

B200, 148 SMs, sm_100a, compute capability 10.0, driver 580.82.07, CUDA
13.4 (nvcc cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0), torch 2.14.1+cu130. SM
clock median 1965 MHz (99 % of samples at max), memory clock 3996 MHz, 4
GPUs of one node, no foreign GPU processes. Rows: 78 shapes + 36 small-T
shapes, x 3 ops = 342 rows. The small-T shapes are T1, T4, T16 and T64
of H2048, H2048 w32, H4096, H4096 w32, H5120, H6144, H6144 w32, H6144
res and H6144 res w32. New and det meet the budget on every row. No
matched candidate meets it on the 2 `!` rows. 39 rows were re-timed in a
second run on another B200 node with the same software, because tc did
not run on them in the first run: H1536 T65536, plus T256/T1024/T4096 of
H5120 w32, H6144 w32, H6144 res and H6144 res w32. All columns of those
rows come from the second run.

- `~`: 117 rows
- `!`: 2 rows, [T,24,256] T65536 bwd and 2xfwd+bwd. The fastest matched
candidate is shown (tc, dw err/tol 1.122).

(100 % of samples at max), memory clock 3996 MHz, 4 GPUs of one node.

and SOTA meet the budget on every row.

### [a06f30d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a06f30dc079de78a2a0274449bee711498e4ca5c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T02:39:27Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_grouped_fp8_gemm): 256-byte L2 promotion on the A and B tensor maps of the deep-K N256 program (#8520)

`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm` is Cake's contiguous grouped FP8 (E4M3) GEMM for
MoE layouts on Blackwell. It writes BF16 output, groups rows by
`m_indices`, and is used through `flashinfer.gemm`
`group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise_contiguous`. It supports two block-scale
formats: FP32 per-128-block scales (16 routes) and packed power-of-two
UE8M0 int32 block scales (15 routes). This PR changes one FP32-scale
program, the deep-K N256 program with 128 x 256 output tiles, which is
renamed from `cake_grouped_fp8_gemm_0244c42d588c7898347e` to
`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm_664e5f82737cd4cdfee3`. Its A and B tensor maps
now use 256-byte L2 promotion; the kernel code, outputs, routes and all
other programs are unchanged. On B200, this PR / previous Cake ratios
are 0.9900 to 0.9930 against the previous Cake version of the same
program (FlashInfer main, `0244c42d`) on the three shapes that route to
it, and 0.9867 to 0.9937 on GB300.

**Table 1.** NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1.
Latencies are median kernel times in microseconds. A ratio is the
paired, position-cancelled ratio: the median over 3 seeds of the median
of both timing orders. Because of this, it can differ slightly from the
quotient of the medians. A ratio below 1 means this PR is faster.

| Row | M | N | K | Groups | Rows per group | Previous Cake (us) | This
PR (us) | This PR / previous | CuTe DSL (us) | This PR / CuTe DSL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 16384 | 2048 | 2048 | 64 | 256 | 70.78 | 70.43 | 0.9914 | 71.42 |
0.9849 |
| B | 16384 | 4096 | 2048 | 64 | 256 | 137.28 | 135.94 | 0.9930 | 136.27
| 0.9982 |
| C | 8192 | 4096 | 1024 | 64 | alternating 96 / 160 | 86.46 | 85.54 |
0.9900 | n/a¹ | n/a¹ |

¹ The CuTe DSL backend does not support this layout because it requires
every internal expert boundary to fall on a multiple of 128 rows.

**Table 2.** NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, CUDA 13.4 toolkit. GB300 boards fall
into a faster and a slower performance class, and one board of each
class was measured. The rows match Table 1, and the units and ratio
definition are the same.

| Row | Faster: previous (us) | Faster: this PR (us) | Faster: ratio |
Slower: previous (us) | Slower: this PR (us) | Slower: ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 65.63 | 65.26 | 0.9937 | 65.15 | 64.45 | 0.9867 |
| B | 126.58 | 125.49 | 0.9893 | 124.45 | 123.62 | 0.9887 |
| C | 83.02 | 82.18 | 0.9897 | 82.40 | 81.63 | 0.9906 |

The fused SiLU-and-quantize form `cake_grouped_fp8_fused_silu_quant` and
the masked batch form `cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8` are separate Cake
variants, and the family ships on sm_100a and sm_103a.

### [5335002](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/533500214888b57a99a3914a8167b25c776c9833)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-04T01:22:23Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_gdn): keep the segment transfer plane in the full saved set of the KCP GDN package (#8542)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` is the non-deterministic
KCP (context-parallel) GDN training package (BF16; contiguous, zigzag
and per-document zigzag layouts; optional in-kernel q/k L2 norm;
forward, backward and checkpointed calls). The bug affects
`save_mode="full"` with `save_transfer=False` on a rank whose fragments
split into P > 1 segments. There, the backward's merges read the M_seg^T
staging plane that the forward's transfer walk wrote. But the eager
forward dropped that workspace plane. The saved set kept it only under
`save_transfer=True`, and the full backward runs no transfer walk. So
the merges read a freshly allocated, never-written buffer. As a result,
gradients could differ from the light form's and could change from run
to run with a reused workspace. `exchange="ring"` requires
`save_transfer=False`, so `save_mode="full"` with the ring exchange was
affected too. With this PR, the full saved set carries M_seg at P > 1 in
either `save_transfer` form. The forward allocates the plane fresh
instead of taking it from the workspace pool, so there is no extra
launch. The saved byte query counts the plane, and a full saved set
without M_seg at P > 1 is refused. The forward output, the light form
(the default) and `save_transfer=True` compute the same results as
before. The second commit (83c26d9e) updates two recompute-output test
expectations for torch builds outside the verified set; no package code
changes. The third commit (5b7fd0a6) makes the saved byte query
(`gdn_saved_bytes_kcp` / `gdn_saved_layout_kcp`) count the whole plane,
P x fragments x s with s = v heads x 64 KiB, instead of (P - 1) x
fragments x s (for example, 6 MiB for a 9 MiB plane at P = 3, one
fragment, 48 v heads); this also changes the query value under
`save_transfer=True`, and runtime behavior is unchanged.

This PR does not change the other Cake GDN training variants (the
single-rank packages `cake_gdn_train` and `cake_gdn_det_train` and the
deterministic KCP package `cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`); architecture
coverage stays sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

**Correctness**

The repro on the timed GPUs compares gradients bitwise with the light
form; most checks run with NaN-filled allocations (242 of 262 on B200,
282 of 298 on GB300, 42 of 52 on R200):

- B200: previous is incorrect in 32 of 262 checks (28 non-finite, 4
finite but not bitwise equal to the light form); this PR in 0 of 262 (0
of 408 with its extra checks).
- GB300: previous is incorrect in 54 of 298 checks (52 non-finite, 2
finite but not bitwise equal); this PR in 0 of 298.
- R200: previous is incorrect in 4 of 52 checks (4 non-finite); this PR
in 0 of 52.

With this PR, every form is finite and bitwise equal to the light form.
The controls of previous (light, replay, `save_transfer=True`, P = 1)
are correct. In the timed processes (no NaN fill), forward outputs match
previous bitwise in every record. Gradients differ only in the affected
forms on B200 and GB300 (dbeta, dg, dk and dv in full / a2a and full /
ring). On R200, previous happened to read the right values in the timed
processes (24 of 24 records equal). In the fixed forms previous can read
a never-written buffer and return incorrect gradients (32 of the 36
affected-form repro checks on B200, 54 of 58 on GB300, 4 of 8 on R200),
so its timings there are a timing reference only.

**Conventions**

- Ratio = baseline ms / this PR ms. Above 1 means this PR is faster. `*`
marks a ratio below 1.
- Workload label: B23 = the timing shape (see the table legend), CPn =
context parallel over n GPUs, C = contiguous. Operations: fwd, fwd+bwd,
ckpt (2 x fwd + bwd).
- The repro notes in the tables also use Z = zigzag, D = per-document
zigzag and shape A = 4 documents 98304/65536/57344/40960 (262144
tokens), heads (16, 48).
- Changed forms: full / a2a and full / ring (`save_mode="full"`,
`save_transfer=False`). Unchanged controls: light (the default) and
light / no-st (`save_transfer=False`).
- The shape plans P = 1 at CP1. The R200 rows labelled P = 2 force two
segments per fragment. The R200 light (control) row runs at the planned
P = 1.
- Class per run: per group, c = this PR ms / previous ms and a = A/A ms
/ previous ms. This is the inverse direction of the table ratios. A run
is win if every c is below 1 and below every a, REGRESSION if every c is
above 1 and above every a, and parity otherwise.
- A workload regresses only if two or more of its published runs are
REGRESSION and its fwd+bwd and ckpt cells point the same way.

**Baselines**

- Previous = this package on FlashInfer main
1798b527fa18607ebf59fbba279154650b1ff526. det(main) = the deterministic
KCP package `flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` of the same
main. Both share one process with this PR and an A/A arm (a second byte
copy of previous).
- Non-Cake arms:
- FLA (fla-core / flash-linear-attention 0.6.0) runs as FLA-CP (its own
context parallelism) or FLA-HS (head split around its single-GPU
kernels).
- cuDNN FROST GDN (nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.32.1 with nvidia-cutlass-dsl
4.8.1) runs in the same head split. FROST-ck0 recomputes the states in
the backward; FROST-ck64 stores them every 64 tokens.
- These are the GDN training implementations with forward and backward
that run on these GPUs in one process with the same packed
variable-length inputs.
- Each non-Cake arm's outputs and input gradients are checked against
this PR on the row's inputs (finite, rel-RMS <= 1e-2, max-abs <= 2e-2 x
max|ref|). The non-Cake arms ran in separate processes with this PR's
default light form.
- A process qualifies for a row's non-Cake cell when three conditions
hold in that process:
- This PR and the shown arm (the fastest arm that passes the accuracy
check and drifts <= 2 %) both drift <= 2 %.
- Every other arm of the process with drift above 2 % is slower than the
shown arm in every group, so it cannot be the strongest arm.
  - The power-cap share of this PR and the shown arm is below 5 %.
- If several processes qualify, the table shows the first in time and
lists the others' ratios as further values.
- The non-Cake ratio divides by this PR ms of the row's source run (the
first run of the row with a published det(main) cell, else the first
with a published table A cell, else the first run). It is published only
if this PR drifts <= 2 % in that source run too.
- This PR's light form did not take the same time in the non-Cake
process shown in table B as in its table A run (fwd / fwd+bwd / ckpt,
ms): GB300 CP4 1.300 / 3.046 / 4.948 vs 1.313 / 2.935 / 4.654; R200 CP1
0.995 / 3.566 / 3.894 vs 1.016 / 3.523 / 3.777; B200 CP4 1.076 / 2.799 /
3.862 vs 1.064 / 2.797 / 3.848; B200 CP8 fwd 0.923 vs 0.903, ckpt 4.070
vs 4.001. The non-Cake ratios include this cross-process difference, up
to 6.3 % (GB300 ckpt). With both times from the same process, the GB300
light row gives fwd+bwd 1.909 (5.816 / 3.046) and ckpt 1.666 (8.243 /
4.948), against the published 1.982 and 1.771.
- FlashQLA 0.1.3 needs its own environment and is not an arm. #8521
measured it only at CP1 on its shape M (5 documents
12000/9000/6000/3768/2000, 32768 tokens, heads (16, 48)) on B200 and
GB300. There it was slower than both FROST modes and faster than FLA in
all 12 measured cells. On those B200 inputs FROST failed the accuracy
check, so there FlashQLA could be the strongest passing arm. It was not
measured on shape B23 or on R200.

**Setup**

- GPUs: B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs; CP4 and CP8), GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs;
CP4), R200 (sm_107a, 208 SMs; CP1).
- Software: CUDA 13.4 development container, torch 2.14.1+cu130, NCCL
2.30.7, triton 3.8.0. Eager only; CUDA graph was not timed.
- Cold L2: a 256 MiB fill, a synchronize and a barrier run before every
timed call. An iteration's time is the slowest rank's. The statistic is
the median over the timed iterations.
- Table A and the first non-Cake processes run 5 palindromic groups x 2
blocks x 12 timed calls (2 warm-up) per arm. The non-Cake processes of
B200 CP8, GB300 CP4 and R200 CP1 were re-timed in two more processes
with 7 groups x 2 blocks x 24 timed calls (10 warm-up), the second with
the arm order reversed.
- Drift = |last group median - first group median| / median of the group
medians. A table A or det(main) cell is published only if both compared
arms drift <= 2 %; non-Cake cells follow the rule under **Baselines**.
Unlike #8521, a cell whose per-group paired ratios lie within 1 %
despite a larger drift is not published either.
- A run with >= 5 % of timed samples under the software power cap on any
compared arm is not claimed.
- A/A ms / previous ms per published run (min / median / max): B200
0.988 / 1.001 / 1.004 (19 runs), GB300 0.995 / 1.001 / 1.004 (7 runs),
R200 0.996 / 0.999 / 1.002 (23 runs).

**B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)**

- **vs previous (table A):** no win claimed. fwd 0.996-1.011 (6 runs,
all parity), fwd+bwd 0.998-1.001 (5 runs, all parity), ckpt 0.993-0.999
(8 runs: 7 parity, 1 REGRESSION). 13 of 19 runs are below 1.
- **REGRESSION:** one run of the CP4 full / a2a ckpt cell (0.993). Its
other two runs are parity. No workload regresses (0 of 6).
- **vs det(main) (table B):** this PR is faster on all 12 published
rows: fwd 1.281-1.494, fwd+bwd 1.371-1.406, ckpt 1.278-1.368.
- **vs non-Cake (table B):** CP4 rows: fwd 2.050-2.148 (FROST-ck0),
fwd+bwd 2.048-2.280 (FROST-ck64), ckpt 1.914-2.003 (FROST-ck64). CP8:
light (control) fwd 1.525 (FROST-ck0), and ckpt 1.194-1.304 (FROST-ck64)
over the three forms. The CP8 full / a2a and full / ring fwd rows and
every CP8 fwd+bwd row are not published because this PR drifts above 2 %
in their source run. No value is below 1.

**GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs)**

- **vs previous (table A):** no win claimed. fwd 0.996-0.999 (2 runs),
fwd+bwd 0.992-0.999 (3 runs), ckpt 0.992-0.998 (2 runs). All 7 runs are

**Extra memory**

With `save_transfer=False`, the full saved set now keeps M_seg (fp32, P
x fragments x v heads x 64 KiB per rank) at P > 1. The light form and P
= 1 ranks save nothing extra. The saved byte query reports these bytes.
In the timed rows this is 9.0 MiB on the largest rank at CP4 and CP8
(63.0 MiB over all 8 ranks at CP8) and 24.0 MiB at the forced R200 P = 2
row.

## Performance tables

Previous = the non-deterministic KCP package of FlashInfer main
(1798b527); this PR = this PR's package (aced27d8); both run in one
process with det(main) (the deterministic KCP package of FlashInfer
main) and an A/A arm (a second byte copy of previous).

Table A cells: previous ms -> this PR ms of the first published run
(absolutes are that run's), then the ratios previous / this PR of every
published run in time order and the class per run (A/A envelope of
per-group ratios: win, parity = inside the A/A spread, REGRESSION).
Table B: ratio = baseline ms / this PR ms from the absolutes in the row.
Regression rule: a workload regresses only if two or more published runs
are REGRESSION and their fwd+bwd and ckpt cells point the same way; no
workload regresses.

Legend: '*' = ratio below 1.000 (this PR slower than that baseline);
'n/p unstable' = not published (group drift above 2 % on a compared arm;
for non-Cake cells see the rule under table B), listed at the end; bwd
alone (fwd+bwd minus fwd) is not published. Power-cap share (timed
samples under the software power cap): at most 0.0 % in every published
table A run.

Shape B23: 4 documents 12288/8192/7168/5120 (32768 tokens), heads (16,
48) (q/k heads, v heads), head dim 128; every timed call runs the short
causal convolution over the packed q/k/v channels (10240) and the GDN
layer; layout C = contiguous; CPn = context parallel over n GPUs; P =
the segment count per fragment that the plan picks.

|form|save_mode|save_transfer|exchange|this PR|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|full / a2a|"full"|False|"a2a"|changed: saves M_seg at P > 1|
|full / ring|"full"|False|"ring"|changed: saves M_seg at P > 1|
|light (control)|"light" (default)|True (default)|"a2a"
(default)|unchanged|
|light / no-st (control)|"light"|False|"a2a"|unchanged|

'P = 2': the shape plans P = 1 at CP1, so the R200 rows labelled P = 2
force two segments per fragment (segments=2) to run the affected path;
the R200 light (control) row runs at the planned P = 1. Table B arms:
FLA-CP = flash-linear-attention's own context parallelism; FLA-HS = head
split (all-to-all) around FLA's single-GPU kernels; FROST-ck0 / -ck64 =
the same head split around cuDNN frontend's GDN (states recomputed /
stored every 64 tokens).

Add opt-in `swap_ab=True` to Blackwell (SM100/SM103) split CuTe DSL MoE:
weights on MMA A, activations on B, dynamic MMA N, and FC1 input
gathering inside the GEMM. Existing non-swap blockscaled kernels remain
the default. W4A16 uses the new input-gathering path with either weight
layout.

- **Input pipeline:** a dedicated four-warp group gathers original token
rows, removing standalone activation permutation and its expanded input
buffer. Swap-AB uses TMA gather4 for values and predicated asynchronous
word copies for scale factors; W4A16 gathers BF16 values with TMA.
Routing metadata remains separate; FC2 keeps regular TMA loads.
- **Kernel organization:** swap-AB FC1 has control, epilogue and gather
warpgroups. W4A16 adds gathering as its fifth, final warpgroup.
Role-specific register budgets and compile-time buffer sizing preserve
staged loading, multicast, CLC and PDL; FC2 can prefetch weights/scales
before its activation dependency is ready. Only writer warps commit FC2
TMA stores; MMA scale descriptors use compile-time IDs. Ordinary operand
`producer_tail` calls and the linear quantization maximum remain.
- **API/layout:** select the same `swap_ab` mode for weight preparation
and execution. Gated FC1 uses up16/gate16 rows; W4A16 also supports the
original up64/gate64 layout through in-kernel transpose. NVFP4
W4A4/per-token, MXFP4x8 (`w4a8`) and MXFP8 (`mxfp8`) are supported,
including ClampedReLU² with the upstream runtime clamp tensor. W4A16
retains its existing activation support. Swap-AB keeps one shared
FC1/FC2 CLC autotune choice; W4A16 tactics are unchanged. Nongated FC1
joins converted fragments through integer registers for wider FP4/FP8
stores, preserving scale/conversion order.
- **Reuse:** share routing, combine, the per-token quantizer and
Blackwell utilities. The shared W4A16 dequantizer duplicates each scale
byte with one PRMT. W4A16 pairs SiTU RN arithmetic and skips wholly
unused K-transform groups with a per-group stage cutoff; all phase
transitions remain. MegaMoE explicitly retains its padded-K transform
extent. Keep fused activation/requantization, compile-time partial-K
handling, SM103 NVFP4 K96 MMA, zero-tolerance swap-AB accuracy coverage
and the manual sanitizer script. No separate prepare or inline-PTX
module remains.

**Matched regression check against `a620ce77`:** geomean **-0.09%**
across 396 displayed cases; swap-AB **-0.03%**, W4A16 **-0.29%**,
prefill (4096–16384) **-0.36%**. 197 cases are slower; worst **-6.17%**.
All negatives remain. Maximum repeat spreads are 9.17% control / 6.35%
candidate; small differences do not establish uniform non-regression.
[Full matched
diagnostics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zianglih/flashinfer/e12ed6c3e7c619f06c427bc69e05ff7c3fedd955/2b473279/retained/stats.md).

**Isolated repeat:** 12 predeclared cases were rerun alone in A→C→C→A
(4,800 additional samples): geomean +0.42%. V41F EP4 at 16,384 remains
-2.64% MXFP4x8 / -2.14% MXFP8, with 6.53% / 4.48% control repeat

- **Method:** same-GPU C→A→A→C per job, 10 warmups and 100 strict-CUPTI
cold-L2 CUDA-graph samples per phase: **187,200 total / 93,600 candidate
samples**. Rank-local EP/TP simulation; frozen recorded tactics,
including ten W4A16 defaults; no retuning or event fallback.
W4A4/per-token include initial quantization; W4A16 consumes BF16
directly. Candidate clock windows: 82/3,744 exceptional (median SM clock

Representative split-MoE command (use the archived role-specific frozen
cache):

```bash
export FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3a FLASHINFER_CUTE_DSL_STRICT_CACHE_KEY=1
export FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE=0 TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL=1
export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=0 TRTLLM_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=0
export CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR=/path/to/persistent-cute-cache
python benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py \
  --functional-api --model v3 --ep 8 --tp 1 --quant-family nvfp4 \
  --backends cutedsl --swap-ab --no-fused-finalize --include-activation-quant \
  --num-tokens 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,4096,8192,16384 \
  --cache /path/to/frozen-winners --warmup 10 --iters 100 --no-autotune --output-format both
```

Other presets: `v41-flash` EP/TP4; `kimi-k3` and `nemo3-ultra` EP/TP8.
TP uses `--ep 1 --tp N`. MX uses `--quant-family mxfp --backends
cute-dsl-w4a8,cute-dsl-mxfp8` without `--include-activation-quant`.
Archived per-job commands and observation wrappers enforce frozen
choices and CUPTI without event fallback.

**W4A16 small-token EP regression.** The new FC1 gather also applies to
default `swap_ab=False`. We reproduced the [reviewer's

with frozen tactics, V3 EP8 at 4 tokens goes from 50.416 to 53.600 µs on

all four models at 4/8/16 tokens, default-path EP geomeans are −1.78% /
−0.60% on B200 / B300, while TP gains +6.23% / +6.13%.

These are whole unfused MoE measurements at `14a338579` against pre-PR
`002529e17`, using the same CUDA 13.2 container above, strict CUPTI,

host/API/test fixes in `409a39fae` leave the measured kernels unchanged.

**Historical shared-helper evidence.** The following comparison was
measured at `4376662a` for the single-PRMT scale duplication still
present in this merge. The MegaMoE padded-K handoff has representative
byte-identical native qualification; no distributed timing was rerun for
this refresh.

### Shared W4A16 dequantizer: GLM5 MegaMoE

Following
[#6277](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6277), this
isolates the shared scale-duplication change: both arms use production
`4376662a`; **before** restores only `moe_w4a16_utils.py` from the
parent of `1e4b127a`, and **after** keeps the current helper. MegaMoE
inherits this dequantizer through `_MegaMixedInput._transform_tile`.

- **Workload:** real EP8 on 8×B300 SXM6 AC, D6144/I2048, 256 experts,
top8, SwiGLU, grouped routing 8/top4, scaling 2.5. Precomputed routes;
PDL and fused deterministic combine enabled; in-kernel FC2 reduction
disabled.
- **Measurement:** one control AUTO selection per token count, then the
same frozen tactics/routes in four fresh process groups, C1→A1→A2→C2.
Each uses 3 warmups and 100 untrimmed cold-L2 CUDA-graph CUPTI samples,
aggregated by rank-MAX per iteration. Each reported latency is the
median of 200 samples per arm; speedup=`before/after−1`. Tokens 1/2 are
measured but excluded from aggregates.
- **Environment:** `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.05-py3`, CUDA 13.2, driver
595.91.07, PyTorch `2.12.0a0+5aff3928d8.nv26.5.50603568`, CuTe DSL
4.8.0, CUPTI Python 13.2.0/library 13.2.86, NVSHMEM4Py 0.3.1/library
3.6.5. Native C++ compilation artifacts are retained outside timing.

Geomean speedup: **+1.54% overall**, **+1.79% decode (4–512)** and
**+0.89% prefill (4096–16384)**. All three pooled prefill points
improve. Decode is mixed: 4/8/32 tokens regress by 2.53%/1.21%/3.89%,
while repeat-phase median spreads reach 11.37%; this does **not**
establish uniform per-shape non-regression.

The [local benchmark
wrapper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zianglih/flashinfer/2402bcd61a7cc39f650f6b92dd1aa2293ee50518/pr7290/2026-10-29/glm5-helper-4376662a/native_frozen.py)

tactics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zianglih/flashinfer/2402bcd61a7cc39f650f6b92dd1aa2293ee50518/pr7290/2026-10-29/glm5-helper-4376662a/frozen-tactics.json)
and records untimed route fingerprints; timed forwards use
`benchmarks/bench_cute_dsl_moe_distributed.py` unchanged. For each
source arm, point `MEGA_SOURCE`/`PYTHONPATH` at its checkout and
`MEGA_FROZEN_TACTICS` at the downloaded JSON, then run:

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
export FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3a FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE=0
export FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6=1 FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_E4M3_USE_256=1
export FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_ERR_MODE=MSE FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_ERR_USE_FAST_MATH=1
export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=1
export PYTHONWARNINGS='error:CUPTI is not installed:UserWarning'
torchrun --master-addr=127.0.0.1 --master-port=29672 --nproc-per-node=8 \
  native_frozen.py --model glm5 --mode benchmark --parallel-modes ep \
  --num-gpus 8 --variants w4a16_megamoe \
  --num-tokens 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,4096,8192,16384 \
  --timing cupti --cuda-graph --precomputed-routing --no-fused-finalize \
  --warmup 3 --iters 100 --log-timing-samples --megamoe-knobs auto
```

The wrapper replaces `auto` with the same frozen knob dictionary before
constructing each layer. All 52 timing records, 416 per-rank tactic
records and 416 route fingerprints passed validation; no CUPTI fallback
occurred. Benchmark results are a performance check of the shared
helper, not a new numerical or sanitizer qualification.

### [c0d987d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c0d987da1f72d787f6a01445e826116096d15fe4)
